items.title: Intraoperative Blood Pressure Targeting in Noncardiac Surgery: A Bayesian Random-effects Meta-analysis of Randomized Trials.
items.abstract: Background Whether protocolized intraoperative arterial pressure-targeting strategies provide incremental benefit beyond contemporary usual care remains uncertain. The authors performed a Bayesian meta-analysis of randomized trials in major noncardiac surgery. Methods MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception to January 5, 2026, with additional literature surveillance through June 29, 2026. Randomized trials comparing protocolized intraoperative arterial pressure-targeting strategies with usual care or lower-pressure approaches were included. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes were acute kidney injury (AKI) and myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery (MINS). Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis was prespecified as the primary analytical framework, with confirmatory frequentist analyses. Results Fifteen randomized trials met the inclusion criteria. Mortality (13 trials) remained centered around an odds ratio (OR) of 1.00 (frequentist OR, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.83 to 1.21; Bayesian median OR, 1.00; 95% credible interval [CrI], 0.73 to 1.38), with wide Bayesian prediction intervals (OR, 0.56 to1.78). AKI (14 trials) showed the most favorable estimates (frequentist OR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.73 to 1.03; Bayesian median OR, 0.88; 95% CrI, 0.70 to 1.05), but estimates remained compatible with no clinically important benefit, heterogeneity was moderate, and leave-one-out analyses, excluding each trial in turn, showed sensitivity to individual trial exclusion. MINS (eight trials) likewise remained compatible with no treatment effect (frequentist OR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.93 to 1.15; Bayesian median OR, 1.05; 95% CrI, 0.90 to 1.26). Exploratory analyses suggested that any potential renal benefit may depend on the broader hemodynamic context in which arterial pressure targets are implemented. Conclusions Protocolized intraoperative arterial pressure-targeting strategies did not demonstrate a consistent incremental benefit over contemporary usual care in major noncardiac surgery. Mortality and MINS remained compatible with no treatment effect. Although AKI showed the most favorable estimates, the evidence remained uncertain, was sensitive to individual trial exclusion, and should be interpreted cautiously.

items.title: Beneath the glass ceiling: an examination of gender disparities in Canadian medical education leadership.
items.abstract: This study aims to assess gender representation in leadership and academic ranks within Canadian universities and affiliated medical schools during 2020-2021, and describe scholarly productivity by inferred gender. This cross-sectional study identified 1,163 faculty leaders across 17 medical schools and parent universities. Public records, NamSor-inferred gender and Scopus bibliometrics were analysed using contingency tables, Cramér's V and exploratory unadjusted odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals. Productivity comparisons were descriptive. Gender was associated with leadership category among 1,110 tabulated leaders (χ2(3) = 24.49, p < 0.001; V = 0.149) and academic rank among 823 leaders (χ2(2) = 16.39, p < 0.001; V = 0.141). Women comprised 30.1% of department heads and 36.1% of full professors. Women had lower odds than men of holding department-head versus other listed leadership roles (OR = 0.46, 95% CI 0.33-0.64) and full versus assistant/associate professorships (OR = 0.54, 95% CI 0.40-0.73). Mean bibliometric measures were higher among men. These historical data cannot establish current representation or causal mechanisms. Gender inference, differing analytic denominators, unmeasured confounding and unaddressed institutional clustering limit interpretation. Updated longitudinal studies, interviews and validated surveys are needed. This national analysis examines gender representation in leadership, academic rank and scholarly productivity across Canadian universities and their affiliated medical schools.

items.title: AGNFormer. I: Reconstruction of active galactic nucleus spectra using a probabilistic transformer model
items.abstract: When analysing spectroscopic data to extract physical properties, emphasis is often placed on small portions of a spectrum (e.g. ionisation diagnostic diagrams, broad Hβ or Mg ii emission lines, etc.), potentially discarding a wealth of useful information. We explore how an uncertainty-aware transformer-based architecture can leverage information embedded across the entire observed optical spectra of active galactic nuclei (AGNs), focussing on the algorithm's ability to predict unseen or masked parts of luminous AGN spectra, providing a direct probe of the learnable correlations between AGN continua and broad lines. We introduce AGNFormer -1 $; missing halves), inputting rest-frame spectral fluxes and uncertainties across the entire redshift range of the SDSS DR16 Quasar Catalogue. We evaluate the performance of the model on both full (no S/N limit) and high-quality (S/N $> 10) spectral samples using the negative-log likelihood and via comparisons with existing ̧iv and łyman reconstruction algorithms. The model successfully reconstructs unseen AGN broad lines up to an error floor of ≈2-6% of the flux at S/N ≈ 40, while the predictive power for larger unseen halves diminishes with distance from the cut-off wavelength of the input spectrum. Predictions faithfully reproduce the broad AGN spectral diversity across the entire optical and UV quasi-stellar object (QSO) main sequence parameter spaces, including both Gaussian and Lorentzian profile regimes, complexes, and narrow emission lines. The performance is found to be similar or better compared to previous spectral reconstruction algorithms. The high precision of the broad-line region reconstruction demonstrates that the method successfully aggregates information across the spectrum and highlights how the AGN continuum as well as weaker lines and complexes have the potential to assist astronomers in the extraction of the entire wealth of information embedded in AGN spectra. 's underlying model could be a valuable tool for processing the spectra of many other classes of astrophysical objects. AGNFormer

items.title: Euclid. XI. A two-point correlation approach to diagnosing star-related systematics in the spectroscopic survey
items.abstract: The Euclid spectroscopic survey will measure galaxy clustering with unprecedented precision, which demands stringent control over observational and instrumental systematics. Among these, star-related effects may contaminate the spectroscopic images through photometric persistence and through imperfect masking of stellar images. We characterized the imprint of star-related effects in the spectroscopic exposures and quantified their impact on galaxy clustering analyses. If these effects produce characteristic angular features, they can be identified and characterized in the data, thereby enabling an assessment of their impact on cosmological measurements. We used angular and spatial auto- and cross-correlation statistics to quantify these effects. For the galaxies we used mock spectroscopic catalogues extracted from EuclidLargeMocks. We focused on a 330 region of the Euclid Wide Survey (EWS). For the stars, we considered the real Gaia and star catalogues in the same area. To simulate photometric persistence, we implemented a simplified detector-level model calibrated on spectroscopic measurements and modulated the strength of the effect to introduce varying fractions of `interlopers' into the mock galaxy catalogues. For the stellar mask, we modelled potential inconsistencies between the mask used to remove regions around stars in the data and the mask applied to the random catalogue used to quantify the survey selection function. We measured the star--star, galaxy--galaxy, and star--galaxy angular correlation functions using the Landy--Szalay estimator and quantified deviations from the expected null star–galaxy correlation with a dedicated metric. Finally, we evaluated the impact of these systematics on large scales using the 3D two-point correlation function (2PCF). Our results show that photometric persistence produces a characteristic feature in the star--galaxy angular cross-correlation at scales of order 100 consistent with the scale set by the Euclid dithering pattern and grism dispersion geometry. It also induces a spurious, positive cross-correlation signal that remains approximately constant in amplitude up to 1^̧irc. We find that star–galaxy cross-correlation analysis is a sensitive tool for detecting residual persistence and is capable of revealing spurious contamination levels as low as 10% in a Data Release 1-like spectroscopic catalogue. In contrast, mismatches in stellar masking produce strong small-scale angular signatures but do not significantly impact the large-scale 2PCF under realistic EWS conditions.

items.title: P2D - A Two-Dimensional Multi-Spacecraft Solar Wind Persistence Model
items.abstract: The background solar wind is a key component in space weather forecasting, as it contains geoeffective high-speed streams and provides the medium through which coronal mass ejections propagate and evolve in interplanetary space. Due to the solar rotation and the slow evolution of large-scale solar wind structures, solar wind properties exhibit an autocorrelation with a period of roughly 27 days, particularly at solar minimum. We made use of this property to develop a solar wind persistence model with input from multiple spacecraft (Solar Orbiter, Parker Solar Probe, STEREO-A, STEREO-B and the OMNI database). The model ballistically propagates in-situ data from the position of their measurement radially away from the Sun, as well as longitudinally with the solar rotation rate, producing 2D maps of solar wind parameters. These can be extracted at any point in the heliosphere for a solar wind reconstruction. From Earth’s perspective, the reconstruction performs with an MAE of 65.41 km~s$^{-1}$ and 3.51 $cm^{-3}$ for speed and density, respectively. During high-speed streams, the peak hit rate is 50\% and 48\% for speed and density. It performs best during times when there are spacecraft located between Earth and Lagrange point L5. During these times, the mean absolute error of the predicted solar wind velocity decreases by roughly 35\% in comparison to the benchmark 27-day persistence model. Therefore, future L5 missions like Vigil are expected to provide a robust basis for reliable persistence forecasts.

items.title: The ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST Survey: Investigating the role of interstellar dust, gas, and stars in high-z galaxies at kiloparsec scales
items.abstract: A comprehensive understanding of galaxy evolution requires a detailed analysis of gas and dust, including their distribution and evolution within galaxies. In this work, we analyse spatially resolved (∼,1-2,kpc) rest-frame C ii and dust continuum ALMA observations together with JWST/NIRSpec IFU data of a sample of six massive galaxies at z,∼,4-5. We focus on deriving and comparing the spatial distributions of atomic and molecular gas masses, dust and stellar masses, star formation rates (SFR), and metallicity. The oxygen abundance maps have median values in the range of 12+log(O/H),sim8.1-8.3 with variations of the order of 1,dex within the same galaxy. In four galaxies of our sample, the oxygen abundance shows a minimum at the peak of the Hα emission and an enhancement in the outer parts. The calibration used in this study to estimate the atomic gas mass in our galaxies seems to overestimate the atomic gas mass surface densities by up to one to two orders of magnitude. However, a calibration based on a spatially resolved C ii conversion factor gives a more robust estimation of the total gas mass. The dust-to-gas surface mass density ratio varies between łog Σ_ ̊m dust /Σ_ ̊m gas =-2.2 ^ +0.24 _ -0.19 and łogΣ_ ̊m dust /Σ_ ̊m gas =-2.69^ +0.21 _ -0.16 , while the dust-to-stellar surface mass density ratio ranges from łogΣ_ ̊m dust /Σ_ ̊m star =-2.01^ +0.13 _ -0.12 to łogΣ_ ̊m dust /Σ_ ̊m star =-2.91^ +0.13 _ -0.13 . A detailed analysis of the dust-to-stellar surface mass density ratio and the gas mass fraction versus metallicity revealed that galaxies exhibiting signatures of strong outflows have a lower dust-to-stellar surface mass density ratio and lower gas mass fractions than the galaxies with no outflow signatures. While the latter is consistent with these galaxies ejecting part of their gas reservoir to the circumgalactic medium, the low dust-to-stellar surface mass density ratios also suggest that part of the dust content is expelled outside the galaxy, which reinforces previous theoretical suggestions of dust removal by stellar feedback or radiation pressure to explain the high UV luminosities in galaxies at very high redshifts. Some galaxies of our sample have almost an order of magnitude higher ratios of dust-to-gas and dust-to-stellar surface mass density than galaxies in the local Universe, suggesting that a large dust reservoir has been built up already at timescales of sim1,Gyr in these galaxies.

items.title: Surveying for close binaries among lithium-rich giants
items.abstract: The existence of low-mass giants with high lithium (Li) abundances poses a challenge to our understanding of post-main sequence stellar structure and evolution. Li-rich giants are preferentially found in the red clump (RC) rather than on the first-ascent red giant branch (RGB). One of the scenarios proposed to explain this Li enrichment involves tidal interaction with a close binary companion, which, if dominant, predicts an enhanced binary fraction among Li-rich giants relative to Li-normal ones. We aim to test the binary interaction scenario for the origin of Li-rich giants by using multi-epoch radial velocities (RVs) in order to measure the close binary fraction of a statistically robust sample of Li-rich giants. The surveyed sample contains both RC and RGB targets, which allows us to examine potential differences in the binary fraction as a function of evolutionary stage. We monitored 70 giants (40 RC and 30 RGB) using the ESPRESSO spectrograph, 57 (32 RC and 25 RGB) of which already had four or more visits over a ∼7-month baseline. The analysis presented here is based on these latter targets. We first used a criterion based on surface gravity and the maximum observed RV difference within our data in order to discard RV variations attributable to intrinsic stellar jitter. For the targets with RV variation larger than this threshold, we performed Monte Carlo simulations over a grid of companion mass and orbital period, to estimate the probability that the observed RV variation is due to a stellar (P_SB) or substellar (P_SS) companion. After removing targets consistent with stellar jitter, 11 (34 ± 8%) RC and eight (32 ± 9%) RGB stars remained as binary candidates or stars with a companion. Of these, three targets (16 ± 8% of the filtered sample) are confirmed stellar binaries. The distributions of P_SB and P_SS are statistically indistinguishable between the RC and RGB samples. We find no evidence in our current data for a binary fraction for Li-rich giants (in either evolutionary stage) larger than that expected for a regular Li-normal population, which suggests that binary interaction is unlikely to be the dominant mechanism driving Li enrichment in this sample. Extending the RV baseline to probe longer orbital periods will be important to continue exploring the plausibility of this scenario.

items.title: The Pristine survey. XXIX. Data Release 2: Photometric metallicities for 15 millions stars down to G∼ 20.3
items.abstract: Tailored narrowband photometric observations are an efficient way to measure the metallicity of Milky Way stars. The Pristine survey has been mapping the northern sky since 2015 using narrowband CaHK photometry obtained with the MegaCam imager on the Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope (CFHT). The Pristine Data Release 1 (DR1) provided a high-precision absolute calibration of the survey observed before October 2022 using Gaia DR3 XP synthetic photometry, yielding photometric metallicities over ∼6500 deg2$, but was limited in depth to the availability of Gaia spectro-photometry ($G łesssim 17.65). We present the Pristine Data Release 2 (DR2) that includes all Pristine observations until January 2025, corresponding to an additional 1500,deg2$ of coverage, and including all faint sources down to $G This release aims to exploit the full depth of the Pristine observations to uncover the faint metal-poor halo. We process all images observed from the start of the survey in March 2015 through to January 2025 following the methodology presented in DR1. The core of the calibration utilizes the subset of bright stars with Gaia synthetic CaHK_ neural network. We then derive photometric metallicities using the established Pristine (CaHK, G, G_ magnitudes to train the PhotCalib ̊m BP , G_ ̊m RP ) to FeH model. The resulting catalog covers approximately ∼ 8000 deg 2 and provides photometric metallicities for 15 million FGK stars, which show good agreement with recently published independent Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) metallicities. With its increased coverage and access to a significantly fainter regime compared to DR1, DR2 significantly increases the volume of the survey. We report more than 200,000 and 6500 very and extremely metal-poor star candidates, respectively.

items.title: Forward model of the Gaia DR3 selection function
items.abstract: The completeness of an astronomical catalogue depends on its selection function, which is a combination of the observing strategy, instrumental characteristics, and intrinsic properties of the sources being observed. This is particularly complex for Gaia, whose non-uniform scanning law and onboard prioritisation of bright sources in dense areas make its selection function vary strongly with celestial position and source brightness. We estimate the source catalogue selection function across the whole sky and over the full magnitude range, using only data from the Gaia catalogue and knowledge of the nominal scanning law as provided by the Gaia Observation Forecast Tool. 3 We developed a hierarchical Bayesian model that estimates the number of times Gaia scanned each celestial position jointly with the source detection efficiency, and fitted it via Markov chain Monte Carlo to the 1,806,196,447 sources in 3 with reported celestial positions, G magnitudes, and astrometric matched transit counts. 3 is essentially complete for G ∈ (5,19.5) in the on-sky median. After that, the completeness decreases with magnitude according to the scanning law pattern combined with the imprint of crowded regions. The completeness is also lower at the very bright end of the survey, consistent with the known limitations on Gaia observations of bright stars. We find an unexpected completeness increase beyond G ∼ 21, which we conclude is an artefact caused by extended sources, as confirmed by cross-matching against Euclid's Q1 catalogue. Our approach builds on previous efforts that use the understanding of the Gaia survey strategy to model the survey selection function. Our model does not rely on a precise knowledge of the Gaia scanning law, making it more robust, while retaining the capability of deriving an all-sky selection function without the need to extrapolate from limited external surveys providing `ground truth'. Treating the scanning law as part of the inference process, and anchoring it to all sources of all magnitudes on a fine-grained grid on the sky, removes the need for an explicit crowding correction. The resulting selection function, valid everywhere where Gaia data are available, is released as part of the GaiaUnlimited Python package. 3

items.title: Constraining dust properties along the minor axis of Andromeda
items.abstract: Previous studies of dust emission in the Andromeda galaxy (M31) based primarily on Herschel data have reported inconsistent radial trends in the dust emissivity index (β), partly due to limited wavelength coverage and the degeneracy between dust temperature (T_̊m dust) and β. We aim to improve the constraints of β determinations and obtain the spatial surface density and temperature distributions at giant molecular cloud scales in M31 by extending the spectral coverage into the millimeter regime and by quantifying the impact of wavelength coverage on the T_̊m dust–β degeneracy. We present the 1.15 mm continuum emission along the minor axis of M31 with the 30 m telescope of the Institut de radioastronomie millimétrique (IRAM). The map has an angular resolution of 11.6'', corresponding to approximately 40 pc at the distance of M31. We used these data with Herschel and 450 and 850 μm maps from the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope to perform pixel-by-pixel single-component modified blackbody fitting. Including the 850 μm and 1.15 mm data helps reduce the T_̊m dust–β degeneracy and yields an average emissivity index of β ≈ 1.8, which is systematically lower than values derived from far-infrared–only analyses. Radial analysis shows higher β values in the 5 kpc ring compared to the 10 kpc ring. The elevated β values in the inner 5 kpc may be linked to changes in dust composition, potentially associated with enhanced starlight heating in this region. Millimeter wavelength coverage is important for improving β constraints in M31. The lower β values inferred from the 250--1150 μm spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting suggest possible variations in dust emissivity and highlight the importance of sampling the long-wavelength SED slope in nearby galaxies.

items.title: Impact of the large-scale environment on the baryonic scaling relations of disc galaxies: Insights from the GASP survey
items.abstract: The Tully--Fisher relation (TFR) and the specific angular momentum--mass relation (SAMR) link the baryonic content of a disc to its kinematics and dynamics. Hence, these scaling relations should bear the imprints of any process removing baryons or altering their kinematics, such as those acting in clusters of galaxies. We tested this scenario using the MUSE survey `GAs Stripping Phenomena in galaxies' (GASP), which targets field, group, and cluster members at z ≈ 0.05 and various stages of ram pressure stripping. For the 81 discs with favourable inclinations, we measured the distribution and kinematics of stars and ionised gas and their specific angular momenta. Within their scatter, the stellar and baryonic relations show no significant dependence on the large-scale environment. The TFRs have slopes of α ≈ 3.6 and ≈ 3.5 for any kinematic tracer, and the SAMRs have α ≈ 0.65--0.75, as predicted by tidal torque theory. The same holds for the ten S0-S0/as in our sample, consistent with the `faded spiral' formation scenario. Only the gas SAMR shows an environmental signature, with ram pressure stripped galaxies lying ≈ 0.16 dex below unperturbed ones. This offset is mostly due to their enhanced star formation rate and thus higher gas mass when inferred through the Schmidt-Kennicutt law rather than to kinematic perturbations or disc truncation. Our results suggest that within the area probed by MUSE (łesssim6 disc scale lengths), these discs have preserved the angular momentum acquired at formation not only from cluster processes and pre-processing in filaments but also from mergers and ejective feedback acting in any environment.

items.title: Mitigating variance shrinkage in multitask galaxy property inference from imaging data via statistical manifold alignment
items.abstract: Inferring photometric redshifts (z) and key stellar population properties (łog(M_*/ _⊙), D_n 4000, and mathrm M H δ_A) directly from multiband imaging is increasingly critical for spectroscopically limited large surveys such as LSST and CSST. However, conventional pointwise loss functions (e.g., mean squared error or Huber loss) employed in deep neural networks often induce ``variance shrinkage''---a regression-to-the-mean effect that contracts predicted variances, distorts nonlinear physical manifolds (such as bimodal distributions), and truncates heavy-tailed populations. Here, we present ViTMultiTask, a vision transformer framework that incorporates a multiscale maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) loss to enforce higher-order joint distribution alignment in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. Trained on 83,846 galaxies from Subaru HSC five-band (g,r,i,z,y) imaging cross-matched with DESI Data Release 1 Bright Galaxy Survey spectra, the model achieves high point-estimate precision on an independent test set of 5,000 galaxies: σ_ NMAD = 0.020 for z, 0.169, for łog(M_*/ _⊙), 0.073 for D_n 4000, and 1.185, δ_A. Ablation experiments demonstrate that incorporating the MMD loss effectively mitigates variance shrinkage and more accurately reproduces the observed spectroscopic parameter distributions (including bimodal structures and heavy tails), while maintaining point-estimate accuracy statistically consistent with the baseline (with RMSE changes łe 3.5%) and catastrophic outlier rates fully comparable to the baseline. This kernel-based manifold alignment offers a statistically grounded and practical paradigm for comprehensive galaxy property inference in the deep imaging era. M for mathrm H

items.title: Inferring accretion bursts in intermediate-mass protostars from asteroseismic imprints
items.abstract: During star formation, objects may gain the majority of their final mass through regular and intense bursts of mass accretion. For burst events of the FU Orionis-type (FUor), accretion rates can climb as high as 10^ -3 in short windows of time, amounting to just a few percent of the main accretion phase. Some bursters had not been observed in the preceding quiescent stage, making their classification as FUors difficult. To study the occurrence of such events observationally, signatures of the current accretion bursts and tracers of recent bursts are crucial. In this work, we investigate the potential to identify current accretion bursts and detect recent bursts in protostars and pre-main sequence (pre-MS) stars of intermediate mass using asteroseismology. The aim is to characterize theoretical period-spacing diagrams of pre-MS gravity-mode (g-mode) pulsators that have undergone accretion bursts. We used the stellar structure and evolution code to evolve stellar models from the protostellar seed phase of 0.01 MESA and 1.5 ̊sun up to 4.0 with a constant accretion rate of 10^ -6 A single accretion burst was initialized during the accretion phase. The stellar oscillation code GYRE was employed to compute the resulting asteroseismic properties of the models. Accretion bursts of up to 10^ -3 are sufficient to cause the convective cores of the models to recede, leaving behind a chemical trace that is manifested in the form of quasi-periodic dips in the g-mode period spacing. This effect is strongest during the outburst, but also lingers for up to 475 years before the convective core is re-established and the dips are gone. Our experiment shows that a single accretion burst leaves an imprint in the deep interiors of protostars and pre-MS stars of intermediate mass and that this imprint can be captured with asteroseismology. Well-resolved g-mode pulsations of young stellar objects may therefore help identify current and recent accretion bursts. Our results are most conclusive for burst magnitudes greater than 1 -4 corresponding to FUor-type bursts.

items.title: The long-period central star of the planetary nebula MPAJ1508-6455
items.abstract: A significant fraction of planetary nebulae have been shown to host short-period binary central stars, but longer-period central stars are scarcer. We characterise the central star of the planetary nebula MPAJ1508-6455, which has previously been claimed to be an intermediate-period binary with a period of approximately 12 days. We studied archival and catalogue photometry to probe the previously reported photometric variability and binary spectral energy distribution. We used long-term high-resolution spectroscopic monitoring to measure the radial velocity curves of the two components of the central binary, and to derive their atmospheric parameters. We also undertook kinematical and chemical abundance analyses of the nebula itself. The orbital period of the central binary of exceeds five years and is highly eccentric. The binary comprises a relatively low-temperature sdO-type central star and a spun-up K-type giant companion. The Kiel mass of the central star is approximately half the dynamical mass derived from the radial velocities. While the systemic velocity and inclination of the nebula are consistent with the radial velocities of the binary, its abundance pattern adds support for a lower-mass progenitor that did not experience hot bottom burning (and is thus more consistent with the Kiel mass than the mass derived from the radial velocities). To the best of our knowledge, the central star of is only the fourth planetary nebula central star to have a spectroscopically confirmed orbital period longer than one year.

items.title: Solar Orbiter observations of solar energetic electron events associated with hard microflares
items.abstract: Generally, large solar flares accelerate electrons to high energies more efficiently than microflares. However, there are microflares, known as hard microflares (HMFs), which also produce high-energy electrons, as evidenced by their flat hard X-ray (HXR) spectra. These events are characterised by a footpoint rooted in or at the edge of a sunspot. The mechanisms underlying this efficient acceleration and their connection to solar energetic electrons (SEEs) are not yet understood. We aim to compare, for the first time, the HXR spectra of HMFs with in situ electron spectra of associated SEEs. For this purpose, we used observations from Solar Orbiter STIX and EPD instruments, respectively. This approach is set to provide new insights into the acceleration processes and how these high-energy electrons access interplanetary space. We found eight HMFs (of GOES C class or lower), jointly observed by Solar Orbiter and Earth-bound observatories, associated with SEEs. This association was verified through timing and magnetic-connectivity analysis. Each event was analysed through STIX HXR spectroscopy, SEE velocity-dispersion analysis, and in situ electron spectral analysis of EPD data. Seven out of eight SEE events show consistent timing between HXR emission from the flare and estimated electron injection into interplanetary space. They also exhibit good agreement between the flare location and the estimated magnetic connectivity to the Sun. When compared with correlation between HXR photon and in situ electron spectral indices established by previous studies, our HMFs tend to populate the hard end of the distribution, even though these previous studies include larger C- and M-class flares. This demonstrates, also through in situ observations, that HMFs efficiently accelerate electrons to high energies and efficient acceleration does not necessarily require large flare energy release. We conclude that HMFs produce prompt SEEs with hard spectral properties, consistent with their hard HXR spectra. This indicates efficient electron acceleration to high energies. The magnetic morphology in HMFs, which involves open field lines from the sunspot, suggests that these events may be an important contributor to filling the heliosphere with energetic particles.

items.title: Euclid: Precise inference of the defocus wavefront error from image diffraction spike measurements

items.title: Testing cosmological structure formation in a unified dark matter-energy model with a fast transition
items.abstract: Unified dark matter-energy (UDM) models, a class of models in which dark matter and dark energy exist as a single cosmological fluid, are an alternative approach to Λ cold dark matter (ΛCDM). In this work we focus on a model with a fast transition between dark matter-like and dark energy-like behaviour. The epoch and rapidity of the transition are the key features to enable the formation of structure in this model. We studied its viability using cosmic microwave background and weak lensing data with nested sampling inference methods. We found that the preferred region of the parameter space is the one with early and fast transition models, where the model's ΛCDM limit also lies. Our study confirms that this UDM model is able to form cosmological structure compatible with the data used.

items.title: Euclid: Quick Data Release (Q1) -- Exploring the detailed visual morphology of galaxies in clusters
items.abstract: Galaxy clusters provide unique laboratories for studying environmental effects on galaxy evolution. The morphology--density (T--Σ) and morphology--cluster-centric radius (T--R) relations trace how galaxy morphology is influenced by the environment, but previous studies at intermediate redshifts have been limited in both sample size and radial coverage. We used the Euclid Quick Data Release 1 (Q1) visual morphology catalog to measure the T--Σ and T--R relations for smooth, featured-or-disk, and barred galaxies in known clusters at 0.2łeq złeq 0.5, extending this analysis to large cluster-centric distances (3,R_500c) and studying their dependence on stellar mass. Using photometric redshifts and stellar masses provided by Euclid, we identify 1754 cluster members within 1.5,R_500c, distributed across 71 clusters. We classify the identified galaxies as smooth, featured-or-disk, or barred using the predicted vote fractions provided by the deep learning foundation model in the Q1 visual morphology catalog. Our classification of smooth and featured-or-disk galaxies is similar to the separation between elliptical and disk galaxies. We confirm the T--Σ relation in all the stellar mass ranges studied, with a stronger influence of the cluster environment on galaxy morphology in the densest parts of the cluster and closer to the cluster center. Beyond 1.5,R_500c, the morphological segregation weakens, with featured-or-disk galaxies overtaking smooth galaxies at the lowest densities, consistent with the growing contribution of field interlopers in the cluster outskirts. For barred galaxies, we find a tentative decline of the bar fraction toward lower densities that is most pronounced for the most massive galaxies. In conclusion, our results show that the cluster environment drives a progressive transformation of galaxy morphology, with the loss of disk structure becoming more pronounced toward the cluster core, where environmental processes act most efficiently. These findings, enabled by the unique characteristics of the Q1 visual morphology catalog, advance our physical understanding of how galaxies evolve in dense environments at intermediate redshifts.

items.title: Milliarcsecond-scale jet reorientations in GRS 1915+105 pointing towards a warped accretion disc
items.abstract: The black hole X-ray binary GRS 1915+105 exhibited persistent X-ray activity for more than 26 years after its discovery, prior to entering a prolonged low X-ray flux state in 2018, while remaining bright at radio wavelengths. Multi-wavelength observations suggest that this low X-ray state results from the emergence of a complex layer of absorbing material, whose exact nature remains unknown. Since the X-ray emission is obscured, radio jet observations provide an unobstructed view of the physical changes associated with this phase. Recently published Very Large Array (VLA) and East Asian VLBI Network (EAVN) observations have revealed substantial changes in the jet position angle (PA). Here, we present higher-resolution VLBI observations to investigate the connection between the obscuration event and the jet behaviour close to the launch region. We observed GRS 1915+105 with the Very Long Baseline Array (VLBA) and European VLBI Network (EVN) during the early X-ray obscuration phase across four epochs spanning 2019--2021, sampling a diverse range of jet and accretion behaviours. In this paper, we focus on the milliarcsecond jet morphology and PA changes across the four epochs and contextualize these in relation to the reported X-ray behaviour. Many of the PAs measured post-2018 are significantly offset from GRS 1915+105's pre-obscuration jet axis, which has a weighted mean of 142^ ̧irc ± 7^ ̧irc on milliarcsecond scales. We find a maximum offset of 57^ ̧irc ± 8^ ̧irc from this axis, the largest such offset reported for GRS 1915+105 to date. Our four epochs reveal a broad variety of jet behaviours, ranging from a stable, compact source with a large PA offset, to a bright, flaring source with a similarly large offset, to an extended jet with a PA that is closer to the pre-obscuration axis, and finally to a non-detection. The lack of measurable PA changes within individual eight-hour epochs rules out rapid Lense-Thirring precession of the inner disc as the direct driver of the jet reorientation. Instead, given the timescales involved, coupled with the system's geometry and the apparent connection to the X-ray obscuration event, favour a radiation-driven warped accretion disc, in a configuration that could naturally explain the persistent obscuration.

items.title: The impact of M-dwarf stellar convection on exoplanetary atmospheric signatures. A 3D radiation-hydrodynamics simulation analysis for high-resolution spectroscopy
items.abstract: M-dwarf stars, as the most abundant and long-lived stellar population in the Galaxy, represent prime targets for the detection and characterization of small, temperate exoplanets; however, their complex activity and convective surfaces pose significant challenges for high-resolution spectroscopic studies aimed at identifying atmospheric habitability signatures. This work investigates the impact of stellar convection on high-resolution spectroscopy of M dwarfs, quantifies its contamination of exoplanetary atmospheric signals, and develops an integrated framework combining 3D radiative hydrodynamical (RHD) simulations, spectroscopic modeling, and transit analysis to mitigate stellar noise. We employed 3D RHD simulations of M-dwarf convection to compute synthetic spectra using state-of-the-art molecular and atomic line data and compare them with observations of GJ 3470. We modeled high-resolution transits of the Neptune-size GJ,3470,b, including center-to-limb variations (CLVs) and the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect (RME), and used principal component analysis (PCA) to de-trend stellar effects. We show the contribution of different molecular absorption features in the dense and complex spectra of M dwarfs. We calibrated the empirical velocity parameters used in 1D hydrostatic stellar models. A comparison with observations shows that current H_2O line lists remain inaccurate, with modest agreement in line strength and position within the K-band interval. During the transit of GJ,3470,b, the CLVs+RME amplitude is comparable to exoplanet signals. Principal component analysis can, in principle, de-trend these effects, but its behavior depends on the co-presence of telluric and planetary signals and the observational noise budget. While we detect the exoplanet without bias from stellar residuals, this result is limited to a narrow spectral interval and a specific orbital configuration. This study demonstrates the importance of 3D RHD simulations for modeling convection-induced spectral variability in M dwarfs and provides a framework for quantifying stellar contamination in high-resolution transit spectroscopy, supporting robust atmospheric characterization with ELT observations.

items.title: Chronic neonatal MK-801 treatment attenuates auditory fear conditioning in adult male rats.
items.abstract: Noncompetitive-777-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonists induce schizophrenia-like symptoms, supporting the NMDA receptor hypofunction hypothesis. Neonatal NMDA receptor blockade with MK-801 is widely used to model neurodevelopmental aspects of schizophrenia; however, its impact on cue-specific fear learning remains incompletely characterized. Male Sprague-Dawley pups received subcutaneous injections of MK-801 (0.4 mg/kg) or saline twice daily from postnatal day 7-20. In adulthood, rats underwent auditory fear conditioning (five tone-shock pairings), 4 days of extinction (45 tone-alone trials/session), a retrieval test, and a remote retrieval test. Across acquisition and all test sessions, MK-801-treated rats showed consistently lower freezing than controls. These findings suggest that chronic neonatal MK-801 treatment disrupts acquisition or expression of cue-shock associations, or both. Given the small sample size and the potential contribution of altered locomotion or shock reactivity, future work should incorporate locomotor and sensory controls.

items.title: Plasma D- and L-2-hydroxyglutarate during vorasidenib treatment of isocitrate dehydrogenase-mutant glioma: development and validation of an enantioselective LC-MS/MS assay.
items.abstract: Objectives Mutant forms of isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 and 2 (IDH1/2) produce D-2-hydroxyglutarate (D-2-HG), which may serve as a circulating marker of biochemical target engagement during treatment with vorasidenib, an oral, brain-penetrant inhibitor of mutant IDH1/2. We aimed to develop an enantioselective LC-MS/MS assay for plasma D-2-HG and L-2-HG and evaluate its ability to detect longitudinal pharmacodynamic changes during treatment. Methods We developed an LC-MS/MS assay for plasma D-2-HG and L-2-HG using protein precipitation, diacetyl-L-tartaric anhydride derivatization, reversed-phase separation, isotope-labeled internal standards, and stripped-serum surrogate calibration. Analytical performance was evaluated over the 6.75-2,030 nmol/L measuring interval. The assay was applied to baseline, 3-month, and 6-month samples from 36 patients with IDH -mutant grade 2 glioma receiving vorasidenib. Results Both enantiomers were baseline-resolved within a 10-min run. The lower limit of quantification was 6.75 nmol/L. Relative error remained within ±15 % at all calibration levels, and short-term between-run CVs in plasma-based QC materials were 2.3-5.7 %. Median D-2-HG decreased from 265 nmol/L (IQR, 223-305) at baseline to 121 nmol/L (IQR, 95-160) at 3 months and 128 nmol/L (IQR, 82-174) at 6 months. Model-estimated concentrations were 53.3 % lower at 3 months and 53.8 % lower at 6 months than at baseline, with no difference between follow-up visits (p=0.88). L-2-HG showed no significant time effect (p=0.53). Conclusions The assay provided sensitive, reproducible, enantiomer-specific quantification of plasma 2-HG and detected early, sustained D-2-HG suppression during vorasidenib treatment. It supports pharmacodynamic assessment of mutant IDH inhibition. External validation and studies relating metabolite changes to clinical outcomes are needed before broader clinical implementation.

items.title: Analytical validation of an in-house CSF neurogranin assay for clinical use.
items.abstract: Objectives Synaptic dysfunction is an early and central feature of Alzheimer's disease (AD), and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) neurogranin (Ng) has emerged as a promising biomarker reflecting synaptic pathology. However, despite its increasing use in research, comprehensive analytical and clinical validation supporting its routine clinical use remains limited. Methods We developed an updated version of an in-house CSF Ng enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (UGOT-Ng) and performed a full analytical validation, including precision, selectivity, measurement range, dilution linearity, interference, and sample stability. Method comparison with a previous assay version and instrument comparability were also assessed. A distribution-derived upper threshold was established using a large set of prospectively measured routine clinical samples. Finally, the associations between CSF Ng concentrations and core AD biomarkers were examined in a large retrospective dataset. Results The assay demonstrated acceptable analytical performance, with good repeatability and intermediate precision across the evaluated concentration levels. The measurement range was established at 38-1,200 ng/L, with satisfactory dilution linearity and minimal interference from blood contamination. CSF Ng showed high stability under various preanalytical conditions. Distribution-derived analysis in amyloid-negative clinical samples yielded an upper limit of 390 ng/L. In clinical samples, CSF Ng correlated strongly with total tau and phosphorylated tau, while associations with Aβ42/40 were weaker and largely driven by differences between amyloid-positive and -negative individuals. Conclusions This study provides a comprehensive analytical validation of an in-house CSF Ng assay, supporting its implementation in a routine clinical laboratory. CSF Ng was strongly associated with CSF total tau and phosphorylated tau, supporting its relationship with tau-associated neuronal and synaptic pathology in AD. However, the strength of these correlations also raises the possibility that CSF Ng provides information that overlaps with established tau biomarkers. Further studies should therefore determine whether Ng offers incremental diagnostic or prognostic value, identifies biologically distinct patient subgroups, or improves the monitoring of synaptic dysfunction beyond currently available biomarkers.

items.title: TiO2/ZIF-8/CF-Based Triboelectric Nanogenerator for Intelligent Ammonia Sensing and Wireless Alarm in Livestock Farms.
items.abstract: Ammonia, a common hazardous gas, severely endangers ecosystems and public health through unregulated industrial emissions and accidental leaks. Given the wide distribution and potential hazards of ammonia, a high-speed pulse airflow-powered triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) was constructed to realize ammonia sensing and environmental surveillance in animal breeding facilities. This device adopted a TiO2/ZIF-8/copper foam (CF) composite structure as the friction electrode (TZP-TENG). The composite nanogenerator efficiently harvested energy from high-pressure waste gas and exhibited outstanding electrical output performance. It delivered a short-circuit current output of 3.36 μA together with a peak power density reaching 41.19 μW at an NH3 concentration of 30 ppm. This device could illuminate 60 LEDs and supply different capacitors. For its excellent ammonia-sensing capability, the TZP-TENG could be integrated into a wireless early warning system to realize real-time monitoring and automatic alarming for high-concentration ammonia. Furthermore, the device is applicable to ammonia concentration detection in livestock farms, which helps stabilize the breeding environment and optimize the growth conditions of livestock and poultry. This design not only expands the technical approaches for ammonia detection but also enables intelligent regulation of breeding environments. It provides significant technical references and practical application demonstrations for harmful gas monitoring and environmental management in livestock breeding sites.

items.title: Family feeding environment, food insecurity, and their associations with undernutrition and overnutrition among Indonesian school-aged children.
items.abstract: Introduction The double burden of malnutrition (DBM), the coexistence of stunting and overweight/obesity, has emerged as a growing concern among school-aged children in low-and middle-income countries, yet remains poorly understood. The present study aimed to examine how family feeding environments, food insecurity, and dietary behaviours are associated with undernutrition and overnutrition in an Indonesian population undergoing rapid nutrition transition. Methods This cross-sectional study involved 161 children and 116 parents across three districts in South Sulawesi. Data on dietary intake, nutritional status, feeding practices, and household food insecurity were collected using structured questionnaires, FFQ, and HFIAS. Nutritional status was assessed using BMI-for-age and height-for-age z-scores. Associations were examined using descriptive statistics, correlations, and exploratory multivariate logistic regression. Results Children had low fruit and vegetable (median 127 g/day) intake and high consumption of SSB and UPF (149.5 mL/day and 116 g/day, respectively). Overweight/obesity (OWOB) affected 52.2 % and stunting 29.2 %; 4.3 % had both. Parent-reported feeding practices showed a limited association with children's dietary intake. Food insecurity was prevalent (54 %). In exploratory adjusted models, moderate food insecurity (aOR=7.51; 95 % CI: 1.14-66.76) and residence in Takalar or Makassar compared with Maros were associated with higher odds of OWOB, whereas female sex was associated with lower odds. Stunting was associated with female sex (aOR=3.79; 95 % CI: 1.28-13.08) and residence in Maros, but not with food insecurity. Conclusions Children's diets remained poor despite generally positive parent-reported feeding practices, which may reflect broader environmental influences. The differing correlates of OWOB and stunting highlight the need for tailored, context-specific interventions aiming at improving diet quality and food environments. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation in larger longitudinal studies integrating dietary, environmental, and biological data. Despite generally positive feeding practices reported by parents, children's diets remained poor, which may reflect broader environmental influences.

items.title: A Scoping Review of the Perceptions and Experiences of People From Underserved Groups of Being on Personalized Stratified Follow-Up Following Treatment for Breast Cancer.
items.abstract: Background Personalized Stratified Follow-Up (PSFU) is an approach to cancer follow-up involving patients re-accessing care when they need to, rather than attending predetermined appointments. The benefits of this approach are a more personalized experience for patients and increased capacity in clinics. Objective To understand the evidence relating to the experiences of people on PSFU following breast cancer treatment, specifically in terms of the perceptions of people from underserved groups. Methods A scoping review of the relevant evidence was conducted. Screening was conducted independently by 2 researchers. Data extracted were charted using a predetermined checklist for summary and analysis. Results A total of 2728 results were identified through databases; 11 papers were included. Nineteen gray literature resources were also identified. Findings were presented as: (1) key components of PSFU for breast cancer; (2) experiences and perceptions of patients and health professionals in relation to PSFU for breast cancer; (3) suggestions to enhance PSFU; and (4) evidence relating to underserved groups on PSFU for breast cancer. Conclusion Patients on PSFU are generally satisfied with their care and are confident in managing their own condition. Unmet needs include psychological support and re-accessing clinical teams. This review has highlighted that little is known about the experiences of underserved groups. Implications for nursing practice Nurses should be aware of the importance of providing patients on PSFU with information about self-examination, signs of recurrence, side effects, and re-accessing the clinical team. PSFU services should be designed to ensure that patients from underserved groups do not experience inequalities in their care.

items.title: Language Models Steer on Injected Uncertainty Tokens, but Fail to Self-Monitor In Situ
items.abstract: Prompting language models to verbalize stepwise numerical confidence during generation is an increasingly popular approach for triggering backtracking and error correction in agentic reasoning. This strategy presupposes two capabilities: (1) in-situ monitoring fidelity (does confidence drop when an error occurs?) and (2) downstream steering control (does an uncertainty token causally steer the model to repair its error?). We evaluated four open-weights models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B, and Phi-4, 14.7B) across 15,200 math benchmark attempts, isolating 2,017 reasoning errors within each model's capability frontier. Applying 27,568 counterfactual continuations across these failure points, we demonstrate a consistent decoupling between monitoring and control. On monitoring, all four models fail to detect their own errors. Verbalized confidence does not distinguish mistake steps from sound reasoning, yielding near-chance within-position AUROCs between 0.500 and 0.561. Even at a model's first reasoning error, trajectory confidence remains saturated at 95.1% to 99.9%, with noticeable drops ($\ge 10$ points) appearing on fewer than 9% of errors in Llama and under 1.6% in the other three models. In contrast, models respond readily to external uncertainty: injecting a low-confidence tag (10%) at the error step significantly increases downstream correction across all models (+3.7 to +22.5 points over format-matched 95% certainty; all $p \le 0.0022$), reaching up to 38.5% under active rethinking instructions. However, injecting doubt onto already-correct steps causes models to discard valid reasoning, reducing solve rates by up to 22.8 points. Inference-time self-correction is thus bottlenecked by in-situ error detection rather than downstream repair capacity: models readily steer toward recovery when prompted with doubt, yet fail to self-monitor during generation.

items.title: CTLink: A Text-Prompted Segmentation Model for Linking Radiology Report Findings to 3D Chest CT Scans
items.abstract: Radiology reports describe findings in text only, without visually marking them on the scan, so readers cannot directly see which abnormality each reported finding refers to. We introduce CTLink, a text-prompted 3D segmentation model that segments findings described in a chest CT report. CTLink was trained on 4123 noncontrast chest CT scans with 9547 segmented report findings, including ReXGroundingCTv2, a newly annotated dataset of 1134 scans and 1895 findings with every instance of each finding segmented. On the 200 ReXGroundingCT validation scans, CTLink achieved a hit rate of 0.816, an instance F1 score of 0.456, and a mean Dice score of 0.400, compared with 0.533, 0.175, and 0.234 for VoxTell, a publicly available text-prompted segmentation model (P < .001 for all). On the test set of the MICCAI 2026 ReXGrounding challenge, an ensemble of seven CTLink models achieved the highest hit rate (0.782) and instance F1 score (0.386) of all 48 participating teams. On 50 test scans segmented twice by independent radiologists, CTLink matched or exceeded inter-rater agreement. Diffuse non-focal findings remained the main limitation, partly because their extent is outlined inconsistently even between radiologists. The CTLink model weights are available at https://huggingface.co/rajpurkarlab/CTLink, and the dataset at https://huggingface.co/datasets/rajpurkarlab/ReXGroundingCT.

items.title: A Mixed-Methods Study of Personal Software Creation
items.abstract: People have long wanted software shaped around their own data, routines, and preferences. We refer to such software as \emph{personal software}. For decades, programming expertise limited who could build it: people without that expertise could build software only within constrained end-user programming tools, such as spreadsheets. AI coding agents seem to remove this bottleneck by letting people build full applications from natural-language descriptions, and many people now build and share personal software publicly. Yet personal software has rarely been studied at scale: we know little about what people build and why, how they build it, and what opportunities and challenges they encounter. We investigate these questions with a mixed-methods study. A grey-literature review examines 6,168 web and Reddit posts, and an observation study follows eight people as they build software for their own needs with AI coding agents and use it for up to a week. We find that creators value personal software for how closely it fits a particular person or community. The software takes shape as creators react to what the agent builds: most functionality emerged during building, and creators' effort shifted from writing code to checking it.

items.title: Seeking in Space: Benchmarking Purposeful Active Exploration of Vision-Language Models for Spatial Reasoning
items.abstract: Humans explore unfamiliar spaces with purpose, deciding where to look until they have gathered the evidence a spatial question requires. However, can vision-language models (VLMs), which reason increasingly well over curated images and videos, also seek in space when the evidence is not handed to them? We present ActSpace-Bench, a benchmark of 994 questions across 234 exploration episodes in 72 real-scanned indoor scenes, where a model starts from a single view, navigates real captured frames, and must gather evidence before answering. To assess whether such exploration is purposeful, we introduce a controlled evaluation protocol that fixes each model as the reasoner and compares its own exploration against a same-budget random walk and an oracle route, separating evidence seeking from spatial reasoning. Every question is verified to require exploration and answered from 3D annotations, masked-evidence questions test whether models know when to abstain, and over 95% of sampled questions are confirmed correct by human verification. Evaluations of 23 proprietary, open-weight, and spatially specialized VLMs reveal that the strongest models do seek evidence with purpose but lose much of it to limited memory, whereas weaker and specialized models explore no better than a random walk or fail to reason over the evidence they are given, pointing to memory and evidence-grounded reasoning as the next targets for active spatial intelligence.

items.title: ToolSmith: An Automatic Tool-Generation Framework for Multimodal Search Agents
items.abstract: Recent multimodal search agents use reasoning, vision, and live web search across many turns to answer questions beyond parametric knowledge by orchestrating a small library of hand-crafted search and visual tools. However, the library is laborious to create and maintain, and frozen when new query types, evidence formats, and failure modes are encountered in the wild. Human practitioners, by contrast, cope with insufficient tools by fashioning new ones from familiar parts and reusing them across tasks. Inspired by this, we propose ToolSmith, an automatic tool-generation framework that grows and reuses modules on top of a lean base tool library. We evaluate ToolSmith on three in-domain multimodal search benchmarks and ten out-of-domain benchmarks under a VLM-as-a-Judge protocol. ToolSmith consistently improves over the base library across deployed agents of varying scales, with larger backbones reaping greater gains, demonstrating the scalability of the approach. Our code and data are available at https://threesr.github.io/toolsmith/.

items.title: Learning Neurovascular Codes for EEG-to-fMRI Synthesis
items.abstract: In this paper, we introduce Neurovascular Codes as shared EEG representations for fMRI generation. We first train a separate EEG encoder to predict each fMRI signal, learning target-specific temporal and spectral features from the same EEG window. After training, we freeze the encoders and project their concatenated hidden features into a shared neurovascular code. Conditioned on this code, stochastic interpolant transforms Gaussian noise into a vector of fMRI signals, allowing different responses to be sampled for the same EEG window. We evaluate our approach on eight public simultaneous EEG-fMRI datasets, including four resting-state and four task-based datasets with 61,646 volume-level pairs. Under within-subject and held-out-subject evaluation, our model improves average Pearson correlation over the strongest encoder baselines by 19.1% and 19.8%, respectively. The corresponding improvements over the strongest generator baselines are 18.8% and 47.9%. Beyond reconstruction accuracy, we also evaluate the generated signals using subject-identification classifiers trained on real fMRI. Our method achieves the highest mean accuracy among the evaluated generators. We hope that our work opens up new opportunities for cross-modal brain modeling.

items.title: Know When to Abstain: Conformal Confidence Estimation for Text-to-SQL
items.abstract: Text-to-SQL systems often return queries that execute successfully but answer the wrong question. Detecting these errors at deployment is hard because execution correctness is defined against a gold query, which exists only in labeled data. We formulate confidence estimation for Text-to-SQL as probabilistic query validation under a latent correctness variable that is observable at calibration time through gold-SQL execution and latent at deployment. Our estimator separates generation from validation. A generator LLM writes and executes the query, and a different critic LLM judges the query and its execution result. The critic's validation and execution-grounded alignment scores are fused with the generator's verbalized confidence, token-level uncertainty, and SQL-structural features in a Random Forest, using two sequential LLM calls. Two calibration steps give finite-sample guarantees. A Learn-then-Test threshold ensures, with probability $1-δ$, that the error rate among accepted queries stays below a user-chosen budget. A conformal p-value bounds the false abstention rate. On Spider we use GPT-OSS-120B as generator and Gemma-4-31B as critic. The estimator obtains an AUARC of 0.899. Without abstention, 22.6% of queries are wrong. With a 15% risk budget ($δ=0.1$), a threshold is certified on all 10 resampled splits, and the system accepts 52.4% of queries on average with 9.1% observed error. Five different critic models give similar results. In a controlled comparison on Spider with Olmo-3-32B as generator, the estimator obtains an AUARC of 89.5, compared with 81.2 for the strongest logit-based baseline. Applied to BIRD without retraining, the confidence scores remain informative (AUROC 0.72, against 0.79 on Spider), but the risk guarantee does not transfer, as expected without exchangeability.

items.title: CO-GRAFT: Attributing Reinforcement Learning Gains in Search Agents via Role-Level Policy Grafting
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) improves large language model search agents by up to 32 exact-match (EM) points over their pre-RL initializations, yet overall accuracy gains do not identify which underlying functional capabilities improve or interact during training. We introduce CO-GRAFT, a reward-agnostic interventional attribution framework in which an RL-trained agent and its pre-RL initialization jointly generate a single trajectory under closed-loop execution with live retrieval. Each policy controls a mutually exclusive subset of four functional roles: intermediate reasoning, search-or-answer decision, search query generation, and final answer extraction. Evaluating all 2^4=16 role assignments without modifying weights or retraining defines a cooperative game whose Shapley values decompose the total RL gain across roles, while M"obius interaction terms distinguish standalone role improvements from multi-role coupling. Applying CO-GRAFT to Search-R1 agents across Qwen2.5 and Llama-3.2 models (spanning two sizes, base and instruction-tuned initializations, GRPO and PPO optimizers, and NQ and HotpotQA datasets), we show that query generation never exceeds 15% of the total gain; instead, gains are governed by pre-RL answer validity, search retention, model scale, and fixed task-level search budgets, shifting credit from reasoning toward answer extraction in larger or well-formatted answer response checkpoints while smaller base models rely on reasoning--decision coupling.

items.title: Needwise: Generation-Free Conversational Recommendation from Need-Level Typed Decisions
items.abstract: Conversational recommenders must rank items against needs that catalogs record only in part, while users add, withdraw and reverse needs and switch between requests. LLM rankers re-read the dialogue at every turn: they are slow, and their ordering does not show which needs an item meets. We show that a conversational recommender can be built from typed decisions instead: named questions over fixed options, answered with option probabilities rather than generated text. On each turn, one typed request maps the message onto the catalog's fields, keeps what no field expresses in the user's words, and decides how the turn changes each earlier need. Needwise then ranks candidates must-first: the needs on the kind of item, its place and its price form a tier, and within it one holistic decision and need-level verdicts (supported, contradicted or unknown) are combined with equal weight (Needwise-HF). With the graded attributes withheld from the records, so that needs must be inferred from names, descriptions and reviews, Needwise-HF ranks Google Local requests significantly better than GPT-6 Sol (0.383 against 0.343 nDCG@10) and is not significantly different from the strongest LLM ranker on Google Local and Yelp; these comparisons keep their sign under every treatment of unrecorded attributes we test. It costs a fraction of GPT-6 Sol's API price and answers in 2.5 s at the median on Google Local, against 5.6 s for GPT-6 Sol. In conversations, the typed state keeps the ranking across switches and returns, but it recognizes only 19-27% of withdrawn needs.

items.title: Reducing Order Sensitivity in Decision Models
items.abstract: Decision models are emerging as fast components of larger AI systems. Yet recent decision models, such as Jev, process options sequentially, leading to different predictions based on their ordering. Across ten open- and closed-source decision models, we find that \emph{order-sensitivity} is pervasive, causing substantial accuracy degradation and unreliable decision-making. These effects become more pronounced as the number of options grows and can compound across multi-step decisions. To address this problem, we systematically compare eight methods for mitigating order sensitivity in terms of robustness, predictive accuracy, and inference efficiency. Among these methods, we find that \emph{tree attention} is a surprisingly effective and efficient method. It achieves order invariance by processing options as parallel branches of a shared context. When used during training, it matches the baseline's average accuracy. Applied to the baseline without retraining, it also eliminates order sensitivity with only a 1.1-point drop in accuracy. Our findings demonstrate that order invariance can be enforced directly in decision models with little or no loss in predictive accuracy.

items.title: When Does Overriding the Majority Vote Help?
items.abstract: When should additional reasoning or verification replace a majority-vote answer? We call such a replacement an override. We examine two obstacles: the availability of correct alternatives and the reliability of methods that produce or select them. We compare additional reasoning, executed programs, and cross-model reasoning on 150 competition-mathematics questions with three open reasoning models. Starting from a majority vote over 16 responses, we measure how often overrides occur and how many errors they correct or introduce across agreement thresholds. When the vote is incorrect, the correct answer is often absent from the original responses. Additional same-model reasoning rarely overrides, while executed programs correct more errors than they introduce at every evaluated threshold. Cross-model overrides improve some weaker baselines but do not establish an advantage over the more accurate model alone, even with only eight standalone responses. Stricter agreement reduces how often overrides occur but does not consistently increase the fraction that correct errors. At the strictest thresholds, overrides occur on few distinct questions, limiting conclusions about their reliability.

items.title: Habitats: A Framework for Open-Ended Evolution of Agent Objectives
items.abstract: Designing what an agent should optimize can be as difficult as optimizing the agent itself. Existing language-model-based reward-generation methods typically refine objectives for predefined tasks and couple the decision of what to explore with the synthesis of how to implement it, potentially narrowing the resulting behavioral repertoire. We introduce Habitats, a framework for open-ended evolution of executable agent objectives. Habitats maintains a population of reward-policy pairs and evaluates every policy under every population reward, producing a cross-fitness matrix that exposes self-mastery, transfer, and functional diversity. A population-level Planner uses this information to select parent rewards and issue targeted mutation directives, while a separate Mutator translates those directives into validated reward programs. We evaluate Habitats in a discrete Card Sandbox and three continuous-control environments (Cart-Pole, Hopper, and Cheetah) against Independent Generation and Direct Mutation baselines. Across four environments and three random seeds, Habitats achieves the highest macro-averaged final Specialist Quality and Behavioral Diversity, with final diversity reaching 1.8x that of Direct Mutation and 2.5x that of Independent Generation. Finally, across ten downstream objectives unseen during evolution, frozen Habitats policy libraries achieve higher paired win rates than size-matched Direct Mutation and Independent Generation libraries at 10,000 adaptation episodes, while also surpassing task-specific policies trained from scratch for 20,000 episodes. These results suggest that separating population-level planning from reward synthesis enables the discovery of diverse, learnable, and reusable behaviors.

items.title: Deneb-Vritra: Descriptions, Edges and Names Examined by Blocking Via Restoring Token Representations and Attention
items.abstract: Laya is a 421M-parameter encoder that answers a question about a text in one pass: each answer option, written as a name plus a description, gets a marker token, and one score is read from the network at each marker. We first confirm that such models can follow an option's name when it contradicts the description; the question is where in the network this happens. We locate it. On 951 synthetic questions we move each name onto another option's description and count how often the model picks the option with the right name (the name shortcut): 53% for the released checkpoint, 59% for our fine-tune v1, 11% for a fine-tune with name randomisation. On a 320-item sample, blocking attention from each marker to its own name tokens in layers 14 to 17 of 28 cuts v1's shortcut from 67% to 16% (19% on two schemas held out from component selection) while accuracy with the original names stays at 90%; blocking marker edges to the question, other options or text has no effect. No single head matters (largest effect 9 points), and restoring clean marker states undoes the swap from layer 16. Attention mass tracks the window by layer but not by head. Repeated on 5 checkpoints (released, fine-tuned, name-randomised, and a pair trained without two schemas), the knockout finds similar layers; in the name-randomised ones, blocking the description edges instead brings the shortcut back to 56-58%, so the read persists and is outvoted. Marker states decode the name from layer 0; a one-direction probe erasure changed nothing but was weaker than a random edit. Copying layers 0-13 or 14-27 of a name-randomised sibling into a fine-tune recovers 66% and 65% (v1); 21% and 45% (pair A) of its shortcut reduction. 9 of the 12 predictions we could score, written before running, failed. Head sweeps cover 5 of 5 checkpoints; data are synthetic and LLM-labelled; one architecture.

items.title: SRCWDNet: Semantic-Relational Cross-Window Dual-Graph Network for Multi-Label Remote Sensing Scene Classification
items.abstract: Multi-label remote sensing scene classification remains a challenging task due to complex spatial-spectral patterns, extreme class imbalance, and inter-label dependencies that are often insufficiently modeled. To address these challenges, we introduce a Semantic-Relational Cross-Window Dual-Graph Network (SRCWDNet), which integrates three key modules: (1) a Cross-Window Attention module that captures local and global visual context through learnable global tokens; (2) a Dual Label-Graph module that adaptively combines statistical co-occurrence graphs and learned semantic-embedding graphs to facilitate label-relational reasoning; and (3) a Neural Classifier Chain that sequentially predicts labels to exploit inter-label dependencies. Evaluated using five-fold cross-validation and trained with an Asymmetric-Graph-Consistency loss, SRCWDNet achieves accuracies of 98.93% and 96.53%, with corresponding F1-scores of 0.9365 and 0.8723 on the MLRSNet and China-MAS50k datasets, respectively, outperforming CNN, transformer, and lightweight baselines. These findings demonstrate that jointly modeling visual attention and adaptive label correlations can substantially improve multi-label remote sensing scene classification, particularly under long-tailed class distributions.

items.title: Genome-to-Image Translation: Reconstructing Escherichia coli Morphology from Genomic Sequences
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance in Escherichia coli is established in routine practice by culture-based susceptibility testing, which is slow relative to the clinical need for an early treatment decision. Resistance status also leaves a measurable trace in cell morphology, and whole-genome sequencing of clinical isolates is increasingly available, which raises the question of whether colony appearance can be predicted directly from an isolate's genome. We formulate this as a conditional image-generation problem. The assembled contigs of each isolate are encoded into a single 768-dimensional vector by a frozen genomic language model through a segment-contig-isolate aggregation hierarchy, and a conditional Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty synthesizes colony images from this embedding together with the applied antibiotic and the resistance label. We train on 167,356 single-cell images from 22 clinical blood isolates imaged under azithromycin, ciprofloxacin, tetracycline, and a no-drug control, compare seven pretrained convolutional backbones inside the generator, and select ConvNeXt-Tiny on distributional image-quality metrics. The synthetic images are then assessed extrinsically: added to a reduced real training set, they improve per-antibiotic resistance classification, with a significant gain in resistant-class recall.

items.title: FATCAT: Fault Injection Attacks Targeting Chip-level Alignment
items.abstract: Model alignment is the primary safety and security mechanism for enforcing refusal of malicious prompts in modern foundation models; yet, existing adversarial evaluations implicitly assume underlying hardware integrity. In this paper, we present FATCAT, the first physical fault-injection attacks capable of eliminating refusal in modern large language and vision-language models. Specifically, we present a non-invasive electromagnetic (EM) fault injection attack targeting GPU-accelerated Systems-on-Chip with physical access, requiring neither software execution privileges nor model-layer access. By leveraging an autonomous Radio Frequency (RF) side-channel trigger to synchronize EM faults to the prompt prefill phase, the attack corrupts safety-critical memory transactions across off-chip LPDDR5 DRAM and on-chip LPDDR physical interfaces without crashing the system while preserving model coherence. Evaluated on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano and AGX Thor running Llama 3.2 1B and Gemma 3 1B, localized physical faults reliably force models to fulfill restricted requests, demonstrating that model-level alignment provides no robust security guarantees without hardware-level fault tolerance. Finally, we demonstrate the physical-world consequences of this vulnerability on an active 6-DoF robotic manipulator controlled by a SmolVLA vision-language-action policy. Our attack silently corrupts the model forcing the arm into abrupt, hazardous lunges; in two instances the robotic arm attempted to pinch the paper author -- proving that hardware faults can directly translate into real physical harm.

items.title: Self-Upgrading Embodied Agents
items.abstract: An embodied agent built on a language model goes to work with the weights it was given and keeps them for life. To get better, it needs more training, or reflection, memory, search or prompts that cost every step and are lost when the task changes. Editing weights by reasoning, weight-space programming, could end this, but has stayed with models that only reason or relied on a far larger commercial model. We introduce the self-upgrading embodied agent, to our knowledge the first that learns from its own experience by upgrading its own weights on the job, between its tasks, with no training, no gradient, no reward model, no second model, no test-time scaling and no harness or prompt engineering. By day a 27B agent works in a household environment. At night it reads its record, finds many of its steps wasted on replies that reach the token limit before any action, traces the habit to one direction in its hidden states, and rewrites one tensor of its weights. An agent that rewrites itself must first never break itself, so it is its own examiner: it tests every change against its unchanged self on practice tasks and keeps only what holds. When an edit holds, the next day it is a better agent, at the same cost per step: over thousands of held-out episodes, 48 fresh seeds a task, its one kept edit makes it complete significantly more tasks, in fewer steps, with fewer wasted and fewer tokens. This self-improvement is multi-round, stable and continual: through the nights that follow, the upgrade holds, without collapse. Of four sizes of its family, only the 27B agent does this. From here on, an embodied agent need not keep training and inference apart: as it works, it gathers its own experience and upgrades itself, with no separate pre-training or post-training and no human intervention. We believe this opens lifelong continual learning for robots: stable, continual, recursive self-improvement.
