items.title: Integrative Mendelian Randomization and Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analysis of Aging-Related Genes Associated With Stroke Risk.
items.abstract: Stroke is a major cerebrovascular disease, and aging is a major risk factor associated with poorer outcomes. Identifying genetic mechanisms linking aging-related processes to stroke may help prioritize relevant genes and pathways. To identify aging-related genes associated with stroke risk and explore their molecular and cellular context. An integrated analysis combining eQTL-based Mendelian randomization and single-cell transcriptomics. eQTL data were obtained from eQTLGen, with stroke GWAS data from FinnGen as the discovery dataset and the GWAS Catalog as the validation dataset. MR, sensitivity, and colocalization analyses were used to evaluate associations between genetically predicted gene expression and stroke risk. Single-cell data (GSE174574) were analyzed using Seurat to characterize cell-type-specific expression of prioritized genes. GSEA and GSVA were used for pathway analysis, while RcisTarget, miRWalk, and DGIdb were used to explore regulatory and drug-gene interactions. In 340,999 participants, 22 aging-related genes showed nominal MR associations with stroke risk. Validation in 1,039,382 participants identified LPAR3, MEOX1, VEGFA, and PRKDC. Higher genetically predicted MEOX1 and VEGFA expression was associated with lower stroke risk, whereas LPAR3 and PRKDC were associated with higher risk. VEGFA showed additional support from regional colocalization analysis, whereas LPAR3 and MEOX1 were primarily supported by MR evidence. Regulatory analysis identified 51 predicted miRNAs and 53 drug-gene interaction records involving VEGFA and LPAR3. LPAR3, MEOX1, VEGFA, and PRKDC were prioritized as aging-related genes associated with stroke risk. VEGFA showed additional support from regional colocalization analysis, while LPAR3, MEOX1, and PRKDC require further functional validation.

items.title: Episodic memory consolidation by reactivation of human concept neurons during sleep reflects contents, not sequence of events.
items.abstract: How do our brains manage to store our everyday experiences into memory? Neurons in the human temporal lobe that respond to the concept of an individual person or object have been shown to provide the semantic building blocks for episodic memory. Recording from 1415 neurons in neurosurgical patients who learned a story involving specific concepts, we found reactivation of neurons representing these concepts during slow-wave sleep after learning. Concept neurons were conjointly reactivated, particularly during sharp-wave ripples, with time lags suitable for synaptic modification. However, the temporal sequence of reactivation did not reflect the sequence of concepts in the learned story. Unlike rodent place cells, which can acquire preferred firing locations during exploration of new environments according to their pre-existing preferred sequence of activation, human concept neurons are tuned to specific semantic contents before learning starts. Consequently, pre-existing firing sequences correlate with consecutive place fields in rodents, but not with sequences of events in human experience. Thus, in contrast to reactivation of rodent place cells, reactivation of human concept cells does not reflect sequences of events in human experience.

items.title: Multibiomarker response to environmental concentrations of undoped and doped ZnO nanoparticles with rare earth elements cerium and erbium in Rhamdia quelen embryos.
items.abstract: Zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs) exhibit properties that enable diverse applications, which can be enhanced through doping with rare earth elements. However, their potential environmental risks remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the acute ecotoxicological effects of undoped ZnO NPs and ZnO NPs doped with cerium (Ce-ZnO NPs) and erbium (Er-ZnO NPs) on Rhamdia quelen embryos using a multibiomarker approach. Embryos were exposed to 0.02, 0.2, and 2mg/L of each NPs for 96hours. Mortality and morphological deformities were assessed every 24hours, and biochemical (SOD, CAT, GST, AChE, LPO) and genotoxic (comet assay) analyses were performed on surviving organisms. Fertilization and hatching rates were unaffected; however, post-chorion loss, mortality increased progressively, reaching 100% at 2mg/L for all NPs. Significant deformities were observed in ZnO NPs (0.02mg/L) and Er-ZnO NPs (0.2mg/L) treatments. Er-ZnO NPs (0.2mg/L) also induced cranial malformations, including absence of eyes and delayed barbel development. SOD activity increased in ZnO NPs (0.2mg/L) and Ce-ZnO NPs (0.02mg/L), while Er-ZnO NPs (0.02mg/L) elevated AChE activity. The Integrated Biomarker Response Index indicated that Er-ZnO NPs induced the most pronounced effects, followed by ZnO NPs and Ce-ZnO NPs. These findings suggest that rare earth-doped ZnO NPs may pose ecological risks to aquatic vertebrates even at low concentrations. This study provides preliminary evidence to support further investigation into the environmental safety of engineered nanomaterials.

items.title: Unraveling the synergistic mechanism of phosphorus activation in sewage sludge co-pyrolyzed with coffee grounds Ash: From macroscopic evaluation to atomistic Insights.
items.abstract: The recovery of phosphorus (P) from sewage sludge (SS) is critical for the circular economy, yet its agronomic application is severely limited by low bioavailability. To overcome the intrinsically low bioavailable P (BP) in sludge, this study explored co-pyrolysis of two sludge types (activated sludge (YS) and mechanically dewatered sludge (CS)) with K- and Ca-enriched coffee grounds ash (CGA). The optimal condition was YS co-pyrolyzed with 50 wt% CGA at 700°C, BP reached 62.73 mg g-1, achieving BP to total P (TP) of 97.51%. Synergistic interactions enhanced BP content by 48.83% relative to theoretical physical mixtures. XRD and XPS indicated that reactive K and Ca supplied by CGA disrupt recalcitrant Fe/Al-P associations and reconstruct non-apatite inorganic phosphorus (NAIP) (e.g., AlPO4) into bioavailable K-Ca phosphates (e.g., KCaPO4). A mechanism-informed logistic model further showed that under a given Fe and Al fixation constraint, increasing K/Ca ratio is the primary driver of elevated BP/TP. Specifically, (Al + Fe)/P and K/Ca explain 57.2% and 42.8% of the total variance. Density functional theory supported this interpretation by revealing stronger PO43--Ca2+ anchoring than PO43-K+ interactions (Ca-O 2.21 Å, K-O 2.71 Å), consistent with Ca2+ stabilizing Ca-P frameworks while K+ acts as a labile charge-modulating species that enhances phosphate lability and extractability. Release tests and pot experiments demonstrated slow-release fertilizer performance, with maize growth following: Hydroxyapatite ≈ YS50CGA50 > CS50CGA50 > control > YS700 > CS700. Overall, this work demonstrates a scalable waste-to-resource route that upcycles CGA to enhance BP release from SS.

items.title: Molecular mechanisms of acute heat exposure in marine medaka: From heat perception to responses.
items.abstract: In response to rising ocean temperatures, understanding how the fish brain senses and responds to heat challenge is a key question in physiological ecology. To investigate the underlying neural mechanisms, we examined transcriptional and neuronal responses in marine medaka exposed to 35 °C for 1 h (H1) and 2 h (H2), using a 25 °C group as control. Acute heat exposure significantly altered the expression of heat-sensitive trp channels and the neuronal activity marker c-fos in the brain. Enrichment analyses revealed dominant involvement of molecular binding functions and key signaling pathways, including MAPK (188 DEGs) and calcium signaling (165 DEGs). Electrophysiological recordings showed that thermal stimulation increased firing frequency in telencephalic neurons by 1.7-fold, a response dependent on TRPM2 and TRPM3, as suggested by pharmacological inhibition (JNJ-28583113 and rosiglitazone, respectively). Consistent with neural activation, c-Fos protein levels were elevated throughout the brain. These results reveal that TRPM2- and TRPM3-dependent mechanisms contribute to heat-evoked telencephalic neuronal activity, and that the brain of marine medaka responds to high temperature through a multi-level neurophysiological process involving brain-wide coordinated activation. These findings provide a neural mechanistic basis for understanding behavioral thermoregulation in fish.

items.title: Beyond urban ecology and evolution: socio-eco-evolutionary dynamics in insects and the importance of scales.
items.abstract: Urbanization drives rapid ecological and evolutionary change, creating opportunities for reciprocal feedback among insect phenotypes, ecological processes, and human societies. Yet, despite growing evidence for urban adaptation, empirical demonstrations of urban eco-evolutionary feedback remain rare, and their integration with societal processes is even less developed. Here, we review urban insect ecology and evolution through a socio-eco-evolutionary lens, focusing on pollinators, mosquitoes, and other indoor pests as particularly promising systems. Across these groups, urban environmental change can alter phenotypes through plasticity and evolution, with potential consequences for ecosystem services and disservices including pollination, biological control, pest outbreaks, and disease transmission. We propose a multiscale framework that separates but integrates biological organization, spatiotemporal extent, and urban scales. Phenotypic and evolutionary change can alter ecological processes and societal outcomes beyond the biological, urban, or spatiotemporal scale at which it arises, with resulting feedback propagating, dissipating, or being counteracted across scales. We introduce the concept of socio-eco-evolutionary hotspots, where phenotypic or evolutionary change meaningfully modifies ecological-societal feedback, and coldspots, where these feedback remain weak or fail to propagate. Linking urban insect eco-evolutionary dynamics to their societal consequences and governance scales provides a basis for identifying where biodiversity conservation, urban planning, pest management, and public-health interventions can most effectively shape urban socio-ecological outcomes.

items.title: Oxygen vacancy-rich iron cathode for efficient degradation of polylactic acid microplastics via electro-Fenton.
items.abstract: Electro-Fenton technology is widely used to remove aquatic organic pollutants, but its feasibility for microplastic remediation remains underexplored. Herein, a low-cost AFe-OV cathode enriched with oxygen vacancies and Fe-P/Fe-O active sites was fabricated through the calcination of ferrous precursors pre-reduced by crude tea extract. The as-prepared cathode achieved outstanding performance in polylactic acid microplastics (PLA-MPs) degradation. Such superior performance stems from the lowered energy barriers for cathodic hydrogen peroxide adsorption and activation, which facilitates high-yield hydroxyl radical (•OH) formation. This led to the reduced particle size, enhanced hydrophilicity, decreased molecular weight, and lower negative zeta potentials of PLA-MPs. The constructed electro-Fenton system efficiently removed aqueous PLA-MPs over a wide pH range, with maximum removal efficiencies reaching 91.2% and 96.5% at pH 3.0 and 9.0, respectively. Investigation results revealed that PLA-MPs degradation involved the synergistic hydrolysis and oxidation, with ester bond hydrolysis predominant in alkaline environments and •OH-driven oxidation prevailing under acidic conditions. Meanwhile, the microplastic-derived dissolved organic matter exhibited negligible acute, chronic biotoxicity, and phytotoxicity. This study develops a simple and efficient vacancy-engineered electro-Fenton approach for removing biodegradable microplastics, and offers in-depth insights into the effects of cathodic generated reactive oxygen species on microplastic transformation and degradation.

items.title: Integrated Vector, Canine, and Human Evidence Reveal a Stable Dog-Maintained Cycle of Leishmania Infantum in a Historically Endemic Area From Spain.
items.abstract: Leishmaniosis, caused by Leishmania infantum, is a major zoonotic vector-borne disease in southern Europe. Dogs act as the primary domestic reservoir of the parasite. However, there is growing evidence that transmission cycles involving wild lagomorphs may contribute to both epidemic and endemic human cases in certain settings. Nevertheless, the ecological and epidemiological mechanisms sustaining long-term endemic transmission in stable foci remain poorly understood. This study used an integrated One Health approach combining vector, canine, and human data to investigate transmission dynamics in a long-established endemic area with low human case incidence. An eco-epidemiological study was conducted in Crevillente Municipality in southeast Spain, between 2021 and 2022. Sand flies were collected using CDC light traps and analysed to determine species composition, Leishmania infection by real-time PCR, parasite identification, and blood meal sources. Dogs were tested for anti-Leishmania antibodies using ELISA. Human blood donors were assessed for Leishmania infection by PCR and for anti-Leishmania antibodies and antibodies against Phlebotomus perniciosus saliva as markers of parasite and vector exposure, respectively. A total of 11,375 sand flies were collected, predominantly Sergentomyia minuta and Phlebotomus perniciosus, and displayed marked seasonal and spatial variation. High Leishmania infection rates were detected in confirmed vector species, with L. infantum identified in most samples. Blood meal analysis revealed that the primary feeding sources were dogs and humans, while rabbits and hares were detected but infrequently. Canine seroprevalence was high (43%) and associated with rural exposure. In humans, infection markers were low (3% PCR, 4% serology), despite high exposure to sand fly bites (38% seroprevalence for anti-saliva antibodies). The study characterizes a Mediterranean endemic focus with intense circulation of L. infantum in vectors and dogs, widespread human exposure to sand flies, but low levels of asymptomatic human infection and no reported clinical disease during the decade preceding the study. The findings support a predominantly domestic transmission, with dogs representing the main identified reservoir host and lagomorph-derived blood meals being relatively infrequent. The potential contribution of lagomorphs to local parasite circulation warrants further investigation. The detection of Leishmania DNA in non-confirmed vector species, including sequences consistent with the L. donovani/L. infantum complex, further highlights the need for continued surveillance of Leishmania diversity and transmission dynamics.

items.title: Cultural Significance of Wild Food Plants Among Local Communities Inside and Outside Protected Areas in Northeastern Cambodia.
items.abstract: Wild food plants (WFPs) are important food sources for local communities in Cambodia. However, traditional knowledge of these plants and their uses may be declining. This study documents WFP use, assesses cultural significance, and uses a generalized linear mixed model to examine factors influencing WFP knowledge inside and outside protected areas. Structured interviews were conducted with 1,349 households in northeastern Cambodia. Overall, researchers documented 119 WFP species, including 112 inside and 99 outside protected areas. Azadirachta indica was the most culturally significant species. WFPs contributed approximately US$168 per household annually. WFP knowledge was significantly higher among men, communities inside protected areas, households engaged in crop cultivation, and those collecting forest products. These findings highlight the importance of WFPs in supporting local food security and income diversification and emphasize the need to preserve traditional ecological knowledge of WFPs.

items.title: One of a Kind: Biological Uniqueness and Population Thinking.
items.abstract: Ernst Mayr's idea of "population thinking" remains one of the most discussed -yet arguably least understood- concepts in the philosophy of biology. Recently, a renewed debate concerning the metaphysical significance of population thinking has emerged among prominent philosophers of biology, challenging classical interpretations and claiming the need to clarify one of its central but theoretically underdeveloped notions: biological uniqueness. This article aims to offer support that claim. First, I reconstruct Mayr's original conception of population thinking in terms of four distinct theses, and argue that, under a particular interpretation, all four can be defended against recent criticism. I then classify the main assessments of population thinking as historical, methodological, and metaphysical, before focusing on the two most influential metaphysical interpretations, advanced by Sober (1980) and Nicolson (2025). As an alternative to both, I will defend a functional reading of the ontology presupposed by population thinking. To do so, I clarify the relationship between uniqueness and related notions such as individuality, heterogeneity, and variability. I argue that this clarification resolves longstanding ambiguities concerning both the ontology implied by population thinking and its scope across different biological domains. Finally, I examine two examples -drawn from population ecology and immunology- in order to demonstrate the theoretical and practical relevance of biological uniqueness.

items.title: Crop diversification promotes soil microbial carbon turnover.
items.abstract: Agricultural diversification alters plant residue chemistry and rhizodeposition, with legacy effects on soil organic matter (SOM) cycling. The priming effect (PE) and necromass formation are key processes of SOM dynamics, yet how diversification affects these processes, and SOM persistence remains poorly understood. Using 13C-labelled glucose in a 150-day incubation of soils (0-15 cm) from two contrasting diversification trials (43 and 8 years), we found that diversification increased SOM priming by 153-174% and retention of glucose-derived 13C in microbial necromass by 227-289%. Diversified soils also had more bioavailable C, dissolved organic C, and neutral sugars, stronger stoichiometric nutrient limitation (103% higher C:P imbalance and 15% lower vector angle), and higher microbial activity and N- and P-acquiring enzyme activities. Microbial C use efficiency increased by 65%, while replacing the native microbial community of diversified soils with that of conventional soils reduced CUE by 9% and 45% at the 43- and 8-year sites, respectively. Community-level analyses further linked greater retention of glucose-derived 13C in microbial necromass to putative Discosea and Bacillota co-occurrence patterns. Metagenomic profiling revealed 18-125% higher relative abundances of CAZyme genes involved in degrading plant- and microbial-derived compounds, alongside a modest (~4%) increase in Y-associated functional potential at both sites. Although priming-induced native-C losses exceeded the amount of glucose-derived 13C retained in microbial necromass, the ratio of necromass C retention to priming-induced C loss was 28% higher under diversification than under conventional cropping over the 150-day incubation. Crop diversification thus reshapes microbial C cycling, coupling enhanced native SOM mineralization with greater retention of added C in microbial necromass, making the net effect on SOC dependent on sustained C inputs.

items.title: The Bidirectional Relations Between Perceived Parental Autonomy Support, Subjective Intergenerational Mobility and Academic Engagement in Chinese Adolescents.
items.abstract: Perceived parental autonomy support plays a central role in fostering adolescents' academic engagement, yet little research has simultaneously examined its bidirectional associations with academic engagement or the mechanisms explaining these links. To address this gap, this study used cross-lagged panel modeling (CLPM) and random-intercept cross-lagged panel modeling (RI-CLPM) to investigate reciprocal relationships among perceived parental autonomy support, subjective intergenerational mobility, and academic engagement, while testing the mediating role of subjective intergenerational mobility. Participants were 738 Chinese adolescents (55.9% male; Mage = 14.58 years, SD = 0.59) who completed three waves of data collection at 6-month intervals. Results from the CLPM indicated reciprocal associations between perceived parental autonomy support and subjective intergenerational mobility. In contrast, the RI-CLPM revealed a more differentiated dynamic pattern: perceived parental autonomy support at T1 predicted subjective intergenerational mobility at T2, which subsequently predicted perceived parental autonomy support at T3. Furthermore, subjective intergenerational mobility predicted academic engagement only in the CLPM but not in the RI-CLPM. Importantly, both modeling approaches consistently demonstrated a stable reciprocal association between perceived parental autonomy support and academic engagement. These findings highlight the importance of considering temporal dynamics and individual differences when examining the relationships among perceived parental autonomy support, subjective intergenerational mobility, and adolescents' academic engagement. The results suggest that enhancing perceived parental autonomy support and strengthening adolescents' perceptions of intergenerational mobility may serve as vital pathways to sustain and promote long-term academic engagement.

items.title: Connecting and feeling: Teachers' relational goals, classroom goal structures and emotions.
items.abstract: The social dimension of teachers' goal orientations plays a significant role in instructional settings and is associated with both classroom goal structures and teachers' discrete emotions. However, few studies have directly examined these links. The present research comprises two studies that investigated the role of teachers' relational goal orientation in fostering close, supportive teacher-student relationships and its associations with classroom goal structures and teachers' enjoyment, anxiety and anger. Study 1 surveyed 2180 Chinese teachers (93.9% female; mean age = 31.41, SD = 8.77; 77% kindergarten, 23% primary school) through an online panel. Study 2 recruited 88 primary and middle school teachers (68.2% female; mean age = 39.40, SD = 8.17) and 4137 students (47.4% female; mean age = 12.06, SD = 1.57) from 88 classrooms via paper-based surveys. Study 1 was teacher self-reports, whereas Study 2 included both teacher- and student-reported data. Teachers' relational goals were positively associated with teaching-related enjoyment and negatively associated with anxiety and anger. Classroom goal structures showed significant indirect associations linking relational goals to these emotions. Further analyses revealed that mastery-oriented classroom goal structures accounted for part of the association of relational goals with teachers' emotions, whereas performance-oriented goal structures conveyed adverse associations. These findings highlight the importance of relational goals and their association with classroom motivational climates and teachers' emotional well-being and offer a basis for understanding how relational teaching goals translate into instructional practices and emotional experiences. These results have implications for teacher professional development and classroom climate interventions.

items.title: Teacher-class relationship and student emotional and behavioural engagement: Are they reciprocally related?
items.abstract: Most existing research conceptualizes teacher influence as unidirectional, suggesting that the quality of relationships between teachers and students shapes student engagement. This perspective tends to overlook students as active contributors to classroom climate and as co-constructors of relationships with their teachers. However, within the classroom context, it is more plausible that relationship quality and student engagement mutually influence one another over time. Moreover, previous research has rarely examined the teacher-class relationship (TCR), defined as teachers' perceptions of their relationship with the class as a whole. The present study investigated the reciprocal relation between the TCR and students' emotional and behavioural engagement. A total of 1085 secondary school teachers and 20,142 of their students from 75 secondary schools in Croatia participated in the study. A full-panel longitudinal design was employed, with data collected at two time points: the beginning and the end of the school year. Teachers assessed the TCR, while both teachers and students rated students' emotional and behavioural engagement. Multilevel cross-lagged panel models were used to analyse the data. The findings revealed that both teacher-reported and student-reported engagement predicted subsequent TCR, whereas the reverse prospective association was not supported. These results suggest that student engagement may play an important role in shaping teachers' perceptions of the teacher-class relationship in the classroom.

items.title: Subjective Economic Status and Adolescent Materialism: The Moderating Role of Parental Material Indulgence and the Mediating Role of Self-Esteem.
items.abstract: Previous research has yielded inconsistent findings regarding the relationship between family economic status and adolescent materialism. Drawing on Self-Determination Theory and Goal Content Theory, this study proposes a dual-pathway model explaining how adolescents' subjective family economic status shapes materialistic values. Specifically, we examined whether parental material indulgence moderates this relationship, potentially explaining these inconsistencies. Additionally, we investigated self-esteem as a mediator of this relationship. Data was collected in Poland in 2024 using a cross-sectional survey design. Participants were 2055 adolescents aged 10-18 years (M = 13.47, SD = 1.99; 1024 girls, 937 boys, 94 another gender). Adolescents completed self-report measures assessing subjective family economic status, self-esteem, materialism, and parental material indulgence. The hypothesized moderated mediation model was tested using regression-based analyses. The results supported the proposed model. Parental material indulgence moderated the relationship between adolescents' subjective economic status and materialism. Higher subjective economic status was associated with lower materialism when parental material indulgence was low, but with higher materialism when indulgence was high. Additionally, higher subjective economic status was indirectly associated with lower materialism through higher self-esteem. The findings suggest that parental material indulgence may help explain inconsistent associations between subjective family economic status and adolescent materialism. They also support the mediating role of self-esteem, highlighting the importance of both parenting practices and psychological factors in understanding adolescent materialism.

items.title: Perceived norms, interpersonal communication, and daily e-cigarette use frequency among young adults in the United States: A multilevel mediation analysis of egocentric networks.
items.abstract: Perceived norms (descriptive and injunctive) and discussions about e-cigarettes are directly associated with young adults' e-cigarette use. Young adults often use e-cigarettes in social contexts where discussions about e-cigarettes may reinforce perceptions of peer e-cigarette use, leading to personal e-cigarette use. The current study examined whether frequency of e-cigarette-related discussions mediated the association between perceived norms and daily e-cigarette use frequency. We administered an online vaping survey to 524 college students at a large public university in the southwestern United States (Mage = 20.83 years, SD = 2.43; female = 81.5%). A multilevel mediation analysis was conducted. There was a significant indirect contextual association between descriptive norms and daily e-cigarette use frequency through frequency of e-cigarette-related discussions. The findings highlight both dyadic relationships and broader social networks as potentially relevant contexts for peer-to-peer e-cigarette prevention efforts.

items.title: Quality of sleep and fertility quality of life among women undergoing IVF-ET: Mediating role of self-esteem.
items.abstract: The study aimed to investigate the mediating role of self-esteem in the relationship between quality of sleep and fertility quality of life among women undergoing IVF treatment. The study was conducted among 387 women undergoing IVF in Kerala, using Fertility Quality of Life Questionnaire, Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale and Inventory of Quality of sleep. The results indicated a positive correlation among quality of sleep, self-esteem and quality of life. The findings of the mediation analysis showed that the total effect of quality of sleep on fertility quality of life was significant (β = 0.4392). The direct effect of quality of sleep on fertility quality of life was significant (β = 0.1959). The indirect effect of quality of sleep on fertility quality of life through self-esteem was also statistically significant (β = 0.244). The findings suggest that self-esteem serves as a partial mediator in the relationship between quality of sleep and fertility quality of life for women undergoing IVF.

items.title: Voices from the field: Proceedings of the 2025 Society for Community, Research and Action Biennial Conference.
items.abstract: This themed issue, developed with the Society for Community Research and Action (SCRA) around its 20th Biennial Conference (Michigan State University, June 2025), presents ten articles reflecting the diversity of contemporary community psychology. Topics range from resistance to equity-focused public safety reform, trauma-informed care, and youth participatory action research to stigma among sexual and gender diverse youth, adverse childhood experiences, peer-led recovery, and medical respite for people experiencing homelessness. Despite their varied methods, the articles share a preventive orientation, a commitment to empowerment and social justice, and a systemic, person-in-context lens that avoids individualizing blame and stigmatizing already marginalized communities.

items.title: Healthcare professionals' perspectives on older patients' Mental health treatment engagement.
items.abstract: Older adults face complex challenges in seeking and receiving mental health treatment. While older adults access mental health services less frequently than other populations, strong engagement can predict better treatment outcomes. This study explores practitioners' perspectives on the treatment engagement of patients referred for specialty geriatric mental health services. Guided by Raue and Sirey's late-life treatment engagement model, 11 interviews were conducted with specialty geriatric mental health professionals (psychiatrists, psychologists) and frequent referral sources (primary care physician, neurologist). Interviews assessed practitioners' perspectives on patient treatment engagement barriers to create a refined framework of older adults' mental health treatment engagement. The qualitative framework analysis resulted in three key themes of (1) referral factors; (2) pathway navigation (modifiable); and (3) individual patient factors, and corresponding subthemes including individual, social, and system-level factors that are potential targets of interventions to enhance engagement. Results supported patient-centered care and collaboration among providers and older adults when navigating treatment systems. Streamlined communication between referral sources, specialists, and patients was also proposed. Findings highlight the importance of considering provider factors in patient engagement, and suggest a need for interventions to improve patient and provider knowledge about navigating the mental health system.

items.title: Transfer to adult care - experiences of young adults living with human immunodeficiency virus in Jamaica.
items.abstract: Combination antiretroviral therapy has improved health outcomes for adolescents living with the human Immunodeficiency Virus (ALHIV). Long-term survival necessitates effective interventions for optimal continuity of care as they transition to adult healthcare. No National Transition Policy for adolescents with chronic illnesses exists in Jamaica, despite anecdotal reports of informal, site-specific processes for their transfer from pediatric to adult care settings. We present qualitative evaluative feedback from eleven young adults living with HIV (YALHIV) (18-34 years old) post-transfer from pediatric to adult care. Identified themes included: (1) perceptions of transfer - apprehension and uncertainty, (2) barriers to transfer - remorse about moving to adult clinics, stigma, loss of bond with providers, lack of communication, (3) facilitators - greater personal responsibility, shorter wait times with flexible scheduling at the adult clinic, (4) self-management (adherence to clinic visits and antiretroviral medication) and (5) recommendations - enhanced collaboration between pediatric and adult healthcare providers (HCP), pre-transfer exposure to the adult clinic, and increased psychoeducation pre- and post-transfer. These qualitative findings inform the transition process for YALHIV, which should be optimized through early, continual disclosure of diagnosis and enhanced psychoeducation for clients, while fostering a collaborative approach between pediatric and adult healthcare providers.

items.title: More effort, more variability, but greater relative precision: Distributional modeling of effort-performance coupling.
items.abstract: Ratings of perceived exertion (RPE) are widely used to prescribe exercise intensities. When used this way, researchers and practitioners may implicitly or explicitly rely on assumptions about the coupling between perceived effort and performance. These assumptions refer to two dimensions: the average shape of how effort translates to performance and the variability of performance across effort levels. Straightforwardly, effort-performance coupling can be thought of as linear, with constant variability across the intensity spectrum. However, classic psychophysical scaling laws (e.g., Fechner's law) and motor control research (e.g., signal-dependent noise) predict that such coupling is non-linear, with intensity-contingent increases in variability. These assumptions are rarely made explicit and have not been jointly tested. To address this, we fitted and compared theory-driven Bayesian multilevel models reflecting distinct assumptions about the mean and the variability structure, using leave-one-out cross-validation for model selection. Data were collected from 101 climbers performing an isometric handgrip task with effort prescribed using a RPE 1-10 scale. We found robust evidence for a heteroscedastic variability structure, with a systematic increase in absolute force variability with prescribed RPE. Additionally, we found modest evidence favoring an exponential mean shape over a linear mean shape, suggesting that force increases disproportionately with effort. These effects were gender unspecific and are broadly consistent with Fechner's psychophysical law and signal-dependent noise theory. Together, these findings suggest that a direct translation from effort to performance systematically misrepresents the actual relationship. Instead, practitioners and researchers should expect a disproportionate increase in performance with increasing absolute performance variability.

items.title: Effects of Mindfulness Training on Impulsivity and NoGo-Go-Related Brain Activation in Internet Gaming Disorder.
items.abstract: This study aimed to determine whether the effects of mindfulness meditation training (MMT) on impulsivity and Internet gaming disorder (IGD) severity operate through sequential or parallel pathways, and to identify the neural correlates associated with these effects. Sixty-two IGD participants were randomized to MMT (n = 31) or progressive muscle relaxation (PMR; n = 31). Addiction severity and Barratt Impulsiveness (BIS-11) were assessed pre- and post-intervention. Participants performed a Go/NoGo task in magnetic resonance imaging to examine neural correlates of inhibitory control. Mediation analyses tested potential pathways of MMT effects. MMT significantly reduced addiction severity and non-planning impulsivity, with higher mindfulness associated with greater reductions in non-planning and cognitive impulsivity. Neural analyses revealed decreased activation in the bilateral lingual gyrus (Left: t = 3.98, p =.012; Right: t = 4.51, p =.007) and cerebellum (Left: t = 4.87, cluster p =.005; Right: t = 5.24, cluster p =.005) during NoGo-Go condition following MMT. Mediation analyses provided no evidence for a mediated effect of MMT on impulsivity and addiction severity. Although IGD symptom severity, trait impulsivity, and task-related brain activation all decreased following MMT, these changes co-occurred without evidence of a mediating relationship among them.

items.title: Combined Neuromelanin-Sensitive and Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging Links Midbrain Dopaminergic Dysfunction to Connectome Architecture in First-Episode, Medication-Naïve Major Depressive Disorder.
items.abstract: Accumulating evidence implicates dopaminergic dysfunction in major depressive disorder (MDD), yet direct evidence of such dysfunction and of its altered coupling with the functional connectome remains limited. Using neuromelanin-sensitive MRI (NM-MRI) and resting-state fMRI, we examined differences in substantia nigra/ventral tegmental area NM-MRI signal (NMSSN/VTA) between first-episode, medication-naïve MDD patients (n = 112) and healthy controls (HC; n = 230). Network-based statistics (NBS) assessed MDD-related alterations in NMSSN/VTA-functional connectivity (FC) coupling. Spatial correspondence analyses examined the spatial convergence of these coupling alterations with normative dopaminergic molecular maps and anhedonia-related connectome patterns in MDD. Patients with MDD showed lower NMSSN/VTA, with more pronounced reductions in lateral and rostral regions. NBS identified a widespread component with altered NMSSN/VTA-FC coupling in MDD, characterized predominantly by higher slopes across attention, control, sensory, and medial temporal systems and lower slopes involving limbic-striatal and default-mode connections. Network-level analysis further identified a diagnosis-dependent NMSSN/VTA-striatal-limbic connectivity relationship, with lower NMSSN/VTA associated with higher FC in MDD. Spatially, these coupling alterations converged with dopaminergic molecular architecture, showing negative correspondence with normative dopaminergic receptor and transporter distributions and positive correspondence with the anticipatory-pleasure-related connectome pattern in MDD. These findings provide in vivo evidence of midbrain dopaminergic dysfunction and widespread disruption of dopaminergic-connectome coupling in MDD, with these coupling alterations spatially converging with anhedonia-related connectome organization. Together, these findings advance our understanding of the role of dopaminergic dysfunction in the pathophysiology of MDD.

items.title: Recreational cannabis legalization and psychiatric emergency department visits among cannabis patients in California: A repeated-cohort study.
items.abstract: Recreational cannabis legalization (RCL) has been linked to population-level adverse mental health outcomes, potentially owing to wider use of high-potency cannabis products. We tested whether California's 2018 RCL implementation was associated with increased risk for subsequent psychiatric emergency department (ED) visits among a vulnerable subgroup: patients presenting to the ED with cannabis misuse. Repeated cohort study using statewide, all-payer ED visits from 2010-2022, linked within patient. Groups comprised annual cohorts of (a) all patients aged ≥21 years with an index ED visit for cannabis use disorder (CUD) or poisoning, and (b) a random selection of all other ED patients aged ≥21 years. California, pre- and post-RCL. The sample included 3,043,332 index patient visits (n = 437,057 cannabis patient visits; n = 2,606,275 reference patient visits) across all study years. Cannabis patients, vs. reference patients, were more often male (64.9% vs. 44.3%) and younger (43.9% vs. 17.3% aged 21-29 years). Exposure to recreational cannabis policy period was primarily defined as having an index visit during the pre-RCL implementation (2011-2017) vs. post-RCL implementation (2018-2021) period. The primary study outcome was any psychiatric ED visit within 12 months of patient's index visit. Comparative interrupted time series (CITS) regression models tested whether cannabis patients' risk of a subsequent psychiatric ED visit, relative to reference patients, changed from pre- to post-RCL policy periods. Index visits for cannabis doubled from nearly 25,000 to >52,000 over the study period. Pre-RCL, 20.1% of cannabis patients, vs. 5.0% of reference patients, made a psychiatric ED visit in the 12 months after index visit (covariate-adjusted risk ratio [RR]=1.55 [95% CI=1.52, 1.58]). CITS regression models indicated that RCL implementation was associated with shifting trends in psychiatric risk: reference patients' risk declined, but cannabis patients' risk stayed flat or slightly increased (particularly among those aged 21-29 and those without prior mental disorder). RCL implementation in California was associated with slightly diverging trends in risk of psychiatric ED visits among cannabis patients relative to other ED patients. The growing volume of cannabis ED patients - and their persistently elevated psychiatric risk - underscores the health system burden related to cannabis misuse and warrants ongoing public health surveillance and clinical treatment efforts.

items.title: Cross-identity and cross-attractiveness-level generalization of the "three-foreheads and five-eyes" facial attractiveness prototype: Evidence from visual adaptation.
items.abstract: The study employed a visual adaptation paradigm to examine whether the "three-foreheads and five-eyes" (3F5E) configuration, a traditional Chinese facial aesthetic standard, serves as the prototype representation of facial attractiveness, and whether this representation can generalize across facial identities and feature attractiveness levels. Chinese participants adapted to adaptor faces with various configurations, and then adjusted the distances between the features of a test face until the face appeared most attractive. The results showed evidence supporting that the aftereffect of adapting to 3F5E faces did not differ from 0; whereas adapting to stretched or compressed faces produced significant aftereffects greater than 0 in the corresponding horizontal or vertical distortion directions, meaning the adjusted most attractive test face was also stretched or compressed in the corresponding horizontal or vertical direction. This suggests that the 3F5E configuration is the configural prototype of the most attractive face. In addition, when the identity of the adaptor face and the test face differed, an adaptation aftereffect also occurred, and there was evidence supporting that it did not differ from the aftereffect when their identities were the same. This suggests that the representation can generalize across facial identities. However, the aftereffect was greater when the feature attractiveness levels of the test face and adaptor face were the same than when they were different, suggesting differences in the configural representations of faces with different feature attractiveness levels.

items.title: When takeovers require cognitive control: Effects of partial automation and cognitive load on driver-initiated responses to traffic hazards on urban roads.
items.abstract: Partially automated driving (PAD) systems are becoming increasingly prevalent in consumer vehicles. While drivers are obliged to monitor the roadway and the system during PAD, they do not always comply with this requirement and may engage in non-driving-related tasks (NDRTs). Literature has emphasized the detrimental effects of visual-manual NDRTs on drivers' capability to takeover control from PAD while reporting negligible effects of non-visual NDRTs (e.g., hands-free phone calls) and cognitive load. However, most studies focused on alerted scenarios, with takeover requests lowering drivers' reliance on anticipation and cognitive control, masking the effects of cognitive load. Related work also examined PAD conditions alone, neglecting the combined effects of automation and cognitive load on drivers' responses. To address the gaps, we conducted a driving simulator study examining the influence of cognitive load, induced by a 2-back task, on driver-initiated responses to urban traffic hazards (e.g., crossing pedestrians, oncoming vehicles) during both manual driving and PAD. The timing and quality of driver-initiated responses were analysed separately for each hazard with detail. Results showed that driver-initiated responses during PAD were less anticipatory and relied more on cognitive control. This shift led to higher situational criticality and heightened susceptibility of responses to cognitive load during PAD. Hazard characteristics such as motion speed and cue ambiguity appeared to influence cognitive load effects and warrant systematic examination in future work. Together, these findings underscore an elevated safety risk associated with cognitive load during PAD, especially in scenarios requiring cognitively demanding, driver-initiated intervention.

items.title: Priming sibling warmth boosts empathy: the mediating role of self-worth in adolescents.
items.abstract: Across two experiments, the present research represents the first application of priming methods in sibling research and examines how activating a sibling warmth mindset influences adolescents' state empathy. Guided by relational schema theory, we hypothesized that sibling warmth priming would enhance state empathy by increasing self-worth. In Study 1, adolescents were randomly assigned to either a sibling warmth priming condition, in which they recalled warm interactions with their siblings to activate relational schemas, or a neutral control condition. Following the priming task, participants reported their levels of self-worth and empathy. Results showed that priming sibling warmth significantly increased adolescents' self-worth and empathic responses. Mediation analyses further revealed that self-worth mediated the link between sibling warmth priming and empathy. In Study 2, we independently manipulated sibling warmth priming and self-worth enhancement using a randomized 2 × 2 factorial design. Results showed that both manipulations increased state empathy, and self-worth enhancement attenuated the additional effect of sibling warmth priming on empathy. These findings provide the first experimental evidence that activating relational schemas of close sibling bonds can promote adolescents' empathy, with self-worth serving as an important psychological process linking sibling warmth to empathic responding.

items.title: Visual capture of tactile motion: Evidence from a novel mirror box illusion.
items.abstract: To localize touch, the brain must integrate information from representations of the skin's surface (a somatotopic reference frame) with representations of the surrounding environment (an external reference frame). While vision robustly captures the perceived location of static touches, resolving crossmodal spatial conflicts for continuous, moving stimuli remains poorly understood. Across four experiments, we demonstrate a novel visual-tactile illusion: viewing a moving stroke across the hand substantially alters the perceived trajectory of a simultaneous tactile stroke on a hidden hand, shifting the percept roughly halfway toward the direction of the visual stroke. This visual capture of tactile motion occurs independently of top-down body ownership. By systematically manipulating hand posture, we found that both somatotopic and external reference frames contribute to the perceived direction of tactile motion. Rather than defaulting to a single coordinate system, the brain combines information from both representations to construct a conscious percept of tactile motion. These results extend visual capture from the location of a touch to its trajectory, and suggest that accounts built on brief, punctate stimuli may need to accommodate both continuous tactile motion and contributions from multiple spatial reference frames.

items.title: Factors Associated with Women's Sex-Related Coping and Enhancement Drinking Motives.
items.abstract: Sexual assault and heavy drinking are interrelated public health concerns, particularly among college women. Women's sex-related drinking motives (SRDM), including motivations to cope with negative experiences during sex or to drink to enhance positive aspects of sex, may be particularly relevant in the context of sexual assault and among those with greater emotion regulation difficulties and depression symptoms. This study sought to examine factors associated with coping and enhancement SRDM. Participants were 137 female college students with histories of consensual sex and past year drinking recruited from a large public university in the southeastern U.S. Linear regressions and ANOVAs with planned post-hoc analyses showed that individuals with histories of any past-year sexual assault, relative to individuals with no past year sexual assault, reported greater enhancement SRDM. Heavier drinking was associated with greater coping and enhancement SRDM, and greater depression symptoms were positively associated with coping SRDM. Results suggest that both coping and enhancement SRDM are associated with heavy drinking, whereas characteristics reflective of a lack of adaptive coping skills such as depression symptoms are uniquely associated with coping SRDM and a recent history of sexual assault was associated with enhancement SRDM.

items.title: Unpacking LGBTQIA+ Community Inequity's Influence on Alcohol Use: Examining the Roles of Internalized Stigma and Emotional Lability.
items.abstract: Lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, intersex, and asexual (LGBTQIA+) populations experience disproportionate and concerning rates of alcohol use. Previous scholars posit that experiences of cis-heterosexist discrimination influence internal processes (e.g., internalized stigma, emotional lability) to explain greater risk for alcohol use; however, few studies have examined how experiences of inequity within LGBTQIA+ communities may be associated with alcohol use. Using a sample of 625 LGBTQIA+ people (Mage = 36.81, SD = 14.40), the present study examined whether LGBTQIA+ community inequity functions as a distal stressor associated with alcohol use through internalized stigma and emotional lability. Results from a parallel mediation model indicated that a significant relation between LGBTQIA+ community inequity and alcohol use was explained through internalized stigma and emotional lability. Findings suggest that LGBTQIA+ community inequity may shape self-stigma and emotional processes to increase alcohol use. Implications for clinical practice, outreach, and policy are discussed.

items.title: Associations of hearing impairment with loneliness: a meta-analysis.
items.abstract: The present meta-analysis examined the association between hearing impairment and loneliness. Data collection employed a systematic search involving the electronic databases Google Scholar, Medline, PsycInfo and Web of Science. Quantitative papers were included that provided information on loneliness in individuals with hearing impairment compared to test norms or people without hearing impairment, as well as studies reporting correlation between hearing impairment and loneliness. Random-effects, multilevel meta-analysis was computed. We included 120 studies with 109,707 individuals who are deaf or hard-of-hearing. Individuals with hearing impairments reported higher loneliness than individuals without hearing impairments or test norms (g = 0.389 standard deviation units, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.296 to 0.483). Moderator analysis revealed stronger loneliness elevations in individuals who are deaf (g = 0.971) than in those who are hard-of-hearing (g = 0.291). Loneliness elevations were stronger if people with hearing impairments were younger and more likely to be unpartnered/unmarried and smaller in community-based probability samples than in convenience samples and in studies from high-income countries than in other studies. While measures to prevent and reduce loneliness in individuals with hearing impairments are generally recommended, those who are deaf and younger should be the main target.

items.title: Not knowing as bordering: Immigration status and child protection in Canada.
items.abstract: This paper examines how child protection systems enact everyday bordering through institutionalized forms of not knowing about immigration status. While child protection services (CPS) across Canada are undertaking reforms to address institutionalized racism, immigration-related concerns remain largely overlooked. Drawing on everyday bordering and family policing scholarship, alongside Medina's (2017) concept of racial ignorance, we trace how administrative, epistemic, and carceral practices implicate CPS in migration governance. Through interpretive policy analysis of child welfare documents and interviews with professionals and community advocates in Ontario and British Columbia, we identify how (1) administrative neglect heightens deportation risks; (2) racialized assumptions about age and credibility undermine protection for unaccompanied minors; and (3) concerns about "permanency" can mask racialized bias against kinship caregivers who have a temporary immigration status. We argue that institutionalized forms of knowing and not knowing reproduces differential inclusion within CPS. When immigration precarity remains illegible, opportunities to address structural inequities afficing child-well being may be missed. Yet when interpreted through racialized assumptions about risk and belonging, immigration precarity may also intensify CPS's role in family policing, separation, and exposure to immigration enforcement.

items.title: Anti-Immigrant Policy and Children's Health: A State-Level Analysis of Exposure to Risk.
items.abstract: The US sociopolitical context, characterized by anti-immigrant rhetoric and exclusionary social policies, presents a salient stressor for immigrant families. Exposure to exclusionary policies contributes to stress among foreign-born parents (Perreira & Pedroza, 2019), which then trickles down to their children, contributing to short- and long-term health risks. Using data from the 2023 National Survey of Children's Health (CAHMI, 2024) and a state-level index of immigration-related policies (Samari et al., 2021), this study used generalized linear models to assess the relation between the immigrant policy climate and exposure to risk. Results indicated that state immigration policy climate was predictive of childhood mental, social, and relational risk exposure, with differences by parental nativity (F(6, 13,152) = 1,541.41, p < .001). In an average policy state, children of immigrants exhibited a substantially higher rate of exposure to risk compared to children of native-born parents (B = 5.31, SE = 0.08, p < .001). Moreover, inclusionary policy climates were associated with stronger protective effects for children of immigrants than for children of native-born parents (B = -0.16, SE = 0.01, p < .001), and this pattern persisted after accounting for state socioeconomic conditions. These differences were more pronounced in states with exclusionary policy contexts and attenuated in inclusionary states. Overall, these results illustrate the impact of policy context on children and suggest that inclusionary state policies may play a protective role in child well-being. Advocating for more inclusive structural policy environments may be a critical addition to family- and individual-level interventions targeting childhood risk.

items.title: Psychometric validation of the french endometriosis health profile-5 (EHP-5): structural validity, measurement invariance and recommendations for clinical interpretation.
items.abstract: The Endometriosis Health Profile-5 (EHP-5) is a widely used disease-specific instrument for assessing endometriosis-related quality of life. Despite its growing use, evidence regarding its structural validity and measurement invariance remains limited. This study examined the psychometric properties of the French EHP-5. A total of 1,439 French-speaking women with medically diagnosed endometriosis completed an online survey. Preliminary item analyses included difficulty and discrimination indices, floor and ceiling effects, and Ferguson's delta coefficient. Internal consistency was evaluated using Cronbach's alpha and McDonald's omega. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) was conducted using robust weighted least squares estimation (WLSMV). Hypothesis testing for construct validity was conducted using 0-10 numerical rating scales for pain intensity and frequency and dichotomous indicators of fatigue and constant pelvic pain. Measurement invariance was tested across infertility, parenthood, and comorbidity groups. The five core items demonstrated satisfactory item functioning and internal consistency (α = 0.71; ω = 0.71). CFA generally supported a unidimensional structure of the core scale (CFI = 0.956, TLI = 0.912, SRMR = 0.047), although RMSEA (= 0.111) exceeded conventional recommendations. EHP-5 scores were significantly associated with pain intensity, pain frequency, fatigue, and constant pelvic pain, consistent with the predefined hypotheses for construct validity. Measurement invariance was generally supported across infertility, parenthood, and comorbidity groups. The French EHP-5 core scale appears to be a brief measure of endometriosis-related quality of life with satisfactory psychometric properties. Clinical implications and recommendations are discussed, particularly regarding the complementary roles of the core and modular components of the instrument and their implications for score interpretation.

items.title: Basophil Activation Testing: From Diagnostic Adjunct to Precision Allergy Management.
items.abstract: Basophils are rare circulating granulocytes that trigger immediate hypersensitivity reactions through IgE-mediated degranulation and also contribute to innate immunity. The basophil activation test (BAT) is a flow cytometry-based functional assay that quantifies basophil reactivity and sensitivity following allergen stimulation, offering a safe, blood-based alternative to in vivo provocation testing. This review summarizes the immunological basis of the BAT, its technical requirements, and its expanding clinical applications across food, respiratory, drug, and hymenoptera venom allergies, autoimmune chronic spontaneous urticaria, and vaccine hypersensitivity. Beyond diagnosis, the BAT increasingly supports monitoring of allergen immunotherapy and biologic treatments, prediction of reaction severity and treatment response, and personalized management decisions. Its performance varies by allergen and clinical context, and wider adoption is constrained by the absence of standardized protocols, validated cut-offs, and reference materials, as well as by basophil non-releasers and dependence on fresh viable blood. Passive BAT and mast cell activation test formats extend testing to patients in whom the conventional BAT is uninterpretable. Automated, data-driven analysis and machine learning-assisted, label-free platforms offer promising routes toward more objective, scalable interpretation. With continued standardization, harmonization, and prospective validation, the BAT is positioned not only as a diagnostic adjunct but as a platform for precision-based allergy management.

items.title: Sprint National Anaesthesia Project 3: A survey of perioperative medicine services for older surgical patients in Australia.
items.abstract: Increasing numbers of older people with age-related conditions such as frailty and multimorbidity are presenting for surgical procedures, which is associated with an increased risk of postoperative complications. This study aimed to assess the provision of perioperative medicine services for older surgical patients across Australian hospitals participating in the third Sprint National Anaesthesia Project. An organisational survey was conducted involving 23 Australian hospitals, collecting data on hospital characteristics, clinical governance, preoperative assessments (including frailty, cognition, and risk of delirium), and postoperative care practices for high-risk older patients. Responses were analysed to evaluate the structure and function of perioperative services for older surgical patients. Twenty-one hospitals completed the survey. Preoperative assessments of older surgical patients were predominantly nurse- or anaesthetist-led, with limited geriatrician involvement. Routine preoperative screening of frailty and cognition was rare, and there was significant variability in approaches to the assessment of postoperative delirium. The survey highlights inconsistencies in perioperative care delivery for older surgical patients, revealing gaps in the implementation of established guidelines and recommendations. There is a need for a structured approach to integrate geriatric services into surgical pathways, with an emphasis on routine screening for frailty, cognitive impairment, multimorbidity, and delirium.

items.title: Schwann cell targeted gene delivery in peripheral neuropathy models and non-human primates.
items.abstract: Gene therapy using recombinant adeno-associated viral (rAAV) vectors is a promising strategy for treating inherited demyelinating neuropathies such as Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1X (CMT1X). Efficient and safe targeting of myelinating Schwann cells remains a key challenge for clinical translation. Here, we evaluated the safety, efficacy and scale-up potential of Schwann cell targeting by clinically relevant rAAVrh10 and rAAVrh74 vectors following lumbar intrathecal delivery in CMT1X mice and non-human primates (NHPs). Both rAAVrh10 and rAAVrh74 achieved efficient, dose-dependent biodistribution to the peripheral nerves with expression in Schwann cells driven by cell-specific promoter. In the Gjb1-null CMT1X mouse model, delivery of the therapeutic human GJB1 gene led to significant functional and morphological improvements, including increased grip strength, faster nerve conduction velocities, improved myelination and decreased inflammation. In NHPs, both serotypes demonstrated robust PNS biodistribution and Schwann cell targeting without adverse neurological effects, or liver toxicity related to therapeutic vectors. Overall, a single lumbar intrathecal injection of rAAVrh10 or rAAVrh74 enables efficient, dose-dependent Schwann cell transduction and therapeutic gene expression with functional benefit in the Gjb1- null demyelinating neuropathy mouse model, without toxicity in NHPs. This study supports the clinical translation of rAAV-mediated gene therapy targeting Schwann cells for treating CMT1X.

items.title: A pilot randomized feasibility trial of perioperative melatonin for cardiac arrhythmias during CPB weaning, sedative and analgesic medication use, and mechanical ventilation following CABG.
items.abstract: Background Perioperative complications remain common following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Although melatonin may have cardioprotective and sedative-sparing effects, its feasibility and potential effects on early postoperative cardiac rhythm and recovery in patients undergoing CABG remain unclear. Objectives To assess the feasibility of a future definitive randomized controlled trial (RCT) of perioperative melatonin in patients undergoing on-pump CABG and to obtain preliminary estimates of its effects on cardiac arrhythmias during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) weaning, duration of mechanical ventilation, and postoperative sedative and analgesic medication use. Methods In this pilot randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled feasibility trial, 22 adults undergoing elective on-pump CABG were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive oral melatonin (3 mg) or placebo nightly, from three nights before to three nights after surgery. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, retention, protocol adherence, completeness of outcome assessment, and intervention safety. Exploratory clinical outcomes included cardiac arrhythmias during CPB weaning, duration of mechanical ventilation, and postoperative sedative and analgesic medication use. Results Twenty-two participants were randomized. The recruitment rate was 68.75%, while retention, protocol adherence, and completeness of outcome assessment were all 100%; no treatment-related adverse events were observed. Arrhythmias during CPB weaning occurred in 2 of 11 participants (18.2%) in each group (OR, 1.00; 95% CI: 0.11-8.73). The median duration of mechanical ventilation was 9.5 hours with melatonin and 15.0 hours with placebo (Hodges-Lehmann estimate of the between-group location shift, -3.30 hours; 95% CI: -6.90 to 1.05). Postoperative sedative and analgesic medication use was generally comparable between groups, although the corresponding effect estimates were imprecise. Conclusion Melatonin was feasible and well tolerated in this pilot cohort, with no treatment-related adverse events observed. The exploratory estimates were imprecise and do not provide evidence of efficacy, supporting a larger, adequately powered randomized trial to further evaluate the efficacy and safety of melatonin. Trial registration number IRCT20250206064666N1, date of registration: 2025-02-24.

items.title: Rehabilitation Strategies for Upper Limb Function After Breast Cancer Treatment, with and Without Lymphedema: The Potential of Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation - A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Purpose Upper limb dysfunction (pain, reduced shoulder mobility and strength, activity limitation) is common after breast cancer treatment, with or without breast cancer-related lymphedema (BCRL). Proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation (PNF) has been proposed to improve upper limb function and range of motion (ROM). This systematic review evaluates PNF for upper limb dysfunction in women treated for breast cancer, analyzing women with and without BCRL separately. Methods The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement was followed. Four databases were searched without date restrictions. Randomized or quasi-randomized English-language trials of PNF-containing interventions in women treated for breast cancer were included. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool and certainty of evidence with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Results Six trials (366 women) were included: three enrolled women with confirmed BCRL and three women without BCRL. PNF was mostly part of multimodal programs, but the between-group contrast isolated PNF in four trials. In BCRL trials, limb volume decreased in all groups, with no consistent advantage of PNF over active comparators. In women without BCRL, single trials reported improvements in ROM, strength and function. Risk of bias was low in one trial, high in one and of some concern in four; certainty of evidence was low or very low. Conclusion PNF may be a promising component of multimodal rehabilitation for upper limb dysfunction after breast cancer treatment; its independent effectiveness and its effects on BCRL remain unproven, and in women with BCRL it should complement, not replace, decongestive treatment. Trials in women with confirmed BCRL and standardized PNF protocols are needed. Trial registration PROSPERO CRD42025641774, registered on 2 February 2025 (retrospectively registered).

items.title: Biosynthesis of iboga alkaloids.
items.abstract: Tabernanthe iboga (iboga) is the source of voacangine, which is widely used as a semi-synthetic starting material for the anti-addiction agent ibogaine. Despite extensive investigation of voacangine biosynthesis, production of this compound cannot be reconstituted in a heterologous host, suggesting that one or more enzymes required for biosynthesis are missing. Additionally, T. iboga produces ibophyllidine, a pyrroloindole alkaloid that utilizes the same upstream precursor as voacangine, but is a member of a structurally distinct alkaloid class. Here we use bulk and single cell gene expression from leaf and root tissue to identify the unknown enzymes from these two pathways. We identify two additional enzymes that enable biosynthesis of voacangine in a heterologous host. The missing enzymes includes a pathogenesis-related (PR)10 family protein that likely catalyzes cyclization of a transient intermediate. Careful analysis of gene expression profiles in leaf and root also enabled the discovery of four additional enzymes that convert an upstream intermediate to ibophyllidine. This work reveals the chemical logic that generates two distinct alkaloid scaffolds in this important medicinal plant.

items.title: Algal composition and toxigenic risk decouple from nutrient levels across eutrophic lakes.
items.abstract: Eutrophication increasingly threatens lake ecosystems worldwide, yet how algal community structure and associated potential toxigenic risk vary along trophic gradients remains poorly understood. Here, we employed 23S rRNA gene sequencing to investigate algal community dynamics across three lakes spanning a trophic gradient from slight to high eutrophication. We found that algal diversity peaked under slight eutrophication and declined to a minimum at moderate levels, while community composition shifted from cyanobacteria-diatom co-dominance in the slight-eutrophic lake to cyanobacterial dominance under high-eutrophic conditions. Along this gradient, algal co-occurrence networks and keystone taxa were reshaped, with several potentially toxigenic algae occupying putative keystone positions under eutrophic conditions. Although stochastic processes (mainly ecological drift) predominantly governed the algal community assembly in all three lakes, the contribution of deterministic homogeneous selection increased markedly in the high-eutrophic lake (33.54%), indicating a significant intensification of environmental filtering under severe eutrophication. Notably, nitrogen and phosphorus nutrients partitioned taxa into positive responders (favoring high-eutrophic conditions) and negative responders (prevailing in the slight-eutrophic lake), decoupling algal risk from nutrient enrichment alone and revealing that eutrophication reshapes which taxa drive potential toxicity rather than uniformly amplifying it. These findings highlight that accurate algal risk predictions demand taxon- and context-dependent approaches rather than nutrient-focused proxies alone, providing a foundation for targeted management of harmful algal blooms across trophic gradients.

items.title: Health Literacy Measures for Migrant Populations: A Systematic Review of Cross-Cultural Adaptation and Psychometric Properties.
items.abstract: Evidence supporting the interpretation and use of health-literacy scores among migrant populations remains fragmented. This systematic review examined instruments used with international migrants, their measurement-property evidence, cross-cultural adaptation, score comparability, and contextual conditions documented alongside use. We searched seven databases and supplementary sources for English-language quantitative or mixed-methods studies published from February 2015 to March 2025. Measurement-property evidence was appraised using COSMIN methodology, while applied quantitative studies were appraised using design-specific JBI tools. Forty-seven studies were conducted in 18 host countries and examined 35 instruments; 21 were dedicated instrument-development or measurement-property studies, and 26 were applied studies. Among the dedicated studies, internal consistency was reported in 20 (95%), structural validity in 17 (81%), content-validity evidence in 13 (62%), and hypothesis testing in 14 (67%). Four studies reported test-retest reliability, one reported responsiveness, and none reported measurement error. Three studies examined measurement invariance or differential item functioning, and only four instruments had evidence of measurement properties from more than one study. Translation and cultural adaptation supported accessibility and conceptual relevance but did not establish score comparability. Affordability, documentation or legal concerns, and trust or discrimination were rarely documented. All host settings were high-income or upper-middle-income contexts. Instrument selection should match intended score use: tailored assessment may suit local service design, whereas cross-group comparisons are best supported by a common construct and evidence of comparability.

items.title: Affective responses to dental instrument images and dental anxiety: Potential implications for patient-centered dental care.
items.abstract: Objectives Dental anxiety remains a major barrier to dental care and is associated with adverse oral health outcomes. This study investigated affective responses to dental instrument images, their association with dental anxiety, and whether dental students differ from adult participants' emotional responses. Materials and methods In a cross-sectional online study, 57 adults evaluated images of dental instruments and normed neutral, negative, and positive images. An independent sample of 57 dental students rated the same images according to how they believed patients would respond. Affective responses were assessed using standardized ratings of valence, arousal, and dominance. Associations with dental anxiety and differences between dental instrument categories were examined. Results Dental instrument images elicited stronger affective responses than normed neutral and positive images and were comparable to normed negative images. Guided and invasive instruments, as well as drills and syringes, evoked pronounced affective responses. Higher dental anxiety was associated with more negative valence and higher arousal. No statistically significant group differences were observed for overall arousal, valence, or dominance ratings. However, group differences emerged in the differentiation between guided and unguided instruments and in the affective impact attributed to invasiveness. Conclusions Dental instrument images elicited pronounced affective responses even in a non-clinical sample. Their association with dental anxiety highlights the potential relevance of visual treatment cues in dental care. Clinical relevance Affective responses to visual dental treatment cues may be relevant to patient-centered communication and anxiety-sensitive dental care. Their implications should be further examined in clinical settings.

items.title: HVLT-R process variables in neuro-oncology: relationship with measures of executive functioning and utility in clinical and research settings.
items.abstract: Executive functioning (EF) is frequently impaired in people with brain tumors (PwBT) and may be reflected in neuropsychological "process variables" (e.g., semantic clustering) derived from verbal memory tasks. Although prior studies have linked these variables to memory performance, their construct validity and convergence with established EF measures remain unclear. This study aimed to: (1) replicate prior findings linking Hopkins Verbal Learning Test-Revised (HVLT-R) process variables with memory performance; (2) compare process variables between PwBT and healthy controls (HCs); (3) evaluate construct validity by examining associations with standardized EF measures; and (4) explore relationships with tumor location. PwBT (N = 127; Mage = 56.7; 63.8% female) completed the HVLT-R and at least two validated EF measures. Process variables included semantic clustering, intrusions, and repetitions. EF test scores were converted to normative z-scores and averaged to create a composite EF Index. Spearman correlations examined associations between process variables and EF. Comparisons with published HC data used summary t-tests. Independent samples t-tests evaluated differences by tumor location. EF performance (M = - 0.75, SD = 1.53) was positively associated with semantic clustering (r = .397, p<.01), but not with intrusions or repetitions. PwBT demonstrated fewer semantic clusters than HC during learning and delayed recall (ps<.01), with no differences in intrusion rates. Process variables did not differ by tumor location. Semantic clustering was associated with EF performance, supporting its construct validity, and was used less frequently by PwBT. Reduced clustering may represent a readily available, low-burden, supplemental marker of EF with potential utility for rehabilitation planning and clinical research.
