items.title: Predictors of anemia among children 6-59 months of age in Tanzania: a multilevel analysis of TDHS-MIS 2022.
items.abstract: Anemia remains a major public health problem among children in developing countries, including Tanzania, despite ongoing nutritional and health interventions. This study aimed to identify individual- and community-level factors associated with anemia in children aged 6-59 months in Tanzania. The study used data from the 2022 Tanzania Demographic and Health Survey and Malaria Indicator Survey (TDHS-MIS), a nationally representative cross-sectional survey conducted between February and July of 2022. Multilevel logistic regression was performed to identify individual- and community-level factors associated with childhood anemia. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported, and statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. A total of 4334 children aged 6-59 months were included in the analysis. The overall prevalence of anemia among children aged 6-59 months was 59.9% (95% CI: 58.48-61.39). Of these, 1.9%, 32.4%, and 25.6% had severe, moderate, and mild anemia, respectively. In the final multilevel model, children aged 6-23 months (AOR = 2.48; 95% CI: 2.01-3.07), those who were fourth or fifth born (AOR = 1.78; 95% CI: 1.25-2.52), those having recent diarrhea (AOR = 1.57; 95% CI: 1.11-2.21), those with stunting (AOR = 1.31; 95% CI: 1.08-1.59), and those with positive malaria test results (AOR = 4.87; 95% CI: 3.06-7.75) had significantly higher odds of anemia. Maternal age of 15-24 years (AOR = 1.55; 95% CI: 1.05-2.27), maternal anemia (AOR = 1.74; 95% CI: 1.44-2.10), and lack of health insurance (AOR = 1.67; 95% CI: 1.09-2.55) were also associated with increased odds of childhood anemia, whereas maternal overweight was associated with lower odds of anemia (AOR = 0.75; 95% CI: 0.59-0.96). Significant geographical disparities in childhood anemia were also observed across zones. Conclusion: Anemia affects approximately six out of ten children aged 6-59 months in Tanzania, indicating that it remains a public health concern in the country. Both individual- and community-level factors contribute to childhood anemia. Integrated interventions targeting child nutrition, malaria and diarrheal disease prevention, maternal anemia, and geographically tailored strategies are needed to reduce the burden of childhood anemia in Tanzania. What is known: • Anemia is a persistent public health problem among children under five years of age in sub-Saharan Africa, including Tanzania, with several individual-level risk factors (nutritional status, infections, and maternal characteristics) previously documented. What is new: • Using nationally representative data from the 2022 Tanzania Demographic and Health Survey and Malaria Indicator Survey (TDHS-MIS) and a multilevel logistic regression model, this study found that childhood anemia remains highly prevalent. • In addition to confirming established child-related predictors (younger child age, higher birth order, diarrhea, stunting, malaria infection, younger maternal age, and maternal anemia), this study demonstrated the independent influence of household factors (lack of health insurance) and community-level geographic disparities on childhood anemia.

items.title: Inhaled cannabis and oral alcohol: driving performance and subjective driving confidence in a human laboratory study.
items.abstract: Cannabis is the most commonly detected drug (second only to alcohol) among crash-involved drivers. Determining cannabis effects on driving performance is imperative to public health. The aim of this study was to assess a range of inhaled cannabis doses and an intoxicating dose of oral alcohol on simulated driving outcomes and subjective driving confidence. Healthy participants who used cannabis (n = 9) were enrolled in this within-subject, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, placebo-controlled, outpatient human laboratory study. Participants completed five experimental sessions to examine the effects of inhaled cannabis (0, 15, 30 mg THC; 15 mg THC + 7.5 mg CBD) and oral alcohol (0, 0.8 g/kg [15% less for women]). Data were collected at baseline and for 7.5 h after drug administration. Alcohol produced robust impairment on simulated driving performance outcomes (e.g., decreased lateral control; p<0.05). Cannabis decreased brake force and altered headway distance during obstacle navigation (p<0.05). All active doses of cannabis and alcohol decreased driving confidence (e.g., willingness to operate a real vehicle; p<0.05) and increased ratings of abuse potential (e.g., drug liking, p<0.05). High dose cannabis (30 mg) and alcohol increased subjective ratings of impairment and sedation (p<0.05). Cannabis did not produce profound alcohol-like driving impairment; however, it was not without risk, and driving impairment was evident. All active cannabis doses decreased participants' driving confidence, while the highest dose of cannabis (30 mg) and alcohol increased self-reported impairment and sedation. Overall, even in a sample of near-daily cannabis users, cannabis negatively impacted driving performance, decreased driving acuity, and reduced confidence in safe driving ability.

items.title: Unexpected Long Range Actions of AAV8
items.abstract: Adeno-associated virus vectors (AAVs) have broad utility in neuroscience. A variety of features, such as titer, capsid, enhancers and promoters, coding and non-coding elements, can be utilized to pursue diverse experimental ends. The net effects of titer and capsid have been used experimentally to pursue retrograde and anterograde studies, such as through the monosynaptic spread of high-titer AAV1. The literature on AAV8 is conflicting, with evidence for and against its long-range action outside of the infected starter population. Using the mouse corticopontocerebellar tract, we report that AAV8, when used at high titers, can be associated with long range recombination outside of the starter population. This phenomenon depended upon the viral titer and was influenced by the presence of other experimental injections. Surprisingly, separate injections of high-titer AAV8 recombinase and recombinase-reporter AAV8s gave rise to recombination across long distances in populations not known to be monosynaptically connected. Given the possibility of long range and emergent effects, we suggest that investigators empirically determine titer, capsid, and injection designs that reduce false positives and/or indirect effects.

items.title: Distinct innate immune states associate with divergent serological outcomes after syphilis treatment
items.abstract: The global resurgence of syphilis poses a major public health challenge, even in the era of effective antibiotic therapy. Following treatment, some patients achieve seroreversion, whereas others remain serofast with persistent nontreponemal antibody reactivity. Although nontreponemal antibody titers guide clinical follow-up, it remains unclear how closely they reflect the resolution of inflammation and recovery of immune function. We integrated single-cell transcriptomics, immunophenotyping in clinical samples, and functional assays to characterize circulating monocytes and natural killer (NK) cells across seroreversion and low- and high-titer serofast states, and further examined the impact of HIV coinfection. CD14+ monocytes retained inflammatory and CD163-associated scavenging programs after seroreversion, whereas serofast patients showed additional IFN-STAT1 activation in this subset. NK cells from serofast patients exhibited reduced JUN expression and impaired degranulation. JNK inhibition reduced the magnitude and altered the kinetics of NK cell degranulation, IFN-γ production, and amphiregulin (AREG) induction. Among low-titer serofast patients, HIV coinfection was associated with higher mitochondrial complex I gene expression and partially restored NK cell degranulation compared with patients with syphilis alone. Complex I inhibition also reduced NK cell degranulation. These findings suggest that seroreversion does not necessarily indicate immune normalization and identify post-treatment immune alterations not fully captured by conventional serological monitoring, providing a rationale for investigating cellular immune markers as complementary measures of recovery after syphilis treatment.

Data collected includes questionnaires, hirsutism self-assessment, clinical and blood parameters. items.title: Tens of MeV, collimated, bright fluxes of protons from ordered nanostructured targets in ultrarelativistic laser-matter interaction
items.abstract: Laser-driven proton acceleration from nanostructured solid targets has been extensively studied, yet its performance under realistic temporal contrast conditions at petawatt-class facilities remains an open question. We present an experimental investigation of proton generation from nanostructured and flat solid targets performed at the ELI-NP facility using femtosecond laser pulses at peak intensities of $\sim 3\times10^{21}$ \wcm. Proton spectra are compared for two contrast regimes: $\sim 10^{-10}$ without plasma mirror and $\sim 10^{-13}$ with single plasma mirror. Importantly, measurable enhancement in the cutoff energy persists for the nanowire targets at both contrast levels, indicating robustness of nanowire targets against moderate pre-pulse intensities. Alongside, study of energy resolved angular distribution reveals that nanowires promote more directional emission with higher flux of high-energy protons along the target normal, while flat targets produce broader angular distributions. The results are well supported and explained by 3D particle-in-cell simulations.

items.abstract: The Hidden Rotation That Collapses Collatz **Abstract** What looks like a failure of algebra is only a rotation waiting to be written down. Ptolemy’s planetary loops and Einstein’s velocity composition are composition engines of the same type: each hides a uniform generator behind a nonlinear stacking rule. Once the native geometry of that rule is exposed, the apparent chaos compresses into short identities. The same pattern supplies a natural extrapolation to the Collatz map, where residual non-commutativity becomes a precession that forces striking intersections. --- **Author:** Darren Pettis **Affiliation:** Independent Researcher **DOI:** 10.5281/zenodo.24431183 **Extrapolating the Collatz conjecture through the shared-process framework of your article.** Your article shows that both Ptolemy’s epicycles and relativistic velocity composition are composition engines of the same type: a uniform generator (angle on a circle, or rapidity on a hyperbola) is stacked by a nonlinear rule, producing an apparently irregular exterior that resolves once the native geometry of the composition law is written down. Forward iteration is a word in the free monoid generated by {H, O}. The exterior looks chaotic (hailstone bounces, irregular stopping times). The interior is simply the successive application of these two generators. Exactly as in your black boxes, the apparent mess is composed uniformity wearing a mask. In the language of your article this is precisely a Thomas-type gyration. It is the precession idea made concrete for Collatz. Concretely, the reverse of C consists of- always the even pre-image 2n,- and, when n ≡ 2 (mod 3), the additional odd pre-image (n-1)/3. Composing two different reverse words of the same length and comparing them produces a residual integer translation (or modular shift) whose size is controlled by the number of O-steps. That residual shift is the precession. When the accumulated precession angle (measured, for example, by the total exponent of 3 modulo the 2-adic valuation, or by a complex phase arg(3^k n + c)) closes, distinct forward trajectories are forced to land on the same later integer. Those landings are the intersects. [IMAGE 2] ### Interesting intersects produced by the precession1. Modular coalescence. After k odd steps the precession multiplies by 3^k. Whenever 3^k ≡ 1 (mod 2^m) for sufficiently large m, every residue class that is reachable by a word of length k collapses onto a single arithmetic progression. The classical “shortcut” maps (e.g., n ↦ (3n+1)/2^ℓ) are exactly the points where this precession has cancelled the intermediate 2-powers. The resulting nodes have in-degree greater than 2 and are the visual “crossings” that appear in Collatz coral diagrams. [IMAGE 3] 2. Phase-locked reverse branches. Represent an integer by a complex coordinate whose argument tracks the cumulative precession: z(n) = n · exp(i θ Σ_{odd steps} 1). Two different reverse paths meet when their arguments differ by a multiple of 2π and their magnitudes satisfy the same linear relation produced by the shared word in {H, O}. The condition is identical in form to the equant condition in your Ptolemaic generator: a hidden linear parameter (the rapidity-like count of odd steps) linearizes the apparent irregularity and forces an intersection. [IMAGE 4] 3. Gyro-Ptolemy relation on Collatz “cycles”. On any four integers that lie on a common reverse orbit segment of equal precession length one obtains the discrete analogue of your hyperbolic Ptolemy identity: |A ⊖ B|_C · |C ⊖ D|_C + |A ⊖ D|_C · |B ⊖ C|_C = |A ⊖ C|_C · |B ⊖ D|_C, where |X ⊖ Y|_C is the Collatz gyrolength (the number of steps, weighted by the precession factor 3^{#O}). items.title: Polyols and Sugars as a Molecular Platform for Prebiotic Evolution: From Mineral Selection to RNA and Cellular Life
items.abstract: The emergence of life required the progressive integration of organic synthesis, molecular selection, chemical activation, compartmentalization, and information storage. Although prebiotic research has extensively investigated amino acids, nucleobases, lipids, and RNA, the potential role of polyols and sugars as molecular connectors among these chemical systems remains comparatively underexplored. This review examines the hypothesis that polyhydroxylated compounds provided a versatile molecular platform during prebiotic evolution. Their multiple hydroxyl groups, stereochemical diversity, hydration properties, reversible complexation, and capacity for covalent modification enabled interactions with minerals, borate, phosphate, activated organic intermediates, and hydrophobic molecules. Particular attention is given to the complementary functions of boron- and sulfur-containing systems. Borate can selectively complex and stabilize appropriately configured polyols and sugars, whereas sulfur chemistry can facilitate redox transformations, molecular activation, and the formation of reactive intermediates. The proposed coupling of these processes may have promoted the persistence and transformation of selected organic molecules, although a continuous boron–sulfur-mediated prebiotic pathway has not been experimentally demonstrated. Polyol-derived amphiphiles, particularly glycerol derivatives, provide a possible connection between carbohydrate chemistry and primitive membrane formation, while ribose and related intermediates connect polyhydroxylated molecular chemistry with nucleotide synthesis and RNA evolution. Within this framework, chemical selection and supramolecular organization preceded, and subsequently overlapped with, sequence-based genetic evolution. The proposed model does not assume that polyols were the exclusive precursors of biological systems or that evolutionary transitions followed a single linear pathway. Instead, it identifies polyhydroxylated compounds as potentially important components of interconnected reaction networks linking geochemistry with emerging biological organization. Experimental approaches capable of testing mineral selectivity, reaction-network connectivity, amphiphile formation, and compatibility with nucleotide chemistry are discussed. This perspective provides a testable framework for investigating how chemically diverse abiotic systems may have developed toward increasingly integrated protocellular and genetic organization.

items.title: Patient perception of robotic-assisted spine surgery.
items.abstract: Patient behaviors related to pursuing robotic-assisted spine surgery remain poorly characterized. This study evaluated patients' perceptions of robotic-assisted spine surgery and behaviors related to seeking robotic-assisted care. We surveyed 116 adult spine patients at initial consultation (n = 101) or postoperative follow-up after confirmed robotic-assisted surgery (n = 15). Questions assessed perceived attributes of robotic-assisted versus traditional surgery, comfort, surgical preference, willingness to recommend robotic spine surgery, perceived robotic involvement, and whether patients had actively sought surgeons using robotics. Analyses included descriptive statistics, 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and exploratory subgroup comparisons. Patients perceived robotic-assisted surgery as more accurate (65%) and less invasive (63%), with smaller incisions (74%) and shorter surgery (53%) and recovery times (46%). Robotic and traditional surgery were most commonly perceived as comparable in pain (56%) and radiation exposure (51%). 69% believed a robot could perform most or all of the surgery; 60% would recommend robotic spine surgery, and 56% were somewhat or very comfortable with robotics. For otherwise identical surgeries, 73% (85/116, 95% CI 64.6-80.5%) reported no preference, 16% preferred robotic assistance, and 11% preferred surgery without robotics. Of 94 yes/no respondents, 6 (6.4%, 95% CI 3.0-13.2%) reported actively seeking a surgeon using robotics. The other 22 selected "Not Applicable." Although perceptions were generally favorable, most patients had no preference regarding robotic assistance, and few reported actively seeking surgeons using robotics. Robotic availability was not a prominent stated selection factor in this small, single-center sample.

items.title: Preparation-need concordance and patient readiness in robot-assisted surgery: a scoping review.
items.abstract: Patients preparing for robot-assisted surgery need information about the technology, the planned procedure, and recovery. This review mapped whether preparation addresses expressed needs and how patient readiness has been evaluated. This scoping review followed JBI guidance and PRISMA-ScR. Six databases were searched from inception to September 10, 2026, supplemented by Google Scholar and citation searching. Primary reports were mapped by preparation-need concordance, TIDieR-informed intervention reporting, and informational, psychological, decisional, and recovery outcomes. Design-specific JBI tools supported appraisal. Twenty reports mapped patient and caregiver needs, preparation approaches, and readiness outcomes across robotic surgical specialties. Selected visual, educational, and psychological approaches showed favourable immediate understanding ratings, care experiences, or emotional responses, while comparative and longer-term evidence remained limited. One report linked elicited needs to intervention development; most preparation-need alignment was inferred across studies rather than demonstrated within recipients. Incomplete intervention descriptions limited reproducibility, and decisional readiness and sustained understanding were rarely assessed. The evidence map distinguished common questions about robotic assistance from procedure-specific emotional and recovery requirements, informing practical options for multidisciplinary preparation. The evidence identifies tools for procedure-specific explanation, emotional support, and recovery preparation, but does not establish a most effective approach across robotic procedures. Counseling can distinguish surgeon-robot roles from operation-specific risks and recovery needs. Nurses can use these distinctions to coordinate preparation around patients' questions and recovery priorities. The exploratory preparation-to-readiness framework requires prospective evaluation.

items.title: Design of Co–Cr substituted BaM/PANI composites for enhanced microwave absorption
items.abstract: This study details the design and optimization of Co 2+ /Cr 3+ substituted (BaFe 12 O 19 /polyaniline BaM/PANI) composites, BaCo x Cr x Fe 12-2x O 19 /PANI (ZP1 for x = 0.0, ZP2 for x = 0.6, and ZP3 for x = 0.8), for superior microwave absorption performance. The M-type hexagonal structure was confirmed by XRD, showing slight unit cell contraction with doping. Magnetic analysis revealed that increasing Co–Cr substitution efficiently tunes the magnetic properties, leading to a significant decrease in saturation magnetization (M s ) from 45.92 emu/g (x = 0.0) to 22.55 emu/g (x = 0.8) and a notable reduction in coercivity (H c ). The tailored substitution level successfully balanced the dielectric and magnetic loss mechanisms, achieving optimal impedance matching for microwave absorption. Notably, the BaCo 0.8 Cr 0.8 Fe 10.4 O 19 /PANI composite (ZP3) exhibited the highest performance, achieving a minimum reflection loss (RL) of -41.01 dB at 11.31 GHz with a thin absorber thickness. These results demonstrate that Co–Cr substitution provides an effective strategy for creating high-performance, lightweight electromagnetic wave absorbers.

items.title: INVESTIGATING THE EXCITATION MECHANISM OF H30α RRL IN HIGH-MASS PROTOSTELLAR OBJECT IRAS 16445-4459
items.abstract: We present a study of the high-mass protostellar object IRAS~16445$-$4459 using high-resolution ALMA Band~6 ($\lambda \sim 1.3$~mm) QUARKS survey observations of the H30$\alpha$ Radio Recombination Line (RRL) and MeerKAT 1.3~GHz continuum to investigate the excitation mechanism of the H30$\alpha$ emission. Our analysis reveals a single, compact dust continuum core coincident with both the MeerKAT free--free continuum peak and the WISE infrared position. The derived core mass is $47.17\pm20.48$~M$_{\odot}$ at 100~K and $23.58\pm10.24$~M$_{\odot}$ at 200~K, with hydrogen column densities of $(13.9\pm5.35)\times10^{24}$~cm$^{-2}$ and $(6.94\pm2.68)\times10^{24}$~cm$^{-2}$, respectively. The MeerKAT continuum yields an ionizing photon rate of $S^{*} = (2.10\pm0.10)\times10^{48}$~s$^{-1}$ ($\log S^{*} = 48.32 \pm 0.002$), consistent with an O8 zero-age main-sequence (ZAMS) star or small stellar cluster typical of compact H\,\textsc{ii} regions. The H30$\alpha$ RRL is well described by a single Gaussian profile ($v_0 = -127.15\pm0.26$~km~s$^{-1}$, $\sigma = 10.47\pm0.42$~km~s$^{-1}$, $\mathrm{FWHM} = 24.65\pm0.98$~km~s$^{-1}$), while position--velocity slices reveal compact ($\lesssim 0.4''$) ionized gas with no high-velocity jet wings, supporting a compact, rotating or dynamically confined H\,\textsc{ii} region.

items.title: High-Resolution 3D Micro-CT Database of Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) Coils for More Accurate Modelling, Technology Benchmarking, and Progress in Coil Design
items.abstract: Accurate modelling of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) coils requires coil-specific geometric and electrical parameters. Yet detailed manufacturer models are rarely available, and internals may be widely available to companies in the field but not to researchers. The development of new coils should ideally build on all existing prior art. This work presents a technology benchmark and modelling-ready dataset for seventeen widely used commercial TMS coils across multiple manufacturers and geometries. High-resolution micro-CT (0.0495 mm resolution, material and density contrast) serves to reconstruct winding and casing structures and to extract parameters directly usable in numerical models, including loop dimensions, conductor cross-section, turn count, winding height, and winding-to-surface (casing) thickness. Complementary electrical measurements provide spectral impedance (series resistance and inductance) scans from 20 Hz to 200 kHz, together with dc resistance. In addition to baseline geometry and impedance, the study documents practical construction features relevant to safety and usability with detailed insights into their internal construction (e.g., cooling architectures and embedded sensing). The resulting benchmark dataset supports coil-specific electric-field simulations, reduces modelling uncertainty associated with generic assumptions (e.g., fixed coil-scalp spacing), and provides a quantitative reference for designing and evaluating new coil technologies against established commercial solutions. As a simulation-readiness example, we generated a calibrated CT-derived MCB70 line-current model for SimNIBS and evaluated its effect on predicted electric-field metrics. Compared with the SimNIBS MCB70 model, the CT-derived model produced measurable differences under identical placement conditions. We provide the dataset online.

items.title: Topological Neural Collapse
items.abstract: Neural collapse (NC) predicts that, late in training, last-layer class features concentrate at their means and the means form a simplex equiangular tight frame (ETF). We ask whether NC also leaves a signature in the functional connectome of each layer: the graph of Pearson correlations between hidden-unit activations, built per class and summarized by persistent graph homology. Using deep MLPs, we observe two topological phenomena that co-occur with the well-studied geometric NC in the final layers during the terminal phase. Contrary to NC1, the split-half variability of a class connectome increases (TNC1). The mean pairwise $H_0$ distance $\bar{D}$ between class connectomes also rises (TNC2), but unevenly across class pairs, unlike the equidistance of NC2. We find that 24-56% of last-layer units become dead for some classes yet stay active for others, which inflates $\bar{D}$. After correcting for these units, both signatures remain elevated. These results from MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 provide preliminary evidence that a topological mechanism may accompany the geometric signatures of NC.

items.title: History-bearing thalamocortical signals reconstruct and redirect later decisions in a circuit model
items.abstract: Experience can guide an ambiguous choice or bias a choice despite strong current evidence. We asked how a thalamocortical circuit carries historical content forward and regulates its influence across successive decisions. In published data from adult male mice, suppressing posterior parietal cortex (PPC) or pulvinar (PUL) improved current judgments most when sensory history conflicted with the stimulus, reflecting reduced historical weighting. In trained thalamocortical circuit models, replaying recorded PUL input to PPC reconstructed a historical trace after equalizing complete recipient states across histories. Replaying the opposite history redirected the later choice, even after the circuit correctly judged an intervening strong stimulus. This historical message occupied a low-dimensional direction in thalamic output that remained broadly reachable under firing-rate bounds; redistributing the arriving current at matched energy showed that fine spatial organization, beyond total input strength, selectively shapes later history use without disrupting current choices. Strong sensory evidence suppressed historical output while preserving internal state differences, whereas ambiguity recruited neuronal rectification thresholds and readout alignment to express history. Small shifts in the cortical operating point modulated later historical influence, and partial attenuation of recurrent drive reduced it across all circuits while preserving current commitments; correspondingly, recurrent dynamics were essential for predicting post-stimulus trajectories in held-out histories. Together, these findings distinguish three operations in history-guided choice: returning thalamocortical input determines which past is reconstructed, recurrent dynamics carry its influence forward across intervening demands, and current sensory evidence gates how strongly it enters the decision.

items.title: From local competition to bump attractors:how excitation width sets capacity, interference and updating in recurrent models of visual working memory
items.abstract: On-centre off-surround (OCOS) networks and bump attractors, the two main recurrent models of visual working memory, differ chiefly in how far recurrent excitation spreads. We place them in one family parameterised by excitation width at fixed total excitation, and ask how stable each stored item is and what it costs the circuit to hold and change it. The answer is that excitation width sets the price of continuity. In the OCOS limit, which we solve exactly by completing the energy-function formalism of \citet{Sengupta2024}, an item occupies a single unit, relaxes quickly and never drifts, and capacity follows in closed form, exact over all stable states. As excitation widens towards a bump-like regime, items become continuous but costly: per item, the circuit uses 15--29 units instead of one and 6.5--11 times the activity, relaxes 35--60 times more slowly after a perturbation, needs a 35--230 times stronger cue to accept a second item, and holds 7--10 items instead of at least 40. Under noise, with background false alarms approximately matched, about a third of wide items drift, whereas narrow items never move. Yet even as an item's translation mode softens towards zero, items remain locked to the lattice. Locking is poorly predicted by energy differences between item positions, but strongly predicted by how far the unit just beyond an item's edge sits below threshold (rank correlation 0.91 across 40 parameter settings). Where that margin vanishes, a new input captures the stored item instead of being added to memory.

items.title: A generative framework for unified representations bridging electrophysiological and haemodynamic brain activity
items.abstract: Electrophysiological and haemodynamic recordings resolve brain activity at complementary temporal and spatial scales, yet paired acquisition remains difficult to scale. We propose a generative framework that aligns paired multimodal recordings in a unified representation space and generates modality-specific haemodynamic responses from EEG. In paired cohorts, the framework generated fMRI BOLD and fNIRS haemoglobin responses that reproduced regional dynamics, cortical maps, functional connectivity and task structure. Generated BOLD followed Real BOLD time courses and cortical patterns, while Generated haemoglobin responses tracked task-evoked HbO and HbR dynamics. The framework enabled decoding across visual, motor-imagery and mental-arithmetic tasks, independent-record decoding, external BOLD localization and low-sample augmentation. Paired feature-space calibration supported bidirectional retrieval. The proposed framework extends cortical analysis and brain decoding to EEG recordings when Real haemodynamic data are sparse.

items.title: Validating Gaia DR3 Astrometric Accelerations with Close Visual Binaries
items.abstract: We validate a subset of the astrometric accelerations reported in Gaia DR3 non-single-star solutions by their consistency with the gravitational pull of known, resolved companions. Cross-matching 338,215 DR3 acceleration solutions against the Washington Double Star (WDS) catalog of visual binaries yields 2,466 unique pairs within 2". For each pair we compare the measured acceleration with alpha_max, the Newtonian bound on the acceleration the companion can impart on the Gaia-tracked photocenter. For 98.1% of the pairs the measured acceleration exceeds this bound by more than a factor of 10, so the cataloged companion cannot be responsible and the perturber must be a closer, unresolved one. The remaining 45 plausible wide binaries are close pairs at the WDS resolution limit. We fit orbits with an updated orvara, extended to accept the DR3 acceleration and jerk coefficients as direct constraints and released with htof as part of this work. The fits converge for 16 of the 45 and one boundary case, the rest having too few resolved measures or a perturber other than the cataloged pair, and 13 of the 17 carry enough data to test the coefficients. Eleven of the 13 statistically accommodate the reported accelerations, for seven- and nine-parameter solutions alike, and the dynamical companion masses agree with the photometric estimates where the photocenter conversion is well determined. Independently of the fits, 33 of the 43 plausible systems with a usable position angle (77%) have the acceleration directed within 45 degrees of the primary-companion axis, against 50% for a control sample: DR3's measured accelerations point in the directions of the cataloged companions.

items.title: DIPS-OjOS I: Project Design and Science Validation
items.abstract: Automated pipelines and machine-learning algorithms are efficient at detecting standard planetary transits, but can miss subtle, non-periodic morphological anomalies. We present the pilot phase of DIPS-OjOS (Detecting Irregular Photometric Signals - OjímetrO Survey), a professional-amateur collaboration designed to develop and validate a scalable workflow for identifying irregular photometric signals in exoplanet transit light curves through trained visual inspection. The project targets starspot-crossing events, stellar flares, circumplanetary structures, exomoon-like signatures, and transit-duration or timing anomalies overlooked by automated searches. We built the infrastructure required for a controlled visual-inspection experiment: simulated control light curves, preparation and detrending of real short-cadence Kepler data, a transit-modeling pipeline that computes an optimized average transit profile for each light curve, and a web-based classification platform. The real sample was deliberately restricted to 51 well-characterized Kepler systems. Collaborators inspected 917 transit events: 555 real transits and 362 simulated controls. The simulated sample quantified observer performance and calibrated a weighted consensus scheme; collaborators recovered injected signals with an average efficiency of 87.6%, while the null-case false-positive rate was 15.3%. After expert validation, we retained 88 viable candidate anomalies from the real sample, including 26 starspot-crossing event candidates across eight targets, seven stellar flares, 31 systematic transit-duration deviations motivating refined orbital parameters in four systems, and a mutual transit event in Kepler-89. Recovering candidate signals in this well-studied sample validates the sensitivity of DIPS-OjOS and establishes the basis for future applications to Kepler, TESS, PLATO, and ground-based datasets.

items.title: Reassessment of Planetary Parameters and Statistical Validation of 187 Kepler Habitable-Zone and Near Habitable Confirmed and Candidate Planets
items.abstract: Confirmed and candidate planets in the Habitable or near-Habitable Zones (HZ) orbiting Sun-like stars are crucial not only for the search for life beyond the Solar System, but also for understanding the architecture and formation of other solar systems and for conducting demographic studies. Current analyses of such planetary systems are limited both by the small sample size revealed by Kepler as well as by uncertainties in system parameters. Although a larger sample of HZ and near-HZ planets must await new observations from wide-field, space-based surveys, follow-up analyses and observations with existing facilities can improve the precision on stellar and planetary parameters, enable more accurate planetary classification, and a more reliable assessment of whether candidate systems are true planets or merely astrophysical false positives. Here, we present a homogeneous transit light curve analysis of 187 HZ and near-HZ systems discovered by Kepler. Our analysis incorporates the latest Gaia DR3-derived stellar parameters, and we also present a statistical validation effort for all targets. The result is a uniform set of planetary radii, instellation fluxes, and orbital ephemerides suitable for prioritizing and scheduling follow-up observations to improve our understanding of planets in this regime. We show that longer-period (>300days) systems would particularly benefit from transit follow-up: just a single transit from facilities such as the 6m James Webb or the planned 3m Lazuli space telescopes could provide ~2 times tighter precision on planet radii than four years of Kepler photometry, thereby dramatically shrinking relevant parameter uncertainties and allowing more confident planet/false-positive assessments.

items.title: Large Deviations and Critical Scaling in the Finite-Population Granovetter Threshold Model
items.abstract: We develop a systematic asymptotic analysis of the exact finite-population solution of Granovetter's threshold model, in which a single initial instigator triggers a cascade among agents with independently distributed adoption thresholds. By expressing the propagation probability as an order-statistic boundary-crossing event, we formulate its macroscopic large-deviation rate as a constrained relative-entropy minimization problem. For Beta-distributed thresholds, we obtain explicit solutions for all shape parameters $α$ and $β$, identifying four possible optimal empirical threshold profiles: fully free, fully pinned, pinned--free, and free--pinned. These profiles determine both the exponential probability of macroscopic cascades and the threshold configurations responsible for their occurrence. Importance-sampling estimates confirm the analytical rate functions, while sequential Monte Carlo simulations independently reproduce the predicted optimal profiles. We also revisit the critical scaling near $α_c=1$ and confirm the principal finite-size scaling laws: the mean active fraction decays as $N^{-1/2}$ for uniform thresholds and as $N^{-1}$ for $α=1$ and $0<β<1$. In the latter regime, we further derive an explicit scaling function for the logarithmic critical window from the microscopic branching-process limit. Our results provide a general framework for determining the probabilities and characteristic configurations of rare collective events in threshold-driven cascade processes

items.title: Neural-Network Approximators for Low-Thrust Multi-Asteroid Rendezvous Optimization
items.abstract: Designing low-thrust multi-asteroid rendezvous missions requires the coupled selection of asteroid sequences, encounter epochs, and low-thrust trajectories. Lambert transfers support rapid beam search but do not directly describe thrust-limited transfer capacity or propellant consumption. This paper develops two complementary low-thrust neural approximators. The first directly predicts the continuous maximum admissible initial mass from numerically optimized low-thrust transfers, providing a transfer-capacity estimate for comparison with the current spacecraft mass. The second predicts mass-dependent propellant consumption and propagates spacecraft mass to subsequent legs. With the carefully-designed input features and network structure, the approximators reduce mean absolute errors by 72.2% and 75.5%, respectively, relative to conventional deep neural network baselines. These predictions are incorporated into a Lambert-ranked beam search through resource filtering and recursive mass propagation before final beam selection. The method is evaluated on fixed-visit, maximum-visit, and deployment-collection missions. Across the tested cases, the proposed resource filtering increases the fraction of candidate sequences that yield accepted low-thrust solutions, raises the maximum validated asteroid-visit count by up to 15.4%, and improves the best mission objective by up to 17.8%. These results demonstrate that continuous transfer-capacity and propellant predictions can improve finite-width sequence search.

items.title: Time-variable tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems
items.abstract: Most stars in the field are part of binary, triple, or higher-order systems, which we primarily observe in hierarchical configurations that allow long-term stability. Over long timescales, hierarchical triple systems interact primarily through gravitational dynamics, but more complex interactions arise when stellar evolution drives mass transfer. In this paper, we study tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems using three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations. We find that the finite separation of the inner binary produces oscillations in the Roche potential that critically alter both the donor star's variability and its mean mass-loss rate. For compact inner binaries, the mass-loss rate approaches that of a single accretor, while at larger separations the orbit-averaged mass-loss rate increases steeply, approximately as $\langle \dot{M}_d\rangle \propto \langle \dot{M}_{d,0}\rangle (1+C a_b^{6.1 \pm 0.9})$. For the $γ= 5/3$ polytropic donor considered here, this scaling is consistent with the nonlinear response of Roche-lobe overflow to the leading quadrupolar perturbation of the inner-binary potential, which scales as $δΦ_2 \propto a_b^2$. We also examine the donor's response to periodic forcing from the inner binary and find a transition between individual and collaborative accretion that determines whether the transferred material can form and sustain a circumbinary disk. Our results show that the finite separation of the inner binary can strongly regulate both the rate and fate of tertiary mass transfer, constraining a poorly understood phase of hierarchical triple evolution.

items.title: Constraining Planet Nine with Pulsar Timing: Orbit Determination Method from the Acceleration, Jerk, and Snap of the Solar System Barycenter
items.abstract: Planet Nine is hypothesized to exist in the outer solar system in order to explain the physical orbital clustering of several trans-Neptunian objects. A Planet Nine would systematically change the location of the solar system barycenter (SSB). Therefore, the precise timing properties of millisecond radio pulsars would measure the acceleration, jerk, and snap of the currently-perceived SSB under the gravitational influence of a Planet Nine. We present a method on how to use pulsar spin frequency derivatives and binary pulsar orbital period derivatives to constrain the Planet Nine parameter space. We find that searches for unidentified massive objects in the solar system require at least cubic and quartic variations in the pulse times of arrival (corresponding to jerk and snap, respectively) in order to uniquely constrain an orbit. Otherwise, additional assumptions are required to fully constrain the mass and orbital parameters of the object. We use our method to weigh the ice giants Uranus and Neptune and obtain results consistent with the literature. This method could be used to weigh a Planet Nine after a putative optical detection. Future work will use updated pulsar timing datasets that benefit from longer observational baselines and advances in statistical modeling and noise characterization.

items.title: Cortical spreading depression on Riemannian 2-manifolds: eikonal-curvature analysis and sulcal trapping.
items.abstract: Cortical spreading depression (CSD) is a slowly propagating wave of near-complete neuronal depolarization underlying migraine aura and implicated in stroke, traumatic brain injury, and subarachnoid hemorrhage. Existing reaction-diffusion models of CSD treat the cortex as a flat Euclidean domain, ignoring its highly folded, individually variable geometry. We develop a fully covariant FitzHugh-Nagumo (FHN) reaction-diffusion system on a smooth compact Riemannian 2-manifold [Formula: see text] representing the cortical sheet, in which the Euclidean Laplacian is replaced by the Laplace-Beltrami operator [Formula: see text]. Three mathematical results are established: (i) local and global well-posedness in [Formula: see text] together with positive invariance of the physiological region via parabolic semigroup theory; (ii) a curvature-corrected eikonal relation [Formula: see text], in which the wavefront speed is modulated by the geodesic curvature of the front; and (iii) a sulcal-trapping theorem giving an explicit criterion under which an excitable wave entering a sulcus (negative Gauss curvature region) remains confined to it. Numerically, we develop two complementary solvers: a discrete exterior calculus (DEC) scheme on triangulated surfaces using the cotangent Laplacian with implicit-explicit (IMEX) time-stepping, and a physics-informed neural network (PINN) surrogate that evaluates [Formula: see text] via the closest-point projection of the ambient Euclidean Laplacian. The PINN framework supports both forward simulation and the inverse identification of excitability fields from sparse observations, and a noise-ablation study quantifies its practical identifiability. The parameters of the slow subsystem and of the coupling functions are inherited from our published, cohort-calibrated thalamocortical model, which was calibrated against 67 paired-pulse somatosensory evoked potential (SEP) recordings from nine analysable animals of a cohort of 14 male Wistar rats (1, 233 sweeps) acquired in the Neuroscience Laboratory of Gazi University, with CSD induced by topical KCl application. We validate convergence on [Formula: see text] with the spectral ground-truth [Formula: see text], exhibit a propagating ring wave with a refractory tail, and verify the eikonal-curvature prediction across two orders of magnitude in geodesic curvature, including the leading correction due to the recovery variable; a mesh-convergence study yields explicit resolution requirements for evaluating the trapping criterion on MRI-derived cortical surfaces.

items.title: Bidirectional Relations Between Spirituality and Adolescent Depression and Anxiety: The Moderating Role of Religious Involvement.
items.abstract: Typically, spirituality is viewed as a protective factor against mental health challenges. But it is possible that inversely mental health challenges are a risk factor for hindered spirituality. This study examined longitudinal bidirectional relations between spirituality and adolescent depression and anxiety, and the moderating role of religious involvement. Participants included 1862 adolescents from the western US (Time 2 Mage = 16; 53% female; 77% European American). Adolescents completed self-report measures of spirituality, depression, anxiety, and religious involvement across three waves, 2 years apart. Bidirectional relations between adolescent spirituality and mental health were examined using Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Models (RI-CLPM). Analyses revealed that at the within-person level, spirituality did not significantly predict later depression, but depression did negatively predict later spirituality. Additionally, spirituality negatively predicted subsequent anxiety, and anxiety negatively predicted later spirituality. The model was also tested across two groups based on the level of religious involvement, comparing those who attended religious worship services less than weekly to those who attended at least weekly. Bidirectional within-person associations between spirituality and mental health were found for frequent attenders but not infrequent attenders (for both depression and anxiety). These findings suggest potential bidirectional dynamics between adolescent spirituality and mental health, especially for religiously engaged youth.

items.title: Dual-DUBTACs Enable Targeted Protein Stabilization via Multi-DUB Engagement.
items.abstract: Targeted protein stabilization has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy for restoring the abundance and function of disease-relevant proteins. Deubiquitinase-targeting chimeras (DUBTACs) offer a chemical approach to protein stabilization by recruiting deubiquitinases (DUBs) to promote target deubiquitination. However, current DUBTAC strategies generally rely on the recruitment of a single DUB, leaving the potential of engaging multiple DUBs through a common recruiter largely unexplored. Here, we report a dual-DUBTAC strategy that enables targeted protein stabilization through the recruitment of two distinct DUBs. Using Degrasyn, a small-molecule reversible covalent inhibitor of multiple DUBs, as a privileged scaffold, we engineered small molecules that selectively stabilize CFTR and cGAS and demonstrate that these compounds enhance target protein homeostasis through USP9X- and USP5-mediated deubiquitination in cells. By decoupling substrate stabilization from reliance on a single DUB, the Dual-DUB platform confers adaptability across diverse ubiquitin chain architectures and rewired proteostasis networks characteristic of heterogeneous tumors and could overcome potential drug resistance in future clinical applications. This strategy expands the chemical space for restoring protective proteins and establishes a general framework for functional reactivation of destabilized tumor-suppressive pathways.

items.title: The relationship between socio-environmental factors, brain growth and cognition in middle childhood.
items.abstract: The relationship between socio-environmental factors, brain growth, and cognition in childhood is unknown. This study aimed to characterize associations between (i) regional brain growth from birth to 6-8 years and socio-environmental factors; and (ii) regional brain growth and cognitive outcomes in middle childhood. One hundred and thirty-seven 6-8-year-old children (25 with congenital heart disease) underwent neonatal and paediatric brain MRI and a full-scale IQ assessment. Data on household income, maternal education, neighborhood deprivation, and early cognitively stimulating home environment were collected. Regional brain growth (extracerebral CSF, ventricles, cortical grey matter, white matter, deep grey matter, cerebellum, brainstem) from the neonatal period to 6-8 years was assessed using Gaussian process regression. Low household income was associated with reduced cortical grey matter growth (B, 95% CI -1.14, -1.88 to -0.396; pFWE = 0.044) and extracerebral CSF expansion (-1.55, -2.51 to -0.585; pFWE = 0.042). Higher cortical grey matter (3.89, 1.12-6.65; pFWE = 0.038) and brainstem (3.24, 0.894-5.58; pFWE = 0.038) growth were associated with better full-scale IQ. Brainstem (p = 0.014), but not cortical grey matter (p = 0.177), remained significant after adjustment for socio-environmental factors. Support for financially vulnerable families may promote brain growth. Brainstem growth is a brain correlate of childhood cognition independent of the effects of socio-environmental factors. One hundred and thirty-seven children (25 with congenital heart disease) underwent neuroimaging at birth and at 6-8 years and a full-scale IQ assessment at 6-8 years. Household income, maternal education, neighborhood deprivation and early home environment data were collected. After adjustment for other socio-environmental factors and group, low household income was associated with reduced cortical grey matter growth and extracerebral CSF expansion. Higher cortical grey matter and brainstem growth were associated with higher full-scale IQ in middle childhood. Household poverty was linked to reduced brain growth, while cortical grey matter and brainstem growth were associated with cognitive abilities in childhood.

items.title: Motor pre-selection modulates action observation effects in sensorimotor cortices: a MEG study.
items.abstract: According to the Motor Simulation theory, observing an action automatically activates matching motor representations. This can explain why, in automatic imitation tasks, responses are faster when the observed action matches the required one, compared to when it differs. However, the automatic imitation task setting represents a very peculiar situation where participants need to pre-select the motor representations corresponding to the actions that they might observe, a situation quite different from daily-life contexts such as sports (e.g., tennis or basketball) where actions pre-selected for output are typically different from those observed, and where imitation errors or tendencies are seldom observed. This leads to the following question: Does the motor cortex response to observed actions depend on whether they match the motor representations pre-selected for output? In the present magnetoencephalography experiment, we studied, within the hand-related primary sensorimotor cortex, the oscillatory dynamics produced by the observation of hand actions in two conditions: either while participants pre-selected motor representations similar to those observed, or while they pre-selected markedly different motor representations, such as those involved in feet actions. Our data show that the motor cortex reacts differently to action observation in the two pre-selection conditions: alpha- and beta-band activity showed stronger desynchronization when the pre-selection involved motor representations matching those observed compared to non-matching ones. Specifically, observing hand actions while pre-selecting non-matching feet movements elicited a late rebound-like increase in alpha- and beta-band activity that was not observed when hand actions were pre-selected.

items.title: LOCALIZED shoulder fatigue alters early movement scaling during learning of Upper-Limb orientation.
items.abstract: Neuromuscular fatigue alters force-generating capacity and sensorimotor information, yet its consequences for motor learning remain unclear. We examined whether practicing goal-directed shoulder abduction under localized muscle fatigue altered angular endpoint accuracy and early movement velocity at acquisition and delayed retention. Forty healthy adults were randomly assigned to the Fatigue or Control group (n = 20 each). Objective performance fatigability and perceived fatigue were monitored. Retention was assessed one week later, first without fatigue and then under re-induced shoulder fatigue. Angular errors were quantified after an initial ballistic phase and after proprioceptive repositioning. Angular velocity 100 ms after movement onset reflected early, predominantly feedforward, movement production. Both groups reduced absolute and constant angular errors during acquisition. However, early angular velocity increased less during fatigued practice, and lower values in the Fatigue group persisted during non-fatigued retention at all target angles. Final absolute angular error was also higher in the Fatigue group during non-fatigued retention. Between-group differences were not detected during fatigued retention. These findings identify a retained change in how the shoulder movement was produced, within the limits of a simple single-joint angular movement and the fixed retention order.

items.title: Functional transcriptomic profile of mouse controlled cortical impact model of post-traumatic epilepsy with robust spontaneous recurrent seizures.
items.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a major cause of acquired epilepsy, yet the molecular changes linking the initial injury to post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE) remain incompletely understood. Here, we used a severe controlled cortical impact mouse model that develops robust spontaneous recurrent seizures to characterize the temporal and regional progression of post-traumatic transcriptional responses. Bulk RNA sequencing was performed on the contralateral cortex and hippocampus collected from TBI and time-matched sham mice at 7, 21, and 60 days after injury, corresponding to the acute injury, latent period, and chronic epilepsy phases, respectively. Transcriptomic changes were characterized using differentially expressed gene (DEG) analysis, Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes gene-set enrichment analyses, and Ingenuity Pathway Analysis. Transcriptomic responses were strongly dependent on brain region and disease phase. At 7 days, the cortex showed enhanced neuronal and structural signaling alongside suppression of immune, metabolic, and cell-cycle processes, whereas the hippocampus showed prominent neuroimmune activation and metabolic stress. By 21 days, before the emergence of spontaneous seizures, the hippocampus shifted toward partial normalization of metabolic pathway enrichment, accompanied by suppression of neurotransmission, synaptic plasticity, and neuronal organization. In contrast, the cortex showed increased enrichment of immune and tissue-remodeling processes. Although relatively few DEGs were detected at 60 days, a selective hippocampal signature persisted after PTE was established. Pathway analyses converged on coordinated changes in neuroimmune, metabolic, lipid-regulatory, and synaptic processes. Upstream Regulator Analysis further identified a temporal reversal in APOE-associated regulatory activity, linking inflammatory and lipid-metabolic responses with later synaptic remodeling. The 21-day post-injury hippocampus represents a critical disease-modification window. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that PTE progression involves phase-specific molecular remodeling that shifts from an early cortical response to sustained hippocampal dysregulation. The latent hippocampal signature identifies a potentially actionable molecular window before recurrent seizure onset.

items.title: Intrasegmental and propriospinal phrenic circuit interneurons in intact CNS and following cervical spinal cord injury.
items.abstract: Cervical spinal cord injury disrupts descending respiratory circuitry, resulting in debilitating and often persistent ventilatory deficits. Respiratory drive emerges within medulla from the rostral ventral respiratory group, whose neurons project to C3-C6 phrenic motor neurons (PhMNs), which then innervate diaphragm, the primary muscle of inspiration. Though rostral ventral respiratory group neurons make extensive monosynaptic connection with PhMNs, this input can also be relayed through phrenic circuit interneurons (PC-INs) via polysynaptic pathways. However, the neuroanatomical connectivity between PC-INs and PhMNs remains incompletely understood. In both uninjured rats and the C2 hemisection model of cervical spinal cord injury, we performed tracing of interneurons that were part of the circuitry connected to PhMNs located in rostral (C3-C4) or caudal (C5-C6) portions of the phrenic nucleus by unilaterally injecting retrograde trans-synaptic tracer, pseudorabies virus, selectively into ventral or dorsal regions of hemidiaphragm. We quantified numbers of pseudorabies virus-labeled PC-INs individually at segments across cervical spinal cord, including separately in dorsal horn, intermediate gray, and ventral horn. We found that PC-INs are widespread throughout C1-C7 spinal cord in the uninjured condition. These PC-INs have a predominant intrasegmental connectivity pattern, though significant numbers of longer distance projecting propriospinal PC-INs also exist both rostral and caudal to the PhMN pool. Furthermore, while PC-INs connect both ipsilaterally and contralaterally, there is a strong bias to ipsilateral projection. C2 hemisection induced major disconnection between PhMNs and ipsilesional propriospinal PC-INs located rostral to the SCI, but induced more limited plasticity in connectivity of intrasegmental PC-INs located within C3-C6 spinal cord. These findings greatly improve our knowledge about PC-IN circuitry and also provide important information to aid in developing approaches to target PC-IN plasticity for promoting spinal cord repair.

items.title: Transient hippocampal CA1 responses follow the end of a treadmill delay during rat navigation.
items.abstract: The hippocampus is thought to organize experience in time, but how CA1 activity is structured around transitions between successive phases of behavior remains unclear. We recorded dorsal CA1 neurons in five rats navigating a route that included two motor-driven treadmills, with the treadmill delay changed blockwise. About half of the pyramidal neurons (45 of 89, in four of five animals) showed temporally modulated firing that improved cross-validated prediction of spiking beyond measured position and head movement. Most of these neurons (36 of 45) fired transiently at treadmill onset, after treadmill offset, or both, and their transition-related firing profiles were neuron-specific and recurred across task stages. When the delay was doubled, post-offset responses shifted with treadmill offset rather than remaining at a fixed time from onset; this effect was consistent within the recorded animals but was not established across animals. Post-offset responses coincided with the resumption of movement. These findings indicate that CA1 temporal modulation is not confined to activity within the delay but is also aligned to the end of the delay, when navigation resumes, and suggest that transition-related CA1 activity may help link successive phases of structured behavior.

items.title: Genetically selected alcohol-preferring rats show increased heroin self-administration and upregulated VTA Oprm1 expression.
items.abstract: Alcohol use disorder and opioid use disorder (OUD) are chronic relapsing conditions that share genetic and neurobiological substrates, particularly within mesolimbic circuits and opioid receptor signaling. Understanding their overlapping genetic vulnerabilities is crucial for developing translational models of cross-vulnerability. The Marchigian Sardinian alcohol-preferring (msP) rat line, selectively bred for high alcohol intake and preference, displays altered expression of stress- and opioid-related genes, including Oprm1, which encodes the μ-opioid receptor (MOP). However, Oprm1 expression and function in the ventral tegmental area (VTA), a key region mediating drug reinforcement, had not yet been characterized in this strain. Quantitative PCR revealed higher Oprm1 mRNA levels in the VTA of male msP rats compared to Wistars, while no difference was observed in females. Across two independent cohorts, male msP rats self-administered significantly more heroin than Wistar controls. To test causality between higher VTA Oprm1 expression and higher heroin self-administration, Oprm1 expression was downregulated in the VTA via shRNA, resulting in reduction of heroin self-administration over time with a larger effect in msP than Wistar rats. These findings indicate that elevated VTA Oprm1 expression contributes to the higher heroin self-administration observed in male msP rats. Given the lack of selectively bred lines for opioid preference, the msP strain offers a valuable genetic model for studying vulnerability to OUD and for exploring mechanisms underlying alcohol-opioid cross-vulnerability.

items.title: Social relevance reshapes memory encoding and promotes false memories across sensory modalities.
items.abstract: Memory is shaped not only by the information itself but also by its social relevance. The present study investigated whether, in the absence of misleading information, social relevance can increase false memory by altering encoding processes, and whether this effect depends on sensory modality. Using a social DRM paradigm combined with fNIRS, we manipulated item relevance (self-relevant, partner-relevant, irrelevant) and encoding modality (visual, auditory). Behavioral results showed that partner-relevant (vs. irrelevant) items elicited more false memories, indicating that social relevance can enhance false memory even in the absence of explicit misinformation. Neural findings revealed that socially relevant encoding elicited activity within frontal, temporal, and temporoparietal regions, consistent with the notion that social relevance may be linked to spontaneous monitoring processes. Further analyses indicated that frontal and temporal activity predicted subsequent false memory, whereas temporoparietal activity reflected social orienting rather than directly predicting memory distortion. These results suggest that false memory may arise not only from external misinformation but also from encoding biases triggered by social cues. Overall, this study provides new evidence for understanding how social contexts influence false memory and suggests that social relevance may shape subsequent memory performance through attentional and encoding-related processes.

items.title: Reproducible transversal mouse brain sections using low-cost 3D printable resin matrix.
items.abstract: Rodent brain matrices that produce coronal or sagittal brain sections for histology confer reproducibility and enable high throughput processing of tissues. However, a stainless steel or acrylic brain matrix that produces tissue sections in a transversal (or horizontal) orientation is currently unavailable as a standard tool. This limits the direct comparison of bilateral brain hemispheres within a single histological section, as freehand trimming to obtain horizontal planes is not easily replicable across samples. To mitigate this challenge, we designed a low-cost (USD 7 per unit), 3D-printed resin-based transverse brain matrix that accommodates mouse brains ranging from 12 to 16 mm in length from the olfactory bulb to the brainstem. Our matrix reproducibly generates horizontal tissue sections with a minimum of 1-mm-thickness without causing visible tissue deformation, which is comparable to the performance of commercial rodent brain matrices. We validated the quality of the horizontal brain tissue slices by histology and immunohistochemistry. Users may adapt the accompanying CAD code using our video tutorials to customize the transverse brain matrix for their specific needs, including alternative brain size, shape, and tissue thickness.

items.title: Epilepsy landscape in the Democratic Republic of Congo: A narrative review.
items.abstract: Epilepsy is a major public health problem in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), disproportionately affecting a young population in a context of limited resources. In this narrative review, we synthesise available epilepsy data from the DRC published between 1990 and 2025. No nationwide, population-based study has been conducted, and existing data come from heterogeneous sources, mostly hospital-based or small regional surveys. The overall epilepsy prevalence is estimated to be between 0.7 % and 1.8 % nationally, representing approximately 700,000 to 1,900,000 people living with epilepsy in a population of 105-109 million. The predominant epilepsy risk factors for epilepsy in DRC include perinatal encephalopathies, central nervous system infections, particularly cerebral malaria, neurocysticercosis, onchocerciasis, meningitis, and traumatic brain injuries. Recent clinic-based data suggest that the average age of seizure onset is 13.1 years +/- 11.2 years, with a wide range spanning from 5 days, and male-to-female ratios ranging from 1.1 to 1.9. Convulsive seizures dominate the clinical picture in the available series. The therapeutic gap remains considerable, with an estimated 75-80 % of people with epilepsy lacking access to appropriate care, a situation exacerbated by persistent sociocultural stigma, a shortage of neurologists (10 per 109 million inhabitants), and the scarcity of diagnostic and monitoring facilities. These findings underscore the urgent need for national management strategies that integrate prevention of avoidable causes, decentralised diagnostic services, improved access to antiseizure medication, and sustained community awareness campaigns.

items.title: Axial Skeletal Divergence and Body Depth Evolution in an Adaptive Radiation of Midas Cichlid Fishes in Nicaraguan Crater Lakes.
items.abstract: Fish body depth is a common axis of phenotypic diversification. We investigated the evolutionary relationships between postcranial skeletal divergence and body depth evolution in the Nicaraguan Midas cichlid fish species complex (Amphilophus spp.). This lineage of at least 13 species has rapidly differentiated and repeatedly ecologically diverged across several crater lake habitats over the past < 20,000 years. We used X-ray images to examine the osteological axial skeleton of all named Midas species, as well as several genetically distinct Midas populations endemic to isolated crater lakes. Vertebrae numbers and 14 linear size-adjusted axial skeletal measurements were used for phylogenetically controlled correlations to evaluate whether these traits were highly associated with body depth evolution. Vertebral morphometric and meristic traits showed little correlation with body depth in these Central American cichlids. Conversely, we found strong positive phylogenetic correlations among the pectoral girdle depth, several fin-proximal pterygiophores, and the hemal and neural spines, suggesting a cohesive morphological scaffold. Unlike many teleosts, which have evolved more dorso-ventrally compressed and elongate body forms via increases in the number of vertebrae, the Midas cichlid radiation has diverged primarily in the pectoral girdle and spine architecture to produce their body depth divergence.

items.title: Localized Dipoles Enable Synergistic Kinetic and Thermodynamic Piezoreforming of Waste Plastics.
items.abstract: The piezocatalytic plastic wastes into clean fuels at ambient conditions offers considerable promise, but hindering by both rapid carrier recombination in kinetics and slow surface reactions in thermodynamics. Here, we present a conceptually distinct strategy to simultaneously tackle both core challenges by tailoring localized dipole via anchoring FeSe2 nanoclusters onto MoSe2 piezocatalysts. These clusters induce localized lattice distortions via strong metal-support interaction, generating localized dipole that serve a dual function. Kinetically, localized dipole can effectively capture the electrons excited by piezoelectricity, suppressing recombination and establishing a dominant, long-lived interfacial charge transfer channel directly to the reactants. Thermodynamically, localized dipole can lower the d-band center of the active sites, enhance the adsorption of reaction intermediates, and significantly reduce the activation energy barrier of key intermediates. Therefore, the optimized catalyst exhibits carbon monoxide (CO) evolution of 87.65 µmol·g-1 with high selectivity in the piezocatalytic peroxydisulfate (PDS) system, 30.5 times that of MoSe2. Importantly, after simple pretreatment of polylactic acid (PLA), the CO production reaches 1886.55 µmol·g-1 with stable long-term performance. This work elucidates the fundamental role of localized dipole in harmonizing charge dynamics with surface catalysis, providing an effective approach for designing highly efficient and durable piezocatalysts for challenging chemical transformations.

items.title: Concentration-dependent modulation of cadmium toxicity by molybdenum in Chlorella pyrenoidosa: Multi-endpoint evidence for an antioxidant compensation-to-overload transition.
items.abstract: Molybdenum (Mo) is an essential trace element with potential risks under elevated exposure, whereas cadmium (Cd) is a non-essential toxic metal. Although they may co-occur in mining- and industry-affected aquatic environments, multi-endpoint evidence for how Mo modulates Cd toxicity in aquatic primary producers remains limited. Using Chlorella pyrenoidosa as a freshwater microalgal model, we assessed growth, photosynthetic pigments, protein content, lipid peroxidation and antioxidant responses under single-metal exposures and Mo-Cd co-exposure with Cd fixed at 1 mg L-1. Single Mo exposure showed relatively high algal tolerance, with growth stimulation accompanied by mild stress-related regulation, whereas single Cd exposure caused clear concentration-dependent toxicity, with a 96 h IC50 of 3.298 mg L-1. Under fixed Cd stress, Mo modulated Cd toxicity in a concentration-dependent manner. Compared with Cd-only treatment, 5 mg L-1 Mo reduced 96 h growth inhibition from 10.1% to 3.0% and increased total chlorophyll and protein by 26.2% and 21.4%, respectively, indicating a mitigation-like response at 1-5 mg L-1 Mo. In contrast, 200 mg L-1 Mo increased growth inhibition to 16.5%, reduced total chlorophyll and protein by 25.3% and 45.3%, and increased malondialdehyde (MDA) by 179%. Expected-effect deviation analysis supported this biphasic pattern, with integrated toxicity-oriented deviation scores (Dtox) of -0.263 at 5 mg L-1 and 0.270-0.489 at 50-200 mg L-1. Oxidative-response patterns indicated a shift from antioxidant compensation to oxidative overload under high-Mo co-exposure. These findings identify Mo as a concentration-dependent modulator of Cd toxicity and support multi-endpoint algal biomarkers for interpreting combined-metal stress.

items.title: Responses of fungal communities in roots and soil to sulfur-induced acidification in a meadow steppe: A pH threshold for soil fungal richness.
items.abstract: Although atmospheric sulfur (S) deposition has declined substantially in China in recent decades, it remains an important contributor to soil acidification, with its contribution comparable to or greater than that of nitrogen (N) deposition in Asia; whilst substantial S inputs persist in northeastern China and Inner Mongolia. Yet how reduced soil pH would affect fungal diversity loss and the driving factors underlying diversity changes remains poorly understood. Based on a 6-year field experiment with eight S addition rates ranging from 0 to 50 g S m-2 yr-1 in a meadow steppe in Inner Mongolia, we elucidated how S addition modulates root and soil fungal communities. Our results show that the effects of S addition on fungal α-diversity were niche-specific. S15 and S20 increased root symbiotic fungal richness, possibly in association with changes in plant-fungal mutualisms, whereas soil fungal α-diversity was lowest at S50, possibly reflecting soil acidification induced by S addition. Soil fungal richness at S50 did not differ significantly from the control. Segmented regression estimated pH breakpoints of 5.88 (95% CI 4.51-6.29) for soil fungal richness and 5.62 (95% CI 4.89-6.42) for root fungal richness. The Davies test supported a change in slope in soil (P = 0.042), with limited evidence for a slope change in roots (P = 0.14). Variance partitioning analyses showed that below the soil pH threshold, the largest fraction of variation in soil fungal richness was jointly explained by soil properties, plant factors, and fungal network attributes. Overall, root and soil fungal communities responded differently to S addition, and the factors associated with fungal richness differed above and below the fitted pH breakpoints.

items.title: Age- and sex-related differences in Staphylococcus epidermidis and Corynebacterium spp. on the adult ocular surface.
items.abstract: Ocular surface bacterial flora is a potential source of bacterial keratitis and post-operative endophthalmitis, but age- and sex-related differences in ocular surface bacterial flora and antimicrobial resistance remain unclear. We investigated these differences in bacterial isolates and levofloxacin (LVFX) susceptibility in adults. Retrospective study. We reviewed microbiological data on conjunctival isolates from 18,053 eyes of 11,677 adults without ocular infection undergoing ophthalmic surgery at the Miyata Eye Hospital between June 2018 and December 2023. Data were analyzed using generalized additive and log-linear model. LVFX susceptibility was determined using the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute broth microdilution protocol. 22,561 bacterial isolates (11,081 from women; 11480 from men) were obtained from adults aged >19 years. The number of species isolated from women was lower than men, and increased at a rate of 1.19 and 1.09 per 10 years of age in women and men, respectively (p < 0.0001). Staphylococcus epidermidis and Corynebacterium spp. were predominant across all age groups. Under 80 years of age, methicillin-sensitive S. epidermidis (MSSE) was isolated more frequently from men than from women. Corynebacterium spp. increased with age in both sexes. Between age 40-90 years, LVFX resistance in MSSE was higher in women than in men, whereas LVFX resistance in Corynebacterium spp. increased with age regardless of sex. S. epidermidis and Corynebacterium spp. showed age- and sex-related differences in isolation frequency and fluoroquinolone susceptibility. Age and sex may influence ocular surface microbial ecology, antimicrobial resistance, and perioperative infection control.

items.title: Biodegradation of corn stover cuticle by Streptomyces griseorubens CUT-1: Performance, key enzymes, and metabolic pathway.
items.abstract: Efficient biodegradation of crop stover is important for agricultural waste management and sustainable biomass utilization. In this study, an esterase-producing strain, Streptomyces griseorubens CUT-1, was screened using polycaprolactone selective medium and evaluated for its ability to transform the corn stover epidermal surface. The strain was able to grow with pretreated corn stover epidermis as the sole carbon source. SEM and AFM analyses showed disruption of the epidermal surface and a marked increase in surface roughness after strain treatment. XPS analysis revealed increased oxygen-containing functional groups and surface polarity, while the average water contact angle decreased from 90.55° to 60.59°, indicating reduced surface hydrophobicity and modification of the associated cuticular barrier. Transcriptomic analysis showed significant changes in genes related to carbon metabolism, substrate transport, and lignocellulose-associated functions. Genes encoding putative cuticle-related enzymes, including cutinase, esterases, lipases, oxidases, and dehydrogenases, were also up-regulated. LC-MS analysis detected several C16- and C18-derived metabolites, including 16-hydroxyhexadecanoic acid, consistent with the transformation of cutin-derived components. Based on the combined surface characterization, transcriptomic responses, and metabolite profiles, a potential biodegradation process involving hydrolysis of ester-linked cuticular components, subsequent oxidation and chain shortening of aliphatic compounds, and further incorporation into central carbon metabolism was proposed. These results provide new insights into actinomycete-mediated transformation of corn stover epidermal and cuticular components.
