items.title: Longitudinal patterns of problematic internet use and subsequent mental health problems in adolescents.
items.abstract: Aims To evaluate the association between longitudinal patterns of problematic internet use (PIU) and later adolescent mental health, addressing time-varying confounding not fully accounted for in prior research. Methods Longitudinal data were obtained from 3,171 adolescents who participated in the Tokyo Teen Cohort (2012-2021). PIU at ages 12 and 14 was categorized into tertiles (low, medium and high) to define longitudinal patterns. We applied the g-formula to estimate associations between these PIU patterns and mental health outcomes at age 16, accounting for baseline and time-varying confounders. Results Adolescents with persistently high PIU at ages 12 and 14 had higher risk and severity of mental health problems at age 16 compared with those with persistently low PIU: internalizing symptoms (risk difference [RD] 4.6%, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.8%-7.6%; risk ratio [RR] 2.19, 95% CI 1.35-3.68; mean difference 1.21, 95% CI 0.49-1.95), depression (RD 6.3%, 95% CI 1.8-10.8%; RR 1.70, 95% CI 1.18-2.48; mean difference 0.97, 95% CI 0.33-1.64), anxiety (RD 5.0%, 95% CI 2.0-8.2%; RR 2.06, 95% CI 1.33-3.36; mean difference 0.64, 95% CI 0.26-1.03) and externalizing symptoms (RD 7.0%, 95% CI 3.9-10.0%; RR 3.21, 95% CI 1.84-6.56; mean difference 1.19, 95% CI 0.72-1.68). Patterns in which PIU remitted showed weaker and less consistent associations. Associations with depression were more pronounced in girls. Conclusions The present study showed that persistent PIU is associated with subsequent internalizing, depressive, anxiety and externalizing symptoms in adolescents. Remission of PIU may be associated with attenuated severity. Approaches to reduce PIU appear indicated, which may include home-, school- and population-level interventions.

items.title: Research Trends in Suicide Bereavement and Postvention - A Global Bibliometric and Content Analysis.
items.abstract: Background: Suicide bereavement refers to the grief experienced by individuals who have lost a close contact to suicide. It is often characterized by intense emotional distress, feelings of guilt, stigma, and social isolation, and may increase the risk of mental health problems and suicidal behavior. As research on suicide bereavement and postvention continues to expand globally, there is a growing need to map its development systematically and identify key trends. Aims: This study aimed to describe patterns in published literature on suicide bereavement and postvention through a global bibliometric analysis. Method: Systematic searches in eight databases (Web of Science; Scopus; CINAHL; PsycINFO; MEDLINE; Embase; Emcare; APA PsycArticles) yielded 49,386 references. After deduplication and screening, 1,072 articles published between 1953 and 2025 were included. Eligible peer-reviewed publications included empirical research, evidence syntheses (systematic reviews, scoping reviews, meta-analyses) and nonempirical publications (such as opinion pieces, and personal experiences). There were no restrictions on language, location, or year of publication. Results: The 1,072 eligible publications demonstrated a steady increase in suicide bereavement/postvention publications annually. 95% of publications were by first authors from high-income countries, while 1.3% of first authors were from lower-middle-income and low-income countries. Most studies were empirical and followed a quantitative or qualitative design, primarily cross-sectional, increasing over the years, while nonempirical publications declined. We identified few longitudinal or interventional studies. Populations sampled most frequently were working-age adults, with few studies focused on older adults. Limitations: The results provide little information about the methodological quality of the included studies. Some full texts could not be found and were unavailable for data extraction. Conclusion: The research gaps identified suggest that future studies should focus on underrepresented populations as well as on high-quality intervention studies to address adverse outcomes among suicide loss survivors.

items.title: From individual movement to ecosystem response: how landscape structure shapes herbivore impacts
items.abstract: Understanding how local interactions generate large-scale ecological dynamics is a central challenge in ecology. In heterogeneous environments, consumer movement links resource distribution with exploitation, producing responses that may not be predicted from consumer abundance or resource availability alone. Here, we develop a spatially explicit stochastic individual-based model of two herbivore populations with contrasting movement and foraging strategies that share renewable resources. The model incorporates heterogeneous resources, consumer movement and feeding, resource regeneration, predation, and refuge availability. Using Monte Carlo simulations, we examine how herbivore pressure and landscape structure shape population dynamics and resource depletion. Movement strongly determines the spatial pattern of depletion, while resource vulnerability depends on the overlap between resource distribution and consumer activity. Counterintuitively, increasing the extent of a productive region increases initial resource biomass but can also increase relative resource loss. Additional resources sustain consumer activity where herbivores concentrate, showing that greater resource availability does not necessarily buffer ecosystems against herbivory. Resource biomass can also decline substantially before major reductions in vegetation occupancy become apparent. These results demonstrate how individual behaviour and landscape structure jointly shape ecosystem responses. The model provides a framework for investigating how spatially coupled consumer-resource interactions generate ecological dynamics.

items.title: Mining-driven Forest Fragmentation Shapes Malaria Vector Ecology in the Venezuelan Amazon
items.abstract: Abstract Malaria persistence in the Americas has paralleled rapid Amazonian deforestation, with Venezuela emerging as a critical hotspot where gold mining and forest loss drive intense epidemics. Because malaria transmission is tightly linked to mosquito ecology, clarifying how deforestation amplifies vector traits is essential. We examined forest fragmentation along mining gradients in the southern Venezuelan Amazon to assess impacts on anthropophilic anopheline mosquito communities. As expected, anopheline richness and abundance peaked at forest edges, particularly under intermediate fragmentation where edge effects were strongest, while mining pits further expanded populations. At broader scales, forest cover shaped species distributions, and long-degraded mining landscapes supported the greatest diversity and density of primary Plasmodium vectors, where malaria risk was particularly elevated during the dry-rainy transition. Vector mosquito assemblages were dominated by Nyssorhynchus albitarsis s.l. ( Ny. albitarsis F, Ny. janconnae ), Ny. goeldii , and Ny. darlingi . Notably, Ny. janconnae was reported for the first time in Venezuela and found infected with both Plasmodium species, while Ny. rondoniensis , also newly recorded, carried P. falciparum . These findings emphasize how escalating ecological pressures in the Amazon rainforest reshape vector composition, abundance, and infection dynamics, posing major challenges for malaria elimination in the region.

items.title: Dependence of vegetation productivity on taxa constituting microbial networks and its aspect-specific differentiation
items.abstract: Abstract Background Soil microbes strongly shape alpine meadow productivity; however, previous studies have focused mainly on key taxa or functional genes. How taxa constituting networks differentially modulate aboveground biomass (AGB) and belowground biomass (BGB) remains unclear. Methods We sampled a continuous 0–360° aspect gradient on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau and divided it into east, south, west and north aspects. We characterised plant communities, soil properties and metagenomes, and analyzed diversity, community/functional composition and network topology. Random forest and variance partitioning were used to quantify the relative contributions of taxa constituting microbial networks, core taxa (bacteria and fungi) and core functional pathways to AGB and BGB. Results Aspect strongly influenced biomass allocation and soil properties, yet neither community nor functional composition of bacteria or fungi differed among aspects. In contrast, network topologies — modularity, betweenness centrality, and robustness — diverged markedly. Taxa constituting networks consistently explained more variation in BGB than in AGB, with aspect-dependent explanation: on west and south aspects, bacterial taxa constituting networks and core fungi jointly explained AGB; on east aspects, metabolic pathways explained BGB; on north aspects, bacterial taxa constituting networks alone contributed most to BGB. These patterns were spatially complementary, with south/west aspects primarily explaining AGB and east/north aspects primarily explaining BGB. Conclusions Taxa constituting networks, rather than community or functional composition, are the key predicted factors AGB and BGB. BGB depends more on the integrity of taxa constituting networks, and the explanation of above- versus belowground productivity shows a clear spatial division among aspects. Incorporating network analysis into soil microbial ecology will greatly enhance predictions of ecosystem functioning under environmental change.

items.title: Whole-soil microbial inoculation accelerates post-fire soil recovery in a mixed conifer forest.
items.abstract: High-severity wildfires of increasing size and frequency result in release of carbon dioxide and destroy timber resources, and reduce biodiversity, soil integrity, water quality, and recreational opportunities. Forest recovery strongly depends on the reestablishment of soil microbial communities, motivating research on how restoration of soil microbiomes in burned forests can be accelerated. Here, we used a high-intensity burn pile experiment to test the effectiveness of post-fire native soil amendment as a microbial coalescence experiment. This design enabled simultaneous and repeated sampling of unburned, burned, and inoculated burned soils while holding abiotic factors constant. All conditions were sampled at six time points across an annual hydrological cycle and analyzed using amplicon sequencing, genome-resolved metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and soil chemistry. Fire sharply reduced bacterial and fungal diversity in surface soils and nearly eliminated ectomycorrhizal fungi. Inoculation shifted bulk community composition toward the unburned reference state, without measurably accelerating subsequent convergence. Inoculation also accelerated recovery of functions associated with nutrient cycling, especially nitrogen transformations, and introduced a diverse assemblage of mycorrhizal fungi, including genera capable of forming essential symbioses with conifers, though this signal declined over the study period. However, the introduction of host plants and the establishment of functional plant-fungal symbioses, which may prolong persistence, were not tested. Despite introducing the full diversity of soil microbes, only a subset of organisms engrafted, likely due to selection linked to pyrogenic effects. We conclude that whole-soil inoculation can shorten the dispersal-limited phase of post-fire microbial recovery, a promising step towards restoration of the soil microbiome.

items.title: Parasite impairment of host mobility favours reduced virulence.
items.abstract: Parasite fitness is often constrained by the transmission-virulence trade-off, where excessive replication within a host shortens infection duration and reduces overall transmission. Spatial structure has been shown to influence selection acting on this evolutionary trade-off: limited parasite dispersal shapes how transmission affects fitness and alters population genetic structure. However, while current theory assumes that parasite dispersal is fixed and independent of virulence, parasites typically modulate host mobility, a sublethal effect that has a direct impact on the spatial structure of populations. Here, we expand the classical virulence-transmission trade-off framework by considering the impact of virulence on host mobility. We find that when parasites reduce host movement, relatedness and local demographic conditions change in ways that favour more prudent parasite strategies that inflict less harm. Furthermore, while parasite-impaired host mobility leads to higher host density, long-lived hosts also shed parasites for longer periods leading to increased parasite prevalence across the population. We further show that such population-level demographic feedbacks are crucial for clarifying previous results on why limited parasite dispersal reduces virulence. Our work highlights the importance of incorporating host behaviour in models of parasite virulence and suggests new avenues for managing infectious disease in natural populations.

items.title: Comparative analysis of bacterial and fungal microbiomes and predicted functional potential in Balkan and Caucasus cheeses.
items.abstract: Despite the cultural and historical connections between the Balkans and the Caucasus, and the ethnic and cultural differences between neighboring countries within each region, comparative information on cheese microbiomes from these regions remains limited. This study compared microbial communities in 84 cheese samples from Bulgaria, Greece, Armenia and Georgia and assessed predicted bacterial functional potential. High-throughput sequencing of bacterial 16S rRNA and fungal ITS markers was used to characterize community composition and diversity, while PICRUSt2 predicted bacterial functional potential and MetaCyc pathways. Bacterial richness and Shannon diversity did not differ significantly among countries, whereas fungal richness and diversity were significantly lower in Armenian than in Bulgarian and Greek cheeses. Bray-Curtis analyses revealed significant country-associated differences in bacterial (R² = 0.142, P = 0.001) and fungal (R² = 0.114, P = 0.001) community composition, with consistent separation between Balkan and Caucasus cheeses. Dominant taxa included lactic acid bacteria and cheese-associated yeasts, with substantial differences in relative abundance among countries. PICRUSt2 predicted 415 MetaCyc pathways, 99 of which differed significantly among countries, including pathways related to carbohydrate fermentation, pyruvate metabolism and amino acid biosynthesis. These findings reveal country-associated variation in microbial community composition and predicted bacterial functional potential across cheese collections.

items.title: The ecological impact of Ulva prolifera green tide outbreaks: microbial connectivity and metabolic divergence.
items.abstract: Green tides in coastal areas have become an increasing eco-environmental concern around the world. However, the influence of massive green tides on microorganism dispersal has not yet been explored in detail. In this study, we used amplicon and metagenomic sequencing to first systematically examine the dynamics of the microbial community among continuous microhabitats in the Ulva prolifera bloom area. We found that the phycospheric microbiota exhibited increased α-diversity and complex network topologies. The tracking of bacterial sources indicated that phycospheric microorganisms originated from the algal-surface microhabitat and were widely shared with the surrounding seawater, indicating that U. prolifera blooms strengthen horizontal connectivity among microhabitats and thus facilitate the dispersal of phycospheric microorganisms into the surrounding seawater. With respect to microbial assemblages, the phycosphere was governed primarily by deterministic processes, indicating that environmental factors strongly influence the community structure of the phycosphere. Furthermore, genes involved in carbon degradation, nitrogen retention, and sulfate reduction were enriched in the algal surfaces and phycosphere, facilitating the transformation and accumulation of complex algae-derived organic matter into dissolved organic matter. Bacteroidia , Gammaproteobacteria , and Alphaproteobacteria were the key taxa contributing to organic matter transformation in the phycosphere and algal surfaces, likely reflecting their high substrate utilization strategies. In general, these findings highlight the microscale dynamics and ecological risks of microbial dispersal and demonstrate the combined effects of large-scale U. prolifera blooms on microbial structure and function, thus forming a precise assessment of the effects of macroalgal blooms on marine biogeochemical cycles. Importance Ulva prolifera green tides are among the largest macroalgal blooms worldwide, yet how these events reshape microbial communities and their ecological functions remains poorly understood. This study reveals that green tide formation restructures microbial connectivity across algal-associated habitats and promotes distinct microbial metabolic strategies involved in organic matter transformation. These findings improve our understanding of how large-scale macroalgal blooms alter coastal microbial processes and provide new insights into the ecological consequences of expanding green tide events.

items.title: Optimization of a Lab-screening Procedure to Evaluate Seed Treatment Efficacy: Detection of Ustilago nuda in Hordeum vulgare Seedlings.
items.abstract: To prevent plant disease outbreaks and economic losses, rapid and reliable tools to evaluate newly developed, low-risk treatments are needed. Visual inspections of grown plants are used to assess treatment efficacy a labor-intensive and costly process, especially for seedborne pathogens that are asymptomatic until flowering. For one such pathogen, Ustilago nuda that causes loose smut of barley ( Hordeum vulgare ), we developed a lab-screening procedure combining optimized growth procedures and qPCR to quantify its DNA in seedlings, thereby accelerating seed treatment evaluations. We cultivated seedlings for 5, 10 and 14 days with two techniques: growth on filter paper in dark and in potting soil under light-dark conditions. Seedlings were grown from two naturally infected seed lots, which were either not treated or treated with a synthetic fungicide or warm water. During two seasons, these non-treated and treated seeds were also grown in the field. Infection levels in the seedlings were based on qPCR-measured U. nuda DNA normalized to H. vulgare DNA. Treatment efficacies were calculated using laboratory-measured infection levels and field-observed disease incidence, and a lab-to-field predictability factor was used to compare seed treatment evaluations among the seedling growth procedures. Infection levels assessed using qPCR on seedlings grown for 10 days on filter paper and 14 days in potting soil most accurately represented field results and showed clear treatment effects. Our lab-screening method could provide an early and efficient evaluation of seed treatment efficacy, aiding in the development of new, low-risk control strategies to reduce synthetic plant protection product applications.

items.title: New indices for evaluating host specificity in parasite assemblages infecting a group of hosts with known phylogenetic relationships.
items.abstract: Host specificity is an essential parasite trait that influences ecology, evolution, and epidemiology. Quantifying host specificity using indices provides a standardized way to assess its degree and gain insights into parasite strategies. In this study, I introduce three new indices designed to describe host specificity. H SP quantifies host specificity based on differences in parasite prevalence among hosts, whereas H SP * additionally incorporates host phylogeny. These indices range from 0 to 1 and approach 1 when a parasite is more host-specific. The third index, P E , compares H SP and H SP * and assesses how phylogenetic information affects these host specificity indices. A positive P E means a parasite infects closely related hosts more often, while a negative P E indicates that a parasite frequently infects distantly related hosts. These three indices provide useful tools for understanding characteristics of parasites infecting a set of host species with known phylogenetic relationships.

items.title: Music exposure reduces anxiety- and depression-like behavior in rodents: a systematic review and multilevel meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Music exposure may alter affect-related behavior in rodents, but findings vary among studies, and little is known about effects on behavioral variability. We conducted a preregistered systematic review and multilevel meta-analysis of 20 experimental studies (298 effect sizes) of music exposure in laboratory rodents. We quantified changes in average anxiety- and depression-like behavior using the log response ratio and changes in between-animal variability using the log variability ratio, while accounting for nonindependence among effects. We also assessed reporting, methodological quality, and risk of bias using the Critical Appraisal of Methodological (technical) Quality, Quality of Reporting and Risk of Bias in Animal Research. Music exposure was associated with about a 20% reduction in anxiety- and depression-like behavior relative to controls, but there was no overall change in behavioral variability. Average responses differed among behavioral assays, while exploratory analyses of variability suggested context-dependent effects: anxiety-like outcomes tended toward greater variability and depression-like outcomes toward lower variability, and behavioral assay and music meta-genre explained larger shares of heterogeneity in the log variability ratio. Reporting of sample-size justification, allocation, blinding, attrition, and acoustic delivery was often incomplete in the primary studies. Evidence was limited to 20 studies and predominantly to young adult rodents and short-term exposures, constraining inference about variability and generalization beyond the laboratory contexts studied.

items.title: Tales from the CREP: A Report on Varied Implementations of the Collaborative Replications and Education Project

Students are well-positioned to contribute to this literature through classroom replications.Statement of the Problem: Teaching open science practices and engaging students in the replication process is difficult for instructors who have no prior training.Literature Review: We review literature detailing why instructors choose not to implement replications in the classroom. The Collaborative Replications and Education Project (CREP) provides a template for such efforts, carried out by students under the guidance of an instructor knowledgeable in open science practices. We discuss the outcomes from a series of instructor workshops aimed at teaching instructors of psychology how to implement CREP within classrooms of varying demographics.Teaching Implications: Five instructors – ranging from private, primarily undergraduate institutes to large, public R1s – discuss their experiences, challenges, and recommendations for including CREP replications in classroom settings. Conclusion: The outcomes for students, and lessons learned for instructors, should provide first-time instructors with a guide map for including such efforts within their own classrooms.

items.title: Dispositifs of the Narrative: A New Poststructuralist Radicalization of Narrative Therapy
items.abstract: Narrative therapy made narration the medium of its clinical work and the means through which it contests the truths of psychology; the status it grants the narrative shapes its accounts of knowledge, subject, problem, and change. This article reconstructs that status in White and Epston and in the poststructuralist radicalizations of Madigan and Guilfoyle. The tradition historicized psychopathological truths and the authority of expert knowledge and stabilized certain narrative properties (temporal sequence, biographical coherence, and attribution to a subject) as general conditions for understanding experience, an asymmetry of historicization. Taking Foucault's concept of dispositif as he formulated it, we shift the object of analysis from narratives to dispositifs of the narrative, configurations of discursive and nondiscursive practices, relations of force, and practices of the self within which narrating oneself becomes possible, required, and credible. Because the asymmetry concerns forms that periods and cultures made available and the clinic works with persons, the concept has a sociohistorical use, which follows them over time, and a clinical use, developed here, which describes their configuration in a particular life. This displacement makes the radicalization poststructuralist in lineage and postconstructionist in position, reorienting how narrative therapy conceives its object, listening, knowledge, agency, and change.

The tradition historicized psychopathological truths and the authority of expert knowledge and stabilized certain narrative properties (temporal sequence, biographical coherence, and attribution to a subject) as general conditions for understanding experience, an asymmetry of historicization. Taking Foucault's concept of dispositif as he formulated it, we shift the object of analysis from narratives to dispositifs of the narrative, configurations of discursive and nondiscursive practices, relations of force, and practices of the self within which narrating oneself becomes possible, required, and credible. Because the asymmetry concerns forms that periods and cultures made available and the clinic works with persons, the concept has a sociohistorical use, which follows them over time, and a clinical use, developed here, which describes their configuration in a particular life. This displacement makes the radicalization poststructuralist in lineage and postconstructionist in position, reorienting how narrative therapy conceives its object, listening, knowledge, agency, and change.

items.title: Mapping the noetic quality: A computational analysis of the elicitors and experience of profound truth
items.abstract: Profound experiences have been studied under many constructs in psychology, such as mystical and religious experiences, aesthetic experiences, awe, and the sublime. Despite differing in appraisal structure, emotional content and valence, and typical triggers, common among their nomological networks seems to be the noetic quality: the subjective sense of apprehending something which feels nonrational but true, self-evident, immediate, and real. This suggests that the noetic quality might be a unique and separable phenomenon. It has rarely been studied as such, however, partly because these experiences tend to be highly subjectively intense and specific, making them difficult to induce in a laboratory and their retrospective accounts costly to analyze qualitatively. In the present study, we analyzed a sample of N = 318 participants who wrote narrative essays about their experiences with the noetic quality and answered questions about their emotional and motivational content, and subjective epistemic change. Essays were classified using natural language processing. Elicitors spanned aesthetic experiences, psychedelic experiences, religious and mystical experiences, and experiences with death, and experiences were affectively heterogeneous (34% negative, 66% positive). Across elicitors, experiences were consistently marked by high emotional intensity, action tendency, and subjective epistemic change, suggesting an emotion-like structure. The study demonstrates the feasibility of computational approaches for studying rare and non-ordinary experiences.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Dynamic Cognitive Partner Integrating Working Memory Theory and AI Supported Reading Development in Dyslexia
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly emerged as a promising resource for supporting students with dyslexia. Nevertheless, much of the existing literature examines AI primarily as an assistive technology, with limited attention to the cognitive mechanisms through which it may enhance reading development. This paper addresses that gap by proposing a conceptual framework that integrates Baddeley’s multicomponent model of working memory with contemporary AI-supported educational tools. Drawing on research in cognitive psychology, special education, cognitive load theory, Universal Design for Learning (UDL), and self-determination theory, the paper argues that AI should be understood not merely as an instructional aid but as an external cognitive support system that complements and extends the functional capacity of working memory during reading. Specifically, the framework illustrates how AI technologies—including text-to-speech systems, speech recognition, adaptive learning environments, and generative AI applications—may reduce cognitive load while supporting the phonological loop, visuospatial sketchpad, central executive, and episodic buffer. Through this cognitive alignment, AI has the potential to facilitate decoding, comprehension, learner engagement, and reading autonomy among students with dyslexia. The proposed framework contributes to the literature by offering a theoretically grounded perspective that connects cognitive theory with emerging educational technologies. Rather than evaluating the effectiveness of a specific intervention, the paper provides an integrative model to guide future empirical research, instructional design, and the development of AI-supported reading interventions for learners with dyslexia.

items.title: Kinship, Faith and Classroom Routines: An Integrative Review of Young Children’s Emotional Resilience after Disasters in West Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Lombok and the wider province of West Nusa Tenggara (NTB), Indonesia, face recurring earthquakes, and the 2018 Lombok sequence displaced hundreds of thousands of people. How young children recover depends not only on clinical services but also on the families, faith communities and early childhood settings around them, resources that disaster psychology developed in Western contexts has tended to overlook. Aim: This review examines what is known about the protective processes that support the emotional resilience of children aged 3–6 after disasters, with particular attention to Sasak kinship, Islamic religious coping and early childhood education in NTB. Method: An integrative review drew on literature identified through structured searches of Google Scholar, PubMed, SciSpace and reference databases, covering empirical studies, reviews and foundational theory published in English or Indonesian. Evidence was appraised with reference to CASP and MMAT criteria and synthesised thematically across the levels of Bronfenbrenner’s ecological systems theory. Findings: Four themes emerged: (1) caregivers and extended kin as the first buffer against disaster stress; (2) Islamic practices and local traditions of mutual aid as sources of meaning, routine and solidarity; (3) early childhood settings as safe and predictable spaces when staff are prepared for trauma-informed practice; and (4) the alignment of supports across family, school, community and policy. Direct evidence on young children in Lombok remains limited; much of it comes from adolescents, adults, families or other disaster settings. Implications: Disaster response in NTB should keep extended families together, recognise religious and community resources, and prepare early childhood educators for trauma-informed practice. Longitudinal and controlled studies with young children are needed to test these pathways

items.title: Mirrored Suspicion: Conspiracy, Securitization, and the Opposition to Jewish–Muslim Engagement in the United States since 9/11
items.abstract: Abstract Since September 11, 2001, efforts to build durable relationships between American Jewish and American Muslim communities have met organized opposition from within both communities. This article argues that the opposition follows a logic of mirrored suspicion: opponents of engagement in each community read the other’s outreach as a surface concealing hostile intent. The form that suspicion takes, however, tracks each community’s position relative to the American security state. Among American Muslims, opposition tends toward a conspiratorial register in which interfaith programs, particularly those connected to Zionist institutions, are read as covert normalization, surveillance, or co-optation. Among American Jews, opposition tends toward a securitizing register in which Muslim partners are read as fronts for Islamist networks or for a “red-green” convergence of Islamism and the radical left. Drawing on peer-reviewed research in social psychology, the sociology of religion, security studies, and digital religion, and on five episodes from 2001 to 2024, the article shows that the two registers share a narrative grammar of concealment and exposure, that both are concentrated in organizational and online arenas rather than in lay opinion, and that digital platforms reward them. It proposes symmetrical criteria for distinguishing principled dissent from suspicion and outlines a research design for testing the argument. Mirrored suspicion, the article concludes, is a structural obstacle to pluralism that neither community can dismantle alone.

items.title: The Effect of a Diabetes-Educated Psychologist on HbA1c and Diabetes Distress in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes: A Multicenter, Open-Label, Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: Objective To evaluate whether integrating a diabetes-educated psychologist into conventional care improves HbA1c, diabetes distress, treatment satisfaction, and diabetes-related quality of life in adults with type 1 diabetes and elevated HbA1c. Research design and methods This 52-week randomized controlled trial was conducted at six clinics in Sweden. Ten psychologists with structured diabetes-specific training provided individual counseling. Adults with type 1 diabetes and HbA1c >7.8% (62 mmol/mol) were randomized to conventional care or conventional care supplemented by a diabetes-educated psychologist. Results A total of 151 participants were included (mean age 43 years, 51% women, mean HbA1c 9.2% [76.5 mmol/mol]). Participants in the psychologist group attended a median of 9 counseling sessions (interquartile range 7-11). All reported between-group estimates, 95% CIs, and P values were adjusted. At week 52, HbA1c decreased by 0.58% (6.3 mmol/mol) in the psychologist group and by 0.36% (3.9 mmol/mol) in the conventional group (mean difference -0.2% [95% CI -0.6, 0.2]; P = 0.31). Diabetes distress decreased (mean difference -0.2 [95% CI -0.4, -0.03]; P = 0.040) and treatment satisfaction improved (mean difference 3.5 [95% CI 1.3, 5.6]; P = 0.004), whereas diabetes-related quality of life did not differ between groups (mean difference 0.3 [95% CI -0.1, 0.7]; P = 0.15). Participants rated the psychologist visits as highly useful (median score 9 out of 10). Conclusions Integrating a diabetes-educated psychologist into routine care for adults with type 1 diabetes did not significantly improve HbA1c but reduced diabetes distress and improved treatment satisfaction.

items.title: Brief Acceptance and Commitment Therapy: a systematic review and meta-analysis of effects on depression and anxiety across mental health, physical/medical, and non-clinical populations.
items.abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effectiveness of brief Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), operationalized using modality-specific thresholds (individual: ≤6 sessions/≤6 hours; group: ≤6 weeks/≤12 hours), on depression and anxiety across mental health, physical/medical, and non-clinical populations. Forty-nine RCTs were included in the review. Random-effects models (Hedges' g ) were used, with subgroup analyses by control condition and population type. (PROSPERO registration: CRD42024531152). For depression ( k = 41), brief ACT showed a moderate overall effect ( g = 0.56; I 2 = 90.61%), significant versus passive ( g = 0.67) but not active controls ( g = 0.14). For anxiety ( k = 35), a small-to-moderate overall effect emerged ( g = 0.42; I 2 = 86.22%), significant versus passive ( g = 0.53) but not active controls ( g = 0.01). For depressive symptoms, significant effects were observed in mental health and physical/medical populations, but not non-clinical populations. For anxiety symptoms, the pooled effect reached significance in non-clinical populations but not mental health or physical/medical populations; tests of between-subgroup differences were non-significant. Brief ACT was associated with reduced depression and anxiety relative to passive controls, but not active interventions, and heterogeneity was substantial. Brief ACT may serve as a viable option in resource-constrained settings.

items.title: DiaMEETes: A Collective Narrative and Play-Based Group Intervention for Children Aged 8-10 Living With Type 1 Diabetes.
items.abstract: Children aged 8-10 living with Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) may experience emotional distress, isolation, and difficulties adjusting to diabetes management. While collective narrative practice groups have been adapted successfully for older children with T1D, a developmentally appropriate intervention for younger children was needed. This paper describes DiaMEETes, a multidisciplinary group intervention combining collective narrative practices, play, and peer support. DiaMEETes was co-developed with young people with lived experience of T1D and delivered within a paediatric psychology service. Activities aimed to externalise diabetes, strengthen identity beyond illness, foster peer connection, and build hope. Thirty children aged 8-11 attended between 2021 and 2025. Quantitative and qualitative feedback was collected from children and parents/carers and analysed using thematic analysis. Seventy-two percent of attendees rated the group 10/10 and 89% would recommend it to others. Five themes were identified: connection and shared experiences, enjoyment of activities, finding hope and strength, valuing peer trainers, and ideas for future groups. Parents reported increased confidence, pride, and acceptance in their children. DiaMEETes highlights the value of developmentally tailored collective narrative interventions within paediatric diabetes services.

items.title: When recall fails: can cue familiarity extend search times?
items.abstract: In the study of recognition memory, familiarity is the sense that something has been encountered before while failing to recall specifics of that prior encounter. We tested if familiarity could increase search times for specific details. In two experiments, we used the Recognition Without Cued Recall paradigm where participants study words and are then given test cues with varying levels of feature overlap with studied words. This paradigm can be used to manipulate familiarity when cued recall fails. We examined how long participants took attempting to recall the target words. We found evidence that increasing familiarity increased search times. Search times also correlated positively with reported familiarity intensity. Experiment 2 also showed associations between search times and curiosity regarding the target word, or the to be recalled information. This suggests a possible role of curiosity in driving extended search. These results suggest that familiarity acts as more than just a secondary method of recognition. Instead, familiarity can prompt a person to keep trying to recall specifics of a prior encounter, similar to a tip of the tongue state.

items.title: The Role of Perceptual Rhythmic Ability in the Perception of Accented Second Language Speech.
items.abstract: Purpose The present study examined the relationship between perceptual rhythmic ability and cognitive load during second language (L2) speech perception and whether variation in cognitive load across accents differing in their rhythmic properties is more consistent with accounts emphasizing first language (L1)-based rhythmic interference or L2 target-language alignment. Method Eighty-two L1 Spanish-L2 English bilinguals completed a pupillometry experiment in which they listened to English sentences spoken with accents differing in rhythmic properties (Spanish-accented English: lowest temporal variability, Mandarin-accented English: intermediate temporal variability, American-accented English: highest temporal variability). Cognitive load was indexed using pupil dilation. Participants also completed a perceptual rhythm discrimination task, along with additional tasks relevant to L2 speech processing. Results Listeners with stronger perceptual rhythmic ability showed greater pupil dilation (indexing greater cognitive load) for Spanish-accented English, a reduced effect for Mandarin-accented English, and the weakest effect for American-accented English. This pattern suggests that alignment with listeners' internalized expectations about the typical rhythmic properties of English is associated with more efficient processing of English sentences and that listeners with better perceptual rhythmic ability are more sensitive to this alignment. Conclusions The findings suggest that alignment between listeners' rhythmic sensitivity and the rhythmic properties of the target language is correlated with cognitive load during L2 speech processing. Future research should examine how rhythmic sensitivity interacts with other factors across diverse L2 listening contexts and populations. items.title: Return to School and Readmission Risk After Pain-Related Hospitalizations in Pediatric Sickle Cell Disease.
items.abstract: Introduction Pain is the primary cause of inpatient admissions in sickle cell disease (SCD) and readmission is common. For school-aged youth, successful transition from the hospital necessitates school reentry. This study assessed rates of school return following a pain-related admission and the relationship between school return and readmission. Methods Sixteen youth (7-17 years) admitted for SCD-related pain and caregivers completed daily surveys about school attendance and pain severity for 10 consecutive school days after discharge. Descriptive, independent samples t-test, and chi-square analyses were used to assess differences in pain, school attendance, and readmission. Results On average, participants (age M = 13.75; 69% female; 75% HbSS) attended 6.13 out of 10 school days, with 25% returning the next school day after discharge and 13% attending all 10 days. Almost all (94%) reported ongoing pain throughout the monitoring period. Most youth (63%) exhibited variable school attendance after initial school return. Those with variable attendance attended fewer school days (M = 4.40, SD = 2.46) compared to "consistent school attenders" (M = 9, SD = 0.89), p VariableAttenders = 3.78, SD VariableAttenders = 1.68; M ConsistentAttenders = 1.47, SD ConsistentAttenders = 0.81), p = 0.007. Half of "variable school attenders" were readmitted, compared to none of the consistent attenders, χ 2 (df = 1) = 4.36, p = 0.037. Conclusions Our findings suggest that school reentry after a pain-related hospitalization is difficult for many patients and essential to consider in discharge planning. Youth continue reporting pain following discharge, with some experiencing variable school attendance and readmission for pain. Promoting school attendance should be a core component of comprehensive SCD management plans, with implications for pain management and healthcare utilization.

items.title: Breaking Continuity: How Patient Vulnerabilities and Treatment Characteristics Shape Methadone Discontinuation.
items.abstract: Background Sustained retention in opioid agonist treatment is crucial for achieving treatment goals; however, published retention rates vary widely. Treatment discontinuation has been consistently associated with adverse outcomes (all-cause mortality, nonfatal overdose, hospitalization, and psychosocial deterioration), partly due to the loss of opioid tolerance following treatment cessation. Understanding patient-related and treatment-related factors that increase the risk of cycling in and out of treatment is essential for tailoring interventions and achieving continuity of care. Methods A retrospective observational study with a sample of 12 736 patients with opioid use disorder was conducted using real-world electronic-health-record data to examine patient-level factors (sex, age, education, frequency of use, comorbid substance use, and psychiatric comorbidities) and treatment-related factors (dispensing schedule, methadone dose, and adherence to outpatient treatment center) associated with methadone treatment discontinuation. This was modeled using a generalized linear model (negative binomial regression) to provide incidence rate ratios and an overall picture of this phenomenon. Clinical utility of a 14-day threshold was examined by comparing discontinuation rates between patients who died or dropped out and those who achieved therapeutic discharge. Results Overall, 21.9% of patients discontinued methadone treatment at least once during the study period. Being female, lower age, longer dispensing schedules, and higher frequency of prior use increased the risk of discontinuation. Conversely, greater treatment adherence reduced the risk of discontinuation. Patients who finally dropped out of treatment or died presented a higher number of treatment discontinuation than those with a therapeutic discharge. Moreover, a threshold of at least 14-day interruptions was identified as a clinically meaningful gap, associated with higher rates of dropout and mortality. Conclusions Real-world evidence supports discontinuation as an early alert for professionals and provides a basis for tailoring treatments and improving strategies for patients with the risk factors identified in the present study.

items.title: Practitioner Self-Compassion as a Relational Mechanism in Breastfeeding Support: A Framework and Research Agenda.
items.abstract: Breastfeeding disparities in the United States fall unevenly across populations and persist despite sustained attention to access, education, and clinical training. Support is often understood in terms of clinical guidance and communication, yet mothers' experiences also depend on the relational quality of the encounter and on practitioner attributes that may shape it. Existing research links self-compassion to emotion regulation, reduced self-criticism, practitioner wellbeing, maternal coping, and interpersonal functioning, but it has not been examined as a practitioner-level mechanism shaping mothers' experiences of breastfeeding support. Unlike approaches that target how practitioners attend to mothers, self-compassion concerns how practitioners attend to themselves, supporting the capacity to remain present and responsive when relational quality is most likely to falter. We propose practitioner self-compassion as a theoretically grounded, testable mechanism that may support internal regulation and relational presence during emotionally demanding encounters, indirectly shaping mothers' perceptions of support as validating, emotionally safe, trustworthy, and responsive, and thereby influencing engagement. We outline a staged research agenda using observational, multilevel, mediation, and intervention designs to test whether practitioner self-compassion predicts mothers' perceptions, engagement with support services, and downstream breastfeeding outcomes, with Black mothers as the priority population. If supported, practitioner self-compassion could become a scalable target for lactation education, professional development, and workforce training without shifting additional intervention burden onto mothers.

items.title: Dynamic associations between received social support, PTSD, and depressive symptoms during post-burn recovery.
items.abstract: Background: Social support is an important determinant of psychological adjustment following trauma, yet its temporal relationship with posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depressive symptoms remains incompletely understood among burn survivors. The present study examined the dynamic associations between received social support, PTSD symptoms, and depressive symptoms during the first two years following burn injury. Method: A total of 118 adult burn patients were recruited from the largest burn centre in Taiwan. Received social support, PTSD symptoms, and depressive symptoms were assessed at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months post-burn. Four-wave cross-lagged panel analyses were conducted to examine longitudinal associations among these variables. Results: Higher levels of received social support at 3 months predicted lower PTSD symptoms and depressive symptoms at 6 months. In contrast, higher depressive symptoms at 12 months predicted lower received social support at 24 months. No significant associations were observed between PTSD symptoms and subsequent social support. Conclusions: Early received social support may promote psychological adjustment following burn injury, whereas persistent depressive symptoms may contribute to later reductions in social support.

items.title: Coping strategies facing daily difficulties related to cognitive impairment attributed to hormone therapy: a qualitative study among breast cancer patients.
items.abstract: Purpose Self-perceived cognitive impairment attributed to hormone therapy is common among patients with breast cancer and negatively affects quality of life. Although some patients develop coping strategies, the specific mechanisms involved remain underexplored. This study aimed to examine coping strategies used by patients experiencing hormone therapy-related cognitive impairment. Methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 13 female participants with breast cancer (mean age = 52 years) receiving hormone therapy. Data were analysed using a deductive thematic analysis guided by the transactional model of stress and coping. Results The thematic analysis identified four categories of coping strategies was employed by participants: emotion-focused intrapersonal strategies (e.g. cognitive reappraisal, acceptance, social image management), problem-focused intrapersonal strategies (e.g. task reorganisation, planning, cognitive exercises), emotion-focused interpersonal strategies (e.g. psychological support, peers, family and problem-focused interpersonal strategies (e.g. help from relatives, medical support). Conclusion Among women with breast cancer undergoing hormone therapy, perceived cognitive difficulties are managed through a multifaceted coping system that draws on both individual resources and the social environment. These findings highlight the importance of supportive care that recognises and validates these difficulties and addresses their practical, emotional, and relational consequences.

items.title: Child chaos: parent-reported sibling differences in chaos at home in association with externalising and internalising behaviours.
items.abstract: Background Household chaos has long been associated with children's adjustment, relating to both externalising and-though somewhat less so-internalising behaviours. Original conceptualisations view chaos as an aspect of the home environment that may be shared by family members and/or differentially influence or be influenced by them. There is increasing recognition that home experiences can differ for siblings in ways important for their outcomes. To capture this for chaos, examining differential sibling perspectives has gained attention, but the extent to which parents perceive sibling differences in chaos and their relation to adjustment remains unstudied. In a preliminary study, for the first time, we distinguished family-wide and child-specific parent-reported chaos in association with sibling externalising and internalising behaviours. Methods In a UK sample of 261 families with young sibling pairs (3-11 years; 522 children), we adapted the response format of the widely used measure, CHAOS, to assess parent reports of child chaos, that is, chaos 'for and around' each child in the home. Multilevel modelling examined family-wide (family average) and child-specific (child differentiation from the family average) chaos reported by mothers in the prediction of between- and within-family variances in externalising and internalising behaviours. Results As hypothesised, accounting for key demographic and parenting confounders, family-wide chaos was associated with both externalising and internalising behaviours, whereas child-specific chaos was associated only with externalising behaviours. Conclusions Exploring parent perceptions of child chaos may offer key insights into associations between household chaos and young children's adjustment.

items.title: Early Life Adversity and Adolescent Sleep: A Longitudinal Study Examining Associations Between Dimensions of Early Adversity and Adolescent Sleep Metrics.
items.abstract: Objectives A dimensional approach was utilized to examine associations between early environmental adversity (deprivation, unpredictability) and adolescent sleep metrics (average and night-to-night variability in bedtime, wake time, and sleep duration). We predict that greater deprivation and unpredictability are uniquely associated with worse adolescent sleep. Methods In this study ( N = 337), preschool unpredictability and deprivation were measured via home observation and parent report; adolescent sleep was measured by actigraphy. Multilevel structural equation modeling examined longitudinal associations between early adversity dimensions and adolescent sleep, controlling for sex, adolescent age, maternal education, preschool family income, and adolescent family income. Results In independent models, greater deprivation was associated with more sleep duration variability (β = .18 [.01, .34]), greater bedtime variability (β = .30 [.14, .45]), and shorter average sleep duration (β = -.20 [-.35, -.03]); greater unpredictability was associated with shorter average sleep duration (β = -.21 [-.39, -.02]) and greater bedtime variability (β = .23 [.04, .40]). In the combined model, only greater deprivation (β = .26 [.09, .42]) was associated with greater bedtime variability, controlling for unpredictability. Conclusions While deprivation and unpredictability predict sleep independently, only deprivation played a unique role in adolescents' bedtime variability, beyond other aspects of early childhood adversity. Results inform early intervention and prevention efforts to promote healthy adolescent sleep.

items.title: Prenatal alcohol exposure and adolescent sleep in clinical pathways: a commentary on Devine et al.
items.abstract: Devine et al. provide timely evidence that parent-reported adolescent sleep disturbances are associated with prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development cohort, even when most exposure was low to moderate. This commentary argues that the central contribution of the study is not only the replication of a sleep signal after PAE, but the identification of a clinically recognisable phenotype: sleep-wake transition problems, excessive somnolence, and possible sleep breathing symptoms. We highlight three implications: sleep should be treated as a developmental mediator and modifiable target, future studies should triangulate retrospective PAE and parent-reported sleep with objective measures, and prevention messages about alcohol in pregnancy should be paired with non-stigmatising family support. Building clinical pathways from screening to intervention may transform small epidemiologic effects into meaningful benefits for affected adolescents.

items.title: A scoping review mapping the role of rural peer support service models in substance use and mental health care.
items.abstract: Background and objectives Rural communities experience disparities in treatment and healthcare engagement. Peer support services may address gaps in service linkage and engagement. This scoping review aimed to map the availability, structure, and reported outcomes of peer support services to address substance use and mental health conditions in rural United States communities or regions. Methods A scoping review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed, PsycINFO, and Web of Science were searched for peer-reviewed US-based studies published between January 2003 and March 2026. Studies were included if they described peer support program models or reported engagement, linkage to care, or recovery-related outcomes among adults in rural settings. Twenty-one studies were included in analysis (N = 21). Results Twenty-one studies were included, representing randomized trials, observational studies, qualitative research, and program descriptions. Reported outcomes included improved treatment engagement, referrals, and symptom change and reduction in social isolation. Rural-specific challenges to linkage were geographic isolation, work force shortages, stigma, and limited infrastructure. Emerging evidence identifies the importance of peer support in harm reduction, contingency management, telehealth navigation, and criminal justice settings for individuals who use drugs. Discussion and conclusions Existing literature reports that rural peer support services support engagement, navigation, and linkage to care for behavioral and health conditions; however, the evidence base remains limited. Scientific significance Peer-support models have the potential to expand linkage and access to behavioral health services, especially in rural areas where significant barriers may hinder patient engagement. Future research is needed to evaluate rural-specific implementation and sustainability.

items.title: An exploration of the roles of cognitive reactivity and ego depletion in the relationship between entrapment and suicidal ideation.
items.abstract: Objectives Entrapment is theorized as a key driver of suicidal ideation, yet the cognitive processes leading to entrapment, particularly the activating role of negative affect, and those through which entrapment translates into suicidal ideation are not well understood. Grounded in the Integrated Motivational-Volitional Model, this study used mediation analyses to examine cognitive reactivity in relation to suicidal ideation via entrapment, and ego depletion as a mediator of the entrapment-suicidal ideation link. Design A cross-sectional online survey was used to collect self-report data from participants recruited through opportunity sampling. Methods The sample consisted of 312 adults living in the United Kingdom. Data analyses were conducted on a subsample of participants who reported a lifetime history of suicidal ideation and/or suicide attempts (N = 269; M age = 28.50, SD = 10.06; 82.9% White; 66.5% female). Results The relationship between cognitive reactivity and suicidal ideation was accounted for by entrapment; this indirect association was not moderated by trait mindfulness. Additionally, the entrapment-suicidal ideation relationship was partially accounted for by self-regulatory fatigue, but not by depletion sensitivity; this indirect effect remained significant after controlling for depression, but not anxiety diagnosis. Conclusions The findings highlight cognitive reactivity as a cognitive vulnerability to suicidal ideation and underscore the value of understanding suicide risk through the lens of self-regulation. The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and the observed associations should be interpreted as correlational in nature.

items.title: Conceptual and psychometric characteristics of instruments used in adults with CHD quality of life research: a scoping review.
items.abstract: Background Improved survival among people with congenital heart disease (CHD) has increased the emphasis on quality of life as a long-term outcome. However, inconsistent distinctions between quality of life, health-related quality of life, health status and functioning complicate the interpretation of this evidence. Examining the conceptual basis and measurement properties of instruments used in contemporary CHD research is therefore necessary to establish which outcomes are being assessed. Aim To identify instruments used in studies reporting quality of life outcomes in adults with moderate or severe CHD, classify their intended constructs and summarise reported evidence of validity, reliability and suitability. Methods This scoping review followed Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR reporting guidance. CINAHL, MEDLINE, PsycINFO and Scopus were searched for English-language quantitative and mixed-methods studies published from 2015 in high-income countries. Citation mining identified instrument development and validation literature. Instruments were classified by their primary intended purpose, and reported psychometric evidence and study definitions of quality of life were summarised descriptively. Results Sixty-six records published between 2015 and 2026 identified 16 instruments. Five measured overall quality of life, eight assessed health-related quality of life, health status or functioning, and three were disease-specific. Studies using overall quality of life measures more commonly defined the construct, whereas those using short-form health surveys frequently reported quality of life without conceptual clarification. Validation evidence supported some instruments in adult CHD populations, although the suitability of measures developed for paediatric populations remained uncertain. Conclusion Contemporary CHD research reports conceptually distinct outcomes under the term quality of life, limiting comparability and interpretation. Explicit definitions and instrument selection informed by the intended construct and population are required to strengthen the assessment of patient-reported outcomes.

items.title: Following the Money: How Financial Data Can Transform Mental Health Research and Care.
items.abstract: Money is deeply intertwined with mental health, yet data on financial behavior remain largely absent from mental health assessment and interventions. This column argues that financial data represent an untapped opportunity for mental health support by posing the following questions: Can financial behavior be measured objectively? Would patients share such data? Do clinically meaningful signals exist? Recent studies involving >1,000 people with bipolar disorder demonstrate that tracking financial decisions is feasible and broadly acceptable; preliminary evidence has also linked spending to mood states. Building on these findings, this column discusses the potential for clinical integration of financial data and outlines responsible development for this emerging field.

items.title: Sharing Lived Experience: An Intentional Approach.
items.abstract: A unique element of peer support is the use of personal narratives to share lived experiences of recovery from behavioral health conditions. Competency in this sharing requires peer support specialists (PSSs) to use intentionality, structure, and reflective practice to safely inspire hope and foster trust among those they serve. Supervision, including reflective practice, feedback, and modeling of effective techniques, is needed to support these specialists. An intentional approach to disclosure helps supervisors and mentors guide PSSs in developing this essential competency. This column outlines an approach to training, mentoring, and providing feedback to equip PSSs with the skills necessary to authentically and effectively share their personal lived experience.

items.title: Epidemiology of Cardiac Structure and Function Among African Caribbeans in Tobago: A Population-based Cohort Study
items.abstract: Background: Individuals of African genetic ancestry are at high risk for heart failure (HF), which is often preceded by cardiac structural and functional abnormalities. Nevertheless, little is known about cardiac structure and function among Afro-Caribbeans residing in Tobago. This study aimed to investigate the epidemiology of cardiac structure and function among African Caribbeans in Tobago. Methods: A total of 924 participants (41-83 years) underwent clinical evaluation and transthoracic echocardiography. Images were analyzed for left ventricular (LV) mass index (MI), left atrial volume index, diastolic dysfunction (DD), LV ejection fraction (LVEF), global longitudinal strain (GLS), E/e′ ratio, E/A ratio, and other echocardiographic measures. Cardiac structure and function were evaluated by age, sex, and HF stage. Results: The mean age was 61.7 years, with 61.4% women, 47.8% obesity, and 20.2% diabetes. Average systolic blood pressure was approximately 140 mmHg, and 76.7% had hypertension. Abnormal LV geometry was present in 77.1% of participants, predominantly concentric remodeling (69.5%). The prevalence of DD was 13.4%, LVEF Conclusions: Women and older adults have higher LV structural abnormalities and DD than men and younger adults. These results will be helpful to inform public health priorities related to cardiovascular health in Tobago.

items.title: Development and community evaluation of continuous pressure monitoring for pressure ulcer prevention and management: protocol for a mixed-methods co-design programme
items.abstract: Pressure ulcers cause substantial preventable harm, reduce quality of life and increased health and care costs. Continuous pressure monitoring (CPM) provides longitudinal information on interface pressure, posture and mobility, but evidence remains limited on its implementation, design requirements, safety and acceptability in community care. The overall aim is to develop and evaluate a theory-informed, co-produced CPM system and implementation strategy for pressure ulcer prevention and management in community settings. This sequential, theory-informed programme will comprise three linked work packages and a supporting technical-development strand. Work package 1 will use realist evaluation involving focus groups, observations and interviews to develop and refine theories explaining how CPM works, for whom and under which community circumstances. Work package 2 will use appreciative inquiry to co-produce design and implementation requirements. Technical development will integrate these requirements with mobility and pressure exposure analytics. Work package 3 is a nine-month, multisite observational mixed-methods evaluation involving 60 adults at risk of, or living with, pressure ulcers and approximately 20 carers, professionals and NHS staff across private homes, care homes and nursing homes. Outcomes will include usability, user experience, technology acceptance, feasibility, implementation, posture and mobility, pressure exposure, skin status, health-related quality of life and safety. The University of Southampton sponsors the programme, with approvals governed through the relevant UK Health Research Authority and research ethics processes. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, stakeholder networks, accessible summaries and patient and public involvement and engagement activities. This multi-site community evaluation will link evidence synthesis, programme theory, co-design, technical analytics and human-factors evaluation, to identify the conditions required for CPM to be usable, acceptable and feasible in community practice, creating the basis for a future definitive evaluation.

items.title: The Impact of Hurricane Helene on the Incidence of Acute Gastrointestinal Illness in North Carolina, US: A Controlled Interrupted Time Series Analysis
items.abstract: In September 2024, Hurricane Helene caused significant flooding in western North Carolina (NC), leading to concerns surrounding water quality, including the risk of acute gastrointestinal illness (AGI). The potential for flooding-related drinking water contamination is exacerbated for private well users, who comprised a large proportion of the population most affected by the hurricane. Here we investigated the impact of Hurricane Helene on AGI and determined if this impact was different in areas with greater proportions of residents using private wells. We used electronic health records from Truveta to identify inpatient and outpatient visits to hospitals for AGI in NC from 2016-2024 at the zip3-by-week level and classified exposure to flooding using satellite-derived flood depth estimates. We conducted a controlled interrupted time series analysis to estimate the effect of the hurricane on the incidence of AGI among flooded zip3 units. From 2017 to 2024, there were approximately 548k AGI visits in NC across 20 zip3 units. Our findings show that the hurricane was associated with positive, insignificant changes in the incidence of AGI three weeks following the hurricane (incidence rate ratio: 1.11 [0.59, 2.07]), controlled for pre-hurricane trends and post-hurricane changes in lesser flooded regions. Results were consistent across several time windows and analyses examining sensitivity to geographic data masking, model specification, and study design. Our findings warrant re-evaluation at finer spatial and temporal scales and examination of other public health impacts of hurricanes, which are expected to increase in severity and frequency in the eastern United States due to climate change.

items.title: Unmet needs of Polish patients with cystic fibrosis seen through the lens of crowdfunding
items.abstract: Medical crowdfunding allows for funding for needs not covered by the local healthcare system. We aimed to characterize the crowdfunding campaigns for the needs of Polish individuals with cystic fibrosis (CF). In our study, we analyzed data from a leading medical crowdfunding webpage in Poland, focusing on campaigns for individual medical needs initiated between 2009 and 2017. We characterized the features of individuals with CF and the declared goals for which the funds from the online campaigns were intended. Of all 2,656 campaigns, 96 (3.6%) were related to individuals with CF. Approximately two-thirds of these campaigns reached their target amount. Individuals with CF primarily raised funds to cover treatment costs, medical equipment, and entertainment. The successful collection had a significantly lower financial target than unsuccessful campaigns. If the receivers were living in a city or fundraising to gather funds for an inhaler, these were also associated with the campaign's success. However, these associations were slightly above the threshold of statistical significance. Crowdfunding campaigns can be an effective funding source for the needs of patients with CF that are not covered by the public healthcare system. Analyzing crowdfunding efforts for specific patient groups can help reveal their unmet health needs.

items.title: Social determination of health and intersectionality in child hunger: A multilevel qualitative comparative case study in Chocó and Risaralda, Colombia
items.abstract: Acute child malnutrition has historically been approached in public health as an individual nutritional deficit, despite its persistence in territories marked by structural inequity. This study analyzed how the general, particular, and singular domains of the social determination of health articulate with the intersectional axes of gender, ethnicity, class, and territory in the social production of child hunger in Chocó and Risaralda, two Colombian departments with a high burden of acute child malnutrition. We conducted a qualitative comparative case study grounded in a socio-critical paradigm and a critical feminist epistemology, based on fieldwork carried out in 2024. In-depth interviews with 28 participants—mothers and caregivers, health workers, and decision-makers—were combined with a field diary and a documentary review. Analysis followed open coding, axial coding, and categorical integration, yielding 722 coded units and 207 analytical categories, which were organized through a convergence matrix across the three domains of social determination and the intersectional axes. In the particular domain, informal work, food restriction, and institutional fragmentation shaped ways of life marked by the feminization of care, while formally established care pathways failed to sustain nutritional recovery. In the singular domain, trajectories of accumulated violence, forced early unions, and female genital mutilation preceded and shaped motherhood under precarious conditions, together with guilt, anguish, and fear produced by the institutional moralization of maternal care. Across domains, structural conditions were subsumed into collective ways of life and embodied in singular trajectories, without cancelling situated forms of agency, resistance, and care. A multilevel integration of social determination and intersectionality allows child hunger to be understood as a historically produced process that simultaneously traverses structures, ways of life, and bodies, and that cannot be resolved through exclusively clinical or welfare-based responses. The proposed model offers a transferable analytical tool for critical public health research seeking to integrate structural, collective, and biographical evidence.

items.title: Motherly Plus: Study Protocol of a Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating a Smartphone-Assisted Single-Session Psychotherapy Intervention for Postpartum Depression
items.abstract: Introduction: Postpartum depression (PPD) is a public health problem, affecting approximately 17% of women worldwide. PPD is associated with significant costs to the healthcare system and impairments for the child. Although evidence shows that psychotherapy and pharmacotherapy are effective in reducing PPD symptoms, access to these treatments is limited, especially in low- and middle-income countries where there is a shortage of professionals and unequal distribution of mental health services. In this context, telehealth, smartphone apps, and brief psychotherapies emerge as viable, low-cost, and potentially scalable alternatives. However, gaps remain regarding the efficacy of single-session psychotherapies for PPD, especially when combined with digital support. Objectives: The primary objective is to test the efficacy of an intervention package combining single-session psychotherapy with subsequent self-guided use of a smartphone app for the treatment of PPD. Secondary objectives are to investigate moderators, mediators, and specific intervention processes. Method: A randomized clinical trial in which 104 women aged 18-40 years, up to 12 months postpartum, with a diagnosis of PPD will be randomized to the intervention (single-session psychotherapy supported by the Motherly app) or a waitlist. Participants in the intervention arm will retain access to the app throughout the study; waitlist participants will receive the intervention after post-treatment assessment. Assessments will occur at T1 (week 1, baseline), T2 (week 2, mid-treatment), T3 (week 4, post-treatment), and T4 (week 8, follow-up). The primary outcome will be depression assessed by the QIDS-C16 at T3. Secondary outcomes include anxiety, sleep, parental stress, and self-reported depression. Data will be analyzed using generalized estimating equations (GEE) models considering an intention-to-treat (ITT) perspective. Mediation models will be used to analyze mediators, while interaction models will be used to explore potential moderators. Regression models will be used to analyze the association between specific processes (therapeutic alliance and app engagement) and clinical outcomes. Perspectives: This study has potential public health relevance and innovation by testing an intervention package that combines single-session psychotherapy and technology, with high potential for scalability. Trial registration: clinicaltrials.gov NCT07925762 Key words: Postpartum depression; clinical trial; cognitive-behavior therapy; digital intervention; smartphone app; single session psychotherapy

items.title: Comparative landscape of extracellular vesicles across three pathogenic trematodes identifies a key conserved miRNA cargo involved in host liver fibrosis
items.abstract: Liver fibrosis caused by Schistosoma japonicum, Clonorchis sinensis, and Opisthorchis felineus represents a major global public health burden. Here, we systematically characterized extracellular vesicles (EVs) released by key stages of these parasites and uncovered, for the first time, a conserved repertoire of EV-derived miRNAs shared across all three species. By integrating animal models, single-cell RNA sequencing, and bioinformatic analyses, we comprehensively identified the targetome of miR-36-3p, a cross-species conserved miRNA cargo. Mechanistically, we found that miR-36-3p directly targets Atox1 in Kupffer cells, driving intracellular copper and reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and thereby activating hepatic stellate cells. Strikingly, in vivo delivery of an AAV8-encoded miR-36-3p sponge markedly attenuated liver fibrosis across all three infection models. Collectively, these findings establish a conserved, parasite-derived EV miRNA cargo as a previously unrecognized driver of host liver pathology and identify it as a promising therapeutic target for preventing parasite-induced liver fibrosis.
