items.title: MAGNITUDE OF METABOLIC SYNDROME AND ITS ASSOCIATED FACTORS AMONG PATIENTS WITH TYPE 2 DIABETES MELLITUS WHO ARE ON FOLLOW-UP AT ASELLA REFERRAL AND TEACHING HOSPITAL DIABETIC CLINIC, ASELLA, OROMIA, ETHIOPIA IN 2022.
items.abstract: Background: - Type 2 Diabetes mellites and Metabolic syndrome are global public health problems, and their burden is rising, particularly in developing countries. Metabolic syndrome (syndrome X, insulin resistance syndrome) consists of a constellation of metabolic abnormalities that confer increased risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and diabetes mellitus. There are limited data on prevalence of metabolic syndrome in type II DM patients in Ethiopia and in the horn of Africa at large, and no research has been done in our institution on this topic. Objective: - To determine the prevalence of metabolic syndrome and its associated factors in patients with type 2 diabetes on follow up at Asella Referral and Teaching Hospital diabetes follow up clinic, Asella, Oromia, Ethiopia. Method: - Cross-sectional, prospective, hospital-based survey was conducted to assess the prevalence of metabolic syndrome and its associated factors in type II DM patients among those who visited diabetic follow-up clinic of Asella referral and teaching Hospital. All type II DM patients, who visited the diabetic follow-up clinic in the study period was included in the study. 285 participants were selected using systemic random sampling technique. Data was collected from patients and their chart and filled on a checklist by trained data collectors. Data was entered to epi-data cleared and analyzed by SPSS version 26.0 and Odds ratio with 95% CI and P-value of Results: - Using the NCEP-ATP III criteria the magnitude of Metabolic syndrome was 75.1% in this study. Among the components of Metabolic syndrome high blood pressure was the commonest (70.9%) followed by low HDL Cholesterol (70.5%), high Triglyceride (46%) and high Waist circumference (12.6%) respectively. Female and Male had comparable prevalence of Metabolic syndrome and the study showed that 55.4% of participants were taking Lipid lowering medications. Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed four factors; frequency of taking Meat (AOR = 2.47; 95% CI = 1.323-4.6), Alcohol intake (AOR = 2.79; 95% CI = 1.146-6.806), total Cholesterol level (AOR = 2.72; 95% CI = 1.023-7.224) and LDL Cholesterol level (AOR = 2.31; 95% CI = (1.029-5.161) were significantly associated with Metabolic syndrome according to this study. Conclusion: - In this study the magnitude of Metabolic syndrome was found to be 75.1% and the associated factors were Alcohol intake, Frequency of taking Meat, Total and LDL Cholesterol level. Recommendation: - Counseling of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus patients on the need of decreasing Alcohol and Meat consumption and physicians need to improve the habit of prescribing Lipid lowering medication. Key words: Metabolic syndrome, Type II diabetes, Cardiovascular disease, Waist circumference, Alcohol intake, Cholesterol level.

items.title: Predicting county-level opioid overdose mortality in Ohio through multimodal data: A spatiotemporal study using toxicology and EMS indicators, 2020-2024
items.abstract: Background: The opioid crisis is the leading driver of overdose mortality in the United States. While overdose deaths have decreased in recent years, the reporting lag in official overdose deaths presents a hurdle in implementing public health interventions to combat the crisis. Objective To address these data-reporting delays and improve prediction during highly volatile periods, we developed a Bayesian hierarchical spatiotemporal model using real-time drug overdose data sources to predict quarterly overdose deaths across Ohio counties from 2020 to 2024. Methods We implemented a Bayesian spatiotemporal model using Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation (INLA). Rapid-reporting surveillance metrics, specifically urine drug test (UDT) positivity rates and Emergency Medical Services (EMS) naloxone administration events, were incorporated as fixed covariates. Models were constructed stepwise by first optimizing the spatiotemporal random effect structure and then sequentially adding fixed effects to minimize prediction error. A rolling training window was implemented and evaluated across different training window sizes. Results were assessed overall and stratified by county population size. Results We found that the optimal predictive model structure consists of a two-year training window, a random walk temporal effect, a structured spatial effect, and fentanyl UDT positivity and EMS naloxone events. Incorporating these UDT and EMS data significantly enhanced predictive performance, with the most pronounced accuracy gains occurring during the unprecedented overdose increase associated with the COVID-19 pandemic in the second quarter of 2020. While predictive performance was highly robust in large, urban counties, predictive capability in smaller counties was limited by low data availability. Conclusion Our spatiotemporal prediction model successfully bridges the administrative reporting lags and offers near-real-time quarterly overdose prediction. The study also showed that integration of real-time data sources is especially beneficial for capturing sudden, volatile spikes in overdose deaths.

items.title: Title “Not in my backyard”: Online narratives of societal perceptions and skepticism towards emerging infectious disease research
items.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the increasing threat of emerging infectious diseases (EID) and the power of a unified response from scientific institutions for generating public health solutions. Societal perceptions of scientific research directly impact the success and sustainability of public health initiatives. As potential for zoonotic EIDs remains, it is vital to consider societal perceptions of the scientific research enterprise. This study characterizes the online narratives regarding EID research involving animal models. The scope of these narratives spanned n=31 news sources and n=140 social media sources discussing high-containment research facilities in the U.S. Mountain West. These narratives are compared across news and social media, pre- and post-COVID-19, and for research involving bats versus non-bat animal models. A thematic analysis of news media reveals narratives of “not in my backyard” (NIMBY) and distrust of government and universities. A content analysis of social media posts and comments highlights public frustration due to uncertainty regarding EID research, primarily post-COVID-19. These perceptions reveal potential avenues for misinformation correction and better public engagement about EID and animal research.

items.title: Children as Key Stakeholders in Combating Antimicrobial Resistance: Lessons from UK-Nigeria School Outreach During World Antimicrobial Awareness Week 2024
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a serious global health threat accounting for millions of deaths yearly, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Public health initiatives are being implemented to create awareness on AMR, but educational interventions targeting children remain limited despite their critical role in shaping household awareness. Early engagement through schools offers a unique opportunity to shape health-related knowledge, attitudes, and behaviours. During World Antimicrobial Awareness Week 2024, a school-based educational intervention was conducted across eight schools in the United Kingdom (n=292) and Nigeria (n=450), reaching 742 pupils aged 8–15 years. The programme combined interactive lessons, handwashing demonstrations, and biofilm-building activities targeting AMR understanding, hygiene self-efficacy, and risk perception. Pre- and post-intervention assessments revealed significant knowledge gains in most schools, with effect sizes ranging from 0.40 to 1.07 (small-to-medium to large) depending on pre-test knowledge levels. In the UK, schools with the highest pre-test scores showed minimal improvement in the post-test assessment, while Nigerian schools demonstrated consistent gains across all schools. Knowledge gains were similar between the two countries, highlighting the effectiveness of participatory, behaviourally informed interventions across diverse contexts. Feedback from students and teachers indicated high engagement, cultural relevance, and acceptability of the programme. These findings suggest that structured AMR education in schools can enhance understanding of microbiology, hygiene, and responsible antimicrobial use, supporting long-term pro-health behaviours. Integrating such programmes into school curricula offers a scalable way to raise early AMR awareness and strengthen community-level stewardship.

items.title: Examining HiTOP Through Naturalistic Symptom Descriptions in Anonymous Online Mental Health Forums: A Mixed-Methods Study Protocol
items.abstract: AbstractBackground: The Hierarchical Taxonomy of Psychopathology (HiTOP) organises covarying symptoms and maladaptive traits into transdiagnostic dimensions to address limitations of categorical diagnosis. Naturalistic symptom descriptions may complement structured assessments. Objective: This protocol describes a reproducible mixed-methods workflow to derive symptom indicators from forum posts and examine their organisation relative to HiTOP. Methods and analysis: The target sample is 80,000 public Reddit posts. After local de-identification, a large language model (LLM) will extract symptom labels and supporting paraphrases. Two human experts will independently review outputs for up to 250 posts. Three embedding models will flag potentially equivalent symptom labels for local LLM assessment. Two experts will qualitatively review the most frequent canonical symptom labels (at least 1,000) and develop a codebook of symptom categories, continuing until a prespecified saturation criterion is met. An LLM will assign canonical symptom labels to these categories, producing binary post-level indicators. Multiverse-inspired structural analyses will compare network, component, factor, and clustering representations across discovery, internal tuning, and holdout partitions. Evaluation will assess interpretability, stability, and agreement with expert mapping to HiTOP. Supplementary analyses will include agent-assisted exploration, codebook application to DepressionEmo and the Reddit Mental Health Dataset, and pooled integrative analysis that may include additional comparable corpora. Discussion: The study will examine whether symptom co-expression within posts forms interpretable patterns corresponding to HiTOP.Ethics: The Ethics Committee of Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin approved the study (EA2/274/25). The study was preregistered on 8 May 2026 (German Clinical Trials Register, DRKS00040244). Keywords: Hierarchical Taxonomy of Psychopathology, natural language processing, large language models, Reddit, mixed methods, study protocol

items.title: Reward sensitivity is associated with gambling participation, and financial vulnerability with problem gambling in U.S. adults
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of legal and online gambling in the United States has renewed public-health concern about gambling participation and gambling-related problems. These outcomes may have partly distinct correlates, yet they are rarely examined together within a single sample. We therefore tested whether demographic, contextual, financial, and psychological factors differentiated non-gamblers, recreational gamblers, and participants classified as problem gamblers. A nationally recruited, cross-sectional sample of 726 U.S. adults aged 18–80 completed measures of gambling behavior and symptoms, socioeconomic and financial vulnerability, mental health, loneliness, risk-taking, reward sensitivity, and neighborhood conditions. After adjustment for age and gender, reward sensitivity differed across all three groups, with the lowest scores among non-gamblers and the highest among problem gamblers. In adjusted models, reward sensitivity distinguished gamblers from non-gamblers. Among gamblers, socioeconomic deprivation and financial-exploitation vulnerability distinguished problem from recreational gambling, whereas reward sensitivity did not. In exploratory analyses, financial-exploitation vulnerability was more strongly associated with symptom severity among problem gamblers than among recreational gamblers after correction for multiple comparisons. Evidence for a similar group difference in socioeconomic deprivation depended on the scoring method. Reward sensitivity was positively associated with symptom severity at both low and high loneliness, with a stronger association at high loneliness. These findings suggest that gambling participation and problem gambling have partly distinct correlates: reward sensitivity distinguished gamblers from non-gamblers but not problem from recreational gamblers in fully adjusted models, whereas socioeconomic and financial vulnerability more clearly differentiated problem from recreational gambling.

items.title: Trends and associated factors of Premature or Early Menopause Among Bangladeshi Women: a repeated cross-sectional analysis of six Bangladesh Demographic and Health Surveys
items.abstract: Abstract Objective Premature menopause (PM; menopause before age 40) and early menopause (EM; menopause at ages 40–44) are associated with increased risks of cardiovascular disease, osteoporosis, adverse psychosocial outcomes, and many other long-term illnesses. Despite Bangladesh's rapid demographic and fertility transitions, national evidence on PM and EM remains limited. This study examined trends and associated factors of PM or EM among Bangladeshi women over the past two decades. Methods We analyzed data from six rounds (2004–2022) of the Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey, including 41,697 ever-married women aged 30–44 years. The outcome variable was premature or early menopause (PM/EM) was defined as menopause before age 45 years, based on ≥ 6 months (according to DHS) of amenorrhea (excluding pregnancy and postpartum amenorrhea) or self-reported menopause/hysterectomy. Weighted prevalence estimates were calculated across survey years. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify associated factors. Results PM/EM prevalence increased between 2004 and 2014 and subsequently declined by 2022 (2004: 10.0% to 2014: 14.9% to 2022: 11.0%), although level remains substantial. PM (6.5% to 10.0% to 6.7%) and EM (19.3% to 26.1% to 22.5%) prevalence individually followed the same pattern. Adolescent first birth showed consistently significant association PM/EM over time (AOR in 2004: 0.97; in 2022: 0.60). Contraceptive use and higher educational attainment were associated with lower odds of PM/EM. Conclusions PM/EM remains a public health concern in Bangladesh. Persistent disparities by education and birth history highlight the importance of policies promoting female education and delaying early marriage and childbearing to reduce early reproductive aging and long-term health risks.

items.title: Protocol for a qualitative systematic review and thematic synthesis of caregivers’ perceptions and practices of fall prevention among older adults with prior falls
items.abstract: Abstract Background Falls among older adults are common, potentially preventable, and remain a major global public health concern. Despite the availability of evidence-based fall prevention guidelines and interventions, falls continue to occur frequently among older adults, particularly among those with a history of previous falls. Falls may have substantial physical, psychological, and social consequences for both older adults and their caregivers. Caregivers play an important role in supporting and implementing fall prevention strategies; however, their perceptions, experiences, and caregiving practices may influence the effectiveness of these interventions. To date, no qualitative evidence synthesis has specifically explored caregivers’ perceptions and practices regarding fall prevention among older adults with prior falls. This review therefore aims to synthesize qualitative evidence relating to caregivers’ experiences, perceptions, and practices of fall prevention for older adults with a history of falls. Methods/design: This protocol has been developed in accordance with the PRISMA-P guidelines and the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology for qualitative systematic reviews and meta-aggregation. A comprehensive search will be conducted across the databases MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, PsycINFO, PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, CNKI, WanFang, and VIP from database inception onwards. The search strategy will incorporate subject headings, index terms, and relevant free-text terms in both English and Chinese. Two reviewers will independently screen titles, abstracts, and full-text articles according to predefined eligibility criteria. Data extraction and methodological quality appraisal will also be conducted independently by two reviewers. Qualitative findings will be synthesized using the JBI meta-aggregation approach, and the results will be presented in a narrative format. Discussion This qualitative systematic review aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of caregivers’ perspectives, experiences, and practices related to fall prevention among older adults with a history of falls. By synthesizing qualitative evidence across diverse care contexts, the review may identify barriers, facilitators, and contextual factors influencing the implementation of fall prevention strategies. The findings are expected to inform clinical practice, guideline implementation, and policy development, and may support the design of more person-centered and feasible interventions to reduce recurrent falls among older adults. Systematic review registration: PROSPERO CRD42024545563

items.title: ArcTrace: Black-Box Ownership Verification of LLM-Based Forecasting Models via Learned Numeric Preferences
items.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) adapted into numeric forecasters increasingly inform decisions in energy, transport, finance and public health. Enforcing trade-secret protection, model licenses and the traceability expected by recent AI regulations requires tracing such a model to its source after it has been copied, fine-tuned or imitated, yet a suspicious forecasting service reveals nothing but numbers. In this paper, we revisit black-box model watermarking for LLM-based forecasters. We argue that a watermark survives clean adaptation only when the model learns it as a strong, recurring part of ordinary forecasting. Direct ports of existing designs fail this condition, because clean adaptation erases behavior outside ordinary forecasting and keyed, context-dependent preferences are learned only weakly from decimal text. We further reveal a bias--evidence inversion, which identifies the keyed rule rather than the returned output as the unit of ownership evidence. Motivated by these findings, we propose ArcTrace, which embeds a watermark by modifying the forecaster's conditional digit distribution and counts its evidence per keyed rule, and we analyze the calibration and detection power of its test. Across 32 owner keys and 17 models from six series, ArcTrace detects the watermark for all 32 owner keys, verifies ownership from 375 forecasts on synthetic histories, and persists through quantization, light fine-tuning, key overwriting and distillation, at a cost of about 1\% in mean absolute scaled error on the development data and a median of 6.5\% across 17 models. These results suggest the provenance of a deployed forecaster can be established from numbers it returns.

items.title: Policy-Oriented Multiresolution CNN–Transformer Fusion for Synoptic-Scale PM₂.₅ Prognostication and Low-Emission Zone Stratification in Hypermetropolitan Aerosol Regimes
items.abstract: Abstract Megacities represent a paradigmatic nexus of anthropogenic density and resource accretion, wherein the proliferation of PM₂.₅ aerosols, characterized by their polymorphic chemical speciation, exerts multifactorial pathophysiological burdens on urban cohorts. Prevailing regulatory frameworks, which homogenize monitoring and management protocols across urban hierarchies, fail to accommodate the spatiotemporal heterogeneities inherent to hypermetropolises, where the confluence of stationary point sources and high‑flux mobile emitters generates non‑Gaussian dispersion fields. To redress this lacuna, we introduce a hybrid CNN-Transformer ensemble engineered to concurrently resolve high‑frequency, localized emission pulses via hierarchical convolutional filters and protracted autocorrelative regimes through multi‑head self‑attention layers. Leveraging a sextennial dataset of meteorological covariates and station‑based PM₂.₅ readings across thirteen delineated districts of the Tehran megacity, our model extends predictive horizons to 72 hours, quadrupling the temporal ambit of antecedent sub‑6‑hour studies, while preserving sub‑3 µg/m³ error magnitudes. The network attained an R² exceeding 0.95, an RMSE of 3.372 µg/m³, and an MSE of 11.37 µg/m³, marking the most stringent performance metrics reported to date in urban air‑quality prognostication. Spatioclustering analyses revealed discordance between administrative zoning and aerosol concentration gradients, underscoring the necessity for delineating LEZs within megacities to enable targeted mitigation. Moreover, the model’s granular outputs facilitate the construction of dynamic public‑health protection maps, enabling preemptive exposure abatement for vulnerable demographics, particularly pediatric cohorts, and the temporal‑spatial identification of low‑pollution refugia. these findings advance the methodological frontier of precision air quality management and furnish a robust decision‑support scaffold for the formulation of bespoke regulatory standards tailored to the idiosyncratic pollutant topographies of megacities.

items.title: Burden of TB cases in a conflict-affected region in Central Myanmar: A secondary data analysis from a TB program
items.abstract: Abstract Background Tuberculosis (TB) control in Myanmar has been severely affected by ongoing political unrest, particularly in conflict-affected and hard-to-reach areas where healthcare services have been disrupted. This study assessed TB case-finding modalities and diagnostic services in 25 conflict-affected townships in Central Myanmar. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted using secondary data from individuals screened for TB registered at general health clinics in conflict-affected areas between October 2023 and December 2024. TB screening was primarily symptom-based, with chest X-ray (CXR) performed where available. Diagnosis was based on smear microscopy and confirmed by rapid molecular testing when accessible. In areas without rapid molecular testing, bacteriological confirmation relied solely on smear microscopy, while clinical diagnosis was based on CXR. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 25 and R version 4.4.3. Results A total of 4,558 individuals were screened for TB. Overall, 348 (7.6%) individuals were diagnosed with TB, with a mean age of 46.9 years; 78% were males. Among diagnosed cases, 205 (59%) were bacteriologically confirmed and 143 (41%) were clinically diagnosed. Of the bacteriologically confirmed cases, 78% were aged 15–64 years. Conclusion Significant gaps in case detection practices were identified, with diagnosis largely dependent on smear microscopy and limited access to rapid molecular testing. Reliance on symptom-based screening and smear microscopy alone likely leaves many TB cases undetected, and sustaining community transmission. Expanding access to CXR and rapid molecular testing including recent WHO-approved near-point-of-care tests, adaptive community-led service delivery model and minimal standardized routine program data recording and reporting are public health priorities to improve case detection, ensure continuity of care, and enhance outcomes in conflict-affected settings.

items.title: Global Research Trends on Antimicrobial Resistance Transmission in Broiler Chickens and Poultry Products—A Bibliometric and Scientometric Analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in broiler chickens and poultry products is an important research concern at the intersection of veterinary medicine, food safety, microbiology, and public health. Despite increasing scholarly attention, the development, intellectual structure, and collaborative patterns of this research area remain insufficiently characterized. This study examines global research trends on AMR transmission in broiler chickens and poultry products through a bibliometric and scientometric analysis of Scopus-indexed literature published between 1984 and 2025. A total of 451 documents from 234 sources were analyzed using performance indicators and science-mapping techniques to examine publication growth, citation patterns, authorship, geographical and institutional contributions, journal distribution, and thematic relationships. Results revealed an annual publication growth rate of 12.07%, an average of 67.98 citations per document, and an international co-authorship rate of 45.68%. Research production was predominantly collaborative, with an average of 5.98 co-authors per document. The United States and the United Kingdom led in total citations, whereas Sweden, Switzerland, South Africa, and Pakistan demonstrated comparatively high citation intensity relative to their publication output. Journal distribution followed Bradford's Law, identifying 19 core sources among 234 publication outlets. Overall, the findings provide a structured overview of the evolution, scholarly influence, and intellectual organization of research on poultry-associated AMR. This study offers a bibliometric foundation for identifying established research areas, strengthening international collaboration, and guiding future interdisciplinary investigations. The findings represent the Scopus-indexed literature and do not directly measure AMR prevalence or establish biological transmission pathways.

items.title: Problematic Media Use Measure – Short Form in a Polish Sample of Children: Adaptation, Validation, and Association with Parental Problematic Internet Use
items.abstract: Abstract Problematic Media Use (PMU) has become a global public health concern. Children are beginning to use digital media at increasingly younger ages, which has led to growing research interest in PMU during early developmental stages. The aim of the study was the Polish adaptation and validation of the PMUM-SF scale. Additionally, the prevalence of PMU among children aged 4–11 years was examined in a large, representative sample, along with its association with parental PIU. The study included 1,692 parents of children aged 4–11 years (respondents aged 18–70; M = 37.29; SD = 6.85), including 62.5% women, in a nationwide representative quantitative study. Confirmatory factor analysis supported a unidimensional model with acceptable fit [χ²(27) = 429.916; p 0.90). Criterion validity was confirmed, and its interpretative utility was enhanced through standard-ten normalization. items.title: Can sexuality teaching be monitored? An analysis of curricular documentation among Brazilian public medical schools
items.abstract: Abstract Background Sexuality is part of clinical care and of health policy, yet how Brazilian medical schools teach it is poorly documented, particularly at state universities. Without public curricular information, national monitoring is not possible. We assess whether sexuality teaching in undergraduate medical programs can be monitored from public documents, to characterize and compare its curricular inclusion at Brazilian federal and state universities. Methods We conducted a national documentary study of institutional records available through August 2026. Programs/campuses were first classified as having sufficient or insufficient evidence. Those with sufficient evidence were then classified by form of inclusion, required and total provision, mode of incorporation, longitudinal integration, confirmation of teaching delivery, administrative affiliation, and region. Results Among 91 universities and 124 programs/campuses, only 21 had public documentation sufficient for classification. In these, sexuality was integrated into required components in 15, offered as a standalone elective course in five, and offered as a standalone required course in one. Seventeen had an explicit required offering, four had only elective provision, and teaching delivery was confirmed in seven. Standalone courses were found only at federal universities, whereas classifiable state-university records contained only integrated content. Most documented offerings appeared in a single curricular period. Detailed syllabi varied considerably; most centered on women’s health, reproduction, and family planning, although some also addressed diversity, violence, clinical communication, rights, and primary care. Conclusions For most public programs/campuses, the available documents do not allow sexuality teaching to be verified, and our findings describe what the formal curriculum shows, not the true prevalence of teaching. Where the curriculum could be characterized, sexuality was usually integrated into other components, concentrated in one period, and unevenly specified. More transparent curricular documentation is a precondition for curricular review and for assessing whether national competencies reach all medical students.

items.title: Quantifying Food and Beverage Marketing Exposure Among US Adults: Insights from Facebook Data Donation
items.abstract: Abstract As digital media reshape where and how people encounter product marketing, measuring exposure to branded food marketing on platforms like Facebook is essential for public health surveillance and policy. We demonstrate a data‑donation approach to quantify paid food and beverage advertising exposure on Facebook over a seven‑day period. Among 58 respondents who viewed any Facebook advertisements, 51 (80.3%) saw at least one food or beverage advertisement. Of 607 distinct advertisements coded, 23.7% promoted fast‑food restaurants; many promoted products high in free sugars, sodium, or total fats. On days of Facebook use among the respondents, mean exposure to branded food or beverage advertisements was 3.54 per day per person (median = 1.25). Users averaged 4.6 days/week of platform use—equating to roughly 847 advertisement exposures per year (median = 299). Donated social media data provide a feasible, ethical, platform‑specific method to monitor digital food marketing and inform the development of policy aimed at reducing exposure to nutritionally poor products.

items.title: AutoMeta: LLM Agent-based Automated Meta-Analysis in Public Health
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Meta-analysis supports public health decision-making, yet conducting and updating reviews remain time- and labour-intensive. Although large language model (LLM) agent systems have been proposed to automate literature reviews, heterogeneous exposure definitions, effect measures and covariate-adjustment models pose challenges for public health evidence synthesis. Methods: We present AutoMeta, an LLM-based agentic workflow for public health meta-analysis that uses stage-specific instructions to guide planning and tool use across literature search, screening, data extraction and statistical synthesis, with structured outputs linking each stage. To address the heterogeneity of public health evidence, it expands exposure terminology, structures eligibility assessments, links extracted estimates to their analytical context, and uses tested functions for effect-size transformation and synthesis. For systematic evaluation, we constructed AutoMetaBench from 27 systematic reviews spanning environmental health, nutrition and health behaviours, encompassing 421 included-study records, 4164 data fields and 95 effect units. We used this benchmark to assess performance at each stage and end to end. Results: AutoMeta improved evidence coverage and synthesis accuracy while supporting rapid end-to-end execution. In stage-specific evaluations, it outperformed the respective comparators across all four stages, achieving 93.1% search recall, 94.8% recall among the top 50 ranked records, and 93.6% data extraction accuracy. Agreement with reference pooled effects and 95% confidence intervals reached 96.8% and 95.8%, respectively. Across 27 end-to-end tasks, AutoMeta reproduced reference pooled effects and both 95% confidence interval bounds within 5% relative error in 85.2% of tasks, compared with 7.4% for the single-agent comparator, while taking an average of only 26 minutes per task. Conclusions: AutoMeta demonstrates substantial advantages in evidence synthesis and statistical analysis for public health meta-analysis. Its LLM-based agentic workflow improves synthesis efficiency and accuracy, while AutoMetaBench provides a dedicated benchmark for the systematic evaluation of automated methods. These contributions advance automated public health evidence synthesis and support timely evidence updates.

items.title: Effectiveness of Husband-Involved Maternity Education on Skilled Delivery Service Utilization in Rural Communities of Central Ethiopia: A Cluster-Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: In low-income countries, skilled delivery service utilization remains disproportionately low among rural women, resulting in a high rate of preventable maternal and neonatal mortality. Poor husband involvement in maternity care is one of the major contributing factors in Ethiopia. Hence, the purpose of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of husband-involved maternity education on skilled delivery service utilization in rural communities of central Ethiopia. A two-arm parallel-group cluster-randomized controlled trial was carried out among couples in the rural community of Central Ethiopia. The intervention group received group maternity education and individual home visits. A total of 496 couples from 16 clusters were randomly assigned to either the intervention (n=248) or the control group (n=248). A generalized estimating equation analysis was done to evaluate the intervention effectiveness. At the end line, 97.9% of the couples in the intervention group and 98.7% of the couples in the control group were available for analysis. There were no significant differences in baseline characteristics between the control and intervention groups. SDSU was significantly higher among pregnant women who received HIME intervention than those who did not receive the interventions, with a net effect of 21% (95% CI 18.7% - 23.2%, p < 0.001). In the GEE model, the SDSU was a 2-fold increase compared to the control group (AOR: 2.435, 95% CI 1.531, 3.874). This research indicates that involving husbands in the maternity education has a great effect on improving skilled delivery service utilization among pregnant women.

items.title: Dietary anthocyanidin intake and incident autoimmune hypothyroidism: prospective and multi-omic analyses in UK Biobank.
items.abstract: Anthocyanidins have antioxidant and immunomodulatory properties, but prospective evidence linking dietary intake to autoimmune hypothyroidism remains limited. We examined this association in 118 724 UK Biobank adults with at least two valid 24 h dietary recalls. Follow-up began at the last recall; 2350 events occurred over a median of 13.28 years. In sex-stratified multivariable Cox models, participants in the highest intake category had a lower hazard than those consuming ≤1 mg d -1 (HR 0.75; 95% CI 0.65-0.87; P for trend P for trend = 0.005). For nonalcoholic-source intake, the highest-category HR was 0.95 (95% CI 0.83-1.08; P for trend = 0.216). Among 247 nuclear magnetic resonance biomarkers measured after dietary assessment, five fatty-acid measures and two small-LDL lipid-composition measures met the FDR criterion after adjustment for recruitment biomarker values and ethanol dose. Among 73 807 genetically eligible participants, neither thyroid polygenic score showed evidence of interaction with intake. Higher anthocyanidin intake was associated with a lower hazard of autoimmune hypothyroidism and subsequent lipid-related biomarker differences. Residual confounding and uncertainty about nonalcoholic sources limit causal interpretation.

items.title: Terminology Without Consensus: A Thematic Analysis of Nomenclature Choice and Program Structure Among Expanded EMS Programs in a Single State.
items.abstract: Objectives Expanded emergency medical services (E-EMS) programs, such as mobile integrated health care (MIH) and community paramedicine (CP), are increasingly common in the United States (U.S.). Although an international consensus definition exists specifically for CP, the terminology used by active U.S. E-EMS programs is poorly described, yet has important implications for program visibility, stakeholder engagement, evaluation, and policy. We sought to characterize how E-EMS programs in a single state describe themselves and factors associated with their chosen terminology. Methods We conducted a qualitative thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with E-EMS programs in Ohio. We used "E-EMS" as a historically established, neutral umbrella term to avoid prespecifying MIH, CP, or MIH-CP terminology during program identification. We identified E-EMS programs through voluntary reports to Ohio EMS, the Emergency Triage, Treat, and Transport (ET3) roster, publicly reported E-EMS programs on national dashboards, and snowball sampling. An interviewee from each E-EMS program participated in a recorded semi-structured interview focused on E-EMS program terminology, goals, services, and partnerships. Interview transcripts were reviewed by two coders, with discrepancies discussed with and adjudicated by a third reviewer. We used an inductive approach to develop the codebook, followed by thematic analysis to identify themes and subthemes. Results We identified 58 E-EMS programs meeting inclusion criteria; 23 participated and were included in the analysis. Participants described inconsistent use and varying interpretation of common terms such as MIH, CP, or MIH-CP; one in four used alternative terminology (e.g., neighborhood paramedic, EMS outreach). Participants attributed their terminology choices to the variability in MIH definitions and to limited understanding of MIH or CP among patients or external stakeholders. Despite variation in program terminology, program goals were consistently focused on filling unmet community needs, and program services were uniformly described as adaptable and reliant upon partnerships outside of EMS. Conclusions The terminology used to describe E-EMS programs in a single state varied considerably. Despite this, E-EMS program goals and services were consistent, suggesting early convergence upon the core mission of E-EMS programs. Participants perceived inconsistent or unfamiliar terminology as a barrier to patient awareness, referral generation, and stakeholder engagement.

items.title: More Than a Tobacco Problem: Cigarette Smoking as a Marker of Poorer Cardiovascular Health Among Emergency Medical Services Clinicians.
items.abstract: Objectives Emergency medical services (EMS) work demands physical capacity, sustained alertness, and performance under stress, making cardiovascular health a workforce concern, not only a personal one. Cigarette smoking persists in portions of the EMS workforce, but whether it signals cardiovascular risk beyond tobacco exposure itself is unknown. We examined whether cigarette smoking was associated with poorer cardiovascular health across the non-tobacco domains of the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (LE8) framework among nationally certified EMS clinicians. Methods We conducted an observational study and cross-sectional secondary analysis of a voluntary survey offered to nationally certified emergency medical technicians (EMTs), advanced EMTs, and paramedics upon completion of recertification (October 2023-April 2024). To isolate associations beyond tobacco exposure, the primary outcome was a modified composite score (mLE7) averaging the seven non-nicotine LE8 domains (0-100 scale). Ideal cardiovascular health was defined as mLE7 ≥ 80. Multivariable linear and logistic regression models adjusted for demographic, educational, occupational, and organizational characteristics. Results Among 36,436 survey respondents, 7,703 had complete data for smoking status and all seven non-nicotine domains. Of these, 48.8% had never smoked, 45.2% formerly smoked, and 6.0% currently smoked. Mean mLE7 scores were 59.2 among never smokers, 56.9 among former smokers, and 51.5 among current smokers. Compared with never smokers, current smokers had lower adjusted mLE7 scores (β, -6.02; 95% CI, -7.63 to -4.41) and lower odds of ideal cardiovascular health (aOR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.23 to 0.61). Former smokers had intermediate results (β, -1.62; 95% CI, -2.37 to -0.87; aOR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.62 to 0.86). Current smoking was associated with poorer scores across diet, physical activity, sleep, blood pressure, cholesterol, and blood glucose domains (p Conclusions Among EMS clinicians, current cigarette smoking was associated with poorer cardiovascular health across nearly every non-tobacco domain, suggesting that smoking may serve as a readily identifiable marker of broader cardiovascular risk in this workforce. Agencies may consider pairing cessation support with broader cardiovascular health initiatives for clinicians who smoke. Sensitivity analyses addressing missing data yielded consistent results.

items.title: A Pathway Analysis of Factors Associated With Community-Based Home Palliative Care Needs Among Older Adults.
items.abstract: BackgroundCommunity-based home palliative care may improve end-of-life quality for older adults, yet evidence from Chinese primary care settings remains limited.ObjectiveTo examine factors associated with community-based home palliative care needs among older adults and explore their direct and indirect associations using path analysis.MethodsA cross-sectional survey was conducted among 550 older adults from 11 communities in Chongqing where public primary healthcare institutions provided palliative care services. Data were collected using demographic and elder-care questionnaires, a self-developed palliative care needs questionnaire, and the Brief Health Literacy Assessment Scale. Univariate analyses, regression, and path analysis were performed.ResultsEducational attainment, household income, medical insurance type, self-rated health, and health literacy were directly associated with palliative care needs. Education was also indirectly associated with needs through health literacy, income, and insurance participation. Findings highlight the need to strengthen health literacy, insurance support, and primary care capacity.

items.title: Why don't they tell women about these issues? A qualitative investigation into barriers for women seeking help for pelvic floor symptoms.
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo investigate barriers to help-seeking for women with pelvic floor dysfunction.DesignQualitative semi-structured interview and focus group study, reflexive thematic analysis to develop overarching themes.SettingInterviews and focus groups were conducted online, via TEAMs.ParticipantsThirty adult women were recruited by email from an existing database of women who previously self-reported pelvic floor symptoms. Poster adverts and word of mouth were also used to purposefully increase representation. Twelve interviewees took part in three focus groups ( n = 3, n = 4, n = 5). Most, 24 (80%), were white, and six (20%) were Pakistani Muslims. The majority (23, 76.7%) were educated to degree level or above. Other demographics such as age, reported symptoms, and employment status varied.ResultsThree main themes were developed: (1) 'An inevitable part of womanhood: the daily and ongoing challenges of pelvic floor symptoms', the embarrassment of coping with symptoms in public and the inevitability of this as part of women's lives; (2) 'The challenges: stumbling blocks to healthcare', with the key barrier identified as being lack of knowledge regarding symptoms, how and where to seek help; (3) 'The solution: navigating the route to pelvic health', including the need for clear public health messaging and education throughout the lifespan.ConclusionWomen believed that public health messaging regarding women's health issues should include clear, reliable information about pelvic health, delivered at all stages of women's lives. Simple education could empower women to make informed, appropriate choices regarding their pelvic health, thereby improving their quality of life.

items.title: Relationship of Psychosocial Factors and Physical Health Indicators With Mental Health in Elementary School-Aged Children.
items.abstract: PurposeThis study examined (1) associations of social emotional learning (SEL) skills, resilience, vitality, cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF), in-school physical activity (PA), and out-of-school PA with mental health in fourth- and fifth-grade students, and (2) whether these associations differed by gender.DesignCross-sectional study.SettingThis study was conducted at eleven public elementary schools in one of the Mid-West States.Sample815 students in 4th-5th grades voluntarily participate in this study.MeasuresParticipants completed the PACER test for assessing CRF and Qualtrics surveys measuring mental health, SEL skills, resilience, vitality, and PA.AnalysisMultiple linear regression analyses were conducted for the total sample and by gender.ResultsSEL, resilience, vitality, CRF, and both in-school and out-of-school PA were significantly associated with mental health in the total sample (F = 36.89, P 2 = 0.317), boys (F = 19.35, P 2 = 0.317), and girls (F = 18.26, P 2 = 0.334). Key predictors included SEL self-management and relationship skills, vitality, and CRF. Gender differences showed mental health in boys was linked to SEL, vitality, resilience, and out-of-school PA, whereas in girls it was associated with SEL self-awareness and self-management, vitality, and CRF.ConclusionsMental health in children is influenced by social-emotional, psychological, and physical factors, supporting school-based interventions that consider gender differences.

items.title: Age-Related Tibetan-Han Differences in Continuity of Care Among Insured Populations in High-Altitude Western China: Retrospective Longitudinal Observational Study.
items.abstract: Background Continuity of Care (CoC) is an important dimension of health system performance and health equity, reflecting whether individuals can maintain stable and coordinated care relationships over time, rather than merely gaining access to services. Although ethnic differences in CoC have been documented, most existing studies have examined average group differences and have paid limited attention to whether such differences vary across the life course. Claims-based analyses can provide a population-level approach to monitoring CoC and identifying age-specific equity gaps in routine health service use. Objective This study aimed to examine whether Tibetan-Han differences in CoC vary by age among insured populations in high-altitude western China and to assess whether these age-related patterns differ across outpatient, inpatient, chronic disease, and nonchronic disease care settings. Methods We used deidentified health insurance claims data from 3 major cities in high-altitude western China between January 1, 2021, and December 1, 2024. After data cleaning, we constructed a person-year dataset and restricted analyses to individuals with at least 3 annual health care encounters, yielding 850,469 person-years. The Bice-Boxerman CoC index was the primary outcome. Fixed-effects models with year and insurance-region fixed effects included ethnicity, age, age squared, and their interaction terms, adjusting for covariates derived from the Andersen behavioral model. SEs were clustered at the individual level. Subgroup analyses were conducted for outpatient, inpatient, chronic disease, and nonchronic disease samples. Results Mean CoC in the overall sample was 0.52 (SD 0.33). A significant nonlinear interaction between ethnicity and age was observed. Fixed-effects models showed a positive Tibetan coefficient (β=0.0582, P P P P Conclusions Ethnic differences in CoC were age-dependent and nonlinear rather than constant across age groups. Because the study covers 4 calendar years, these age-related associations may also reflect birth-cohort differences and should not be interpreted as within-person aging effects. Policies should pay greater attention to continuity barriers faced by middle-aged and older Tibetan populations.

items.title: Health-related social needs, biological aging, and long-term mortality risk among a nationally representative cohort of cancer survivors.
items.abstract: Background Unmet health-related social needs (HRSNs, such as food insecurity, and inadequate health insurance coverage) may interplay with accelerated biological aging, and lead to higher mortality risks. We examined the associations of HRSNs with long-term mortality risks along with accelerated aging in a nationally representative cohort of cancer survivors. Methods Cancer survivors aged 20-84 years were identified from the 1999-2010 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) with linked mortality follow-up through December 31, 2022. Data on HRSNs, including poverty, lack of home ownership, food insecurity, unemployment, lack of health insurance, and coverage instability, were collected at in-person interviews. Biological aging was measured by a validated composite of biomarkers. Associations of HRSNs with all-cause and cancer-specific mortality risks were examined using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models, and associations of HRSNs with accelerated biological aging were examined using multivariable linear regression models. Results Among 715 cancer survivors (mean age 59.8 at interview, 64.3% women), 261 (36.3%) had any HRSNs and 21 (2.2%) had ≥3 HRSNs. In ≥ 12 years of follow-up, there were 315 deaths, including 103 from cancer. Having ≥3 HRSNs (compared to 0) was associated with an increased risk of death (Hazard Ratio=3.12, 95%CI=1.57-6.21) and 0.46 (95%CI=0.07-0.85) years of accelerated aging. Individual HRSNs were also associated with higher mortality risks and accelerated aging. Conclusions Our findings suggest that proactively addressing HRSNs leveraging the biosocial framework may improve well-being and health outcomes among cancer survivors. Investing in public assistance programs and policy efforts may benefit individuals across the healthcare continuum.

items.title: Renal outcomes in patients affected by familial Mediterranean fever treated with canakinumab: real-life data from the AIDA Network.
items.abstract: Objectives AA amyloidosis is the most severe complication of familial Mediterranean fever (FMF), primarily involving the kidneys. This study evaluates renal outcomes in FMF patients treated with canakinumab, one of the anti-IL-1 agents employed when the patient is colchicine intolerant or resistant. Methods Patients' data were collected in the International Autoinflammatory Disease Alliance (AIDA) Network registry dedicated to monogenic autoinflammatory diseases (MAIDs). Results Overall, 158 FMF patients received canakinumab (CAN) for a mean of 45.2±34.5 months (590.9 patient-years). Amyloidosis was present in 14 patients (8.9%) at baseline, with one new case during follow-up. Proteinuria was observed in 24 cases (15.2%) at baseline, with one new and two recurrent cases. Mean 24-hour proteinuria significantly decreased from 2932±2473 mg to 1593±1135 mg at 12 months and 1149±1125 mg at last assessment (p = 0.005). Reduction correlated with treatment with CAN duration (rho=0.77) and baseline proteinuria (rho=0.91). Linear regression showed a decline of 34.95 mg/24 h per month, greater in the first 12 months, but still significant till the assessment. Kidney failure occurred in 5 (3.2%) at baseline and one new case during treatment. Overall, 28 patients were treated in monotherapy with CAN, and did not develop any kidney complications in a median follow-up period of 24 (3-121, IQR 51) months. Conclusions Canakinumab is effective in FMF patients with kidney involvement, inducing significant and progressive reductions in 24-hour proteinuria in both the short and long term. It seems as well to prevent new renal complications in most patients, also when used as monotherapy.

items.title: Indocyanine Green Assists in Identification of Solid Tumor Pulmonary Metastases.
items.abstract: Background The presence of pulmonary metastases reduces overall survival in patients with certain solid tumors; therefore, surgical clearance is crucial to cure for some types. This multi-institutional prospective study sought to determine the utility and diagnostic accuracy of indocyanine green (ICG) for delineating pulmonary metastases in diverse pediatric, adolescent, and young adult solid cancers. Procedure Thirteen member institutions of the Pediatric Surgical Oncology Research Collaborative administered preoperative ICG to patients undergoing pulmonary metastasectomy for primary or recurrent solid tumor malignancy (2019-2023). Surgeons reported their perspective on ICG utility for pulmonary metastasectomy following each operation. The diagnostic accuracy of ICG fluorescence to identify a pathologically confirmed tumor-containing specimen was determined. Results Of 829 specimens resected during 134 pulmonary metastasectomies (30.6% hepatic, 47.0% osteosarcoma, 17.2% non-osteosarcoma-type sarcomas ["other sarcomas"], 5.2% other non-hepatic and non-sarcoma tumor types ["other tumor types"]). Surgeons reported ICG as helpful in 77.6% of procedures. In 11.9% of cases, ICG identified viable metastases not visualized on preoperative imaging. Adjusted diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity (95% confidence interval [CI]) for metastases from all tumor types was 80.7% (77.9%-83.3%) and 82.5% (78.9%-85.8%), respectively. By primary tumor histology, adjusted accuracy and sensitivity (95% CI) were 83.2% (74.4%-89.9%), 46.7% (28.3%-65.7%) for metastases from other sarcomas, 80.6% (75.3%-85.2%), 95.6% (91.8%-98.0%) for hepatic tumors, 80.6% (76.6%-84.2%), 77.1% (71.4%-82.2%) for osteosarcoma, and 72.7% (49.8%-89.3%), 60.0% (26.2%-87.8%) for other tumor types. Conclusions During pulmonary metastasectomy, adjusted diagnostic accuracy of ICG was 80.7%, and, importantly, 11.9% of metastasectomies contained viable tumors identified by ICG but not by preoperative imaging.

items.title: Changes in Past 30-Day Smoked, Vaped, and Edible Cannabis Use Among Young Adults in Texas, 2022-2026.
items.abstract: Background Little is known about recent trends in cannabis use among young adults residing in states where recreational cannabis remains prohibited. We examined trends in the prevalence of past 30-day cannabis use overall and by mode among Texas college students from 2022-2026. Methods Participants were 48,860 18-25-year-olds attending 11 Texas colleges/universities who completed annual cross-sectional surveys between 2022-2026; and were predominantly female (60.2%) and Hispanic/Latino (41.5%). Generalized linear mixed-effects regressions examined trends in past 30-day any cannabis, smoked, vaped, and edible cannabis use. Models adjusted for sociodemographics, tobacco use, depression, and anxiety. Results Across all outcomes, prevalence increased from 2022-2024, peaked in 2024, and subsequently declined from 2025-2026. The adjusted prevalence of any past 30-day cannabis use more than doubled from 17.4% in 2022 to 39.2% in 2024 before declining to 17.0% in 2026. Similar patterns were observed for smoked, vaped, and edible cannabis. Past 30-day tobacco use and depression were associated with greater odds of cannabis use; associations with age, sex, race/ethnicity, and anxiety varied by outcome. Conclusions Cannabis use among Texas college students varied substantially between 2022-2026. Continued surveillance is needed to understand temporal changes in cannabis use within evolving cannabis policy environments.

items.title: Magneto-Optical Coupling in Chiral Nanoparticles Synergistically Boosts Photothermal Antibacterial Therapy Through Magnetic Plasmon Synergistic Effect.
items.abstract: Antibiotic overuse has triggered a drug-resistant bacteria crisis, severely endangering global public health security. Near-infrared (NIR) light-mediated photothermal therapy based on nanomaterials offers a promising antibiotic-free strategy, but it is often hampered by the intrinsically low photothermal conversion efficiency due to the high damping constant. In this study, magneto-plasmonic nanoparticles with chiral core-shell structure (CAu NRs@Fe 3 O 4 ) were constructed, where the outer magnetic Fe 3 O 4 shell induced a magneto-optical effect. The unique chiral configuration can provide abundant parallel interfacial lattices between Fe 3 O 4 and chiral Au nanorods to introduce stronger coupling, which strengthens the interfacial magneto-optical coupling at the Fe 3 O 4 /Au heterointerface and thus reduces the plasmon damping constant to enable more efficient utilization of incident NIR light. Under the irradiation of 808 nm NIR light, the bactericidal efficiency of CAu NRs@Fe 3 O 4 against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) reached 97.2%. In addition, in vivo wound infection treatment confirmed that wounds can be basically healed within 10 days after treating with CAu NRs@Fe 3 O 4 . Herein, this work not only elucidates the interfacial regulation mechanism of chiral magneto-optical nanomaterials for enhanced photothermal antibiosis, but also establishes potential therapeutic reagents toward drug-resistant bacterial infectious diseases.

items.title: Cannabis Retail Responses to Pregnant Individuals in New York: Business Practices and Policy Compliance.
items.abstract: Background New York State prohibits cannabis retailers from providing individualized medical advice, including to pregnant or nursing individuals. This study sought to understand cannabis retailer recommendations and practices when interacting with pregnant individuals. Methods We conducted cross-sectional mystery-shopper calls to all licensed adult-use cannabis retailers in New York State (February-April 2026). Callers posed as pregnant individuals and retailers were randomized to nausea or non-nausea scripts. Outcomes included retailer characterization of the safety of cannabis use during pregnancy, mode-specific recommendations, and referral to a health care professional. Retailer websites were also reviewed for pregnancy-related warning statements. Multinomial logistic regression examined differences in retailer advice by geography and business characteristics (region, Conditional Adult-Use Retail Dispensary status, and pregnancy-related website warnings), using "deferred medical guidance" as the reference category. Results Among 422 retailers who were called, 3% indicated cannabis use during pregnancy was safe, 51% advised it was unsafe, 12% expressed uncertainty, and 35% deferred medical guidance. Thirty percent suggested differences in safety by mode of use with edibles most endorsed as safer (27%) and smoking most identified as harmful (22%). Over half of retailers (54%) recommended consulting a health care professional without prompting, and 39% did so only after prompting. No significant differences were observed by script assignment. Retailer advice differed significantly by region ( P Conclusions Cannabis retailer messaging during pregnancy was variable but largely aligned with regulatory and public health guidance, with most retailers advising against use or deferring medical guidance. A smaller proportion provided inconsistent or unclear recommendations. These findings suggest overall compliance alongside remaining gaps in standardization, highlighting the need for clearer guidance to ensure consistent, evidence-based communication in retail settings.

items.title: Data quality assessment of maternal and newborn indicators from District Health Information Software 2 in five African countries for the period 2014-2023.
items.abstract: Background Tracking progress of sustainable development goal (SDG) targets requires robust monitoring systems, yet data quality remains challenging across sub-Saharan Africa. Most countries rely on aggregated data from District Health Information Software 2 (DHIS2) or surveys to track maternal, newborn and child health (MNCH) indicators. We evaluated MNCH data quality in DHIS2 across Ghana, Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, and Zimbabwe (2014-2023). Methods We analysed 16 ENAP-aligned indicators and their 29 corresponding data elements captured in DHIS2 across health facility levels. We applied the WHO Data Quality Review framework to assess availability, reporting completeness, internal consistency (ratio-based validation metrics and temporal trends), and external consistency (comparison with UN Inter-agency Group for Child Mortality Estimation (UN IGME), Maternal Mortality Estimation Inter-Agency Group (MMEIG), and World Health Organization Global Health Observatory data). Results Of 29 data elements, Uganda had highest availability (72-76% during 2020-2023), followed by Kenya (62-66%), Tanzania (52%), and Ghana and Zimbabwe (41% each). Reporting completeness varied substantially: Tanzania achieved >95% facility reporting across all levels, while other countries showed disparities between hospitals and lower-level facilities. Internal consistency revealed problematic patterns for mortality-related ratios in Ghana (stillbirth-to-neonatal mortality ratios reaching 5.0-12.5) and Kenya (KMC-to-low birthweight ratios >2.0). After adjusting DHIS2 estimates for facility birth coverage, stillbirth rates generally exceeded or matched UN IGME estimates, whereas maternal mortality ratios showed substantial underreporting relative to MMEIG estimates. Ghana showed the closest MMR alignment and Kenya the largest discrepancy. Neonatal mortality was underreported in Ghana and Uganda but appeared higher than UN IGME estimates in Tanzania, a finding sensitive to aggregation method. Conclusions DHIS2 data quality varies substantially across countries, with country-specific challenges in availability, completeness and consistency. Strengthening facility-level data capture and developing an MNCH data quality module are crucial for improving data reliability.

items.title: Culturally Responsive Smokeless Tobacco Cessation in Dental Practice: A Qualitative Study of Practitioner Perspectives from the South Texas Oral Health Network.
items.abstract: Smokeless tobacco (SLT) remains a significant public health concern associated with adverse oral and systemic health outcomes. However, the use of culturally specific products such as gutka, naswar, and betel quid remains understudied in dental settings despite the important role of oral health providers in prevention and cessation. This qualitative study explored dental practitioners' knowledge, attitudes, and clinical practices regarding culturally specific SLT use and cessation, with a focus on training needs, system-level barriers, and opportunities to improve culturally responsive care. Twenty-five dentists and dental hygienists participated in four virtual focus groups conducted through the South Texas Oral Health Network (STOHN), a Practice-Based Research Network between March and July 2024. Discussions were guided by the 5As framework and analyzed using inductive thematic analysis. Six themes emerged: training gaps, system barriers, patient education needs, cultural sensitivity and provider self-efficacy, practitioner perceptions of patient receptiveness, and health risks associated with SLT use. Although participants demonstrated awareness of smokeless tobacco-related health risks and routinely initiated cessation discussions, limited familiarity with culturally specific products, lack of tailored resources, insufficient referral and follow-up systems, and low confidence in addressing culturally embedded tobacco use constrained comprehensive cessation support. Participants also emphasized the value of technology-enabled and patient-centered approaches to improve engagement. These findings suggest that dental practitioners are well-positioned to address SLT use but require additional training, system-level supports, and culturally responsive resources to strengthen cessation efforts and reduce tobacco-related disease burden in increasingly diverse populations.

items.title: Association of Medications for Opioid Use Disorder Use With Addiction Medicine Consultation and Hospital Service Line: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Background Opioid use disorder (OUD) is a major public health challenge. Medications for OUD (MOUD) are effective and life-saving treatments. Our objective was to examine the frequency of MOUD treatment among OUD patients at our institution over the past 6 years. Methods A retrospective cohort study conducted at an academic, tertiary care hospital located in the Midwest from July 2018 to June 2024. Patients aged 18 to 85 years old were included if they were hospitalized at our hospital, had an International Classification of Diseases, 10th revision diagnosis for an opioid-related disorder, or a positive urine drug screen for fentanyl during the encounter or up to 6 months prior to the encounter. Descriptive statistics and multivariable logistic regression were used to examine predictors of MOUD use. Results We identified 5919 patient encounters. Patients were predominantly between 27 and 59 years old (3890, 66.2%), non-white (2948, 50.9%), and male (3350, 56.6%). A minority of patient encounters received MOUD (1228, 20.7%). Ages 27 to 59, white race, Medicaid insurance status, and Elixhauser Comorbidity Index were associated with MOUD treatment. Addiction medicine (AM) consultation was strongly associated with MOUD treatment (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 4.43, 95% CI 3.64-5.4, P P P P Conclusions A minority of hospitalized patients with OUD received MOUD. Age, race, insurance status, Elixhauser Comorbidity Index, discharge specialty service, AM consult, and discharge after the Drug Enforcement Administration X-waiver removal were associated with inpatient MOUD treatment. Future research should explore how clinicians can collaborate across specialties to improve MOUD implementation.

items.title: The associations of outdoor and indoor air pollution with cognitive function among older adults in China.
items.abstract: Background Air pollution exposure has been associated with cognitive decline, but evidence remains limited regarding outdoor and household air pollution, different cognitive domains, and urban-rural differences. This study examined the longitudinal associations of outdoor particulate matter and household solid fuel use with cognitive function among older Chinese adults. Methods We used nationally representative data from 8,806 participants aged ≥60 years in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study from 2013 to 2020. Outdoor air pollution was assessed using annual mean PM1, PM2.5, and PM10 concentrations, and household air pollution was assessed by solid fuel use for cooking and heating. Cognitive function included global cognition, memory, and mental status. Linear mixed-effects models were used to examine the associations of air pollution exposure with subsequent cognitive function. Stratified analyses were conducted by urban-rural residence. Results Higher outdoor particulate matter exposure was generally associated with poorer subsequent global cognition and memory. PM2.5 exposure in 2013 was inversely associated with global cognition in both 2015 and 2018. Solid fuel use for cooking in 2013 was associated with lower global cognition (β = -0.57; 95% confidence interval (CI) = -0.93, -0.22), memory (β = -0.53; 95% CI = -0.77, -0.31), and mental status (β = -0.23; 95% CI = -0.40, -0.06) in 2018, while solid fuel use for heating was associated with lower global cognition (β = -0.42; 95% CI = -0.79, -0.05) and memory (β = -0.67; 95% CI = -0.92, -0.41). In stratified analyses, inverse associations appeared more evident among rural participants. Conclusions Outdoor particulate matter exposure and household solid fuel use were associated with poorer subsequent cognitive function among older adults in China, particularly global cognition and memory. These findings suggest that ambient and household air pollution may be relevant to cognitive ageing.

items.title: Delirium prevalence and practices across intensive care units in Singapore: a point prevalence survey.
items.abstract: Introduction Delirium is characterised by a disturbance in attention and awareness, alongside an acute change in cognition that develops over a short period and fluctuates in severity. It is associated with critical illness. This study aimed to determine the point prevalence of delirium in Singapore's intensive care units (ICUs) and assess the adherence of local delirium management practices and evidence-based international guidelines. Methods A point prevalence survey was conducted on World Delirium Awareness Day, 13 March 2024. Local ICU leads completed questionnaires, and data on delirium prevalence and management practices were collected and compared with international guidelines. Results Responses were received from 12 adult and two paediatric ICU leads, representing 66% of adult and 100% of paediatric ICUs in Singapore's public health institutions. Of 143 ICU patients, 92 (81.4%) were assessed for delirium, with 32 (34.8%) screening positive. Adult ICUs generally adhered to PADIS recommendations, including limiting benzodiazepine use, routinely assessing for delirium, and implementing protocols for pain management and sedation. However, holistic non-pharmacological care was lacking. Paediatric ICUs showed strong adherence to PANDEM guidelines, although deficiencies remained in delirium assessment and noise reduction practices. The most frequently reported barriers to improving management strategies were manpower shortages, time constraints and educational gaps. Conclusion Overall, local practices aligned well with international guidelines, but gaps remained in non-pharmacological interventions, resources, time and education. Addressing these gaps through quality improvement initiatives may enhance delirium management in ICUs.

items.title: Phage therapy reduces bacterial burden and inflammation in a neutropenic murine sepsis model caused by hyperinvasive carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.
items.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae is an emerging opportunistic pathogen associated with severe clinical outcomes, and carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae (CRKP) has become a critical threat requiring alternative therapeutic strategies. Phage therapy has recently gained attention as a promising alternative to combat antimicrobial resistance. However, its efficacy alone and in combination with antibiotics in immunocompromised hosts remains understudied. Here, we established a cyclophosphamide-induced neutropenic murine sepsis model due to a hyperinvasive CRKP strain carrying multiple virulence factors. In vitro , ceftazidime-avibactam (CAZ-AVI) at 8/4 μg/mL was required to suppress growth of this strain for 48 h, and this concentration was slightly reduced to 4/4 μg/mL when combined with a cocktail of three taxonomically distinct phages (P24, P39, and P49). In vivo , a single dose of the phage cocktail (9 × 10 8 plaque-forming units/mouse), administered intravenously or intraperitoneally following bacterial challenge, achieved 2.5-5.1 log 10 reductions of bacterial burdens across multiple tissues and organs. Correspondingly, serum tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-6, and interleukin-1β levels decreased significantly, and histopathological analysis revealed markedly mitigated inflammatory infiltration and tissue damage in the lung and liver. Both administration routes achieved comparable outcomes. Furthermore, in a delayed-treatment survival experiment, treatment with the phage cocktail combined with CAZ-AVI, initiated 2 h after lethal challenge, resulted in an 83.3% survival over the 28-day observation period. In contrast, all untreated mice succumbed within 2 days, and phage cocktail alone resulted in only 8.3% survival. Collectively, these findings provide in vivo evidence supporting the combination of phage cocktail and CAZ-AVI against CRKP infection in immunocompromised hosts. Importance Carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae (CRKP) has emerged as a critical threat to global public health, causing life-threatening infections, disproportionately affecting immunocompromised patients who often fail to respond to conventional antibiotic therapy and experience high mortality rates. However, the efficacy of phage therapy in this vulnerable population and the comparative performance of different administration routes remain largely unexplored. Here, we established a cyclophosphamide-induced neutropenic murine sepsis model to evaluate the therapeutic potential of a phage cocktail against CRKP. We demonstrate that both intravenous and intraperitoneal phage administration achieve substantial bacterial load reduction and significant attenuation of systemic inflammation, revealing that phage therapy retains a robust positive response even in the absence of a fully functional host immune system. These findings underscore the clinical translational potential of phage as a viable alternative to antibiotics for combating CRKP infections in immunocompromised patients and provide critical evidence supporting intravenous phage delivery as a feasible administration route.

items.title: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 1 Transmission Risk During Commercial Air Travel, 2000-2025.
items.abstract: Objectives Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 1 (SARS-CoV-1) have the potential for global translocation and transmission through infected travelers. This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed transmission of these viruses during commercial air travel. Methods We searched 8 databases for studies published during 2000-2025 of MERS-CoV and SARS-CoV-1 transmission during air travel. We included studies describing contact investigation(s) and outcome(s) of MERS-CoV or SARS-CoV-1 exposures on aircraft. We completed title and abstract screening, full-text review, and data extraction in Covidence. We assessed risk of bias using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. We classified contacts of index cases as close contacts according to study-defined contact definitions. We calculated attack rates for close contacts, non-close contacts, and passengers (and/or crew) on the whole plane. We used a random-effects meta-analysis to estimate pooled attack rates (PARs) and pooled risk differences (PRDs). A leave-one-out sensitivity analysis assessed the robustness of pooled estimates. Results Nineteen studies met inclusion criteria. No secondary cases were identified from 11 MERS-CoV studies. Among 5 SARS-CoV-1 studies reporting whole-plane data, the PAR was 1.2% (95% CI, 0.3%-4.3%). Sensitivity analyses indicated that this estimate was robust. Among 4 studies reporting outcomes for close contacts, the PAR was 3.4% (95% CI, 1.0%-11.1%), while 2 studies of non-close contacts yielded a PAR of 0.3% (95% CI, 0.1%-1.3%). The PRD comparing close and non-close contacts was 0.8% (95% CI, -5.5% to 7.1%). Conclusions Although both viruses are capable of person-to-person transmission, evidence of transmission during air travel was identified only for SARS-CoV-1. The findings support an evidence- and risk-based, pathogen-specific approach to aircraft contact investigations rather than a uniform strategy for all emerging respiratory viruses.

items.title: Development and validation of the health literacy-sensitive pharmacist-patient communication scale.
items.abstract: Introduction Health literacy is central to healthcare quality, and clinical pharmacists play a crucial role in improving patients' health literacy and medication safety. China, however, lacks a locally validated tool for evaluating health literacy-sensitive pharmacist-patient communication (HL-SPPC). Objective This study aims to develop and validate an evaluation indicator system and a patient self-assessment scale for HL-SPPC in Chinese inpatient pharmaceutical care. Methods An initial indicator pool was generated through a systematic literature review and focus group discussion and refined through two rounds of modified Delphi consultation; indicator weights were determined using the precedence chart method. A cross-sectional survey of inpatients who had received medication guidance from clinical pharmacists was conducted to evaluate psychometric properties, including item analysis, content validity, reliability, exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, convergent, discriminant, and criterion validity. Results The final indicator system comprised 5 primaries and 19 secondary indicators, with the higher weights for visualization and tool support (36%), communication strategies (28%), and feedback responsiveness (20%). The validated 11-item patient scale yielded two factors, empathic communication (7 items) and concrete guidance (4 items), which explained 68.827% of the total variance. The overall Cronbach's α was 0.859, and the test-retest ICC (2,1) was 0.710. Confirmatory factor analysis indicated acceptable fit (χ²/df = 1.779, CFI = 0.959, TLI = 0.947, RMSEA = 0.080, SRMR = 0.045). Convergent, discriminant, and criterion validity were acceptable. Conclusion This study provides the first validated indicator system and patient self-assessment scale for HL-SPPC in China, offering practical tools for pharmacist training, pharmaceutical care quality evaluation, and patient engagement.
