items.title: Epigenetic programming of immune cells: unleashing anti-tumor potential and clinical perspectives.
items.abstract: Immune cell plasticity is a defining feature of tumor immunity and is increasingly recognized as being governed by epigenetic regulation. Advances in single-cell and spatial multi-omics have uncovered an epigenetic checkpoint that integrates environmental cues within the tumor microenvironment (TME) to shape immune cell fate and function. In this review, we synthesize recent evidence supporting three interconnected paradigms of epigenetic control in tumor immunity from the perspective of immune cell heterogeneity, ecology, and state transitions. First, dynamic chromatin remodeling programs myeloid cell polarization and functional diversification. Second, epitranscriptomic regulation constrains T and B cell states, contributing to immune dysfunction and exhaustion. Third, spatially resolved epigenetic remodeling influences immune cell trafficking, positioning, and retention within tumors. Collectively, these mechanisms establish durable immune states that reinforce TME-driven immunosuppression. We further highlight emerging pharmacological strategies targeting epigenetic regulators to reprogram immune cell function and enhance anti-tumor immunity. This framework provides a foundation for leveraging epigenetic plasticity to improve the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: Meta-analysis shows that immunization reduces amphibian susceptibility to the chytrid fungus.
items.abstract: Emerging infectious diseases are increasingly impacting vertebrates, sometimes causing severe population declines. Chytridiomycosis, caused by the fungal pathogen Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd), is one of the most devastating wildlife diseases known, driving widespread amphibian collapses and extinctions. Developing strategies that improve host survival in the presence of Bd have therefore become a conservation priority. Here we conducted a meta-analysis to evaluate whether immunizing individuals reduces disease susceptibility. Using 208 effect sizes from 36 studies and 22 species, we compared infection prevalence, infection intensity and mortality between experimentally immunized and non-immunized individuals subsequently exposed to Bd, representing the first such synthesis for a major emerging wildlife disease. Immunization using live pathogens significantly reduced host infection intensity and lowered mortality after re-exposure, whereas immunization using Bd-derived natural chemicals reduced infection prevalence. Other immunization approaches showed non-significant effects across species. Immunization effects also varied across disease progression stages, host life stages and taxonomic groups. Our findings suggest that live-pathogen immunization could be an effective strategy for increasing survival during reintroductions. Supplementing vulnerable populations with immunized individuals or helping wild amphibians clear infections may thus increase survival.

items.title: A hidden trigger of near-road microplastic release from asphalt surfaces: Low-frequency vibration from vehicle motion lowers the detachment threshold of tyre wear particles.
items.abstract: Tyre and road wear particles (TRWPs) are an important component of road dust and a major source of microplastic (MP) pollution. The mechanisms controlling their release from road surfaces are multifactorial with complicated interactions, and remain subject to field experimental and modelling investigation. Unlike most detachment studies, which treat surfaces as static, real pavements are repeatedly exposed to vibration from passing vehicles. Here, we developed a field-informed wind-tunnel approach using pristine car tyre wear particles (TWPs) as a well characterized and thus reproducible proxy for traffic-derived MPs. These particles were generated through vehicle motion on a laboratory test stand supplied by Continental Reifen Deutschland GmbH. The particles were deposited on asphalt that was thinly spray-coated white to allow optical detection. We investigated whether traffic-mimicking vibration lowers the threshold windspeed (u ∗ th ) of TWPs on asphalt. For the tested TWPs (80-300 μm), vibration increased the detached fraction and reduced the threshold windspeed across the field-relevant frequency range (5-30 Hz). Without vibration, asphalt retained most particles with only 19% detached at a u ∗ th of 0.39 ms -1 . Under the field-informed vibration scenario, the detached fraction increased to 41%. At the highest tested intensity, it reached 86%, while the u ∗ th decreased by 26% down to 0.29 ms -1 Particle size and shape also modulate detachment. Among the two size cohorts tested, vibration preferentially lowered the thresholds of smaller TWPs (80-135 μm), with more rounded particles being more readily mobilized than irregular ones. Our experiments demonstrate that pavement vibration can reduce the aerodynamic forcing needed to release TWPs retained on asphalt. This previously hidden mechanism increases their susceptibility to mobilization and has implications for the potential short-range transport and redistribution of near-road TRWPs into adjacent environmental compartments.

items.title: Alpine meadow degradation reshapes soil trace element-microbe relationships in community structure and functional potential.
items.abstract: Trace elements are closely linked to soil microbial communities and biogeochemical functions, yet how these relationships change during ecosystem degradation remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how alpine meadow degradation reshapes relationships between soil trace elements and microbial community structure and functional potential in the Sanjiangyuan region of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. Total and available concentrations of Fe, Al, Mn, Cu, Zn, Co and Ni were measured across degradation stages and related to bacterial and fungal community composition, microbial co-occurrence networks, and functional genes involved in C, N, P and S cycling. Degradation reorganised trace element-microbe relationships in a strongly stage-dependent manner. In lightly degraded meadows, trace elements were broadly associated with microbial abundance, community composition and network topology. As degradation intensified, these associations became more selective, with persistent relationships in highly degraded soils more frequently involving available than total trace elements. Bacterial and fungal communities showed stage-dependent compositional and network changes. Degradation also altered the coupling between trace elements and microbial nutrient-cycling genes. Associations with C- and N-cycle genes were strongest under light degradation and weakened thereafter, whereas P-cycle genes showed the greatest number of trace element associations under high degradation. Overall, alpine meadow degradation reorganised the ecological and functional linkages between trace elements and soil microorganisms in a stage- and element-form-dependent manner. These findings highlight the ecological relevance of trace element availability within the broader soil environmental context and provide new insight into belowground microbial functional potential during alpine meadow degradation.

items.title: Involvement of abscisic acid in the regulation of postharvest senescence in cut roses.
items.abstract: Abscisic acid (ABA) is a major hormonal regulator of senescence in ethylene-insensitive flowers, but its involvement in ethylene-sensitive flowers remains unclear. This study examined the involvement of ABA in the postharvest senescence of cut roses (Rosa hybrida) from two cultivars differing in ethylene sensitivity, 'Deep Purple' and 'Iguana'. Senescence indicators and endogenous ABA levels were monitored throughout vase life. The effects of exogenous ABA and 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylic acid (ACC), the direct precursor of ethylene, were also assessed. Results showed that endogenous ABA contents increased as senescence progressed in both cultivars. However, basal ABA levels were one order of magnitude higher in 'Deep Purple', the more ethylene-sensitive cultivar, which also had the shortest vase life. ABA content was strongly correlated with flower neck bending, petal dehydration, ion leakage, and color changes in 'Iguana', but only with petal dehydration in 'Deep Purple'. Exogenous ABA accelerated senescence in both cultivars, although its effects differed: it increased petal dehydration and flower neck bending in 'Deep Purple', whereas it affected all measured parameters in 'Iguana', suggesting greater ABA sensitivity in this cultivar. ACC also accelerated senescence in both cultivars but increased endogenous ABA content only in 'Iguana'. These results indicate that ABA is involved in regulating postharvest senescence in cut roses, particularly through its effects on water homeostasis, with a more prominent contribution in the cultivar less sensitive to ethylene.

items.title: Effects of parental diapause duration on egg morphology, chromatic properties, and hatching phenology in the cabbage beetle Colaphellus bowringi.
items.abstract: Diapause is a key life-history strategy that enables insects to survive adverse conditions, but whether parental diapause experience carries over to offspring early development remains poorly understood. We examined the transgenerational effects of parental diapause duration (0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, and 2.5 years) on egg area, egg colour (red, green, and blue RGB components), hatching incidence, hatching peak day, and hatching duration in the cabbage beetle Colaphellus bowringi. Egg area showed a significant, though modest, inverted-U relationship with parental diapause duration (quadratic R 2 = 0.072; ΔAIC = 11.1; vertex 1.96 years), while the red component of egg colour declined with prolonged diapause (linear R 2 = 0.020); green and blue components differed among groups but showed only weak linear declines (R 2 ≤ 0.05). Hatching incidence was significantly affected by diapause history, being highest in the 1.5-year group (91.8%) and lower at both extremes (0 years, 82.8%; 2.5 years, 83.6%), again consistent with an inverted-U pattern (quadratic GLM, ΔAIC = 22.65; vertex 1.34 years). Hatching peak day varied significantly among groups, but hatching duration did not. Egg area and R value were weakly correlated with diapause duration at the individual level, but neither trait predicted hatching incidence at the group level. Effect sizes were generally small (η 2 = 0.238 for egg area; 0.050 for R value), so the biological magnitude of these transgenerational effects should be interpreted with caution. Nevertheless, parental diapause duration appears to modulate offspring egg morphology and hatching success non-linearly, with an intermediate diapause window (~1.5-2 years) tending to maximise maternal investment and offspring fitness. This study provides experimental evidence for the transgenerational costs and benefits of diapause evolution.

items.title: Contrasting physiological and rhizosphere responses of wheat to benzotriazole UV stabilizers and phthalate esters.
items.abstract: The pervasive presence of plastic additives in agricultural soils poses emerging threats to crop productivity and rhizosphere ecology. However, comparative evidence linking plant physiological responses with rhizosphere biochemical and microbial changes across chemically distinct plastic additives remains limited. This study investigated the physiological, metabolic, and microbial responses of wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) to UV-328, UV-P, DBP, and DEHP at nominal concentrations of 0.1-1 mg/kg over a 30-day cultivation period. The four plastic additives induced distinct physiological and morphological responses in wheat roots. UV-328 generally caused pronounced root growth inhibition, ultrastructural alterations, and oxidative stress, whereas the relative effects of UV-P, DBP, and DEHP varied across the measured endpoints. These findings highlight the compound-specific and endpoint-dependent nature of phytotoxic responses to chemically distinct plastic additives. Root-exudate metabolomics revealed altered metabolic profiles, with glycerol and malic acid reaching 7.3- and 6.9-fold the control levels, respectively, under the highest UV-328 treatment. Metabolic pathway enrichment identified shared associations with tyrosine metabolism, glycerolipid metabolism, and isoquinoline alkaloid biosynthesis. At 1 mg/kg, rhizosphere urease and sucrase activities were 1.25-1.42 and 2.72-8.64 times the control levels, respectively, indicating higher potential hydrolytic activity under the stressed conditions. In parallel, 16S rRNA sequencing revealed shifts in rhizosphere bacterial community composition and diversity. Correlation analyses further identified associations among root-exudate metabolites, soil enzyme activities, bacterial community characteristics, and plant antioxidant responses, suggesting interconnected physiological and rhizosphere responses to plastic additive exposure. Collectively, these findings reveal distinct physiological and rhizosphere responses of wheat to BUVSs and PAEs, highlighting potential associations among plant oxidative stress, metabolic alterations, and rhizosphere microbial community restructuring. These results provide insights into the ecotoxicological effects of chemically distinct plastic additives in agricultural soil-plant systems.

items.title: Species-specific responses and mixed-cultivation buffering of emergent macrophytes exposed to combined pollution of size-fractionated polyethylene terephthalate microplastics and sulfamethoxazole.
items.abstract: The co-occurrence of microplastics (MPs) and antibiotics is widespread in freshwater environments, yet their combined effects on emergent macrophytes remain unclear. A 42-day high-exposure pot experiment was conducted to evaluate the species-specific responses of Iris pseudacorus L. and Iris sibirica L. grown in monoculture or mixed cultivation and exposed to polyethylene terephthalate microplastics (PET MPs; 30 and 300 µm, at 1 g/kg soil) and sulfamethoxazole (SMX; 20 mg/kg soil), alone or in combination. SMX was the dominant toxic factor; PET MPs alone exerted weaker effects, with clear size-fraction differences; 300 µm particles generally produced stronger inhibition. I. pseudacorus maintained higher growth, biomass, and photosynthetic pigment contents, whereas I. sibirica exhibited greater oxidative stress and stronger antioxidant and osmotic responses. At these stress-test concentrations, combined PET MP-SMX exposure showed Abbott-model antagonism (RI = 0.67-0.75). Mixed cultivation generally increased biomass and photosynthetic performance, reduced oxidative damage, and partially alleviated soil nutrient imbalance, indicating preliminary species-level buffering. These findings identify species-specific response patterns and suggest that mixed cultivation may buffer combined MP-SMX stress, warranting further tests under environmentally relevant conditions in constructed wetlands.

items.title: A review of hydrological alteration assessment: refinements to indicators, reference conditions, and alteration-judgment methods since IHA-RVA.
items.abstract: The Indicators of Hydrologic Alteration (IHA) and the Range of Variability Approach (RVA) have served as the operational basis of hydrological alteration assessment for three decades. Later studies have refined three key assessment steps, namely indicators of river conditions, reference conditions for post-impact flows, and judgment rules that translate hydrological departures into alteration magnitudes. From 483 publications screened under the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines, we trace the original setup, the limitations that motivated refinements, and the resulting insights, and make explicit the underlying assumptions. Indicator libraries have expanded from the 32 original IHA parameters to more than 170 metrics, and their ecological validity depends on coverage of the flow attributes and time scales governing habitat, life cycles, and channel geomorphology. Reference-condition techniques have advanced through record extension, control-impact designs, process-based and data-driven simulation, and time-varying modeling. Alteration-judgment workflows have evolved from in-range year counting toward distribution-aware metrics, significance testing, multi-metric aggregation, and ecology-grounded benchmarks. Target ranges, classification thresholds, and weighting schemes remain value-loaded choices seldom calibrated against ecological responses, so one flow record can yield divergent estimates under different conventions. Because the steps were refined largely independently, nine implicit assumptions (four for indicators, four for reference conditions, one for judgment) govern the cross-study comparability of reported magnitudes. Non-perennial, ice-affected, and tidal rivers violate several assumptions at once. We formulate reporting requirements and an assessment framework that tailors indicator selection, reference construction, and alteration judgment to hydrological processes, observational constraints, and ecological evidence.

items.title: Ambient particulate chemical components and dengue incidence: A 10-year nationwide study in Thailand.
items.abstract: Dengue remains a major public health concern in tropical regions, and environmental determinants are increasingly recognized as contributors to its transmission dynamics. Thailand experiences both recurrent dengue outbreaks and episodic air pollution; however, the role of particulate chemical components in dengue epidemiology remains unclear. This study examined the association between specific aerosol components and dengue incidence across 77 provinces in Thailand from 2012 to 2021. Dengue surveillance data were obtained from the Ministry of Public Health, and monthly aerosol concentrations were derived from NASA's MERRA-2 system. A Bayesian spatial modelling approach using integrated nested Laplace approximation (INLA) was applied to estimate associations between particulate components, including dust-PM2.5, organic carbon, black carbon, and sulfate, and dengue incidence, adjusting for demographic and temporal factors. A total of 837,616 dengue cases were recorded over the study period. Higher levels of dust-PM2.5 were positively associated with dengue incidence, whereas higher levels of organic carbon, black carbon, and sulfate were inversely associated with dengue incidence. These findings suggest that particulate chemical composition may contribute to spatial variation in dengue incidence, although the underlying mechanisms remain uncertain. Incorporating particulate composition into environmental surveillance systems may improve early warning models for dengue, particularly in rapidly urbanizing regions of Southeast Asia.

items.title: MOF-on-MOF Heterojunction for Aerobic Photocatalytic Uranium Extraction from Seawater.
items.abstract: The photocatalytic uranium reduction provides an alternative strategy for seawater uranium extraction, yet it remains challenging due to the high carbonate content and aerobic conditions. In this work, a MOF-on-MOF (MOM) heterostructure was constructed by growing NH2-MIL-125(Ti) (M125) onto MIL-101(Cr) (M101) via a hydrothermal method. The composite integrates the excellent U(VI) adsorption capacity of M101 with the superior photoelectric properties and oxygen activation ability of M125. In air atmosphere, MOM achieved over 95% U(VI) removal from carbonate-containing solution within 2 h under light irradiation, which is significantly higher than that of M101 and M125. 90.1% of uranium was recovered from uranium-spiked seawater, and 87.8% of uranium was extracted from real seawater using MOM. In situ irradiated XPS and KPFM confirmed electron transfer from M101 to M125 in the MOM heterojunction. MOM facilitates the generation of superoxide radicals (·O2-), which play a key role in reducing U(VI) to insoluble U(IV). This work presents a synergistic MOF-on-MOF design strategy for efficient photocatalytic uranium extraction under aerobic conditions.

items.title: Toxicity of nitroaromatic explosives for the host-parasite system Tenebrio molitor-Gregarina spp. at different temperatures.
items.abstract: This study investigated the effect of 2,4,6-trinitrotoluene (TNT) and its incomplete detonation products - o-nitrotoluene (o-NT) and 2,4-dinitrotoluene (2,4-DNT) - on mortality, body mass and the intensity of Gregarina spp. invasion in Tenebrio molitor (Coleoptera: Tenebrionidae) larvae at 21-23 °C and 26-28 °C. Six hundred larvae were divided into ten groups (control and three concentrations of three compounds: 30, 90, 270 mg/kg substrate) at two temperatures during a 5-day exposure. The results showed concentration-dependent toxicity: TNT > o-NT > 2,4-DNT; at 270 mg/kg and 26-28 °C, mortality was 40.0% for TNT, 26.7% for o-NT and 10.0% for 2,4-DNT. Nitroaromatic compounds did not affect the intensity of Gregarina spp. parasitic invasion for 2,4-DNT and TNT, while for o-NT parasite counts increased with concentration. All three compounds induced premature pupation (10.0-11.1% vs. 0.0% in the control) regardless of compound type, concentration or temperature, indicating a threshold response. All larvae that pupated survived (100.0%), while among those that remained larvae, survival was lower (88.2%), although the 5-day observation period does not allow this difference to be separated from the shorter time pupae spent feeding. Elevated temperature (26-28 °C) increased toxicity and reduced parasite numbers by 26.0-36.0%.

items.title: Chemical profiling of a supercritical CO2 extract from Scolopendra subspinipes mutilans and identification of 4-hydroxyphenylacetic acid as an anti-melanogenic constituent.
items.abstract: A supercritical CO 2 extract of Scolopendra subspinipes mutilans (SSM) was investigated to identify chemically characterised constituents associated with anti-melanogenic activity. GC-MS profiling revealed 11 constituents, and the extract exhibited dose-dependent inhibitory effects on tyrosinase activity, DOPA oxidation, and melanin production in α-melanocyte-stimulating hormone-stimulated B16F10 melanoma cells. Comparative screening of the identified constituents further showed that 4-hydroxyphenylacetic acid (4-HPAA) was the most promising lead compound, as it suppressed DOPA oxidation and intracellular melanogenesis without detectable cytotoxicity under the tested conditions. Several additional constituents also displayed anti-tyrosinase activity, indicating that the anti-melanogenic effect of the SSM extract is associated with a chemically definable constituent profile rather than a non-specific crude extract effect. Collectively, these findings support 4-HPAA as a candidate marker for quantitative standardisation and further mechanistic investigation.

items.title: Habitat selection differs between social and solitary foraging in a wide-ranging seabird.
items.abstract: Prey detection is driven by both environmental and social cues, but synergistic effects of these two processes are poorly studied. For example, foraging conditions may vary depending on the presence/absence of other animals with consequences for understanding habitat suitability and changing population size. Seabirds feed on prey patches structured by physical and biological oceanography, foraging alone or in groups. However, it is unclear whether habitat selection varies with the degree of sociality. Here, we use co-deployed bird-borne cameras and GPS loggers to quantify foraging habitat choice and determine how it varies under different social conditions for breeding Northern gannets Morus bassanus. Resource selection functions revealed dive bouts were associated with (a) distance to colony, (b) water depth, (c) fishing effort and (d) distance to fronts. However, the strength and direction of these relationships varied with gregariousness: (1) solitary dives occurred away from areas of high apparent fishing effort and ocean fronts, (2) social natural dives occurred in shallow water away from ocean fronts and (3) scavenging was highly localised in deep-water zones, and strongly correlated with remotely-sensed fishing effort. Our work shows how habitat selection varies with social context and how foraging at fisheries may uncouple scavengers from natural environmental cues. These findings also demonstrate that habitat selection plays a key role in shaping social organization in mobile marine predators and highlight the importance of considering environmental context when linking movement ecology and social behaviour.

items.title: Emotion regulation diversity and recovery from negative emotions: the moderating role of negative emotion differentiation.
items.abstract: Emotion regulation (ER) diversity, the variety and balance of strategies used, is often considered adaptive, yet findings have been inconsistent. This study examined whether ER diversity predicts recovery from negative emotions in daily life, and whether negative emotion differentiation (NED), the ability to distinguish between negative emotional states, moderates this relationship. Sixty-four participants completed ecological momentary assessments five times daily for one week (1,458 observations). Emotional recovery was operationalised as the percentage decrease in negative affect from the worst state since the previous prompt to the current one. Multilevel models examined within-person associations of momentary NED and ER diversity with emotional recovery. Participants recovered better during moments of higher NED and worse during moments of greater ER diversity. The negative association between ER diversity and recovery was weaker when NED was higher. When recovery was operationalised as current negative affect controlling for worst negative affect, the ER diversity association replicated, but the NED association and interaction did not. These findings suggest that ER diversity is not inherently beneficial in daily life and that NED may buffer its costs, though this depended on how recovery was operationalised. Understanding when diverse regulation helps or hinders recovery requires attention to momentary emotional processes.

items.title: A Qualitative Exploration of Self-Identity within BDSM/Kink Sexuality.
items.abstract: BDSM and kink are umbrella terms broadly describing the consensual and often erotic manipulation of power dynamics and/or pain/sensation experiences. While prior research has largely focused on BDSM/kink behaviors and fantasies, recent research has also included a focus on BDSM/kink as an identity. This research describes diversity and complexity within self-identities among kink-identified individuals in mostly geographically limited samples. The current project adds to this literature as a qualitative inquiry of the self-identities of 262 individuals with BDSM/kink sexual experiences from around the English-speaking world. Participants in the current sample varied in their connection to a BDSM/kink identity. Many described their identities as tied to specific BDSM/kink pursuits, while others rejected the framework of BDSM/kink as an identity altogether. Participants also described fluidity and intersectionality within their BDSM/kink identities, connected their BDSM/kink identity to consent, and qualified their identities according to strength and specificity. Our findings contribute to the literature on the diversity of BDSM/kink identity and experience.

items.title: Defensive reactivity to interoceptive perturbation in panic disorder: Depressive symptom burden and panic severity dimensions.
items.abstract: Panic disorder (PD) is characterized by exaggerated defensive responding to panic-related somatic sensations. It remains poorly understood how greater PD and depressive symptom severity are linked to dysregulated defensive functioning and how this manifests during disorder-relevant interoceptive threat. Addressing this question is critical for elucidating pathomechanisms underlying disorder maintenance and the frequent PD-depression comorbidity. We therefore examined how depressive symptom severity and PD severity dimensions uniquely and jointly relate to defensive mobilization during interoceptive perturbation. Eighty-five treatment-seeking patients with a principal diagnosis of PD with/without agoraphobia completed a standardized 3-min hyperventilation (HV) task inducing panic-related body symptoms vs. a non-symptom-provocation control condition. Potentiation of the startle eyeblink response was assessed as a cross-species index of defensive mobilization during the 10-min post-HV phase. Defensive mobilization was modeled as a function of clinician-rated and self-reported PD severity and self-reported depressive symptom severity, complemented by exploratory network analyses of PD dimensions (e.g., avoidance), depressive symptoms, and defensive mobilization. HV reliably induced respiratory perturbation, autonomic activation, and increases in panic symptoms and anxiety. Startle responses remained persistently potentiated following HV vs. the control condition. Greater startle potentiation was associated with higher patient-reported and clinician-rated PD severity and, most strongly, with depressive symptom severity. Network models identified depressive symptoms as a robust correlate of defensive mobilization and interoceptive fear. Depressive symptom burden was uniquely associated with defensive mobilization to interoceptive perturbation beyond PD severity. These findings point to mechanisms linking panic-depression comorbidity to persistent interoceptive threat responding and may inform PD treatment optimization.

items.title: Initial investigation of pain intensity and interference in children and adolescents seeking weight management treatment: a secondary analysis of data from the Stay in Treatment (SIT) study.
items.abstract: Chronic pain and obesity commonly co-occur in children and adolescents; however, few studies have investigated pain characteristics (e.g., intensity, interference) in youth seeking obesity treatment. We conducted a secondary analysis of baseline data from an observational study examining predictors of attrition from pediatric weight management treatment at four sites across the United States (i.e., the Stay in Treatment study). Youth with obesity (N = 437, 52.0% female, 45.5% White, 30.0% Black, and 22.2% identifying as Hispanic or Latino) completed PROMIS® measures assessing pain intensity and interference as well as aspects of social-emotional and physical functioning. Results indicated that pain intensity across the sample was in the mild range (M = 2.5, SD = 2.4), and 31.6% (n = 138) reported no pain. However, approximately one-third reported moderate (26.5%, n = 116) or severe (6.0%, n = 26) pain intensity, and 39.8% reported pain interference in a moderate or severe range based on published cut-offs in youth with chronic pain. Pain intensity and interference were significantly associated with anxiety and depressive symptoms, fatigue, mobility issues, and peer relationship challenges. These findings suggest that a considerable proportion of youth seeking obesity treatment experience clinically significant pain. Findings may inform screening, referral, and intervention efforts for pain concerns in pediatric weight management settings.

items.title: From Depression to Expression: A Community Expressive Arts Program for Alleviating Depressive Symptoms in Community-Dwelling Older Adults.
items.abstract: Background and objectives Growing evidence supports the use of arts to improve older adults' psychosocial and spiritual well-being. This study evaluated the effects of an expressive arts-based intervention (EABI) under the train-the-trainer program on depressive symptoms, spiritual well-being, and quality of life of older adults in Hong Kong. Research design and methods In a mixed-methods design, 84 healthcare workers in Hong Kong completed the train-the-trainer program as ambassadors and delivered the 8-week EABI to 915 older adults with mild to moderate depressive symptoms. Older adults completed validated measures of depression, spirituality, and quality of life (QoL) before and after EABI. Ten ambassadors and 34 older adults participated in focus groups. The EABI effects were analyzed by paired sample t-tests and multilevel modeling evaluated the associations between ambassadors' and older adults' changes. Results Ambassadors showed increased self-efficacy (d = 0.53) and older adults showed substantial declines in depressive symptoms (d = 0.91) and significant improvements in spiritual well-being, overall QoL, and QoL subscales (d = 0.18-0.45). Changes in ambassadors' self-efficacy showed significant indirect effects on older adults' depressive symptoms (αβ = -0.23, 95% CI: -0.46, -0.01) and overall QoL (αβ = 0.27, 95% CI: 0.01, 0.52) via changes in spiritual well-being. Thematic analysis indicated improved psychosocial well-being among older adults and enhanced knowledge and service-delivery skills among ambassadors. Discussion and implications The EABI showed preliminary benefits on healthcare workers' self-efficacy and older adults' psychosocial well-being. The findings provide initial support on using EABI in geriatric care via a train-the-trainer framework.

items.title: Clinical and radiographic outcomes of SpineJack mechanical kyphoplasty versus conservative management in traumatic thoraco-lumbar compression fractures.
items.abstract: Study design Prospective, comparative, observational cohort study. Objective To compare the clinical and radiographic outcomes of SpineJack mechanical kyphoplasty versus conservative management in neurologically intact patients with traumatic thoraco-lumbar compression fractures (AO type A). Background Thoraco-lumbar compression fractures can be managed conservatively, with prolonged bed rest and rigid orthoses; with minimally invasive techniques originally developed for osteoporotic fractures, such as vertebroplasty and kyphoplasty; or with open or percutaneous pedicle screw fixation. Methods A total of 246 consecutive patients with a Magerl type A thoraco-lumbar fracture were included in this non-randomized prospective study between January 2018 and December 2023. After counseling, 124 patients elected Group A (conservative management: bed rest and a three-point brace) and 122 elected Group B (percutaneous kyphoplasty with SpineJack). At the final 12-month follow-up, 104 patients in Group A and 100 patients in Group B were evaluated, with a total of 42 patients lost to follow-up. The Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) and Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) were used to assess clinical outcome. Radiographic outcome was assessed by measuring the vertebral height loss rate (HLR) and regional kyphosis angle (RKA). Patients were followed up at 1, 6, and 12 months. Results Pain relief and recovery of functional ability were significantly better in Group B. Radiographic metrics showed a better outcome in the surgical group. Conclusions Mechanical kyphoplasty with the SpineJack system is a safe and effective treatment for post-traumatic compression fractures, providing a significant improvement in pain, disability, and radiographic morphometric parameters that is maintained at long-term follow-up.

items.title: Swatting, Criminal Responsibility, and Risk in Forensic Psychiatry.
items.abstract: Internet and social media use is ubiquitous and pervasive in mainstream culture. This rapid growth has coincided with the emergence of novel antisocial behaviors. One such behavior is swatting, which involves filing false reports of imminent danger to law enforcement, often by people outside of the report's jurisdiction, for the purpose of dispatching a Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT) team to the victim's home. This is not a trivial crime; it places the lives of victims and law enforcement officers in danger. In this article, we review swatting and highlight five salient cases. This analysis and commentary provide a guide for forensic psychiatrists on the evaluation of swatting defendants, with a focus on key psycholegal concerns, including criminal responsibility, violence risk, civil litigation, and developmental considerations for adolescent perpetrators.

items.title: Is Leadership Shared Across Cultures? Evidence from Social Network Analyses of 164 Football Teams in Eight Countries.
items.abstract: Shared leadership, where multiple team members take on leadership roles rather than relying on a single formal leader, has been shown to benefit sport teams. However, we know little about whether shared leadership is prevalent cross-culturally. In particular, it has been suggested that shared leadership may be less prevalent in cultures where hierarchical differences in power and authority are more widely accepted (i.e., cultures with higher power distance). To investigate this, we examined whether leadership structures varied as a function of country- and team-level power distance in 164 football (or soccer) teams across eight countries (N = 2,807 players and coaches). Contrary to theoretical expectations, we found that shared leadership was not only present across different levels of power distance but also tended to be more prevalent where power distance was higher. These findings challenge the view that shared leadership is incompatible with high power distance but merit further investigation.

items.title: Galanin signalling in the locus coeruleus governs depression-like behavioural despair and antidepressant-associated neuroadaptation.
items.abstract: Noradrenergic dysfunction has long been implicated in the pathophysiology of depression and anxiety, yet the contribution of co-released neuropeptides such as galanin remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated whether altered galanin signalling in the locus coeruleus (LC) is associated with affective vulnerability and antidepressant-induced neuroadaptations. Relative to their low-anxiety behaviour (LAB) counterparts, rats selectively bred for high anxiety-related behaviour (HAB) displayed elevated galanin (Gal) mRNA expression in the LC, paraventricular hypothalamus, and central amygdala, but not in the dorsomedial hypothalamus and dorsal raphe, indicating region-specific Gal upregulation associated with their inherent predisposition to heightened behavioural despair. To determine whether the galanin system is also engaged by antidepressant treatment, normotypic rats were chronically treated with desipramine, paroxetine, or tranylcypromine. All three treatments consistently reduced Gal mRNA expression selectively in the LC representing an expression pattern opposite to that observed in HAB rats and, implicating LC galanin in antidepressant-induced neuroadaptation. Functionally, intra-LC administration of galanin increased passive coping in the forced swim test in LAB rats, reaching levels comparable to those of HAB rats whereas local administration of a non-selective galanin receptor antagonist, but not of a GalR3-selective receptor antagonist, reduced immobility in HAB rats. These findings support a functional role of LC galanin signalling in modulating behavioural despair through a receptor mechanism that remains to be fully elucidated. Together, these results identify LC galanin signalling as a bidirectional modulator of behavioural despair and candidate mediator for antidepressant-induced neuroadaptation, warranting further investigation of its therapeutic relevance in mood disorders.

items.title: Modifiable lifestyle behaviours in Barrett's Oesophagus: a scoping review of prevalence, patient variation, and lived experience.
items.abstract: Objective To examine the prevalence, patient profiles, and lived experience of modifiable lifestyle behaviours in Barrett's Oesophagus. Methods Following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews, four databases were searched to 30/08/2025, with citation searching until 14/11/2025. Quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods studies reporting behaviour prevalence, subgroup variation, or lived experience in adults with Barrett's Oesophagus published between 2015 and 2025 were included. Findings were summarised descriptively and synthesised thematically. Results Fifty-five studies were included. Overweight (31.0-52.7%), obesity (20.7-55.8%), physical inactivity (54.7-68.4%), suboptimal diet (91% not meeting fibre recommendations, 64% fruit and vegetable), smoking (up to 46.7%), and current alcohol use (42-75.9%) were common, although definitions and populations varied. Subgroup variation was rarely examined and never formally compared. Three studies examined lived experience. Qualitative findings emphasised lifestyle modification for symptom management, while one survey found that perceived cancer risk was not associated with behavioural change. Conclusions Suboptimal lifestyle characteristics were frequently reported in Barrett's Oesophagus, but the evidence base remains dominated by epidemiological risk profiling. Research is needed to examine how these behaviours vary, change over time, and can be supported within routine surveillance, to advance prevention-focused care.

items.abstract: To examine the association between gross motor function level and Raven's Colored Progressive Matrices (CPM) performance in children and adolescents with cerebral palsy (CP), compare CPM performance with typically developing participants, and explore associations with MRI and EEG findings. CPM totals were converted to center-derived age-referenced scores; the upper available normative age band was applied above age 11.5 years. Gross motor function was classified with the GMFCS. Median CPM score was 72 (IQR 64-81) in the CP group and 98 (IQR 92-104) in the comparison group (adjusted difference -26.4, 95% CI -31.2 to -21.6). The adjusted association with epileptiform EEG abnormalities was inconclusive. CPM performance was associated with GMFCS level and MRI pattern, but the cross-sectional findings do not establish causality. Gross motor classification must not substitute for accessible neuropsychological assessment.

items.title: Mind the cueing design: Order effects mask benefits of congruency pre-cues.
items.abstract: Evidence that individuals proactively adjust cognitive control in response to pre-cues signaling upcoming distraction has been surprisingly sparse, raising questions about the limits of volitional control. The present study tested whether this pattern reflects genuine constraints in proactive control engagement or methodological limitations of standard pre-cueing designs. Across two pre-registered experiments, we examined the role of cueing order (i.e., whether participants started with informative or uninformative pre-cue blocks) in the commonly used between-block design and evaluated an alternative within-block design in which informative and uninformative pre-cues were randomly intermixed. In Experiment 1, the standard approach of collapsing cueing order conditions yielded null pre-cue benefits for the between-block comparison, mirroring what is often observed in the literature. However, when considering cueing order, benefits emerged when informative cues were encountered first (cued-first group) but not when they appeared second (uncued-first group). In contrast, the within-block comparison produced reliable pre-cue benefits regardless of cueing order. Experiment 2 replicated the within-block pre-cue benefit using a fully intermixed design without the cueing order manipulation. Together, these findings indicate that sparse evidence for pre-cue benefits may partly reflect design-related constraints rather than limits in proactive control. Why pre-cue benefits depend on cueing order remains an open question, but the present findings reveal that the intermixed cueing design offers a more sensitive and reliable method for detecting cue-based control adjustments-with important implications for prominent theories of cognitive control.

items.title: Coping with developmental coordination disorder: A comparative study of adults and parents.
items.abstract: Background Developmental Coordination Disorder (DCD/Dyspraxia) is a common, yet under-recognised lifelong neurodevelopmental condition characterised by motor coordination difficulties affecting daily functioning and psychosocial wellbeing. Coping plays an important role in wellbeing, yet little is known about how adults with DCD manage ongoing challenges or how their coping compares with that of parents of individuals with DCD. Methods One hundred and fourteen participants (90 adults with DCD; 24 parents who raised a child with DCD for at least 16 years) completed an online survey assessing coping, acceptance, optimism, resilience, condition perceptions and life satisfaction. Group differences were examined using MANCOVA and t-tests. Results Parents reported greater use of adaptive coping, particularly acceptance, and planning, alongside higher optimism, resilience, and life satisfaction. Adults with DCD relied more on maladaptive coping, notably mental disengagement, which was associated with poorer wellbeing. Acceptance-based coping was a protective factor in both groups. Social support and humour showed no clear association with wellbeing. Greater motor coordination difficulties were associated with increased disengagement and reduced humour use. Conclusions Adults with DCD and parents show distinct coping and wellbeing profiles. Findings highlight the need for tailored interventions that promote adaptive coping and acceptance in adults with DCD overall.

items.title: Non-Prescribing Clinicians' Attitudes Toward Harm Reduction Strategies for Opioid Use.
items.abstract: Background Social workers, counselors, and other non-prescribing clinicians (NPCs) work with people who use opioids, but little is known about their exposure to harm reduction and their attitudes toward harm reduction strategies. We conducted a national survey of NPCs to examine (1) the availability of harm reduction strategies in practice settings and communities; (2) differences by geographical context; (3) attitudes toward harm reduction strategies and medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD); and (4) factors associated with support for harm reduction. Methods We recruited 758 NPCs through professional association mailing lists and social media to complete a survey about their exposure to harm reduction strategies and MOUD, related training, and attitudes toward harm reduction. Results Harm reduction strategies and MOUD were substantially but unevenly available in NPC practice settings, with gaps most apparent in rural areas. NPCs are generally supportive of harm reduction and MOUD. Exposure and training were associated with greater support for harm reduction. Conclusions Harm reduction has gained a foothold in the practice settings of NPCs in the United States, but important gaps remain. Given the continuing crisis of opioid overdoses and the fact that NPCs often function as treatment gatekeepers, expanding harm reduction infrastructure and training, especially in rural areas, is critical.

items.title: Effect of a Multidisciplinary Intervention on Fatigue in Lymphoma Survivors With Persistent Fatigue: A Randomized Controlled Trial (the REFUEL trial).
items.abstract: Persistent fatigue is a prevalent, complex, and distressing late effect among lymphoma survivors. We examined the effect of a multidisciplinary intervention on fatigue among lymphoma survivors with persistent fatigue. Lymphoma survivors with persistent fatigue (moderate to severe fatigue ≥6 months) were randomly assigned to usual care (n = 75) or a 12-week multidisciplinary intervention (n = 75). The intervention consisted of patient education, physical exercise, a cognitive-behavioral therapy-based program, and nutritional counseling. Total fatigue was assessed by the Chalder Fatigue Questionnaire (range, 0-33) 3 months after random assignment (T1; primary outcome) and at 6 (T2) and 9 (T3) months after random assignment (secondary outcomes). Other secondary outcomes were functioning and global health status/quality of life (QoL) assessed by European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer QoL Questionnaire-C30. Effects were analyzed with baseline-adjusted linear mixed models for repeated measures. Compared with usual care, the intervention group reported significantly lower total fatigue at T1 (between-group difference [BGD], -3.5 [95% CI, -5.4 to -1.6]; P < .001). Secondary outcome analyses indicated that total fatigue remained lower in the intervention group at T2 (BGD, -2.4 [95% CI, -4.4 to -0.5]), but not at T3 (BGD, -0.9 [95% CI, -3.0 to 1.2]). At T1, secondary outcome analyses indicated positive intervention effects on physical (BGD, 3.8 [95% CI, 0.2 to 7.3]) and role functioning (BGD, 9.2 [95% CI, 0.9 to 17.5]) and global health status/QoL (BGD, 9.5 [95% CI, 3.5 to 15.4]), but not on social (BGD, -0.1 [95% CI, -7.4 to 7.3]), emotional (BGD, 5.6 [95% CI, 0.0 to 11.3]), or cognitive functioning (BGD, 3.5 [95% CI, -3.3 to 10.2]). A multidisciplinary intervention improved fatigue among lymphoma survivors with persistent fatigue. The effect appeared to be maintained 6 months after random assignment but dissipated at 9 months.

items.title: Comparing the Validity of Commonly Used Risk Assessment Tools in Men With Dual Histories of IPV and Sexual Offending.
items.abstract: Individuals with dual histories of sexual and intimate partner violence (IPV) offending represent a complex subgroup, yet little is known about how well offence-specific risk assessment tools work for them. This field validity study compared the discrimination of an IPV risk tool (Spousal Assault Risk Assessment-Version 2; SARA-V2) with two sexual offending risk tools (Static-99R and STABLE-2007, as well as their combined risk level) in 467 men in British Columbia with dual sexual-IPV offending histories. The sexual offending measures predicted sexual recidivism with small to moderate effects, IPV recidivism with small effects, and violent recidivism with small to moderate effects. SARA-V2 total scores predicted IPV and violent recidivism with small effects but failed to predict sexual recidivism. Confidence intervals for all effects overlapped, indicating the measures had comparable discrimination. The Static-99R and Static/STABLE were the most broadly relevant in incremental validity analyses, predicting all three outcomes over and above the SARA-V2, while results for the STABLE-2007 were mixed. The SARA-V2 added predictive value to the Static-99R and STABLE-2007 for IPV and violent recidivism and to the Static/STABLE for violent recidivism. Given the SARA-V2's risk management benefits, our findings support using the Static-99R or Static/STABLE alongside the SARA-V2 for dual sexual-IPV offending subgroups.

items.title: Predicting early treatment termination in opioid use disorder: a machine learning model for risk stratification.
items.abstract: Background: Half of patients with opioid use disorder (OUD) discontinue opioid agonist treatment within the first year. Identifying premature termination risk at intake could enable targeted clinical responses. Objectives: To develop and externally validate a machine learning model predicting premature treatment termination in OUD; to derive a clinical risk stratification system; and to identify variables most associated with predicted probability. Methods: Retrospective data from the Information System of the Andalusian (South Spain) Plan on Drugs and Addictions (SiPASDA) covered 11,475 patients (86.2% male) admitted to 121 public outpatient centers between 2015 and 2023 (90.8% termination rate). A CatBoost classifier was developed ( n = 10,328) and externally validated ( n = 1147). Predicted probabilities were discretized into low, moderate- and high‑risk strata. Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis quantified global and stratum-specific predictor contributions. Results: CRIBOOST achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) of 0.652 ± 0.018 in cross-validation and 0.646 externally. Termination rates rose monotonically across strata: 34.6% (low); 69.6% (moderate); 80.8% (high). Housing instability was the strongest positive predictor (SHAP= +0.569; +0.601 in high‑risk). Judicial referral was most protective (SHAP = -0.412), attenuating from low (-0.553) to high (-0.254); employment showed a similar gradient. Mood disorder (SHAP = +0.470) and benzodiazepine use disorder contributed positively, escalating with risk. Conclusions: CRIBOOST stratifies OUD patients into risk groups at admission using routine intake data, enabling clinicians to target retention-focused interventions where most needed and supporting efficient resource allocation. Stratum-specific SHAP contributions reveal which factors drive risk within each group, informing intervention design.

items.title: Rollout models of human planning with exact action probabilities.
items.abstract: One proposed mechanism for human planning is the mental simulation, or "rollout," of potential action sequences to evaluate future outcomes. While rollout-based models have seen great success in artificial intelligence, cognitive models that describe how people use rollouts remain scarce, in part because they are difficult to fit to behavioral data. Existing methods rely on computationally intensive simulations that result in approximate, noisy estimates of latent planning parameters. We introduce ROSETTE (Rollouts with Stochastic Early Termination and Tractable Estimation), a rollout-based model for finite goal-directed tasks with absorbing goals that provides analytically tractable, simulation-free model fitting. ROSETTE treats planning as a sequence of mental simulations formalized as an absorbing Markov chain. The model deterministically accumulates analytically computed expected rollout evidence and performs a variable number of policy-update cycles. We fit ROSETTE to data from human participants in two multi-step planning tasks and found that it well accounted for a rich set of summary statistics of behavior. By making this specific class of absorbing-goal rollout models tractable, our framework provides a testable account of how people may simulate and evaluate possible futures.

items.title: Pupil dynamics reflect uncertainty-driven adjustments of probability learning.
items.abstract: Adaptive learning in dynamic environments depends on the brain's ability to represent and respond to uncertainty. Changes in arousal-mediated pupil diameter provide insight into the neural basis of this process. Prior work has focused on magnitude-based inference tasks and revealed that learning is primarily influenced by the detection of change points and the corresponding modulation of arousal. In comparison, the role of arousal systems in learning contexts where changes are harder to detect, such as in probability learning, remains poorly understood. Here, we combined pupillometry with a probability learning task in which human participants estimated a hidden generative probability of stimuli that changed abruptly and unpredictably. A Bayesian ideal observer model was used to estimate trial-by-trial learning rates and two uncertainty-associated factors: change point probability (the probability that the generative process has abruptly changed) and prior uncertainty (about the current beliefs on this generative process). In line with normative theory, participants relied on prior uncertainty to adjust learning rates. Pupil analyses revealed temporally distinct representations of uncertainty, with phasic dilations tracking change point probability and tonic pupil dilations tracking prior uncertainty. Mediation analyses further indicated that both phasic and tonic pupil signals partially carried the effects of change point probability and prior uncertainty on learning, respectively. Critically, high tonic arousal weakened the coupling between phasic pupil responses and change point probability, accompanied by a reduced influence of change point probability on learning. Together, our results demonstrate that probability learning in a dynamic environment is underpinned by computationally rational integration of latent uncertainty factors and its contribution to belief updating,regulated through arousal-associated responses.

items.title: Cognitive control networks in human and macaque.
items.abstract: A much-replicated finding in human brain imaging is a distributed 'multiple-demand' or MD system, increasing in activity for many kinds of cognitive demand, and centrally involved in cognitive control. MD regions are proposed to encode a distributed mental model of critical task events, bound together in the roles and relationships needed to direct action selection. Though previous data hint at a corresponding network in the macaque, there has been no direct comparison to human data. Here we used functional magnetic resonance imaging to measure whole-brain activation in a multi-step saccadic maze task, compared to a control requiring similar moves but without goal-based decisions. Human data were a close match to the canonical MD network, extended to include adjacent regions, and in particular much of the canonical dorsal attention network. Data from two monkeys suggested correspondences in dorsomedial frontal, insula/orbitofrontal, and posterior temporal cortex. In lateral frontal cortex, there was just a single, largely dorsal activation patch, in contrast to multiple distinct human patches. In one animal, as in humans, there was accompanying activation of dorsal and medial parietal cortex. In macaques, as in humans, together with previous data, our findings suggest an extended and strongly interconnected brain network recruited by increased cognitive challenge.

items.title: CogD-ML: Cognitive determinants of social commerce purchase intention in Bangladesh using machine learning and explainable AI.
items.abstract: Cognitive factors are associated with online purchase intentions in developing economies, and the linear models conventionally used to study them can miss non-linear patterns. We report an applied integration of the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) with machine learning and explainable AI (XAI) to predict social media-driven e-commerce purchase intentions in Bangladesh. Survey data from 352 young, student-dominated consumers captured attitudes, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, and purchase behavior on validated Likert scale items. After reliability-based labeling and feature selection, we ran an ablation across seven classical classifiers and one multilayer perceptron, with stratified five-fold cross-validation, threshold sensitivity analysis, and a cross-domain check. With all TPB constructs included, support vector machines and AdaBoost reached 92% accuracy on the held-out test set, and cross-validated mean accuracy ranged from 0.84 to 0.88 for every model except the decision tree. These figures should be read against a positive-class prevalence of 82.1%, which inflates accuracy and F1 relative to imbalance-robust measures. Transfer to an independent North Indian sample was weak, with SVM MCC falling from 0.522 to 0.315 and AUROC from 0.923 to 0.775. In SHAP analyses, the four items the model relied on most were PBC1 (motivation from frequent advertising), SN3 (approval when many others buy through social media), ATTD4 (past purchase), and SN1 (family influence). Bivariate correlations and pathway-level regression with Benjamini-Hochberg correction are interpreted as associations, not causal effects, and Brier score and log loss are reported alongside SHAP and LIME to show whether predicted probabilities are calibrated. These findings are exploratory and specific to the sampled population; given the convenience sample, the class imbalance, and the weak transfer, they are not evidence of robust generalization or of readiness for deployment.

items.title: Associations of meeting the guidelines for 24-hour movement behaviors with depressive symptoms and perceived stress across the first postpartum year.
items.abstract: Postpartum depression and stress have significant consequences for maternal health. While physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep independently influence mental health, their combined effects within the 24-hour movement framework during postpartum are not well understood. A secondary analysis in the Postpartum 24/7 cohort study (n = 50) examined adherence to the 2025 Canadian 24-hour movement behavior guidelines at 3, 6, and 12 months postpartum from device-based and self-reported measures (including a composite score [0-5] representing number of guidelines met). Guideline adherence was associated with self-reported depressive symptoms (Center for Epidemiological Studies-Depression Scale) and perceived stress (Perceived Stress Scale). Logistic and linear mixed-effects models evaluated changes in guideline adherence over time and associations with mental health outcomes. The proportion of participants meeting most guidelines remained stable across postpartum, though self-reported sleep duration (44-63%, p = 0.043) and device-measured sleep efficiency (62-80%, p = 0.017) improved over time. Across postpartum, meeting sleep quality guidelines was associated with lower depressive symptoms (β = -2.44, p = 0.002) and perceived stress (β = -3.87, p < 0.001) and avoiding screen time before bed was associated with lower perceived stress (β = -2.43, p = 0.041). Meeting physical activity and sedentary behavior guidelines was not associated with depressive symptoms or perceived stress after adjustment. Considered collectively, each additional guideline met was associated with lower depressive symptoms (β = -0.81, p = 0.02) and perceived stress (β = -1.90, p < 0.001) scores. Sleep quality guidelines were most consistently associated with better postpartum mental health; meeting more 24-hour movement behavior guidelines may confer additive benefits. These findings suggest a 24-hour behavior approach may help promote postpartum mental health.

items.title: Comparative evaluation of single and multiple camera-based pose estimation methods for gait spatiotemporal parameter estimation.
items.abstract: Single-camera pose estimation may provide a more accessible approach to measure a person's walking patterns (i.e., gait analysis) than multi-camera markerless motion capture (MMC), but its validity and test-retest reliability remain unclear. This study evaluated spatiotemporal gait parameters from a single iPad camera against an eight-camera MMC reference system across four visits, two weeks apart. Thirty-six healthy adults (18.7 ± 1.7, ranging 18‒27 years) completed usual-gait, bag-carrying, and phone-use walking conditions. Validity analyses included 458 paired trials from Visit 1 and used repeated-measures and mixed-effects methods. Reliability analyses included 33 participants with complete four-visit data and evaluated absolute agreement of single visit-level measurements. Using repeated-measures correlation, the strongest within-participant association between systems was gait speed (rrm = 0.588), followed by stance duration (rrm = 0.528), cycle time (rrm = 0.515), and cadence (rrm = 0.446; all p < 0.001). Step length, calculated as half of stride length, and stride length showed weaker associations (rrm = 0.327 and 0.328; both p < 0.001), whereas swing duration was not significantly associated (p = 0.599). Independent step length and left-right step-length asymmetry were not evaluated. Mean system differences were small, but significant proportional bias was present for all seven gait variables, indicating that system differences changed with measurement magnitude. Walking condition influenced bias for cadence, gait speed, cycle time, step length, and stride length. Test-retest reliability varied by parameter and condition, with absolute-agreement intraclass correlation coefficients ranging from 0.499 to 0.862. Gait speed demonstrated good reliability across all three conditions, step and stride length demonstrated their highest reliability during the phone condition, and swing duration consistently demonstrated the lowest reliability. These findings support the feasibility of single-camera MMC for selected spatiotemporal gait outcomes, particularly gait speed, when accessibility and reduced equipment requirements are priorities. However, the approaches should not be considered interchangeable. Multi-camera MMC may remain better suited when three-dimensional reconstruction or more comprehensive spatial and temporal characterization is required.

items.title: Comparing the phenomenological characteristics of involuntary and voluntary autobiographical memories: a systematic review.
items.abstract: Involuntary autobiographical memories (IAMs) are memories of personal events that come to mind with no preceding attempt at retrieval. Over the last three decades, considerable attention has been devoted to understanding if and how IAMs may differ from voluntarily retrieved autobiographical memories (VAMs). However, there is presently little consensus on how the two types of memories may differ with regard to their cognitive, sensory-perceptual and emotional characteristics due to the lack of an exhaustive overview. The present systematic review compares the phenomenological characteristics of IAMs and VAMs across studies involving different populations and methods. Following PRISMA guidelines, we included results from 31 relevant studies, 18 involving a diary methodology and 13 involving an experimental methodology, comparing phenomenological ratings of both memory types. Results were mostly consistent within methodologies but occasionally differed across (i.e., IAMs are more often rated as more vivid, rehearsed, recent, important, and emotionally positive than VAMs in laboratory studies compared to diary studies). However, we also observed robust heightened episodic specificity for IAMs across methodologies, along with more mood impact compared to VAMs. Both memory types predominantly featured emotionally positive or neutral memories. Theoretical implications and directions for future research are discussed.

items.title: Surprise Resets the Mind: An Adaptive Online Reset in Working Memory Selection.
items.abstract: Human cognition rapidly adapts to unexpected events in dynamic environments, but it remains unclear whether expectation violations rapidly influence the selection of attended information into working memory. Using the attribute-amnesia paradigm, we introduced expectation violations during the surprise trial to test whether unexpected changes improve reporting of a target feature that had been attended and used but was normally not reported. Across six experiments (total N = 250 college students, aged 17-27 years; 149 females), expectation violations reliably improved surprise-trial report of this feature, indicating greater availability in working memory. This effect occurred not only when the violation concerned the target, but also when it involved broader contextual or auditory changes, suggesting that the effect cannot be characterized simply as enhanced visual attention to the target. These findings suggest that expectation violations trigger a rapid, flexible adjustment of working-memory selection, highlighting its role in dynamically managing information under uncertainty.

items.title: Regulating for Others' Sake: An Integrative Framework of Prosocial Emotion Regulation.
items.abstract: People often regulate others' emotions for prosocial reasons, but when is emotion regulation considered prosocial? In the current article, we present an integrative framework of prosocial emotion regulation, the process of regulating other people's emotions with the intention of benefiting them. We define prosocial emotion regulation as requiring both a motive to help and a goal to alter or sustain another's emotional state. We outline potential predictors of prosocial emotion regulation, propose criteria evaluating its success (i.e., whether it benefits the recipient or not), and consider both its potential benefits and costs. Although prosocial emotion regulation can promote well-being and support social connection, it may also impose burdens on the regulator. We discuss the implications of prosocial emotion regulation across key domains, including emotion-regulation science, social relationships and group processes, early development, and health and well-being. Finally, we identify critical directions for future research to better understand the mechanisms, outcomes, and contexts in which prosocial emotion regulation operates.

items.title: Co-evaluation of co-production in mind and brain research: A dialogical approach.
items.abstract: Co-production is increasingly used in mental and neurological health research, but less is known about how co-production itself can be co-evaluated. We conducted a study that aimed to systematically co-evaluate a 9-month project that co-produced strategic priorities and internal research-funding procedures for a new mind and brain research centre. The co-evaluation used a mixed-method design, including qualitative, quantitative, dialogical and post-implementation approaches, informed by an adapted RQ + 4 Co-Pro framework. The project involved 14 adult contributors who were also participants in the co-evaluation, including seven community partners alongside academic, clinical and research staff. Contributors across these roles also brought lived or living experience of mental-health difficulties, neurodivergence and marginalisation. Reflexive thematic analysis examined contributors' written reflections; perceived power was measured midway through the project and again at completion; findings were returned to the team for dialogical co-interpretation; and funding-panel members later reflected on implementation of the co-produced procedures. Thematic analysis generated six themes concerning time and resources, roles and identities, leadership and power, communication, institutional barriers and emotional labour and gains. Mean Sense of Power scores increased from 5.34 to 5.61 (p = .023). Dialogical reflection revealed both convergent and differing interpretations of shared experiences. Our central learning was that equitable co-production requires time to build trust, enough structure for collective work to progress without closing down shared influence and institutional systems able to support participation. By retaining rather than resolving different viewpoints, we show how systematic, dialogical co-evaluation can turn contrasting experiences into practical learning for future co-production.

items.title: Ecologically Derived Suicidal Ideation in Adolescents: Proximal Associations with Self-Referential Thoughts.
items.abstract: Objective Suicide is the second leading cause of death among 10-14 and 25-34-year-olds in the U.S. Suicidal ideation (SI) is one of the strongest predictors of death by suicide in children and adolescents. There is a critical need for identifying time-variant short-term risk factors for suicidal ideation. Although trait self-criticism (i.e. thinking focused on negative self-evaluation) and self-reassurance (i.e. providing self-compassion) are known vulnerabilities for SI, their short-term, real-time association with SI remains remarkably understudied. To address this critical gap, we examined how self-critical and self-reassuring responses may affect in-the-moment and subsequent SI in a youth's environment. Method Levels of self-criticism, self-reassurance, and SI were assessed 3 times per day over 2 weeks using ecological momentary assessment (EMA) technology in 114 12- to 15-year-old youth recruited primarily from child psychiatric hospital programs in the Northeast of the U.S. Participants were asked to rate how self-critical and self-reassuring they had been since the last prompt. Results A series of zero-inflated negative binomial mixed models showed that greater levels of self-criticism compared to one's own average levels beyond the overall sample's average were linked to higher SI in both the current and the next assessment window. Lower between but not within-person self-reassurance was linked to higher SI. Conclusions The findings highlight the need for further research on the clinical relevance of assessing and targeting self-criticism and enhancing self-reassurance in the day-to-day lives of youth to reduce SI.

items.title: How Youth Cope: Contributions of Coping Flexibility and Poverty-Related Stress on Internalizing Problems Over Time.
items.abstract: Objective Socioeconomically disadvantaged youth are at greater risk for developing internalizing problems throughout adolescence, often due to unpredictable environments and day-to-day stressors. This study investigated coping flexibility-specifically, how appropriately matching coping strategies to the controllability of a stressor (i.e., situation-strategy match) interacts with poverty-related stress to predict changes in youth internalizing problems over a one-year period. Method Participants included a sample of 74 socioeconomically disadvantaged youth (aged 11-18 years) in the Denver area. A linear growth model was utilized to analyze interindividual differences in internalizing problems across the course of one year, with poverty-related stress and situation-strategy match evaluated as time-invariant predictors. Results Greater poverty-related stress was significantly associated with greater concurrent internalizing problems at baseline. A greater ability to appropriately match coping strategies to the specific demands of a stressful situation (i.e., a higher number of situation-strategy matches) predicted a significant decrease in internalizing problems over time, above and beyond the effects of poverty-related stress. Conclusion Coping flexibility serves as a key protective factor against the development of internalizing problems in high-stress contexts. These findings have notable implications for future research on adolescent coping processes and they development of targeted coping interventions geared toward socioeconomically disadvantaged populations.

items.title: How does body exposure work? Therapists' perspectives and practices.
items.abstract: Purpose Body exposure (BE) is an evidence-based intervention for reducing body image disturbances in eating disorders and body dysmorphic disorder, yet its implementation in routine clinical practice remains insufficiently understood. The present study investigates therapists' assumptions regarding the mechanisms of change underlying BE and examines whether these assumptions are associated with the use of specific BE variants. Methods Data were obtained from an online survey of 230 licensed psychotherapists in Germany treating patients with eating disorders. We conducted logistic and linear regression analyses to examine associations between assumed mechanisms of change and the application of BE as well as specific implementation variations. Results Slightly more than half of the therapists reported current or previous use of BE in clinical practice. Attention bias modification, changes in body perception and change in dysfunctional cognitions were the most frequently endorsed mechanisms. Only endorsement of change in dysfunctional cognitions significantly predicted the use of BE overall. Among therapists using BE, several associations emerged between assumed mechanisms and intervention characteristics, including session duration, clothing, verbalization, focus, and therapist guidance. However, some of these associations were inconsistent with existing theoretical recommendations. Conclusion Overall, the findings suggest that BE is often implemented as a flexible clinical tool rather than as a mechanism-specific intervention. The study highlights the need for stronger theory-driven treatment and experimental research explicitly linking BE variants to mechanisms of change to support individualized and evidence-based clinical practice. items.title: The formation of egocentric bias in visual perspective-taking.
items.abstract: In visual perspective-taking (VPT), individuals may interpret others' viewpoints on the basis of their own perspective, resulting in egocentric bias. Egocentric bias directly leads to failed social interactions. However, the formation of egocentric bias is only partially understood. Previous studies primarily used the participant-oriented view to examine the mechanisms of egocentric bias, while neglecting how people process objects in VPT. Therefore, the present study used the object-oriented view to examine the formation of egocentric bias by integrating the priming paradigm with the Level-2 VPT paradigm. Across two experiments, the participants first heard an auditory cue of the target and then viewed a priming stimulus. Subsequently, a target and a distractor were presented on the 2 × 2 grid, with both vertically inverted. Meanwhile, an avatar was placed next to the grid, facing away from or toward the participants with the same or opposite perspectives. The participants judged the location of the target from the avatar's perspective. The auditory cue and priming stimulus were congruent and incongruent in Experiments 1 and 2, respectively. The results showed that the interaction between the perspective and the priming location significantly affected the participants' egocentric bias. These results indicate that egocentric bias includes two distinct cognitive processes: target selection and interference rejection. Furthermore, these dual processes might be based on visual mental imagery. Overall, this study is the first to use an object-oriented view to reveal the formation of egocentric bias in Level-2 VPT.
