items.title: Reference group use and exploration of age- and self-comparative modifications of the EQ-5D-5L.
items.abstract: We aimed to explore the potential reference groups respondents use when completing EQ-5D-5L and the relevance and comprehensibility of an age-comparative (hereafter: 'Yourage') and a self-comparative (hereafter: 'Youngerself') EQ-5D-5​L modification. In 2024-2025, semi-structured, face-to-face interviews were conducted with 51 adults from the general population, using age- and gender-purposive sampling. A topic guide was developed, and qualitative data were thematically analysed. Alongside the qualitative findings, frequencies were reported for reference group use and preferences regarding the modifications. 29% reported using at least one reference group when completing at least one EQ-5D-5L dimension, with 18% referring to their 'younger self' and 4% to 'people of my age'. Reference group use ranged from 6% (self-care) to 24% (mobility). Some participants found the modifications difficult (e.g. the 'original' is shorter), while others mentioned that they offered a more realistic assessment of their health. Views on the Yourage were mixed, with concerns about the relevance and feasibility of peer comparisons, whereas the Youngerself was more favourably evaluated by respondents for its realistic and reflective nature. The Youngerself descriptive system was preferred over the original by 59% of respondents, while preferences for the Yourage and both EQ VAS modifications remained below 50%. One-third of participants use reference groups when reporting their health on the EQ-5D-5​L, which may lead to response heterogeneity. The findings may be relevant to other multi-item health status measures beyond the EQ-5D. A mix of criticisms and advantages emerged for the two modifications, each potentially valuable in specific circumstances.

items.title: Toward a comprehensive view of peripersonal space: From upper-limb foundations to lower-limb frontiers.
items.abstract: Peripersonal space (PPS) refers to the area immediately surrounding the body, where multisensory signals are more strongly integrated. This space is shaped by neural mechanisms that support both goal-directed actions and defensive behaviors. Most existing research on PPS is based on the upper limbs, however. Consequently, current models of PPS are largely based on hand-centered tasks, leaving open important questions about the generalizability of PPS across other body parts, such as the lower limbs. This is an important limitation, because the lower limbs play an important role in locomotion, postural control, and motor planning, functions that also require a dynamic mapping of nearby space. This review aims to fill parts of this gap in the literature. In doing so, we start by providing a comprehensive review of the existing literature on the upper limb PPS and extrapolate these findings to the lower limbs by discussing the still somewhat limited literature that has focused on lower limb PPS. In doing so, we offer a basic framework for understanding PPS around the feet and list key questions for future research.

items.title: Armillaria mellea Polysaccharides Attenuate Depression-Like Behaviors in Mice Exposed to Chronic Restraint Stress.
items.abstract: Armillaria mellea polysaccharides (AMP) have been investigated for their antioxidant and neuroprotective properties. This study evaluated the behavioral effects of AMP during chronic restraint stress (CRS) exposure and explored accompanying hippocampal protein patterns. Fifty male C57BL/6 mice were assigned to control, CRS, low-dose AMP (50 mg/kg/day), high-dose AMP (100 mg/kg/day), or fluoxetine groups (10 mice per group). AMP was administered orally during 21 days of CRS. Behavioral assessments included sucrose preference, forced swimming, tail suspension, open-field exploration, and Morris water maze (MWM) testing. Histological staining and exploratory western blot measurements were also examined. AMP-treated mice showed lower immobility and improvements in selected sucrose-preference and spatial-learning outcomes relative to CRS mice. Locomotor differences complicate interpretation of the immobility-based outcomes. Hippocampal blots showed descriptive differences in inflammatory, apoptosis-related, synaptic protein, and phosphorylation markers for c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) and p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase. Western blot observations from three independent mice per group were interpreted as exploratory. The behavioral findings support further preclinical investigation of AMP during stress exposure.

items.title: Associations of Neighborhood Retail Availability and Psychosocial Resources with Smoking and Alcohol Co-use in Black Americans.
items.abstract: Smoking and alcohol use are established risk behaviors for cancer, but their co-use may increase cancer risk significantly. These behaviors are shaped not by social determinants of health alone but by the neighborhood retail environment, which often disadvantages Black Americans. Psychosocial resources, however, may serve as protective factors. We examined whether the availability of alcohol and tobacco stores in neighborhoods was associated with smoking and alcohol co-use in Black Americans and whether psychosocial resources moderated these associations. We analyzed data from a nationally representative probability sample of Black Americans linked to census-tract measures. Multinomial logistic regression models assessed the adjusted relative risk ratio (aRRR) of neighborhood alcohol and tobacco availability with two co-use outcomes: (1) current smoking and drinking, (2) current smoking and binge drinking. Greater neighborhood retail availability of alcohol stores was associated with a higher (aRRR = 1.07-1.08) likelihood of co-use. Religious involvement, among the psychosocial resources, was a protective factor; participants with medium (aRRR = 0.39-0.43) or high (aRRR = 0.33) involvement were less likely than those with low involvement to report either co-use; however, no significant moderating effect was detected. Our study underscores the need for multilevel and multisectoral strategies for reducing the risk of smoking and drinking and preventing cancer in Black Americans. Reducing co-use may require stronger regulation of alcohol than of tobacco retail density in underserved neighborhoods, alongside tax and pricing policies that limit access. Partnerships with trusted community institutions may also strengthen culturally relevant protective resources against co-use.

items.title: Information seeking decisions often follow information comparison dynamics in anterior cingulate, orbitofrontal and lateral prefrontal cortex.
items.abstract: Subjects often engage in cognitive activity that requires gathering and evaluating information across multiple stages of a decision process before committing to a choice. To investigate how primate prefrontal subregions collaborate to decide whether sufficient information has been gathered to commit to a choice, we focused on a decision point-whether to continue seeking information or to choose an option immediately-in a decision-making task where two monkeys sequentially gathered information about two options differing in reward size and probability. A Q-learning framework revealed that both animals demonstrated information-seeking biases but followed distinct strategies. To characterize the neural dynamics underlying this decision, we examined the dynamics of latent neural representations in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) using representational similarity-based regression analysis (RSRA) and demixed principal component analysis (dPCA). We identified two latent factors with distinct temporal dynamics: one representing the option comparison and another representing the seek-versus-commit decision. During option comparison, the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) identified the better option before quantifying its advantage, with complementary contributions from the orbitofrontal (OFC) and dorsolateral prefrontal (dlPFC) cortices. The dynamics of information-seeking decision often followed those of option comparison across conditions, consistent with the distinct behavioral strategies of the two monkeys. Based on these dissociable representations in the PFC, a neural network model with a two-stage winner-take-all architecture was constructed. In this network, the first module compares the two options, and the second arbitrates between seeking and committing. The model reproduced the observed behavioral patterns and provided a potential account for subject-specific information-seeking biases. Together, our findings suggest a mechanistic account for how the PFC subregions might support sequential decision making.

items.title: The benefit of external focus of attention is preserved in the VR punching task regardless of haptic information.
items.abstract: In punching a boxing bag, a salient source of information for the movement effect is the felt impact. Using virtual reality (VR), we manipulated the haptic information specifying the impact, to test if indeed the advantage of external focus relates to attention toward the movement effect. Twenty-four participants (18 males, 6 females) performed a punching task under both internal and external focus of attention instructions across two separate sessions. Participants wore a VR headset and punched a bag in two conditions: a virtual bag (without haptic information on the movement effect) and physical bag (with haptic information). Hand velocity at impact functioned as the performance measure. Linear mixed-effects model analysis revealed a significant main effect of attentional focus, with higher punching velocity under external compared to internal focus of attention. A significant main effect of bag was also observed, with higher velocity when striking the physical bag compared to the virtual bag. Critically, the interaction of attentional focus and bag condition was not significant, indicating that the advantage of external focus of attention was preserved regardless of the availability of haptic information related to movement effects. This finding challenges the explanation from common coding theory that the advantage of an external focus is due to its attention for anticipated movement effect. Rather, it is consistent with an ecological perspective that external focus is superior because it fosters attunement to task relevant information specifying the dynamic relation between the fist and the target.

items.title: Subgenome-Resolved Assembly of the Mahseer Tor tambra Reveals Allotetraploid Subgenomes Shared with Tor sinensis.
items.abstract: Mahseers ( Tor spp.) are cyprinids of high conservation and aquaculture value, and their genomes carry extensive gene duplication. Whether this duplication reflects 2 subgenomes has not been resolved at chromosome scale. We assembled a 1.76-Gb genome of a wild female Tor tambra from southern Thailand using Oxford Nanopore and Omni-C data. K-mer spectra were best fitted by a tetraploid model with a monoploid size of 0.85 Gb. Alignment to both subgenomes of Tor sinensis revealed 30 Hi-C joins between homoeologous chromosomes (22 confirmed with Hi-C); most were fold-back joins that leave a mirror-image contact signature yet pass standard contact-continuity checks. After correction, the scaffolds were ordered against the matching T. sinensis chromosomes, placing 1.56 Gb (88.4%) in 25 pseudo-chromosomes per subgenome (consensus quality value [QV] 31.7; 99.4% complete Benchmarking Universal Single-Copy Orthologs [BUSCOs]). Subgenome-specific k-mers separated the 2 subgenomes without a reference (100% bootstrap support for every chromosome; 98.9% of 1-Mb windows consistent). In a joint analysis, each T. tambra chromosome grouped with its T. sinensis ortholog by subgenome rather than by species, and homoeolog divergence (median synonymous divergence 0.11 to 0.13) was about 5 times ortholog divergence (0.02). The 2 species therefore share the same pair of progenitor subgenomes. The public T. sinensis hap1 and hap2 sets each combine chromosomes from both subgenomes. Subgenome-matched gene trees grouped the copies of each subgenome from 4 species (88.1% of 1,602 loci), supporting a single allopolyploidization before the divergence of Tor and Neolissochilus , and placed T. tambra sister to T. tambroides . This assembly is a subgenome-aware reference for mahseer evolution and conservation.

items.title: The Burden of Cancer Attributable to Dietary Risk Factors in China, 1990-2023.
items.abstract: Objective This study aimed to comprehensively analyze the burden of cancer attributable to dietary risk factors in China from 1990-2023 and explore age-and sex-specific patterns to inform targeted prevention strategies. Methods Using data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 study, we evaluated China's diet-attributable cancer burden using absolute death counts, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), age-standardized mortality rates (ASMRs), and age-standardized DALY rates (ASDRs). Estimated annual percentage changes (EAPCs) were computed to characterize temporal trends. Results In 2023, dietary risks were responsible for 168,740.24 (95% UI: 58,919.72-314,396.91) deaths and 4,096,470.77 (95% UI: 1,338,318.09-7,634,577.27) DALYs from the included diet-attributable cancers. Between 1990 and 2023, the overall ASMR (EAPC = -3.09, 95% CI: -3.28--2.90) and ASDR (EAPC = -3.28, 95% CI: -3.47--3.10) for these cancers demonstrated a decreasing trend, with colorectal cancer (CRC) accounting for the largest diet-attributable cancer burden. Diets high in red meat, low in milk, and low in whole grains were the three leading risk contributors, and stratified analyses revealed a markedly higher burden among males and older adults. Conclusion Although age-standardized rates (ASRs) of diet-attributable cancer in China have declined over the past three decades, the absolute disease burden remains substantial. Suboptimal dietary patterns characterized by high red meat intake together with inadequate milk and whole grain consumption continue to drive this burden, particularly among males and older adults, underscoring the urgent need for targeted public health interventions for dietary adjustments in these high-risk groups.

items.title: Care for Sexually Transmitted Infections among Transgender Women Provided by Family Health Strategy Nurses in Brazil: A Cross-sectional Study.
items.abstract: This cross-sectional study examined sexually transmitted infection (STI)-related care for transgender women (TGW) reported by Family Health Strategy (FHS) nurses in Brazil and factors associated with its provision. From June 2023 to March 2024, 442 FHS nurses were recruited through non-probability referral-based sampling. An online questionnaire assessed professional characteristics, TGW care conditions, and STI-related care practices. Analyzes used descriptive statistics, chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, and multivariable Poisson regression with robust variance estimation. Multiple comparisons underwent false discovery rate (FDR) adjustment. Overall, 296 nurses (66.97%) reported providing STI-related care to TGW. The adjusted prevalence of care provision was 31% higher among nurses with training or qualifications in transgender health (aPR = 1.31, 95% CI 1.15-1.50) and 18% higher among those earning five or more minimum wages (aPR = 1.18, 95% CI 1.03-1.35). The income estimate showed greater statistical uncertainty after accounting for municipality-level clustering (p = 0.052), whereas the training association remained statistically significant. Among nurses reporting care provision, PrEP/PEP counseling was more frequently reported by trained than untrained nurses (90.59% vs. 75.36%; FDR-adjusted p = 0.032). Training in transgender health was associated with a higher prevalence of self-reported STI-related care provision for TGW, highlighting its relevance to public health nursing practice.

items.title: Cerebral redistribution in late-onset fetal growth restriction: relation between abnormalities of individual Doppler components and adverse outcomes.
items.abstract: Objectives Cerebral redistribution consists of the preferential redirection of the arterial and well-oxygenated blood flow to the fetal brain and is commonly associated with fetal growth restriction (FGR) secondary to placental insufficiency. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the perinatal outcomes of fetuses with late-onset FGR and cerebral redistribution, examining whether outcomes differed according to the normality or abnormality of the individual Doppler components that determine a reduction in the cerebroplacental ratio (CPR). Methods This was a retrospective, multicenter cohort study conducted across four tertiary maternity units in Italy (University of Parma, Parma; Fondazione Policlinico Universitario 'A. Gemelli' IRCCS, Rome; IRCCS Materno Infantile Burlo Garofolo, Trieste; and University of Brescia, Brescia), including non-anomalous singleton pregnancies complicated by late-onset FGR associated with cerebral redistribution (defined as CPR th percentile according to the Fetal Medicine Foundation reference charts). The study included cases collected at the four participating units between January 2019 and December 2024. Cases were categorized according to umbilical artery (UA) and middle cerebral artery (MCA) Doppler data (Group 1: normal UA-pulsatility index (PI) (≤ 95 th percentile for gestational age) and MCA-PI (≥ 5 th percentile); Group 2: abnormal UA-PI (> 95 th percentile) and normal MCA-PI; Group 3: normal UA-PI and abnormal MCA-PI ( th percentile); and Group 4: abnormal UA-PI and MCA-PI), and perinatal outcomes were compared and evaluated using univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses. Results In total, 352 cases were included, of which 117 (33.2%) were assigned to Group 1, 84 (23.9%) to Group 2, 85 (24.1%) to Group 3 and 66 (18.8%) to Group 4. In the univariate logistic regression analysis, Group 4 showed greater odds of preterm delivery (odds ratio (OR), 2.07 (95% CI, 1.08-3.96); P = 0.03), birth weight rd percentile (OR, 2.44 (95% CI, 1.31-4.57); P = 0.01), neonatal hypoglycemia (OR, 3.34 (95% CI, 1.46-7.67); P rd percentile (OR, 1.92 (95% CI, 1.07-3.46); P = 0.03) and Group 3 showed greater odds of birth weight rd percentile (OR, 1.79 (95% CI, 1.01-3.26); P = 0.02) and CAPO (OR, 1.88 (95% CI, 1.05-3.38); P = 0.03) compared with Group 1. However, in the multivariable logistic regression analysis only Group 4 was associated with greater odds of birth weight rd percentile (adjusted OR, 2.11 (95% CI, 1.11-4.00); P = 0.02) and neonatal hypoglycemia (adjusted OR, 2.68 (95% CI, 1.10-6.50); P = 0.03) compared with Group 1. In the univariate logistic regression analysis, abnormal UA and MCA Doppler parameters were also associated with perinatal complications. However, none of the associations were confirmed after adjustment for gestational age at delivery and birth weight in the multivariable models. Conclusions In cases of late-onset FGR associated with cerebral redistribution, isolated abnormalities of the UA-PI or MCA-PI could not identify fetuses at increased risk of perinatal complications. However, the coexistence of both abnormal UA-PI and abnormal MCA-PI, indicating the highest extent of cerebral redistribution, was independently associated with perinatal complications including neonatal hypoglycemia and birth weight rd percentile. In such cases, birth weight was also independently associated with perinatal complications. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

items.title: Building Workforce Capacity Through the Applied Epidemiology Fellowship Program: A 5-Year Assessment, 2019-2024.
items.abstract: Objectives In 2003, the Council of State and Territorial Epidemiologists (CSTE) partnered with the Centers for Control and Prevention to establish the Applied Epidemiology Fellowship (AEF) program. Fellows are placed for 2 years at a state, Tribal, local, or territorial (STLT) health department. We assessed the immediate career outcomes of AEF graduates during 2019-2024. Methods We used existing administrative and programmatic data collected by CSTE on all participating fellows (N = 174) during 2019-2024 for analysis. We sent a follow-up assessment to the subset of fellows (n = 96) with missing information to improve data completeness. Results During 2019-2024, 158 fellows successfully completed AEF program requirements and were included in the analysis. All were placed in a jurisdictional health department, and most (n = 110; 69.6%) were placed at a state health department. Of those with available employment information, 83.6% (122 of 146) accepted a job at a government public health agency immediately after graduation from the fellowship and 52.9% (82 of 155) took a position at their fellowship host site. When asked, "What type of impact has the fellowship had on your future career plans?," respondents noted that the fellowship was impactful in their career planning and ability to apply to epidemiology positions. Conclusions Our results indicate that the AEF program is a strong pipeline for careers in STLT health departments. In the face of recent workforce shortages and struggles, epidemiology training programs such as AEF are essential to growing epidemiologic workforce capacity in government public health agencies and improving our ability to respond to emerging and persistent public health needs.

items.title: Whole-Exome Sequencing for Diagnostic Investigation of 267 Patients From the Brazilian Public Health System (SUS) Followed by Reanalysis of Nondiagnostic Cases.
items.abstract: Although advances in genetic testing in recent years have improved patient care, especially regarding rare diseases, the path to molecular diagnosis remains lengthy for many patients in Brazil, particularly among families who rely exclusively on the public health system. Between 2017 and 2023, a total of 267 patients with suspected rare diseases were recruited from the Genetics Unit of the Instituto da Criança do Hospital das Clínicas da Universidade de São Paulo; blood samples from the probands and, when available, their parents were sent to Yokohama City University and submitted to whole-exome sequencing (WES). Among the 267 cases, 124 (46.4%) received molecular diagnostic findings; most of these patients had intellectual disability or developmental delay. In addition, 130 cases (48.6%) were classified as "no relevant variant identified" and another 13 cases (4.8%) were considered inconclusive; all underwent reanalysis of WES data, which led to a molecular diagnosis in 10 additional cases (7%) previously undetected, primarily through newly established gene-disease associations or updated interpretations of previously identified variants. Our diagnostic yield (46.4%) was consistent with those reported in large cohorts and meta-analysis published internationally. However, nondiagnostic results warrant further consideration and WES reanalysis should be considered as a strategy to improve diagnostic outcomes, even if mostly through periodic literature reviews and variant reinterpretation.

items.title: GPs' and patients' perceptions regarding the quality of remote consultations: a matched survey from Norwegian general practice.
items.abstract: Background Remote consultations, via text, telephone, or video, are increasingly used in primary care, yet direct comparisons of matched GP and patient evaluations remain limited. This study examines positive concordance between GPs and patients across three predefined dimensions: (1) consultation suitability, (2) confidence in the GP's professional assessment, and (3) willingness to reuse the modality. Methods In a cross-sectional matched GP-patient study, GPs and patients evaluated the same remote consultations. During enrolment in a Norwegian online course, GPs evaluated their own consultations and invited patients to complete corresponding assessments ( n = 580). Descriptive statistics and logistic regression were used to analyse concordance across the three dimensions. Results In 85% of consultations, GPs and patients agreed that the modality was suitable for the main reason for contact. Concordance was lower when the issue was new to the GP (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 0.47, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.28-0.80) and when patients did not receive adequate answers to their questions (aOR = 0.02 (0.002-0.20)). Concordance in confidence in the GP's assessment was 93%, with lower odds in asynchronous text consultations than in video (aOR = 0.06 (0.006-0.50)). 75% of GP-patient pairs were willing to reuse the modality. Concordance in willingness to reuse was higher for scheduled appointments than acute contacts (aOR = 1.62 (1.07-2.46)) and lower when GPs perceived the patient's health literacy as low (aOR = 0.25 (0.08-0.79)). Lower concordance across all three dimensions was associated with patients reporting less opportunity to ask questions or receive answers during the consultation. Conclusion The matched GP-patient design proved feasible and offers a novel approach to evaluating remote consultations. Positive quality concordance was high, particularly in consultations concerning known problems and in scheduled rather than acute contacts. Consultation quality may be strengthened by addressing modifiable factors, including continuity, scheduling, tailoring consultations to patients' vulnerability and health literacy, and ensuring clear communication.

items.title: Listening to the Patient Voice: Patients' Articulation of Dissatisfaction in Dental Practice - a Qualitative Study.
items.abstract: Patients express their complaints and dissatisfaction in different ways in dental practice. Writing a complaint letter is one way where patients communicate their concerns about their dental care. This retrospective study explores how patients express and communicate their complaints, how they express their frustrations and the way they seek closure to their worries about their care. To fulfil this aim, 75 letters of complaint submitted by patients and carers about their general dental practitioners (GDPs) in the UK were reviewed. The letters, received by a dental corporate and a dental indemnity company, were analysed using content analysis and a thematic approach. The analysis focused on the language and emotions expressed by patients in describing their experiences and sources of dissatisfaction. Results showed that patients commented on dental experiences which left them feeling intimidated, frustrated, disappointed and unhappy. Several patients felt that their voice had not been heard, they had been ignored, dismissed, or they had no choices or options to remedy their complaint. Patients cited physical, mental and social issues as a result of what they perceived as poor dental care and their interactions with dental teams. Data showed that patients ascribe much value on communication skills, particularly on how communication is delivered, valued and articulated with them. Complainants' views of what constitutes professionalism are not fully aligned with the regulator and dental teams. This study concluded that dental teams need to be mindful in engaging with the patient voice proactively, both before and during the complaints process with a recognition of the emotional aspects of complaints. Communication and professionalism training, alongside a deeper understanding of public expectations, are essential.

items.title: Youth perspectives on tuberculosis prevention in South Africa: A qualitative study in faith-based organisations.
items.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a leading public health challenge in South Africa, with high rates of co-infection with HIV. Faith-based organisations (FBOs) have untapped potential to support TB prevention, particularly by engaging youth who are often overlooked. This study explored youth perspectives on TB prevention and FBOs' roles in advancing youth-led, culturally grounded health promotion strategies in Johannesburg, South Africa. A qualitative, exploratory study was conducted using five focus group discussions with youth aged 18-30 years from Christian, Muslim, and Rastafarian faith communities. The study was guided by principles of Community-Based Participatory Research and Human-Centered Design, applying the 'Define' and 'Develop' phases of the Double Diamond model. Data were analysed using thematic analysis. Participants demonstrated a blend of biomedical knowledge and persistent TB myths. Youth identified FBOs as trusted yet underutilised platforms and proposed strategies including music, storytelling, drama, peer-led health clubs, and digital campaigns. They expressed readiness to lead within faith institutions but noted barriers, including resistance from traditional hierarchies and limited resources. Youth in faith communities possess the creativity, insight, and commitment to transform TB prevention efforts. Strengthening partnerships between youth and FBOs, and investing in participatory, faith-aligned health promotion models, could yield more equitable and sustainable public health outcomes in high-burden settings.

items.title: Rehabilitating Sexual Offenders in Nigerian Correctional Institutions: A Multidisciplinary Evaluation of Current Practices and Pathways for Reform.
items.abstract: Despite global advances in evidence-based responses to sexual offending, little is known about how individuals convicted of sexual offences are assessed and treated in Nigerian correctional institutions. This study addresses this gap through a multidisciplinary qualitative inquiry conducted across six states in South-West Nigeria, drawing on interviews with incarcerated individuals, correctional staff, health professionals, NGO practitioners and legal officers. Drawing on the Risk-Need-Responsivity model, the Good Lives Model and Cognitive-Behavioural Therapy, the analysis reveals fragmented and non-standardised assessment practices, limited psychological screening at intake and reliance on informal judgement. Rehabilitation is largely generic, focused on vocational and educational programmes, while offence-specific psychological treatment remains marginal. Structural constraints, weak inter-agency coordination, limited NGO collaboration and the absence of integrated reintegration planning result in minimal continuity of post-release programmes. The findings highlight systemic governance and policy gaps, underscoring the need for legally grounded, context-sensitive, evidence-based reforms to strengthen rehabilitation and public safety.

items.title: Maternal Substance Use During Pregnancy and Congenital Syphilis Among Hospitalized Neonates.
items.abstract: Objectives US congenital syphilis (CS) cases have increased 10-fold in the past decade, exceeding 3700 cases in 2022. This study evaluated the association between maternal substance use during pregnancy and CS among hospitalized neonates by region and year. Methods We analyzed hospitalized neonates (postnatal age ≤28 days) in the Kids' Inpatient Database from 2016, 2019, and 2022. We identified CS using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision codes and categorized maternal substance use as no substance use, single substance use, or polysubstance use. Using survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression, we tested effect modification by region and year. Results Among 4 531 346 hospitalized neonates, 217 220 (weighted prevalence = 2.5%) had maternal substance use during pregnancy. CS prevalence among substance-exposed neonates increased 467% from 2.5 to 14.5 per 1000 neonates between 2016 and 2022, compared with 0.2 to 0.8 per 1000 neonates among unexposed neonates. After adjusting for demographic charateristics, health insurance status, median household income, housing insecurity, year, and region, single substance use and polysubstance use were associated with higher odds of CS (single substance use: adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 9.68; 95% CI, 8.88-10.55; and polysubstance use: AOR = 17.18; 95% CI, 15.21-19.40). We observed a significant effect modification: the association was much stronger in the West region of the United States (interaction OR = 4.80; 95% CI, 3.10-7.44) than in the Northeast, and the polysubstance use association was significantly elevated in 2022 relative to 2016 (interaction OR = 3.10; 95% CI, 1.81-5.30). Conclusions Maternal substance use was strongly associated with CS. These findings underscore the need to address structural barriers to prenatal care through the expansion and integration of syphilis screening within substance use treatment and harm-reduction contexts, especially in regions with a high burden of CS.

items.title: Operational criteria for the ethical justification of wastewater surveillance.
items.abstract: Wastewater surveillance (WWS) for pathogen monitoring is transitioning from emergency deployment to routine monitoring of endemic pathogens, yet ethical guidance has not kept pace. As implementation becomes more granular and supported by advanced next-generation sequencing, neither blanket consent waivers nor opt-in/opt-out models can adequately address the complex ethical risks inherent in WWS. Drawing on ethical, legal and scientific expertise, this Perspective article operationalizes five justificatory conditions drawn from public health ethics, namely public justification, effectiveness, proportionality, necessity, and least infringement, for WWS contexts in which individual consent is infeasible. It translates these conditions into scenario-based evaluation criteria and procedures, requiring meaningful public engagement and treating non-deployment as a legitimate option where WWS cannot be sufficiently justified, alongside safeguards such as limited data retention and host-DNA depletion. This Perspective article therefore provides one step towards bridging the gap between high-level guidelines and field implementation, supporting accountable practice and sustained public trust.

items.title: Old threats anew: protecting progress in infectious disease and sexual health.
items.abstract: Background Decades of international collaboration have produced extraordinary advances in infectious disease and sexual health, including effective treatment and prevention of HIV, long-acting prevention technologies, and vaccines against sexually transmitted infections. These achievements have depended not only on individual discoveries, but also on sustained investments in research institutions, clinical trial networks, laboratories, surveillance systems, health services, trained investigators, and trusted partnerships. Main body Recent disruptions to international health assistance and research have exposed the vulnerability of this ecosystem. Reductions in development assistance and major changes in United States foreign assistance have affected HIV testing and prevention, community outreach, health workforces, sexual and reproductive health services, and organizations serving marginalized populations. The effects have been substantial but uneven: treatment programs and mature research institutions have often proved more resilient than prevention and community-based services. This contrast is especially consequential as scientific progress produces powerful new interventions, such as long-acting HIV prevention, whose impact depends on functioning systems capable of delivering them. The experience also demonstrates the value of long-term investments in locally led scientific capacity and durable international partnerships. Conclusion The goal should not be simply to reconstruct the previous global health architecture. Protecting progress against old and emerging threats will require stronger national and regional institutions, diversified and sustainable financing, locally led science, continued investment in global public goods, and reciprocal international partnerships. Scientific capacity and trust take decades to build and should be preserved before the next breakthrough or the next epidemic requires them.

items.title: Network Analysis of Intergenerational Support and Social Frailty Among Older Adults With Chronic Diseases.
items.abstract: Aim To examine the item-level associations between intergenerational support and social frailty using network analysis. Background Existing evidence suggests that intergenerational support is negatively associated with social frailty. However, little is known about how specific components of intergenerational support relate to individual elements of social frailty. Network analysis offers a useful approach for examining these item-level interconnections. Design A cross-sectional survey. Methods A total of 518 older adults with chronic diseases were recruited through convenience sampling from three hospital districts of a tertiary general hospital in Guangzhou, China, between December 2023 and October 2024. Intergenerational support and social frailty were measured using the Intergenerational Support Scale and the Social Frailty Index Scale, respectively. Network analysis was conducted to estimate and characterize the network structure linking intergenerational support and social frailty. The study was reported following the STROBE checklist. Results The network analysis identified SF3 (No confidant) and SF7 (Socioeconomic deprivation) as the most central nodes. IS3 (Children listen), IS7 (Financial support from children), and SF7 (Socioeconomic deprivation) showed potential bridging roles between intergenerational support and social frailty. No significant gender difference was observed in global network strength; however, the overall network structure differed between men and women. Conclusion This study characterized the item-level associations between intergenerational support and social frailty among older adults with chronic diseases. Interventions targeting key central and potential bridge nodes may help strengthen intergenerational support and mitigate social frailty. Patient or public contribution No patient or public contribution. Impact These findings provide insights for nursing practice by identifying potentially important aspects of intergenerational support and social frailty. Nurses may consider assessing intergenerational support and socioeconomic disadvantage when evaluating social frailty, facilitating intergenerational communication, and connecting socially vulnerable older adults with appropriate resources. In addition, exploratory gender-specific findings suggest the potential value of considering gender differences in the manifestation of social frailty among older adults.

items.title: Risk of fragility fractures in individuals with and without HIV infection: a population-based matched case-control study.
items.abstract: HIV infection increases hip fracture risk, but evidence in Asian populations is limited. In this large nationwide matched cohort study, antiretroviral therapy mitigated overall fracture risk and reduced postoperative mortality despite persistent skeletal concerns. These findings highlight the importance of bone health monitoring and prevention in individuals with HIV infection. Purpose Patients with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection are at increased risk of comorbidities, including osteoporosis, which predisposes them to fragility fractures (FFs). Evidence from Asian populations is limited. This study investigated the risk of FFs in an Asian population with and without HIV infection. Methods We conducted a nationwide retrospective matched cohort study using Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database. A total of 3994 individuals with HIV infection and 15,976 matched controls were identified (1:4 ratio). Matching variables included age, sex, monthly income, urbanization, liver cirrhosis, diabetes mellitus, renal failure, and hepatitis B and C infection. Fragility fractures were identified using ICD-9-CM codes, and Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results The incidence of overall fragility fractures (AFF) was similar between HIV-infected and uninfected individuals (12.9% vs. 11.9%, P = 0.097). However, HIV infection was associated with a significantly higher risk of hip fragility fracture (HFF) (HR 2.22, 95% CI 1.62-3.06, P 50 years, modified Charlson Comorbidity Index ≥ 2, hypertension, and diabetes mellitus. Antiretroviral therapy (ART) mitigated overall fracture risk and was associated with substantially lower postoperative mortality after fracture surgery (9.4% vs. 36.1%). Conclusion HIV infection was associated with increased hip fracture risk in this Asian population. ART conferred protective effects on overall fracture risk and survival after fracture, underscoring its net clinical benefit despite skeletal concerns. These findings support targeted bone health monitoring and preventive strategies in individuals with HIV in fection.

items.title: Large-scale antibody reactome profiling identifies herpesvirus-autoantigen associations that underlie chronic diseases.
items.abstract: Herpesviruses infect nearly all humans and have long been implicated in autoimmune and chronic diseases, yet their interactions with host proteins have not been systematically characterized. We profiled immunoglobulin G reactivities to >4,600 herpesvirus peptides and >15,000 human proteins using multiplexed protein display in two Mass General Brigham Biobank cohorts (discovery n = 1,289; replication n = 763), with longitudinal electronic health record follow-up. We identified and replicated 4,943 FDR-significant associations across 106 autoantigens, including previously uncharacterized viral-autoantigen axes, such as PHLDA1 and ZNF550. Eleven autoantigens were predicted by viral reactivities with >85% accuracy in independent validation, two of which exhibited viral-host sequence homology consistent with possible molecular mimicry. Integrating immune reactivities with incident diseases revealed virus-specific networks. Cytomegalovirus formed the largest multimorbid network, Epstein-Barr virus converged on pleiotropic autoimmune hubs and herpes simplex viruses formed partially overlapping networks. These findings define a herpesvirus-autoantigen-disease network atlas and prioritize candidate viral-host immune axes for mechanistic investigation.

items.title: Multiancestry genome-wide association and integrative multiomics analyses implicate key pathways in endometriosis.
items.abstract: Endometriosis is a painful and heterogeneous condition that affects up to one in ten women. Its genetic underpinnings remain partially unknown, and its precise disease mechanisms are yet to be elucidated. Here we report a genome-wide study of endometriosis as part of the Global Biobank Meta-analysis Initiative representing over 1 million participants (32% non-European ancestry). We detected 58 genomic regions (27 previously unreported) across diverse ancestry groups and new procedure-confirmed case identification algorithms. These include loci unique to African and admixed American populations. A search for genetically driven comorbidities revealed dozens of associations with known and previously uncharacterized risk factors. Then, within prioritized cellular contexts, we found numerous examples of gene expression affected by endometriosis status. Including further multiomic analyses, we implicated a total of 314 genes, suggesting multiple targets for therapeutic intervention. Our findings span molecular, cellular and phenotypic scales, highlighting interconnected pathways that underscore the multifaceted etiology of endometriosis.

items.title: Benefits and harms of antihypertensive treatment a modelling study in 5.5 million electronic health records.
items.abstract: Antihypertensive prescription is guided by cardiovascular risk prediction models. However, existing models often exclude individuals with prior cardiovascular disease or those prescribed statin treatment. Consequently, there is limited evidence regarding how the benefits and harms of treatment vary according to an individual's baseline risk. This cohort study includes 5,578,002 patients aged≥40years (mean age 59; 52% women) from the Clinical Practice Research Datalink between 1998-2018. A cardiovascular risk prediction model is developed using the Clinical Practice Research Datalink GOLD dataset and externally validated using the Aurum dataset. The model demonstrates excellent calibration and discrimination. Antihypertensive therapy is more likely to prevent serious major cardiovascular events (eight events prevented per 1,000 patients over 10 years, 95% confidence interval = 1 to 14), than to cause serious falls (two events per 1,000 patients, 95% confidence interval = -4 to 10). The risks of other adverse events indicate more nuanced or potentially harmful trade-offs. Here we show that a cardiovascular risk prediction model developed using routinely collected primary care data accurately predicts risk across a broad population of patients eligible for antihypertensive treatment. These findings will enable clinicians to better communicate individualised benefits and risks of antihypertensive therapy.

items.title: Genome-wide association study identifies a functional myostatin variant increasing lean mass in humans.
items.abstract: Muscle mass is central to physical function and metabolic health, but can decrease with disease, aging and weight loss interventions. As weight loss interventions become more widely used, agents that preserve or increase muscle mass are needed. To identify such therapeutic opportunities, we perform genome-wide association meta-analyses of arm, leg, trunk and total lean mass measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, a widely used method to estimate muscle mass. We identify 63 loci, including a rare missense variant in MSTN (p.Ile225Thr, rs143242500), which has the largest effect on leg lean mass (β = 0.28 SD [95% CI: 0.19, 0.37], P = 1.9 × 10 -9 ). MSTN encodes myostatin, a negative regulator of skeletal muscle mass and a therapeutic target for muscle wasting disorders. Here, we identify a genome-wide significant association at MSTN in humans and characterize its functional consequences, providing genetic evidence that may inform the long-term systemic effects of myostatin inhibition.

items.title: Met4All: a dockerised Shiny application for DNA methylation array analysis, visualization and reporting.
items.abstract: Motivation DNA methylation profiling is widely used for tumour classification, biomarker discovery and the identification of molecular subgroups. However, routine analysis of Infinium methylation-array data typically requires combining multiple R packages and custom scripts for preprocessing, quality control and downstream interpretation. Results We developed Met4All (Methylation For All), a dockerised Shiny application for integrated analysis of Infinium HumanMethylation450K, EPIC and EPIC v2 array data. Met4All accepts both raw IDAT files and precomputed beta matrices, enabling either end-to-end preprocessing or direct downstream analysis within the same interface. It integrates automated quality control, normalisation, dimensionality reduction (MDS, PCA, UMAP), consensus heatmaps, global methylation profiling, two-group differential methylation analysis, gene-set enrichment testing and copy-number analysis. Structure discovery relies on unsupervised learning (UMAP with graph-based community detection, and consensus clustering); no supervised classification or model-based feature selection is implemented. Outputs are exportable as publication-ready plots and tables for use in downstream workflows. In a systematic comparison against nine representative tools, Met4All was the only one to make all 17 assessed criteria available within a single graphical interface, although individual criteria are supported by several of the frameworks compared. The framework has already supported published methylation studies and is illustrated here on independent public data. Met4All provides an accessible and reproducible environment for integrated methylation-array analysis without requiring extensive bioinformatics expertise. Availability Met4All is implemented in R as a dockerised Shiny application. Source code, Docker configuration files and documentation are available at https://github.com/gcampof/Met4All, and the version described here is archived at Zenodo (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23265674). Supplementary information Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

items.title: "We take care of ours": Dementia Care Partner Perspectives on Consumer- vs Agency-Directed Care.
items.abstract: Background and objectives Medicaid-funded personal care provides essential support enabling persons with dementia to remain in the community. This care is managed either by an agency (agency-direction) or by the care recipient or their designee (consumer-direction). Persons with dementia are more likely to use consumer-direction, but little is known about what drives care model choice, or how the motivations for seeking care and resulting care experiences differ for users of each model. Research design and methods We conducted semi-structured interviews with care partners of community-living persons with dementia receiving personal care through New York Medicaid (n = 18), using directed content analysis to identify key themes. Results Three common goals guided the choice of consumer- vs agency-direction: maximize care quality, ensure provider continuity, and minimize care partner burden. The same goal could lead families to opposite decisions: some chose consumer-direction believing family provided higher-quality care, whereas others chose agency-direction trusting that aides were better trained. Ensuring continuity was most salient for consumer-direction users; minimizing burden most salient for agency-direction users. Regardless of care model, cultural norms and negative experiences with institutional care were primary motivators for using home-based personal care. Common challenges included service hours lagging escalating care needs, administrative obstacles to managing care, and insufficient support from the broader social network. Discussion and implications Personal care recipients and their families need flexible Medicaid policies enabling them to choose arrangements-including care setting and model-that best align with their needs and preferences, alongside resources to navigate a complex benefits system.

items.title: Cancer symptom severity progression among adults with severe psychiatric illness: a matched cohort study.
items.abstract: Background Structural-, system-, and individual-level barriers may create difficulty in symptom management for adults diagnosed with cancer living with severe psychiatric illness (SPI). We investigated differences in the overall trajectories of long-term symptom progression between patients with and without an inpatient SPI history. Methods This population-based matched cohort study used health administrative data of Ontario adults diagnosed with cancer between 2007 and 2021. Adults with SPI were matched 1:5 to those without mental illness. We applied Markov multistate models to analyze pain, nausea, and wellbeing transitions over five years between symptom severity states (none, mild, moderate, severe, death). We estimated transition rate ratios (RR) and 60-day transition probabilities to evaluate symptom trajectory differences. Results Among 6,235 patients with SPI and 31,175 matches, patients with SPI exhibited significantly accelerated symptom deterioration. For pain, SPI patients had elevated rates of 'none-to-mild' (RR = 1.69, 95% CI: 1.58-1.82) and 'mild-to-moderate' transitions (RR = 2.02, 95% CI: 1.83-2.22) compared to patients without SPI. They also demonstrated elevated rates of death from a pain-free state (RR = 3.05, 95% CI: 2.85-3.25), possibly reflecting unrecorded symptom decline and different mortality risks. Conversely, SPI patients demonstrated lower transition probabilities of pain improvement; at 60 days, patients with moderate pain were 8.4% less likely to improve to mild pain (SPI: 27.8%, 95% CI: 0.0%-28.5%; non-SPI: 36.2%, 95% CI: 35.8%-36.5%). Nausea and wellbeing exhibited similar trends. Conclusion These findings of differences in cancer symptom progression between individuals with and without an inpatient SPI history highlight the need for tailored interventions for this vulnerable population.

items.title: Implementing a Clinical Decision Support System for Pressure Injury Risk Management in Intensive Care Nursing: A Mixed-Methods Evaluation.
items.abstract: Aim To examine the impact of a Clinical Decision Support System for Pressure Injury Risk Management (CDSS-PIRM) on nurses' pressure injury risk management practices and pressure injury incidence in an intensive care unit, and to explore nurses' experiences of integrating the system into routine care. Design Explanatory sequential mixed-methods study involving pre-test and two post-test evaluation stages followed by qualitative interviews. Methods The study was conducted in an intensive care unit at a tertiary university hospital. The quantitative phase comprised 71 structured observations of nine ICU nurses' pressure injury risk management practices across three sequential stages: pre-test (baseline, n = 26), post-test 1 (CDSS-PIRM implementation without real-time alerts, n = 23) and post-test 2 (CDSS-PIRM implementation with real-time alerts, n = 22). Pressure injury incidence among 165 patients was tracked across the three implementation stages. Following the quantitative phase, the qualitative phase involved semi-structured interviews with seven nurses. Results Risk assessment practice scores were significantly higher at post-test 1 compared with the pre-test (median 3 [IQR 2-6] vs. 2 [IQR 1-2]; p = 0.016), while wound care practice scores improved significantly at post-test 2 (median 1.5 [IQR 0-2] vs. 0 [IQR 0-1]; p = 0.015). Overall pressure injury incidence remained unchanged (10.9%; pre-test: 9.68%; post-test 1: 11.63%; post-test 2: 11.67%; p = 0.920). Two main themes were identified: (i) experienced benefits (a comprehensive clinical guide with real-time prevention support and advanced documentation); and (ii) barriers to clinical integration (workload pressure, reliance on established routines, alert fatigue and infrastructure limitations). Conclusion Clinical decision support systems can strengthen specific nursing practices related to pressure injury prevention; however, contextual and organisational barriers may constrain their translation into measurable clinical outcomes. Reporting methods The Good Reporting of a Mixed Methods Study checklist was followed. Patient or public contribution No patient or public contribution. Implications for the profession and/or patient care These findings highlight the potential of clinical decision support systems to support nursing judgement, documentation and real-time prevention in the intensive care unit. Addressing contextual and organisational barriers is essential to optimise their integration into nursing workflows and improve patient safety outcomes. Impact This study demonstrates how a clinical decision support system can enhance pressure injury risk assessment and wound care practices in intensive care nursing. Findings reveal that improvements in nursing processes do not automatically translate into reduced pressure injury incidence, suggesting the influence of contextual and organisational factors. The study offers practical and conceptual insights for nurses, nurse managers and digital health researchers on implementing decision support technologies in complex care environments.

items.title: From snoring to obstructive sleep apnea: A narrative review of pathophysiology, clinical implications and multimodal management.
items.abstract: Snoring is a highly prevalent acoustic phenomenon generated by vibration of the upper airway soft tissues during sleep. Long regarded as a benign social nuisance, it is increasingly recognised as a clinically informative manifestation of upper airway dysfunction. In adults it is still defined almost exclusively by subjective report, since standardised objective acoustic criteria remain unestablished; this definitional weakness explains much of the extreme heterogeneity of prevalence estimates, which range from 2% to 83% across studies. Pathophysiologically, snoring reflects an imbalance between a collapsible pharynx and the mechanisms defending its patency. Framing it within the endotypic model developed for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), collapsibility, muscle responsiveness, arousal threshold and loop gain, clarifies why the snoring-upper airway resistance syndrome-OSA continuum holds for many patients but not for all, and why apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) thresholds capture only part of the clinical picture. We argue that so-called "isolated" snoring may be less inert than assumed: respiratory-effort-related microarousals provide a plausible mechanism for insomnia-like symptoms in a subset of symptomatic snorers, while observational and experimental data suggest potential links between snoring, autonomic activation and cardiometabolic risk. These relationships remain incompletely established, particularly in the absence of documented OSA, and should not be interpreted as evidence of causality. Diagnostic assessment should follow a pre-test probability-based, stepwise logic integrating history, upper airway examination, sleep testing and, in selected patients, drug-induced sleep endoscopy and airflow phenotyping, the latter promising but not yet validated for routine use. Management is correspondingly phenotype-driven. We conclude that the field's central task is the transition of snoring from a self-reported symptom to a measurable physiological trait, a prerequisite for precision-based care and for identifying, among snorers, those in whom further physiological and cardiometabolic evaluation may be warranted.

items.title: Assessment of the Psychometric Properties of the Turkish Version of the Pediatric Patient Classification Scale (PPCS).
items.abstract: Background Pediatric nurses need a standardized assessment tool to assess the overall condition of pediatric patients accurately and rapidly. Objective In this study, the validity and reliability studies of the Turkish version of the Pediatric Patient Classification Scale were conducted. Design and methods The study sample consisted of 200 pediatric patients aged 0-18 (mean ± SD: 2.14 ± 1.14; median: 2) receiving diagnostic and treatment services at the pediatric units of a hospital. Results The Cronbach's alpha coefficient of the 11-item Pediatric Patient Classification Scale was 0.838, indicating a high level of internal consistency. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) demonstrated that the three factors in the original scale "Family," "Patient," and "Therapeutic Procedures" were preserved in the Turkish form. The CFA fit indices were RMSEA = 0.079, χ 2 /df = 2.24, and CFI = 0.96. These results indicate that the measurement model fits the data well. Scores of the Caregiving Burden Scale, which measures burden according to patient care levels, differed significantly across the categories identified by the Pediatric Patient Classification Scale (minimal care, moderate care, high-level care, semi-intensive care, and intensive care). Conclusion The Turkish version of the Pediatric Patient Classification Scale, developed to classify the care needs of pediatric patients accurately and rapidly, is a valid and reliable assessment tool. Practice implications This tool enables pediatric nurses to assess the overall condition of pediatric patients accurately and rapidly in accordance with the patient classification system.

items.title: Meanings mothers attribute to caring for children with congenital toxoplasmosis: A virtual ethnography on Facebook®.
items.abstract: Introduction Congenital toxoplasmosis is a significant public health concern due to its severity and its profound impact on maternal and family care. Objective To explore how mothers of children with congenital toxoplasmosis use Facebook to share caregiving experiences and construct meanings related to their maternal trajectories within digital support networks. Method This is an exploratory, qualitative study based on virtual ethnography. The study followed six methodological steps: participant search, group characterization, data collection, interviews, transcription, and analysis. Seventeen Facebook® spaces, including personal accounts, pages, and groups, were analyzed, addressing topics such as birth narratives, diagnosis, sequelae, family impact, spirituality, and emotions. Subsequently, interviews were conducted with seven mothers. Results The results were organized into three thematic categories: (1) the impact of the diagnosis on family life and the search for information; (2) the resources mobilized by mothers to cope with atypical motherhood, such as social support, faith, and welcoming networks; and (3) the everyday uses of Facebook, with emphasis on visibility strategies, care with exposure, and the construction of belonging. Initially, mothers turned to virtual groups seeking support and information, later moving on to sharing their own experiences on personal profiles and other platforms. Conclusion The findings highlight the importance of understanding the emotional and informational needs of mothers of children with congenital toxoplasmosis, emphasizing the value of promoting welcoming and collaborative spaces in digital environments that foster mutual support and experience sharing.

items.title: Integrated serum metabolomics and hippocampal transcriptomics reveal metabolic reprogramming associated with BBB impairment and hippocampal injury in HFD-fed mice.
items.abstract: Aims Increasing evidence suggests that high-fat diet (HFD) consumption induces systemic metabolic disturbances and is associated with blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction and hippocampal injury. This study aimed to explore the potential mechanisms linking HFD-induced metabolic disturbances to BBB and hippocampal abnormalities. Methods Male C57BL/6J mice were fed an HFD or a normal diet (ND) for 12 weeks. Systemic metabolic and inflammatory status, hepatic lipid accumulation, neurobehavioral performance, hippocampal injury, BBB integrity, and hippocampal inflammatory alterations were systematically assessed. Integrated serum untargeted metabolomics and hippocampal transcriptomics were performed to identify key molecular pathways. Results HFD-fed mice exhibited systemic metabolic disturbances, increased BBB permeability, hippocampal neuronal injury and inflammation, and impaired motor coordination. Integrated serum metabolomic and hippocampal transcriptomic analyses identified alterations in histidine and glycerophospholipid metabolism. Hippocampal transcriptomic analysis revealed upregulation of carnosine dipeptidase 1 (Cndp1) and phospholipase A2 group IVE (Pla2g4e) and downregulation of diacylglycerol kinase kappa (Dgkk) and ethanolamine-phosphate phospho-lyase (Etnppl), which were further validated by RT-qPCR. Serum metabolomic analysis further revealed decreased serum carnosine levels. Given the reported neuroprotective properties of carnosine, we further investigated its effects in palmitic acid-treated HT22 cells. Carnosine improved cell viability, attenuated oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, and modulated the expression of Cndp1, Pla2g4e, Etnppl, and Dgkk. Conclusion HFD was associated with BBB impairment, hippocampal inflammatory activation, neuronal injury, and behavioral alterations. Integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses implicated histidine and glycerophospholipid metabolism associated with HFD-induced metabolic disturbances and hippocampal injury.

items.title: Second multistate outbreak of tuberculosis caused by a bone allograft product.
items.abstract: In 2021 and 2023, two different bone allograft products caused nationwide tuberculosis outbreaks. We assessed the morbidity and mortality of the second outbreak and reviewed donor and tissue screening to identify deficiencies. Thirty-six people residing in nine states received the product during spinal and dental procedures. Twenty-seven recipients had tuberculosis infection, 11 had microbiologic or imaging evidence of tuberculosis disease, and two died from tuberculosis within 12 months of outbreak detection. Another recipient died from tuberculosis nearly 3 years after product implantation. The bone donor died of pneumonia and septic shock. Polymerase chain reaction testing of the product before and after distribution did not detect Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Mycobacterial culture was not performed until after outbreak detection, when M. tuberculosis was isolated from 2 of 6 unused product units. This outbreak demonstrates persistent gaps in tissue transplant safety. Appropriate selection of donors and mycobacterial culture of donated tissues could reduce but not eliminate the risk of M. tuberculosis transmission. Therefore, it is important that clinicians monitor tissue recipients and promptly report adverse events to tissue establishments and health authorities.

items.title: Prevalence of von Willebrand disease among adolescents and young women with heavy menstrual bleeding in hospital-based settings: A systematic review.
items.abstract: Background Heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB) affects up to 40% of adolescent and reproductive-age females and is a leading cause of complications such as severe anemia, iron deficiency and hospitalization. In adolescents and young women, it is commonly linked to anovulatory cycles and underlying inherited bleeding disorders, with von Willebrand disease (VWD) being the most prevalent but frequently underdiagnosed. This systematic review explores the prevalence of VWD among adolescents and young women aged ≤25 years assessed for HMB within hospital-based settings and evaluates diagnostic setting gradients. Methods This review included six databases - PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, CINAHL, and ProQuest that were searched electronically using relevant keywords and MeSH terms. After the search, the articles were transferred to Rayyan software for further screening. The quality of the included studies was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Prevalence Critical Appraisal Tool. Data extraction was performed, and the findings were presented narratively. Results Among 1,709 young women with heavy menstrual bleeding across 16 studies, 199 were found to have von Willebrand disease, yielding an overall occurrence rate of 11.64%. Subgroup analysis by clinical referral setting revealed a distinct diagnostic gradient: Specialized Hematology and Hemophilia Treatment Centres (HTCs) demonstrated the highest prevalence at 16.78% (77/459), followed by Inpatient / Acute Emergency Admissions at 10.20% (25/245), General Tertiary Referral Hospital Settings at 10.20% (65/637), and Pediatric & Adolescent Gynaecology (PAG) / Multidisciplinary Outpatient HMB Clinics at 8.70% (32/368). Conclusion von Willebrand disease is a highly significant underlying cause of heavy menstrual bleeding in young women, affecting 11.64% of patients presenting to hospital-based settings, including nearly 1 in 11 patients (8.70%) evaluated in specialized Pediatric & Adolescent Gynaecology (PAG) clinics. These findings support targeted diagnostic testing rather than universal screening, specifically for patients who present to hospital-based settings and PAG clinics. Systematic review registration PROSPERO CRD42024563010.

items.title: Predicting personal PM<sub>2.5</sub> exposure among community-dwelling older adults using multi-source environmental, residential, and behavioral information.
items.abstract: Individual exposure to fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) varies according to environmental, residential, and behavioral contexts. This study aimed to predict personal PM 2.5 exposure among community-dwelling older adults and examine candidate variables using a Bayesian LASSO model incorporating information from multiple exposure-related domains. A total of 247 adults aged ≥60 years were recruited in Fuzhou, China. Each participant completed one 72-h personal PM 2.5 monitoring session during either the summer or winter campaign, with outdoor PM 2.5 measured concurrently and residential, environmental, behavioral, and time-activity information collected through a questionnaire survey. Posterior regression coefficients and their 95% credible intervals were estimated for candidate variables. The model yielded a Bayesian R 2 of 0.481 (95% credible interval [CrI]: 0.412-0.539) and an RMSE of 19.260 μg/m 3 (95% CrI: 18.797-19.876). Four variables had positive posterior regression coefficients, with 95% CrIs excluding zero: passive smoking only [16.157 μg/m 3 (95% CrI: 7.920-24.462)], current smoking [12.949 μg/m 3 (95% CrI: 7.047-18.843)], residence near a major road [7.398 μg/m 3 (95% CrI: 0.655-14.195)], and outdoor PM 2.5 concentration (per 1 SD) [6.531 μg/m 3 (95% CrI: 3.798-9.351)]. The coefficient directions of these four variables were highly consistent across repeated cross-validation. These findings may inform future studies aimed at further evaluating and refining individualized PM 2.5 exposure assessment in older populations.

items.title: Improving source identification of volatile organic compounds using Positive Matrix Factorization with adjusted photochemical-age parameterization and time-shifted organic molecular tracers in an industrial area.
items.abstract: Positive Matrix Factorization (PMF) is widely used for volatile organic compound (VOC) source apportionment, but conventional photochemical-age-based initial VOC (VOCini) estimation may be biased by fresh hyperlocal emissions in industrial areas. In addition, the temporal delay between VOC emissions and secondary organic aerosol (SOA) formation is rarely considered in PMF. This study developed a hyperlocal source-adjusted VOCini framework (M-IVOCH) and further incorporated concurrent, 12-h shifted, and 24-h shifted SOA tracers using multiple time resolution PMF (M-IVOCH,SOA). Hourly VOCs and 12-h PM2.5 SOA tracers were measured over four field campaigns at a highly industrialized site in southern Taiwan. Excluding the hyperlocal source before VOCini estimation enabled gasoline evaporation and liquefied petroleum gas emissions to be resolved as distinct factors. Incorporating SOA tracers further resolved a secondary process-related factor and a secondary biomass burning factor that were not identified using routine VOC measurements alone, and the time-shifted tracers revealed day-night differences in secondary biomass burning factor. The industrial factor was also associated with 2-methylerythritol and phthalic acid, suggesting a possible connection between industrial emissions and SOA formation. Accounting for hyperlocal emissions and time-shifted SOA improved source identification and provided additional information for air pollution management in complex industrial environments.

items.title: The atherosclerotic cardiovascular-kidney-liver-metabolic burden in the Asia-Pacific, 1990-2050: A global burden of disease 2023 analysis.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death worldwide, with the Asia-Pacific region bearing over half of this burden. The cardiovascular-kidney-liver-metabolic (CKLM) framework unifies the interrelated conditions of cardiovascular disease (CVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and obesity, which synergistically contribute to heightened cardiovascular risk. However, the combined CKLM burden in the region has not been characterised. Using the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023, we examined mortality and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) of CKLM diseases across 39 Asia-Pacific countries from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts to 2050. The CKLM burden was organized into metabolic antecedents (comprising CKD, MASLD, T2DM and obesity) and downstream atherosclerotic CVD (comprising ischemic heart disease, stroke, aortic aneurysm, and peripheral artery disease). In 2023, the Asia-Pacific recorded 286.9 million CKLM-related DALYs (53.2% of global burden), with an age-standardised DALY rate of 6390.9 per 100,000 population. From 1990 to 2023, crude DALYs rose by 78.7%, outpacing the global trends (61.1%), while age-standardised DALYs fell by 25.0% - driven by improvements in atherosclerotic CVD (-35.2%) but counterbalanced by a 20.4% rise in metabolic antecedents. By 2050, age-standardised DALY rates are projected to show a 7.0% point-estimate increase regionally against an estimated 14.9% global decline, with metabolic antecedents likely to expand from 29.9% to 36.2% of the total burden between 2026 and 2050. Intraregional disparities exist across sociodemographic strata, subregions, and age-sex categories. Risk-deleted analyses identify high systolic blood pressure, high fasting plasma glucose, and dietary risks as the highest-yield modifiable targets. The worsening Asia-Pacific CKLM trajectory is decoupling from improving global trends, driven by a compositional shift from atherosclerotic CVD toward upstream metabolic antecedents. Integrated interventions addressing multiple key modifiable risks are needed.

items.title: The fundamental problem of risk prediction for individuals: health AI, uncertainty, and personalized medicine.
items.abstract: Clinical prediction models are commonly evaluated regarding performance for a population, although decisions are made for individuals. The classic view relates uncertainty in risk estimates for individuals to sample size (estimation uncertainty) while other sources are model uncertainty (variability in modeling choices) and applicability uncertainty (variability in measurement procedures and between populations). We aim to illustrate the uncertainty of prediction models in estimating individual risks with an ovarian cancer example. We used real and synthetic data for ovarian cancer diagnosis to train 59400 models with variations in estimation, model, and applicability uncertainty. We then used these models to estimate the probability of ovarian cancer in a fixed test set of 100 patients and evaluate the variability in individual estimates. We show empirically that estimation uncertainty can be strongly dominated by model uncertainty and applicability uncertainty, even for models that perform well at the population level. Estimation uncertainty decreased considerably with increasing training sample size, whereas model and applicability uncertainty remained large. Individual risk estimates are far more uncertain than often assumed. Model uncertainty and applicability uncertainty usually remain invisible when prediction models or algorithms are based on a single study. Predictive algorithms should inform, not dictate, care and support personalization through clinician-patient interaction.

items.title: Working memory and BMIz in preschool children: an indirect association involving insufficient healthy food intake.
items.abstract: Executive function and health behaviors may be relevant to obesity in preschool children, a critical period for obesity prevention, but their associations remain unclear. Our cross-sectional study investigated these associations in 1,557 preschool children from Wuhan, China. The primary adiposity outcome was body mass index z-score (BMIz). Executive function was assessed using seven tasks, from which standardized task scores were averaged to derive working memory and inhibitory control composite scores. Dietary intake was assessed using a Food Frequency Questionnaire. The insufficient healthy food intake and excessive unhealthy food intake scores were summed to derive an overall dietary risk score. Linear mixed-effects models with a random intercept for kindergarten showed that working memory composite score was inversely associated with BMIz. This association was not observed in inhibitory control composite score. Both insufficient healthy food intake score and overall dietary risk score were positively associated with BMIz. The indirect association analysis indicated that insufficient healthy food intake accounted for 4.94% of the total association between working memory composite score and BMIz. These findings indicate an inverse association between working memory and BMIz in preschool children and suggest a potential indirect association through insufficient healthy food intake. Given the cross-sectional design, prospective studies are needed to clarify the temporal ordering and directionality of these associations.

items.title: Plasma exchange for acute and acute-on-chronic liver failure: A systematic review and patient-level survival data meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Acute liver failure (ALF) and acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) are associated with high short-term mortality. Plasma exchange (PE) has been proposed as a therapeutic strategy, but its effect on survival remains uncertain. We conducted a systematic review and reconstructed patient-level survival data meta-analysis to assess the association between PE and transplant-free survival (TFS) and post-transplant survival in ALF and ACLF. PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus were searched through June 2026. Eligible studies compared PE with standard medical therapy (SMT) and reported Kaplan-Meier data suitable for reconstruction. Patient-level time-to-event data were reconstructed from curves using validated methods and analyzed with one-stage Cox proportional hazards models incorporating shared frailty to account for between-study heterogeneity. The endpoint was TFS. Sensitivity, subgroup, and restricted mean survival time (RMST) analyses were performed to evaluate robustness and clinical relevance. Eighteen studies including 1440 patients were analyzed: nine studies in ALF (n=617) and nine in ACLF (n=823). In ALF, PE was associated with improved TFS compared with SMT (HR 0.46, 95% CI 0.36-0.58). In ACLF, PE was also associated with improved TFS (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.51-0.73). Results were supported by sensitivity analyses and RMST estimates. PE was not associated with improved post-transplant survival. PE was associated with significantly improved TFS in ALF and ACLF compared with SMT. These findings support PE as a valuable supportive strategy to improve TFS in selected patients with severe liver failure, while its role specifically as a bridge to liver transplantation requires further prospective evaluation.
