items.title: People optimistically search for favorite images.
items.abstract: In many real-world decisions, options appear sequentially, and choosing an option ends the search. These situations are often described as "fiancé problems," since one cannot return to a rejected potential marriage partner if a better option is not found. Mathematically optimal decision makers in such scenarios should use prior knowledge about the distribution of option values, such as their expected value and variability, to decide whether continued search is likely to reveal a better option than the one currently available. Previous work shows that people often sample too few options, relative to optimal benchmarks, when searching through numerical economic values such as prices. Recent computational modeling attributes this undersampling to mis-specified, or biased, prior beliefs, whereby participants expect future options to be lower valued than they should. Here, we tested whether biased prior beliefs might also explain the opposite bias: the tendency to sample too many options in image-based searches, such as choosing the most attractive face. In 10 data sets spanning five image-based choice contexts, we replicated oversampling bias in every data set. We applied computational modeling and, across these image-based tasks, most, but not all, participants were best fit by the biased prior model, which expected future option values to be higher than warranted by optimality. Thus, optimistically and pessimistically biased priors may contribute respectively to over- and undersampling biases. These suboptimal search strategies could manifest in real-world decisions such as shopping, choosing dating partners, or evaluating trustworthy job candidates. items.title: How do readers interpret ambiguous constituents in novel Chinese compound words?
items.abstract: Most Chinese words are compounds comprising multiple constituent characters. Research has shown that compounds are routinely broken down into their constituents during word recognition, but it is unknown how readers deal with characters that have multiple possible meanings (e.g., can mean both flower and to spend, depending on the compound in which it appears) and that are highly prevalent in Chinese. The present study investigated how a computational model (Study 1) and human readers (Study 2) compute the meanings of novel Chinese compounds that contain semantically ambiguous characters. We found that both the computational model and human readers prioritize characters that have a consistent meaningful function when making sense of novel compounds, and a further study revealed that semantically consistent characters serve as anchors to help readers determine the contextually appropriate meaning for ambiguous characters. These findings suggest that the stored knowledge of the consistency of form-meaning mappings shapes the comprehension of novel words. We conclude by arguing that, despite its apparent ambiguity, the Chinese writing system may be more systematic and learnable than it appears. items.title: Strategic control or evolutionary bias? Disentangling responsible remembering from adaptive memory.
items.abstract: Memory control processes are selective, favoring information important to the individual. In this article, we explore the mechanisms underlying this selectivity. Adaptive memory views posit that selectivity is driven by automatic, evolutionarily tuned biases (i.e., survival relevant), whereas the responsible remembering framework emphasizes strategic, goal-directed control over encoding. In three experiments, we investigated how these two frameworks interact to guide memory prioritization. In Experiment 1, participants rated words for either survival importance or likeability under incidental or intentional encoding conditions. Importance ratings predicted recall across encoding conditions, suggesting that the prioritization of survival-relevant information occurs automatically during encoding, independent of goal-directed strategies. In Experiment 2, participants studied words paired with either accurate or arbitrarily assigned survival-based importance ratings. Although both types of values predicted recall, accurate survival relevance was the stronger predictor. This suggests that although strategic memory is flexible, it is ultimately optimized for processing inherently meaningful information. In Experiment 3, we introduced a control condition evaluating the importance of words for making money. We replicated the classic survival processing advantage in overall recall; however, both survival and monetary importance ratings similarly predicted item-level memory. This indicates that value-based prioritization can guide encoding outside of survival-specific contexts. Together, these experiments suggest that rather than being competing accounts, responsible remembering may reflect a context-sensitive extension of adaptive memory-one that allows strategic prioritization of information based on shifting modern goals, even when fitness is not directly at stake. items.title: Information-seeking behavior in mice (Mus musculus) during visual discriminations: Evaluating metacognitive and alternative accounts in a target-cueing paradigm.
items.abstract: Information-seeking behavior is often interpreted as evidence of metacognitive monitoring, but nonmetacognitive factors may also explain such behavior. We examined this issue in mice using a target-cueing procedure in which an information-seeking response produced a hint indicating the location of the rewarded stimulus. In Experiment 1, mice performed an orientation discrimination. In Experiment 2, the same mice performed a grating discrimination in which grating coarseness varied across trials. During training, some aspects of performance were compatible with a metacognitive account. In Experiment 1, information seeking did not increase reliably as the discrimination became more difficult, although hint use improved accuracy most clearly at smaller orientation differences. In Experiment 2, mice sought information more often at lower grating coarseness, and hint use was associated with the greatest accuracy benefit under those more difficult conditions. However, the critical test results did not support the prediction that information seeking would track the need for additional information. Mice frequently sought information in target-only trials, in which no additional information was required, and showed relatively low rates of information seeking in trials in which the initial display consisted of two identical, and therefore nondiagnostic, stimuli. These findings indicate that information seeking in the present task was multiply determined. The observed pattern was consistent with contributions from response competition, reinforcement history, and the behavioral utility of the hint. Although some aspects of training remained compatible with confidence-based control, the critical test conditions showed that information seeking was not governed by confidence monitoring alone. items.title: Predicting substance use behaviors: A multi-data set mega-analysis.
items.abstract: Predicting substance use behaviors is a critical public health challenge. Although self-report survey data have been central to understanding substance use, their longitudinal predictive utility has yet to be quantified. We conducted a "mega"-analysis of 44,862 participants, integrating 197 harmonized self-report predictors across demographic, behavioral, familial, and psychosocial domains. Specifically, we employed both linear regression and machine learning approaches to evaluate the extent to which alcohol, tobacco, and cannabis use could be predicted. Models that handled high-dimensional, correlated predictor sets substantially outperformed unregularized linear regression, reflecting the known limitations of fitting unregularized regression to large, collinear predictor sets rather than a general advantage of machine learning. Random forest and regularized regression (Elastic Net) yielded comparable predictive performance (R² ≈ 14% at baseline and ≈4% for longitudinal change). In exploratory leave-one-data-set-out analyses, models did not generalize to independent held-out data sets (R² ≈ 0), indicating that predictive associations were largely context-specific. Externalizing behaviors predicted a significant proportion of substance use variability, particularly at baseline, whereas the predictive power of demographic and familial factors became apparent in models predicting change over time. Combining large-scale harmonization with computational modeling clarifies both the potential and limits of forecasting substance use trajectories. items.title: The hangover of oppression: An ecological momentary assessment study of oppression-based stressors and daily alcohol use and hazardous drinking outcomes among sexual and gender minoritized young adults.
items.abstract: Sexual and gender minoritized (SGM) young adults are at greater risk for hazardous drinking and alcohol use disorder (AUD) than their heterosexual and cisgender counterparts. These inequities are often explained with oppression frameworks, which posit that oppression-based stressors (i.e., discrimination) contribute to hazardous drinking and the development of AUD. However, research examining the daily and within-person associations between oppression-based stressors and alcohol use among SGM young adults is nascent and equivocal. We conducted a 30-day ecological momentary assessment of daily within- and between-person oppression-based stressors and same-day alcohol use outcomes (i.e., alcohol use, quantity of drinks, heavy drinking, alcohol-related consequences, hangover symptoms) among 98 SGM young adults who engaged in heavy drinking (71.4% met criteria for AUD). We also examined multiple person-level moderators (e.g., sociodemographics, addiction severity, stress exposure and sensitivity) to identify for whom oppression-based stressors confer risk for hazardous drinking. Results indicated that on days participants experienced more oppression-based stressors than their average, they reported greater odds of daily heavy drinking. Participants who experienced greater oppression-based stressors overall reported more daily negative and positive alcohol-related consequences and hangovers. The within-person associations between oppression-based stressors and some of the hazardous drinking outcomes were moderated by AUD symptoms, a family history of alcohol problems, greater lifetime exposure to cisheterosexism, and identification as plurisexual (e.g., bisexual). Our findings provide support for oppression and addiction frameworks and further highlight risks that plurisexual young adults experience. The results underscore the need to target oppression to reduce hazardous drinking among SGM young adults. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

items.title: "Getting her to see herself the way I see her": Exploring Black caregivers' hopes and dreams for their daughters.
items.abstract: Drawing upon the radical hope framework (Mosley et al., 2020), the present study explores Black caregivers' hopes and dreams for their adolescent daughters as well as the underlying motivations that inform the gendered racial socialization process. Eleven Black caregivers (39-59 years old, Mage = 50) of adolescent Black girls (11-17 years old, Mage = 13.9) residing in the Southeastern region of the United States were recruited to participate in individual semistructured interviews. Utilizing theoretical thematic analysis, three themes were identified in this exploratory investigation: (1) firm foundation: morality and faith; (2) personal protective equipment reimagined: persistence, pride, and empowerment; and (3) rooted in joy, encouraged to explore. Overall, findings revealed that Black caregivers' hopes and dreams for their daughters revolved around seeing a nurtured confidence and instilled pride in their daughters that inspired their daughters to persist and thrive. Black caregivers were motivated to provide a multifaceted protection from discriminatory stressors in which they affirmed their daughters' agency and sought to provide opportunities for their daughters to experience joy and fulfillment-introducing new metrics of success. Findings underscore the need for scholarship to incorporate more process-oriented approaches in the study of Black families in which Black caregivers are seen as experts and a developmental resource in promoting the positive development of Black girls. items.title: Occurrence of Toxocara spp. in companion animals and serological evidence of human exposure at the human-companion animal interface in Giza, Egypt.
items.abstract: Toxocariasis, caused by Toxocara spp., is one of the most neglected zoonotic parasitic diseases worldwide. In Egypt, integrated One Health studies investigating human, animal, and occupational risk factors remain limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of zoonotic Toxocara spp. in companion animals and to identify associated risk factors within a One Health framework. A cross-sectional study was conducted in Giza, Egypt, including dogs (n = 70) and cats (n = 35) from animal shelters and veterinary clinics, eosinophilic children (n = 227), and shelter workers (n = 22). Animal fecal samples were examined microscopically for intestinal parasites, while human serum samples were tested for anti-Toxocara IgG antibodies using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Demographic characteristics and potential risk factors were collected through standardized questionnaires. Associations were evaluated using Pearson's Chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, followed by binary logistic regression to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Toxocara canis-like eggs were detected in a percentage of 17.1% in canine cases, with no significant difference in positivity rates regarding sex. In contrast, T. canis positivity rate was significantly correlated with younger age, lack of anthelmintic medication, and concurrent detection of Cystoisospora species. Among the studied eosinophilic children, anti-Toxocara IgG antibodies were detected in 41/227 (18.1%). In the univariable analysis, rural residence was significantly associated with anti-T. canis IgG seropositivity (COR = 2.08, 95% CI: 1.00-4.32; P = 0.047). Similarly, contact with soil (COR = 2.51, 95% CI: 1.17-5.42; P = 0.02), consumption of unpurified water (COR = 2.80, 95% CI: 1.15-6.82; P = 0.02), and interaction with pets (COR = 3.19, 95% CI: 1.48-6.87; P = 0.002) were significantly associated with anti IgG seropositivity. In the multivariable binary logistic regression model, contact with soil remained significantly associated with anti-T. canis IgG seropositivity (AOR = 3.10, 95% CI: 1.17-8.66; P = 0.02). Consumption of unpurified water (AOR = 2.64, 95% CI: 1.03-6.78; P = 0.04) and interaction with pets (AOR = 3.60, 95% CI: 1.60-8.10; P = 0.002) were also independently associated with seropositivity. In contrast, the association with rural residence was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for the other variables included in the model (AOR = 0.55, 95% CI: 0.25-1.17; P = 0.12). This study demonstrates substantial exposure to T. canis-like eggs among companion animals and children in Giza, Egypt, highlighting the need for integrated One Health interventions. Regular deworming of pets, public health education, and coordinated veterinary-medical surveillance are recommended to reduce toxocariasis at the human-companion animal interface.

items.title: Association between polypharmacy, fall-risk increasing drugs, and fall characteristics in older adults discharged from the emergency department: cross-sectional data from the SeFallED study.
items.abstract: Polypharmacy and fall-risk-increasing drugs (FRIDs) are known risk factors for falls in older adults. However, the prevalence of polypharmacy and FRIDs in high-risk older adults presenting to the emergency department (ED) after a fall, without hospitalization, is unclear. This study aimed to examine the prevalence of polypharmacy and FRIDs and their associations with specific fall characteristics in this population. The SeFallED study included individuals aged ≥ 60 years who visited an ED in Oldenburg, Germany, after a fall without subsequent hospitalization. Data on fall characteristics and medication use were collected within four weeks of the ED visit. Cross-sectional associations between medication use and fall characteristics were analysed using binary and multinomial logistic regression models. Fall characteristics were characterized by recovery status (recovered vs. unrecovered), location of the fall (indoor vs. outdoor), and direction of the fall (sideways, backward, forward, or collapse). Among 335 participants (75.4 ± 9.1 years), the average number of regular medications was 3.6 ± 3.1; with polypharmacy present in 31.3%. FRIDs were identified in 44.5% of participants using STOPPFall medications and 8.4% using medications from the PRISCUS list. No significant associations were found between polypharmacy or FRID use and fall characteristics. The high prevalence of polypharmacy and FRID use underscores the importance of systematic medication reviews, as recommended in the global guidelines for falls prevention. Implementing medication reviews at the point of care - such as during ED visits - may represent a valuable opportunity to reduce future fall risk in this vulnerable population.

items.title: Residential Evictions Across the Life-Course and Risk of Posttraumatic Stress Disorder Symptoms Among Reproductive Age Black Women: Social Epidemiology to Combat Unjust Residential Evictions (SECURE) Study.
items.abstract: The objectives of the study are to examine associations between five eviction measures, by type, recency, and life stage on risk of high posttraumatic stress disorder symptoms (PTSD), and to use qualitative data to contextualize findings. We used a cross-sectional survey from the Social Epidemiology to Combat Unjust Residential Evictions (SECURE) study (Metropolitan Detroit, MI; 2021-2024; n = 1428), to estimate relative risk of high PTSD symptoms in the past month associated with each eviction measure. In our mixed-method analysis, we also performed textual thematic analysis of open-ended survey responses about what belongings participants lost in a recent court-ordered eviction and how long it took to replace them, to illuminate potential mechanisms. High PTSD symptoms were not rare in the cohort (20%). Women who reported any of the 5 eviction measures, compared to those who did not, had between 32 and 50% higher risk of high PTSD symptoms, in adjusted models, with the strongest association for recent court-ordered eviction (relative risk 1.50; 95% confidence interval 1.17-1.91). The thematic analysis revealed multiple potential mechanisms related to loss of belongings, which could be the target of future interventions. Residential evictions, by type, recency, and life stage all, are understudied predictors of PTSD symptoms among Black reproductive age women. Loss of belongings and inability to replace them may operate as enduring trauma reminders and sources of negative trauma-related thoughts and affect. Policy solutions and mental health interventions are warranted.

items.title: Real-World Risk of Venous Thromboembolism with Bevacizumab Biosimilar versus Reference Biologic in Japanese Patients with Cancer: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Large-scale safety data for newly introduced bevacizumab biosimilars in routine oncology practice remain limited. As part of post-marketing safety evaluations under the Risk Management Plan in Japan, we evaluated the risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE) associated with a bevacizumab biosimilar (CTNK) and compared the findings with those for a reference biologic (Avastin®) in Japanese patients with cancer. In this retrospective cohort study using a large-scale hospital-based claims database (Medical Data Vision) in Japan, we identified new users of bevacizumab diagnosed with colorectal, breast, or ovarian cancer or glioblastoma between November 2020 and February 2025. Patients were classified into the biosimilar group or the reference biologic group. The primary outcome was the incidence of VTE, evaluated using a multivariable Cox proportional hazards model. Exploratory safety outcomes, including bleeding/hemorrhage and infections, were also assessed. A total of 8599 eligible patients (1967 in the biosimilar group and 6632 in the reference biologic group; male versus female patients, 45.60% and 41.74% versus 54.40% and 58.26%, respectively; median age, 69.0 years in both groups) were included in the primary analysis. The overall incidence of VTE was 2.36%. The adjusted hazard ratio for VTE in the biosimilar group compared with that in the reference biologic group was 0.82 (95% confidence interval, 0.57-1.19; P = 0.30), indicating no significant difference. This finding was consistent across subgroups stratified by target cancer type or by VTE history. Furthermore, the incidence of exploratory safety events was comparable between the two treatment groups. This retrospective cohort study showed no evidence of increased VTE risk with the bevacizumab biosimilar or major safety differences between the bevacizumab biosimilar and the reference biologic in Japanese patients with cancer, providing reassuring real-world evidence supporting the safe use of the bevacizumab biosimilar in routine clinical practice. items.title: PINet: A Pediatric Intussusception Network with Dual-Scale Guided Attention for Auxiliary Diagnosis Task Using Ultrasonography Images.
items.abstract: Ultrasonography (USG) is the primary image modality for diagnosing pediatric intussusception, yet automated identification remains challenging due to severe bowel gas artifacts, acoustic reverberation, and edematous boundary blurring. Moreover, diagnostic uncertainty is exacerbated by the scarcity of large-scale clinical cohorts and ubiquitous acoustic speckle that frequently obscures critical pathognomonic landmarks. To address this gap, we propose Pediatric Intussusception Network (PINet) via a dual-scale guided attention to feature fusion trained on a large real-world pediatric intussusception dataset (RPID), which is used to predict anomalous classifications and improve lesion area learning. PINet integrates three complementary modules: (1) a position-attention module (PAM) to model concentric topological priors and suppress isolated gas artifacts; (2) a dual attention feature fusion (DAF) module combining strip pooling attention with dynamic alignment for multi-scale context aggregation; and (3) an informative context enhancement (ICE) module for low-contrast boundary refinement. It was trained on a largest reported dataset using 9871 USG images from 4026 patients. The result of PINet achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance with 87.44% balanced accuracy and 98.09% area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). The clinical utility of the proposed PINet is demonstrated through robust performance across lesion sizes, accurate localization despite anatomical noise, and effective boundary delineation in low-contrast regions.

items.title: Association Between Nutritional Supplements Use During Pregnancy and Postpartum Depressive Symptoms Among Jordanian Women: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: Postpartum depression is a common mental health condition affecting women during the postpartum period and represents a significant public health concern. Maternal nutritional status during pregnancy, including the use of dietary supplements has been proposed as a potentially modifiable factor associated with postpartum mental health outcomes. However, the evidence from Middle Eastern populations and Jordan mainly remains limited. To examine the association between nutritional supplement use during pregnancy and postpartum depressive symptoms among Jordanian women. A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among Jordanian postpartum women. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire covering sociodemographic, obstetric, psychosocial, and nutritional characteristics, alongside the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) to assess depressive symptoms. Appropriate statistical analyses were used to evaluate associations between supplements use, reported nutritional deficiencies, and postpartum depressive symptoms. A significant proportion of participants exhibited postpartum depressive symptoms (44.3%). No statistically significant associations were found between postpartum depressive symptoms and the most commonly used prenatal supplements. In contrast, vitamin D and zinc deficiencies were significantly more prevalent among women experiencing postpartum depressive symptoms. Furthermore, zinc and magnesium supplementation during pregnancy was associated with lower scores on the Postpartum Depression Scale (EPDS). Poor family support and obesity were also significantly associated with higher depressive symptom scores. Postpartum depression was common among this group and was associated with specific nutritional deficiencies, the use of certain supplements, and psychosocial factors. These findings emphasize the need for an integrated approach to maternal mental health that considers both nutritional status and social support and highlight the importance of further research in similar settings.

items.title: Assessing Barriers and Facilitators to Implementation of Risk Minimization Programs in the USA and Europe: An Application of the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research.
items.abstract: New regulatory guidance from the European Medicines Agency (EMA) and the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) emphasizes understanding implementation context to integrate risk minimization programs into healthcare delivery. To demonstrate how to conduct a contextual analysis pre-program implementation (for a formative evaluation) and post-implementation (for a summative evaluation). Two programs were selected: (1) the existing risk minimization program for valproate in Europe and (2) the proposed Risk Mitigation and Evaluation Strategy (REMS) in the USA for tanezumab. Data sources included: (1) a collated set of written statements from stakeholders at the EMA's 2017 Public Hearing for valproate and (2) the 2021 FDA Advisory Committee meeting transcript for tanezumab. Both documents were analyzed qualitatively using codes from the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR). From the valproate document, 26 determinants were identified as having affected the implementation and delivery of the risk minimization program, the majority of which were clustered in the inner setting, individuals, and implementation process domains. From the tanezumab document, ten determinants were identified as having the potential to affect REMS implementation, the majority of which clustered in the innovation and individuals domains. In both cases, more barriers than facilitators were identified. Multiple factors operating at multiple socioecological levels were affecting or had the potential to affect risk minimization program implementation and delivery in the healthcare system. Implementation frameworks such as the CFIR provide a comprehensive and systematic way to identify relevant factors. Findings can be used to guide selection of appropriate strategies to reduce barriers and leverage facilitators.

items.title: Extrachromosomal circular DNA in human cancer: from biogenesis mechanisms to therapeutic vulnerabilities.
items.abstract: Extrachromosomal circular DNA (eccDNA) is an essential type of circular DNA that is mainly characterized by independence from chromosomes and a broad size distribution. Increasing evidence suggests that the distinctive genomic distribution of eccDNA establishes it as a clinical biomarker. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying its biogenesis and function in tumorigenesis have not been fully elucidated. Thus, in this review, we summarize the emerging insights into the biogenesis mechanisms of eccDNA, with particular emphasis on the recently described single-strand break driven internal loop (i-loop) model. We also discuss its critical roles in oncogenesis, including oncogene amplification, tumor heterogeneity, cell death, tumor immunity and drug resistance. We further outline current detection methods for eccDNA and evaluate its potential as a promising diagnostic, prognostic and predictive biomarker for human cancers, as well as a therapeutic vulnerability with implications for chemotherapy, radiotherapy, immunotherapy and nanotherapy.

items.title: Gender disparities in cataract-related blindness and visual impairment: analysis of data from 204 countries.
items.abstract: Identifying macro-level factors associated with gender disparities in cataract-blindness is crucial for identifying opportunities to reduce vision loss and promote equitable eye care access. We used country-level data from 204 countries from the Global Burden of Disease-2019, with gender disparity defined as excess females with age-standardised cataract-vision loss (blindness + moderate- and severe visual impairment) compared to males and six country-level socio-developmental indicators. We measured associations using multivariable linear regression models with robust standard errors. Across countries, combined cataract vision loss was 205.73 ± 196.08 per 100,000 population (range: 200.54-836.23) higher in females (Females: 1179.5 ± 792.4 vs Males: 973.8 ± 634.7) After adjusting for confounders, Middle East North Africa region (MENA) had highest gender disparity [Adj.β: 289.4, 95% CI: 190.4-388.2; p < 0.001)]. Female literacy (Adj.β: -20.6, 95% CI: -37.9, -3.3, p < 0.05), total-cataract-blindness (Adj.β: 0.54, 95% CI: 0.41, 0.66, p < 0.001), and per capita health expenditure [low-expenditure: Adj. β: -80.3, 95% CI: -159.4, -1.2; p < 0.05; medium-expenditure: Adj. β: -98.8, 95% CI: -185.8, -11.7; p < 0.05] were associated with gender disparity in cataract-combined vision loss, moderate and severe vision impairment but not with cataract blindness alone. The total burden of cataract blindness (Adj.β: 1.05 [95% CI: 0.77-1.33] was the only factor strongly related to cataract blindness alone. Gender disparities exist in cataract-related vision loss, with variations across regions. Lower literacy rates, lower health expenditures, and a higher burden of cataract-blindness were associated with such disparities. Although cataract blindness declined globally by 32.2% between 1990 and 2019, gender disparities in cataract-related vision loss have persisted, and in some regions, worsened. The highest disparities were observed in South Asia and the Middle East-North Africa region, underscoring regional inequities in access to eye care for women. Macro-level predictors of disparity: Lower female literacy, lower health expenditure per capita, and poorer national development metrics (low HDI, high GII) were strongly associated with higher gender disparities in cataract-related vision loss. Total burden as a key driver: Countries with a higher total burden of cataract blindness also had greater gender disparity, indicating that overwhelmed health systems may disproportionately disadvantage women. Female literacy as a protective factor: Higher female literacy was linked to significantly lower gender disparity in cataract-related vision impairment, reinforcing the critical role of education in improving health equity. Nonlinear effect of health spending: While increased health expenditure initially reduced gender disparities, the benefit plateaued beyond a certain threshold, suggesting that financial inputs alone are insufficient without addressing structural and sociocultural barriers.

items.title: Parental leave benefits and fathers' postpartum mental health in Sweden.
items.abstract: Mental health conditions in the postpartum period are common. Generous parental leave has been shown to protect against poorer postpartum mental health among mothers; however, evidence for fathers remains limited. We examine whether levels of paid parental leave benefits are associated with fathers' mental health in the first year after childbirth in Sweden. Using national population registers, we include 210,285 first-time fathers whose children were born between 2007 and 2011. Fathers receiving basic benefits have higher odds of receiving any mental healthcare, being prescribed antidepressants or anxiolytics, and using specialist outpatient care than those receiving higher-level earnings-related benefits. The results are robust after adjusting for mental health history, income and employment status, though associations are attenuated. Fathers who do not take parental leave during the first year are more likely to receive any mental healthcare, specialist outpatient care or hospitalisation. Overall, fathers with access to more generous paid parental leave benefits experience better postpartum mental health. These findings suggest that well-compensated parental leave may benefit fathers' mental health and promote gender equality in caregiving. However, further efforts are needed to determine whether parental leave systems mitigate or reproduce health inequalities given that parental leave benefit levels are contingent on labour market conditions.

items.title: Diabetic foot disease.
items.abstract: Diabetic foot disease (DFD) encompasses the lower-extremity complications of diabetes mellitus, including peripheral neuropathy, peripheral artery disease, ulceration, infection and amputation. An estimated 199 million people worldwide had DFD in 2017, including 18.6 million with foot ulcers, which precede most lower-extremity amputations. The 5-year mortality approaches 30% after ulceration and >70% after major amputation, rivalling that of many advanced cancers. DFD disproportionately affects socioeconomically disadvantaged, rural and underserved populations, creating wide disparities in outcomes. Although DFD has traditionally been viewed as a neuropathic complication of diabetes mellitus, most clinically overt disease is neuroischaemic. Neuropathy permits injury to go unnoticed, whereas peripheral artery disease, which is present in ~50% of patients with foot ulcers, impairs healing and substantially increases the risk of amputation. The Wound, Ischemia and foot Infection (WIfI) classification has therefore emerged as a unifying framework for risk stratification, whereas multidisciplinary 'toe and flow' teams and advances in revascularization, wound care and pressure offloading have transformed management. Even after ulcer healing, recurrence reaches 40% at 1 year and ~60% within 3 years, reframing ulcer healing as remission rather than cure and emphasizing the need for lifelong surveillance and secondary prevention.

items.title: A defence-in-depth strategy for securing AI-driven biological sequence design.
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence can design biological sequences, from proteins to whole genomes, opening opportunities for medicine and biotechnology, but the same capability can be misused. The Wübben Sandpit conference brought together experts in biology, AI, biosecurity, ethics, medicine and policy to ask how the field can capture the benefits while managing the risks. Here we set out a defence-in-depth strategy that builds safeguards into every stage, from the data used to train models, to the models themselves, to the synthesis of physical DNA. We argue that responsible governance is not a brake on progress but a precondition for it.

items.title: Plasmonic nano-candle platform for phase-resolved optical tracking of Pd hydrogenation with structure-sensitive readout.
items.abstract: Hydrogen detection requires platforms that are not only highly sensitive but also capable of tracking inherent gas-matter dynamics. This study reports a Λ-shaped Pd/Au nano-candle array that leverages reverse-tapered nano-slits to amplify light-matter interactions and provide dual-mode spectral readouts through extremely strong light localization and enhancement. Resonance shifts were interpreted as being dominated by dielectric variations during Pd→PdH transformation, whereas transmittance changes were used as a structure-sensitive readout to infer model-assisted effective gap evolution under ambient conditions. Comparison between the optical measurements and finite-difference time-domain simulations enabled a model-assisted interpretation of phase-dependent optical responses and effective gap evolution during Pd hydrogenation. The optimized sensing platforms with Pd/Au achieved rapid response (<5 s) and a low detection limit of 0.05% H2 with high reversibility, outperforming the corresponding Pd-only design. Beyond hydrogen monitoring, this dual-mode nanophotonic strategy offers a broadly applicable framework for analyzing coupled optical and structural responses in functional materials, enabling new opportunities in catalytic sensing, reconfigurable meta-surfaces, and adaptive photonic devices.

items.title: Real-World Effectiveness of SGLT2i on Incident Kidney Outcomes in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Normoalbuminuria-A Territory-Wide Retrospective Study.
items.abstract: Normoalbuminuric chronic kidney disease (NACKD) is increasingly prevalent in Type 2 diabetes (T2D). Here, we evaluated the kidney effects of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) among T2D patients with baseline normoalbuminuria, taking into consideration their interim development of albuminuria, a risk factor for kidney function decline. Using a real-world territory-wide electronic health record database, T2D patients with normoalbuminuria between January 2015 and December 2019 were identified. Incident kidney outcome was defined as a composite of sustained ≥ 40% decline in eGFR or end-stage kidney disease. Time-dependent Cox regression was used to evaluate the kidney effects of SGLT2i, modelling SGLT2i use and interim albuminuria status as time-varying covariates. Conditional logistic regression with time-dependent propensity score matching (TDPSM) was conducted to further evaluate the effects of SGLT2i in NACKD patients. Among the 226 434 T2D patients with baseline normoalbuminuria, over a median follow-up of 7.17 years (IQR: 5.50-8.17), use of SGLT2i (HR, 0.62, 95% CI, 0.57-0.66; p < 0.001) and interim development of albuminuria (HR, 1.90, 95% CI, 1.84-1.96; p < 0.001) were independently associated with incident kidney outcome, which remained statistically significant in subgroup and sensitivity analyses. In TDPSM, use of SGLT2i was associated with a lower risk of incident kidney outcome among NACKD patients (OR, 0.61, 95% CI, 0.49-0.77; p < 0.001). In T2D patients with normoalbuminuria, regardless of the presence of CKD, SGLT2i use was associated with a significantly lower risk of incident kidney outcome.

items.title: Structural Determinants of Preventive Dental Care Utilization Among U.S. Adults: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: To map and synthesize published literature examining structural determinants of preventive dental care utilization among U.S. adults. A scoping review was conducted in accordance with Arksey and O'Malley's methodological framework and reported following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Systematic searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and CINAHL identified peer-reviewed studies examining structural determinants of utilization of preventive dental care among U.S. adults. Eligible studies addressed system-, policy-, workforce-, insurance-, financial-, geographic-, or healthcare delivery-level determinants of preventive dental care utilization. Data were extracted using a standardized charting form and synthesized descriptively by structural determinant domain. A total of 16 studies met the inclusion criteria. Structural determinants clustered across five domains: insurance coverage and Medicaid benefit policy, workforce and provider participation, geographic and transportation access, healthcare delivery infrastructure and capacity, and financial and affordability barriers. Comprehensive dental coverage and more generous Medicaid dental benefits were associated with greater utilization of preventive dental care, whereas limited benefits, provider shortages, transportation barriers, and affordability constraints were associated with lower utilization. Considerable heterogeneity was observed in how structural determinants were conceptualized and measured across studies. Preventive dental care utilization among U.S. adults is associated with multiple interacting structural determinants embedded within insurance systems, workforce capacity, public policy, healthcare delivery infrastructure, and affordability. Improving equitable access will likely require multilevel structural interventions extending beyond Medicaid eligibility expansion alone.

items.title: Essential Paediatric Life Support Skills: A Set of Rolling Cart-Based Simulations in the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit.
items.abstract: Frequent high occupancy combined with increased rates of nursing turnover in the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) has led to a limited ability to perform in-room high-fidelity simulations and an increased need for focused life support training for PICU personnel. A multidisciplinary team of physicians, nurses, respiratory therapists, and undergraduate students implemented various simulations in the PICU August through December 2022. Simulations were conducted via a rolling-cart model to capture the largest audience and included, but were not limited to, chest compressions, defibrillation, bag-mask ventilation, push-pull fluid bolus administration, emergency cart utilization, and intraosseous access. Twelve simulation sessions were performed. Twenty-four participants supplied feedback, with the majority of responses being overwhelmingly positive. In answer to the question 'The content of the simulation was relevant to my current role in the PICU', over 83% of the respondents said that they 'strongly agree'. 100% of respondents would recommend the simulation they performed to colleagues. Additionally, the participation rate was high, with a median of 10 participants per session. For comparison, the PICU in-room simulations had a median of six participants per session. Conducting rolling cart-based simulations involving life support practices is a well-received method of education and garners high participation from PICU health care workers. This model can be beneficial in times when resources are limited. Maintaining life support competency for staff in the PICU can be well supported by brief, low-fidelity rolling cart-based simulations. Patients and general public were not involved in the study. Staff from the paediatric intensive care unit were involved by participating in the bedside simulations.

items.title: Food Environments, Structural Disadvantage, and Risk of Gestational Diabetes and Preeclampsia.
items.abstract: Obesity is a modifiable risk factor for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and preeclampsia, conditions that elevate maternal morbidity, mortality, and long-term cardiovascular risk. Lifestyle interventions are standard preconception recommendations for risk reduction, yet their feasibility is shaped by neighborhood and structural contexts. To explore these relationships, we evaluated associations of GDM and preeclampsia with neighborhood food environments, access to vendors authorized to accept benefits from the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC), and racialized economic segregation. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using electronic medical records from individuals with live births (N = 12,635) at three Maryland hospitals (2016-2021). Neighborhood exposures included the following: 1) food swamps-areas with a high density of unhealthy food retailers relative to healthy ones-measured using the modified Retail Food Environment Index (mRFEI); 2) racialized economic segregation, measured using the Index of Concentration at the Extremes (ICE); and 3) WIC vendor density per 1,000 residents. All exposures were modeled in tertiles, with the lowest tertile (Q1) indicating the most disadvantaged or lowest access and the highest (Q3) as reference. We used multivariable logistic regression with generalized estimating equations to assess associations with GDM and preeclampsia. Lower WIC access (lowest vs. highest tertile: adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.20; 95% confidence interval [CI] [1.02, 1.41]) and greater neighborhood disadvantage (ICE Q1 vs. Q3: aOR, 1.21; 95% CI [1.01, 1.44]) were associated with higher odds of GDM. No neighborhood measures were consistently associated with preeclampsia. Structural disadvantage and lower WIC vendor density were associated with higher odds of GDM but not preeclampsia. Expanding nutrition assistance infrastructure and addressing neighborhood disadvantage may improve maternal cardiometabolic health.

items.title: Heart Failure-Related Cardiogenic Shock: A Distinct Haemometabolic Syndrome.
items.abstract: Cardiogenic shock (CS) is increasingly recognised as a heterogeneous syndrome, with heart failure-related cardiogenic shock (HF-CS) now representing the predominant aetiology. However, contemporary diagnostic and therapeutic frameworks remain largely extrapolated from acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS), despite fundamental differences in pathophysiology and clinical trajectories. In HF-CS, pathophysiology is better conceptualised as a haemometabolic construct in which congestion, impaired forward flow, and systemic metabolic dysfunction interact to drive progressive multiorgan failure. These processes are often poorly captured by conventional blood pressure (BP)-based definitions of CS, particularly in heart failure, where patients may have persistently low yet compensated baseline BP. Although the Society of Cardiovascular and Angiographic Interventions shock classification provides a useful severity-based framework, emerging evidence supports a more integrated diagnostic approach that incorporates biomarkers such as lactate, mixed venous oxygen saturation, and invasive haemodynamic profiling. Together, these measures may improve risk stratification and better guide the timing and selection of escalation strategies. In parallel, multidisciplinary shock team models may improve outcomes in HF-CS, particularly when implemented early, before irreversible end-organ dysfunction develops. Future advances in HF-CS will require a shift away from BP-centric definitions derived from AMI-CS towards a comprehensive haemometabolic framework integrating congestion, perfusion, and haemometabolic status. Prospective HF-CS specific trials evaluating early, phenotype-guided care within structured, protocol-driven systems are essential to improving outcomes in this growing and clinically complex population.

items.title: Human Wound and Its Burden: Updated 2027 Compendium.
items.abstract: Human wounds remain a worldwide public health challenge, driving disability, infection, amputation, and premature death. Historical estimates identify 10.5 million Medicare beneficiaries with wounds in 2019 and 18.6 million people affected annually by diabetic foot ulcers worldwide. Successful healing requires restoration of skin barrier function, not simply visible closure complicated by the known threats of leaky skin cover. The NIDDK Diabetic Foot Consortium is advancing this paradigm through multicenter evidence linking impaired barrier restoration to ulcer recurrence, rigorous biomarker evaluation, and an inclusive platform integrating longitudinal clinical data, biospecimens, and patient-reported outcomes. Major mechanistic discoveries reveal how disrupted communication among immune cells, fibroblasts, and nerves sustains wound dysfunction. Biofilm-derived wound-infection signals impair macrophage clearance of dying cells, while excessive fibroblast-directed innervation restricts regeneration. Strategies targeting inflammatory resolution, localized mRNA delivery, and glucose-powered bioelectric signaling offer opportunities to improve repair. Comparative clinical trials emphasize that technological complexity does not guarantee superior healing. Economic and policy developments demand alignment of payment with evidence and meaningful endpoints. Medicare skin-substitute spending skyrocketed 40× from 2019 to 2024. CMS's 2026 shift to incident-to-supply payment under the Physician Fee Schedule projected $19.6 billion in gross fee-for-service savings. The FDA's 2026 patient-focused initiative emphasized daily wound burden and treatment priorities; effects of payment reforms on access and outcomes require evaluation. The emerging agenda unites functional wound closure, mechanism-based innovation, equitable access, and accountable spending. Progress must deliver sustained barrier restoration endpoints, reduced recurrence, preserved mobility, and improved quality of life, grounded in prevention and etiologic care.

items.title: Association of Measured and Functional Hearing Loss With Falls and Fear of Falling: A Nationally Representative Study of Older Adults in the US.
items.abstract: Falls and fear of falling (FoF) are common among older adults and contribute to increased morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Hearing loss affects two in three people aged 70+ and has been linked to falls. However, the association of hearing loss with falls and FoF is not well established as existing studies use heterogeneous measures for hearing loss (audiometry versus functional/self-reported), examine restricted age ranges within older adults, and frequently lack national representativeness. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 4745 adults ≥ 65 years from the National Health and Aging Trends Study (NHATS). Measured hearing loss was assessed by pure-tone audiometry (better-hearing ear's 4-frequency pure-tone average [BPTA] in decibels [dB], categorized as normal [≤ 25 dB], mild [26-40 dB], or moderate or greater hearing loss [> 40 dB]). Functional hearing loss was defined by self-reported hearing difficulty during common activities. Fall-related outcomes included falls in the last year, recurrent falls, FoF, and activity limitation due to FoF. We used weighted logistic regression models adjusted for sociodemographic factors, health conditions including vision loss, and fall history to evaluate the association between hearing and fall-related outcomes. 56.9% had measured hearing loss, and 11.8% had functional hearing loss. Measured moderate or greater hearing loss was associated with FoF (OR = 1.64, 95% CI: 1.17-2.31) in those without Activities of Daily Living (ADL) disability and recurrent falls both in those without (OR = 2.01, 95% CI: 1.02-3.96) and in those with ADL disability (OR = 2.98, 95% CI: 1.65-5.39). Functional hearing loss was associated with activity limitation from FoF (OR = 1.68, 95% CI: 1.04-2.70) in those with ADL disability. There were no associations between fall-related outcomes and hearing aid use among those with hearing loss. Associations with falls were qualitatively stronger with functional hearing loss in those aged 65-75. Measured and functional hearing loss are associated with fall-related outcomes with distinct age-related patterns. Future studies of fall prevention should consider interventions that target hearing impairment.

items.title: Intravaginal tobacco use among women in The Gambia: A qualitative study on the motivators, dependence and health risks.
items.abstract: Intravaginal insertion of smokeless tobacco (taba) is an emerging, little-researched method of tobacco use practiced in several countries in sub-Saharan Africa. This study aimed to characterise patterns of intravaginal taba use and the motivations, perceived benefits, adverse effects and dependence associated with this practice among women in The Gambia and examined whether this practice represents an unrecognised nicotine exposure pathway. Qualitative study using in-depth semi-structured interviews with current and former users of taba recruited through the Medical Research Council Unit The Gambia Pregnancy Care Integrating Translational Science Everywhere (PRECISE) and Mothers Health Foundation databases and supplemented by snowball sampling. Data were analysed thematically. Urban and rural communities across four health regions of The Gambia. Forty-two women aged 18-49 years who were current (n = 31) or former (n = 11) users of taba, recruited through community networks and health research programmes. Interviews explored initiation, patterns of use, composition and preparation of taba, perceived benefits and harms, risk perceptions and indicators of dependence. We translated, transcribed and analysed the data using a deductive-inductive thematic approach. Women commonly initiated taba use for perceived therapeutic purposes, particularly treatment of vaginal infections, pain and reproductive health concerns. Social networks strongly influenced initiation, and early adverse physiological reactions, such as burning, vomiting and dizziness, were frequently normalised as evidence of effectiveness. Its continued use was reinforced by perceived sexual, health and emotional benefits, including vaginal tightening, enhanced pleasure and relief from loneliness or unmet sexual needs. Participants indicated that products often contain potentially toxic additives (caustic soda, ashes, battery acid). Many reported symptoms consistent with nicotine toxicity and described progression to habitual use, characterised by cravings, withdrawal symptoms and difficulty quitting despite recognised harms, including suspected cancer and reproductive complications. Secrecy and stigma surrounding use were common. In The Gambia, intravaginal smokeless tobacco (taba) use appears to be initiated for perceived therapeutic and sexual health benefits, but users report experiences consistent with nicotine dependence and exposure to harmful additives in taba products, highlighting a previously unrecognised form of tobacco exposure among women.

items.title: The dynamic association between multimorbidity, loneliness, and frailty in older adults: A longitudinal study from China.
items.abstract: ObjectiveAlthough the dynamic relationships among multimorbidity, loneliness, and frailty remain unclear, this study aimed to examine their longitudinal associations and underlying mechanisms among older adults in China.MethodsData from 2671 adults aged ≥60 years from three waves of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (2011-2015) were analyzed. A cross-lagged panel model was used to examine bidirectional associations and mediating pathways among multimorbidity, loneliness, and frailty.ResultsIn the early period (T1-T2), multimorbidity and frailty showed significant but small bidirectional associations (multimorbidity → frailty: β = 0.082, p < 0.001; frailty → multimorbidity: β = 0.034, p = 0.002). Baseline frailty predicted changes in early and late multimorbidity (ΔEarly: β = 0.065, p = 0.001; ΔLate: β = 0.074, p < 0.01). Early changes in frailty predicted later changes in multimorbidity (β = 0.050, p < 0.05). Loneliness significantly mediated the longitudinal association between multimorbidity and subsequent frailty (β = 0.017, 95% confidence interval: 0.010, 0.035), indicating partial mediation and underscoring the role of psychosocial factors.ConclusionsMultimorbidity and frailty are bidirectionally associated, with a somewhat stronger temporal path from frailty to subsequent multimorbidity during the early period. Loneliness partially mediates the specific pathway from earlier multimorbidity to later frailty (T1 multimorbidity → T2 loneliness → T3 frailty). These observational findings offer potential implications rather than evidence of intervention effectiveness. Promoting physical activity, family engagement, social engagement, and psychosocial support may be considered candidate components of integrated chronic disease and frailty care, warranting evaluation in future intervention studies. Future studies should examine specific multimorbidity patterns and employ comprehensive loneliness measures.

items.title: Variations in Scheduled Non-Lunch Recess and Withholding: Preliminary Findings from the U.S. Education and Physical Activity Policy Study Physical.
items.abstract: Recess provides a critical school-based venue for student physical activity. However, recess provision and withholding practices remain inconsistently documented. This exploratory study described variability in daily scheduled non-lunch recess minutes, and recess withholding practices among U.S. elementary schools participating in a national physical education teacher questionnaire. This cross-sectional exploratory study used schoolyear 2022-2024 data from the U.S. Physical Education and Physical Activity Policy (US-PEPAP) questionnaire. Physical education teachers reported frequency and duration of scheduled non-lunch recess and whether their school withheld recess. After exclusions for ineligible settings, incomplete data, and multiple same-school responses, the analytic sample included 1,416 elementary, K-8, or K-12 schools across 51 jurisdictions (50 states, plus Washington D.C.). An exploratory composite recess practice score (range: 0-3) was constructed based on provision of the recommended at least 20-minutes/day of recess and whether recess was withheld. Unweighted school-level summaries were calculated overall and by jurisdiction. Mean scheduled non-lunch recess was 16.21-minutes/day (SD=8.84). The mean exploratory composite recess practice score was 1.24 (SD=1.13). Among participating schools, 230 (16.2%) reported the recommended 20-minutes/day and did not withhold, while 421 (29.7%) schools provided recommended 20-minutes/day, but practiced withholding. A total of 221 (15.6%) reported less than 20-minutes/day without withholding, and 544 (38.4%) reported less than the recommended 20-minutes/day and practiced withholding. Scheduled non-lunch recess and withholding varied among participating schools. These preliminary findings provide a current overview of school practices across the nation, and indicate a need for follow-up studies using representative sampling techniques to assess jurisdiction estimates.

items.title: International expert Delphi consensus on the management of metabolic dysfunction- and alcohol-associated liver disease (MetALD).
items.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction- and alcohol-associated liver disease (MetALD) describes steatotic liver disease in individuals with cardiometabolic dysfunction and alcohol consumption. As MetALD-specific evidence remains limited, practical guidance is needed for diagnosis, fibrosis assessment, alcohol use disorder management, cardiometabolic treatment, and transplant evaluation. We conducted a two-round modified Delphi study with an international multidisciplinary expert panel. Statements were developed after a targeted literature review and organized into four domains: diagnosis and disease stratification, alcohol use assessment and alcohol use disorder treatment, metabolic and cardiometabolic management, and liver transplant assessment. Statements were rated on a five-point Likert scale. Consensus agreement was predefined as a median score ≥4, ≥70% of ratings in the 4-5 range, and interquartile range ≤1. All 30 experts from 10 countries participated in round 1, and 29 (97%) in round 2. In round 1, 31 of 33 statements met agreement criteria; two were revised and re-evaluated. After round 2, consensus was achieved for all statements. The panel recognized MetALD as having dual metabolic and alcohol-related drivers and endorsed systematic cardiometabolic assessment, longitudinal quantification of alcohol intake, selective use of direct alcohol biomarkers, and stepwise noninvasive fibrosis risk stratification. Recommended care integrates individualized goals for alcohol reduction or abstinence, evidence-based alcohol use disorder treatment, structured lifestyle intervention, weight loss, physical activity, and optimization of diabetes, dyslipidemia, and hypertension. Transplant assessment should be individualized and multidisciplinary. This consensus provides practical recommendations for integrated MetALD care and identifies priorities for future clinical research and external validation.

items.title: Chronic hypoxia drives coronary artery pathology via TRPC3/4-mediated Ca²⁺ influx and phase separation-dependent cGAS-STING activation.
items.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is frequently complicated by coronary artery remodeling and dysfunction, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly defined. This study investigated whether and how chronic hypoxia drives coronary artery dysfunction through TRPC3/4-mediated Ca²⁺ influx and cGAS-STING activation in smooth muscle cells (SMCs). A rat model of PH was established by exposure to chronic hypoxia. Coronary artery structure and function were assessed by histology and wire myography. In vitro experiments were performed using cultured SMCs, with molecular and cellular analyses including qPCR, western blotting, immunofluorescence, live-cell imaging, mitochondrial assays, and cell-free phase separation assays. PH rats exhibited increased coronary TRPC3/4 expression, enhanced Ca²⁺ influx, and coronary hypercontractility. In cultured SMCs, hypoxia induced mitochondrial dysfunction, mtDNA release, and cGAS condensate formation. TRPC3/4-mediated Ca²⁺ overload promoted mitochondrial damage and cGAS phase separation, while STIM1/ORAI1-mediated store-operated Ca²⁺ entry (SOCE) further contributed to STING activation. Cell-free assays demonstrated that Ca²⁺ promoted cGAS phase separation in both the presence and absence of dsDNA, and this effect was dependent on the cGAS intrinsically disordered region (IDR). Importantly, CIP3 attenuated cGAS phase separation and downstream STING signaling, thereby mitigating hypoxia-induced SMC proliferation, migration, and phenotypic switching. In PH rats, short-term treatment with VAPG-targeted CIP3 reduced right ventricular systolic pressure, attenuated pulmonary and coronary vascular remodeling, and improved coronary contractile responses. Our findings establish a novel mechanistic axis wherein chronic hypoxia drives coronary artery dysfunction via TRPC3/4-mediated Ca²⁺ influx and phase separation-dependent cGAS-STING activation. In our experimental models, targeting cGAS phase separation, particularly through IDR-directed intervention, may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for PH-associated vascular pathology.

items.title: NMA-KIT: An interactive knowledge translation tool for network meta-analysis to bridge evidence and practice.
items.abstract: Network meta-analysis (NMA) is increasingly used to compare multiple interventions and inform clinical guidelines, health policy, and decision-making. However, inconsistent reporting and challenges in communicating complex findings can limit the accessibility, transparency, and practical application of NMA results. To address these challenges, we developed the NMA Knowledge Interactive Translation (NMA-KIT) tool, an interactive web-based application integrated within NMAstudio 2.0, to enable a seamless workflow from analysis to communication of results. The tool was developed to enable a seamless workflow from analysis to communication of results and was demonstrated using an exemplar NMA of systemic treatments for psoriasis. NMA-KIT provides a structured and user-friendly framework for communicating NMA findings. The Detailed Report enables in-depth exploration of treatment effects, underlying data, assumptions, and certainty of evidence, whereas the KIT Summary presents concise, clinically focused results. Additional functionalities include interactive data filtering, customizable visualizations, absolute risk estimation, access to study-level information, and collaborative project sharing. NMA-KIT represents an important step forward for bridging the gap between NMA results and decision-making. By combining interactive visualization, flexible exploration, and integrated project sharing within NMAstudio 2.0, the tool has the potential to improve transparency, reproducibility, and communication, ultimately supporting more informed and collaborative evidence-based decisions.

items.title: Evaluation of Fourier-Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (IR Biotyper Ⓡ ) for Rapid Serotyping of Streptococcus pneumoniae: A Prospective Validation in a Public Health Reference Laboratory.
items.abstract: To validate an expanded Artificial Neural Network (ANN) classifier for S. pneumoniae serotyping using FT-IR spectroscopy and assess its prospective performance in a routine public health reference laboratory. A diagnostic accuracy study was conducted at the Central Public Health Laboratory of Paraná - Brazil, based on the acquisition of 1,603 spectra, corresponding to 27 target groups/serotypes for training models and 70 independent routine clinical isolates (2025-2026) for prospective blind validation. The ANN classifier achieved 100% cross-validation accuracy across 27 target serogroups/serotypes in the derivation dataset. In prospective blind testing (N = 70 clinical isolates), the FT-IR/ANN workflow demonstrated 98.6% overall serotype concordance (69/70) with Quellung reaction (reference method), correctly differentiating high-priority vaccine-escape strains (19A, 3, and 6C). High-reliability classification (≥ 80.0) was obtained for 90.0% of isolates, with a mean Isolate Score of 94.6% (median 100.0%, IQR: 98.2-100.0%). An untested non-target serotype (35F) was flagged by a low Isolate Score (34.2), serving as a preliminary internal quality control indicator requiring confirmation by reference methods. FT-IR spectroscopy combined with ANN provides a rapid, accurate, and scalable alternative to the Quellung reaction for pneumococcal serotyping, supporting its use in routine public health laboratory surveillance.

items.title: Timing of Coronary Angiography After Successful Fibrinolysis and Clinical Outcomes in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Patients.
items.abstract: For patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) who cannot undergo timely primary percutaneous coronary intervention, fibrinolysis followed by routine angiography is recommended, but the clinical outcomes associated with different angiography intervals within the guideline-recommended window remain uncertain. In this nationwide retrospective cohort of 130,322 patients treated between 2018 and 2023, 74,021 underwent angiography 2-6 hours and 56,301 underwent angiography 6-24 hours after successful fibrinolysis. The 2-6-hour group more frequently had TIMI flow grade <3 at initial angiography (35.97% vs 29.86%; adjusted odds ratio [OR], 1.28; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.16-1.39) but had less new-onset heart failure (7.34% vs 8.30%; adjusted OR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.84-0.95), with no significant differences in in-hospital bleeding or mortality. During available follow-up, angiography within 2-6 hours was associated with lower all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 0.87; 95% CI, 0.78-0.98) and cardiac death (adjusted subdistribution HR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.76-0.95). In conclusion, among patients with STEMI undergoing angiography after successful fibrinolysis, a T2C interval of 2-6 hours was associated with lower long-term mortality and less new-onset heart failure without increased in-hospital bleeding or mortality, providing large-scale real-world evidence supporting further prospective evaluation of angiography timing within the recommended 2-24-hour window.

items.title: Knowledge graphs for polypharmacy: A systematic review and critical appraisal of reporting quality.
items.abstract: Ensuring medication safety for patients with multi-morbidity, who are often prescribed multiple drugs concomitantly (i.e., polypharmacy), is challenging due to the high risk of drug-drug interactions (DDIs) and accumulation of side-effects. Leveraging large datasets in the form of Knowledge Graphs (KGs) can improve knowledge on drug safety by modeling complex relationships among biomedical entities such as drugs, diseases, proteins and side effects, allowing for the prediction of novel relations. However, it remains unclear to what extent existing KGs adequately capture the polypharmacy context. Therefore, this systematic review identifies KGs constructed and/or utilized for predicting side effects and DDIs in the polypharmacy context, and evaluates their reporting quality. Publications were identified through a structured search through DBLP, MEDLINE, and the ACM Guide to Computing Literature up to January 2026, and supplemented by snowballing. We included peer-reviewed papers presenting KGs developed for and/or used in the context of polypharmacy-related predictions and containing polypharmacy knowledge. We excluded KGs missing both data and code. We adapted and extended a KG evaluation framework to objectively assess the reporting quality of KGs through a review of their documentation from both a technical and a medical domain-specific perspective. Ten studies were included following full-text screening. We provide an overview of relevant statistics, contents, and limitations using our KG evaluation framework. Our study revealed inconsistent technical documentation on KG construction and KG metadata, as well as a lack of knowledge on granular pharmacogenetics and (patho)physiological pathways within the included KGs. Our results show a need for improved quality of reporting, and the incorporation of fine-grained knowledge on pharmacogenetics and (patho)physiological pathways to ensure the long-term re-usability and relevance of KGs in the context of polypharmacy-related predictions. We also recommend to involve medical experts in KG development in this domain.

items.title: Assessment of the relationship between gender-segregated toilets and urinary health among students.
items.abstract: Assess the potential association between gender-segregated toilets at university and the urinary health of students as well as their toileting behaviors. An observational cross-sectional study was conducted among students in a French city between February and April 2025. The anonymous online questionnaire shared by QR code on social media included the ICIQ-FLUTS score (International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire - Female Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms) and the Toileting Behavior Web Scale (TB Web Scale). The main outcome measure was the existence of urination disorders evaluated by the ICIQ-FLUTS score. Through the 283 participants (71 % cisgender women, 21 % cisgender men and 2 % non-cisgenders), 30 % were using gender-neutral facilities, 27 % gender-segregated facilities and 43 % had the choice. 66 % reported at least one urinary functional disorder, mainly storage disorders. Overall ICIQ-FLUTS score did not differ significantly by facilities type. Sub-score analysis revealed that students with access to gender-segregated restrooms were significantly more likely to prefer voiding at home. Gender-neutral facilities do not appear to be associated with students' urinary health. Their establishment is a lever for promoting inclusive public health, just as is the need for awareness campaigns on proper urination practice.

items.title: Epidemiology, Prevalence, and Risk Factors of Human Brucellosis in Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad Province, Southwestern Iran: A Decade of Surveillance (2015-2025).
items.abstract: Brucellosis remains a public health concern in Iran. This retrospective descriptive surveillance study examined the epidemiology, diagnostic profile, treatment patterns, and reported transmission-related exposures of human brucellosis in Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad Province, southwestern Iran. We analyzed all confirmed cases reported to the Deputy of Health, Yasuj University of Medical Sciences, from 21 March 2015 to 20 March 2025, using routinely collected surveillance data from the National Brucellosis Control Plan. Analyses were descriptive. A total of 2,356 cases were identified (97.3% new, 2.7% recurrent). Annual incidence rose from approximately 15.5 cases per 100,000 population in 2017 to 58.2 per 100,000 in 2025, with 54.8% of cases reported during 2022-2025. The majority of cases were reported among rural residents (82.0%) and adults aged 31-60 years (56.6%). With respect to sex, men accounted for 53.7% of reported cases, compared with 46.3% among women. Unpasteurized dairy consumption was reported by 91.9% of the 2,234 patients with recorded exposure data (87.1% of all cases). Only 34.9% of the 1,560 patients with recorded vaccination responses reported vaccinated household or community livestock. Population-adjusted incidence was highest in several smaller counties rather than in the two counties with the largest case counts. Wright test results were available for 1,757 cases, most commonly at titers of 1:160 and 1:320. Rifampin (37.0%) and doxycycline (34.0%) were the most frequently prescribed antibiotics. These findings describe a substantial increase in reported brucellosis cases over the past decade. Most cases occurred among rural residents, and unpasteurized dairy consumption was commonly reported among patients with recorded exposure data. Strengthened livestock vaccination, community dairy-safety education, and integrated human-veterinary surveillance are suggested priorities for further evaluation.

items.title: Salmonella spp. in Raw Red Meat and Cooked Red Meat-Based Dishes from Five Regions of Mauritania: Prevalence and Serovar Distribution.
items.abstract: Non-typhoidal Salmonella is a major foodborne pathogen, yet data on its occurrence in meat and meat-based foods in Mauritania remain limited. This cross-sectional study estimated the prevalence of Salmonella spp. in raw red meat and cooked red meat-based dishes from Gorgol, Trarza, Brakna, Assaba, and Nouakchott, and identified the circulating serovars. From 25 April to 10 June 2023, 400 samples were collected, comprising 200 raw meat samples from slaughterhouses and butcheries, and 200 cooked meat dishes from restaurants and points of sale. Samples were analyzed according to ISO 6887-1 and ISO 6579-1:2017. Confirmed Salmonella isolates were serotyped using the Kauffmann-White-Le Minor scheme. Salmonella spp. were recovered from 18 of 200 raw meat (9.0%) and 7 of 200 cooked dish (3.5%) samples (odds ratio = 2.73; 95% confidence interval: 1.11-6.68; Pearson χ2 p = 0.023). All positive cooked dishes were beef-based. The recovered serovars were S. Kentucky (n = 9), S. Braenderup (n = 7), S. Mbandaka (n = 6), and S. Brandenburg (n = 3). These findings call for strengthened hygiene along the meat chain and for continued surveillance of Salmonella in Mauritania, including molecular characterization and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of circulating strains.

items.title: Frankincense-Myrrh Essential Oil Modulates Biofilm Formation and the Expression of Quorum Sensing Associated Genes in Multidrug-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa and MRSA: Integrated Metabolomic, Network Pharmacology, and Wound-Healing Evidence.
items.abstract: Biofilm-associated wound infections involving multidrug-resistant pathogens represent a substantial clinical and public health burden, driven by persistent microbial colonization, impaired tissue regeneration, and reduced responsiveness to conventional antimicrobial therapy. This study elucidated the chemical composition and biological properties of a frankincense-myrrh essential-oil blend (FM-EO) through an integrated phytochemical, microbiological, and computational investigation. Its activity was characterized by using clinical isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), with emphasis on pathogen susceptibility, biofilm-associated phenotypes, and wound-healing responses. FM-EO exhibited significant antibacterial activity, with inhibition zones of 25-30 mm and minimum inhibitory concentrations of 1.3 mg/mL against P. aeruginosa and 0.78 mg/mL against MRSA. At sub-inhibitory concentrations, FM-EO inhibited biofilm formation and reduced the expression of quorum-sensing-associated genes (lasR, lasI, rhlR, and rhlI) in P. aeruginosa, as well as the biofilm-associated genes icaA and icaD in MRSA. GC-MS analysis revealed complementary phytochemical profiles, with frankincense oil dominated by D-limonene-rich monoterpenes, whereas myrrh oil was enriched in triterpenoids, including 24-norursa derivatives and α-amyrin. In infected excision wound models, FM-EO accelerated wound closure, achieving healing rates of 92.18% and 95.95%, approaching or exceeding those observed with MEBO. FM-EO increased miR-21 expression and modulated Nrf2-associated antioxidant defense while suppressing miR-125b, TNF-α, NF-κB, nitric oxide, and lipid peroxidation, suggesting modulation of oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, and tissue remodeling. Histopathological and immunohistochemical findings supported enhanced re-epithelialization, VEGF-associated angiogenesis, collagen deposition, and reduced inflammatory infiltration. Network pharmacology analysis identified 191 overlapping targets between the phytochemicals and wound infection, with TNF, NFKB1, NFE2L2, and VEGFA emerging as key network hubs implicated primarily in VEGF- and NF-κB-mediated signaling pathways. These findings demonstrate that FM-EO exhibits antibacterial, biofilm-formation inhibitory activity, downregulates the transcription of QS-associated genes and promotes wound healing in infected wounds, with complementary anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and tissue-repair effects. These integrated findings support further investigation of FM-EO as a potential adjunctive candidate for managing antimicrobial-resistant wound infections.
