items.title: Improved sleep and clinical outcomes following a single-session intervention among adolescents with borderline personality disorder features.
items.abstract: Borderline personality disorder (BPD) is a serious mental illness that often emerges in adolescence. Although efficacious treatments have been developed, they are often lengthy, expensive, inaccessible, and require specialized training to deliver. Optimizing BPD prevention and early treatment is an important public health priority. Disrupted sleep is closely linked to key BPD features, and prior research has documented a range of sleep problems among BPD samples that appear to worsen symptom course and duration. This intervention trial (NCT04507308) assessed the effects of a single-session sleep-focused treatment on adolescent sleep and BPD-related symptoms. Fifty-seven adolescents (ages 13-18) with 3+ clinically impairing BPD features and at least some self-reported sleep-related difficulties participated with a caregiver. Participants completed baseline surveys, interviews, and 10-day ecological momentary assessment (EMA) protocol to examine BPD symptoms and sleep in daily life. Youth also collected at-home ambulatory electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings before undergoing the treatment informed by the Transdiagnostic Sleep and Circadian Intervention. Post-treatment, youth practiced their new sleep routine for approximately one month before undergoing reassessment (EMA, EEG, surveys). Many indices of sleep quantity and quality improved across both objective (EEG) and subjective assessments (EMA and self- and caregiver-report). Youth reported an earlier clock time at sleep onset and earlier waketime, more sleep, and fewer awakenings in daily life. Every sleep-related questionnaire score improved at post-intervention and was maintained at one-month follow-up. Multiple (though not all) indices of BPD symptoms also improved significantly. Findings suggest sleep may be a promising intervention target for at-risk youth.

items.title: Paleoproteomics and public health: from ancient patients to current sanitary issues.
items.abstract: Paleoproteomics is an emerging interdisciplinary field that investigates ancient proteins preserved in archaeological and paleontological materials. The preservation of proteins in materials such as tooth enamel, dental calculus, bone, soft tissues and other archaeological samples provides valuable molecular information about past individuals and populations. This review summarize the principles of paleoproteomic analysis, including protein extraction mass-spectrometry based approaches such as LC-MS/MS and discusses the major sample types used in paleoproteomic research and the use of paleoproteomics for understanding past health, disease, dietary practices, oral health and host-microbe interactions, as well as evolutionary and phylogenetic information. Despite its growing potential, the interpretation of ancient protein evidence remains challenging because of protein degradation, contamination, incomplete protein identification and limitations in reference databases. Here we will try to highlight the usefulness of such a specialty for current public health issues, by defining global and specific tendencies of microbial evolutions and human/host/environment co-existence.

items.title: Early Life Interventions in IgE-mediated Food Allergy Prevention and Management.
items.abstract: Food allergy has become a major public health concern. Over the past decade, advances in understanding early immune development have transformed approaches to both prevention and treatment of IgE-mediated food allergy. Landmark trials demonstrated that early and sustained introduction of allergenic foods, particularly peanut and egg, significantly reduces the risk of food allergy. This lead to a paradigm shift from allergen avoidance to proactive early introduction. For children who develop food allergy, emerging evidence indicates that early intervention may offer unique advantages, possibly due to heightened immune plasticity. Oral, epicutaneous, and sublingual immunotherapy have shown efficacy in increasing allergen tolerance, with studies suggesting improved outcomes and greater likelihood of remission when initiated in early childhood. Mechanistic studies indicate that these therapies modify allergic immune responses through suppression of effector cells, induction of regulatory pathways, and increased production of protective allergen-specific antibodies. In addition, omalizumab has become the first biologic approved in the United States for food allergy in individuals aged ≥1 year. Despite substantial progress, important knowledge gaps remain. Continued integration of mechanistic discoveries, clinical trials, and real-world evidence will be essential to refine precision approaches that maximize prevention, improve treatment outcomes, and reduce the lifelong burden of food allergy.

items.title: Isolation of clonal Klebsiella pneumoniae strains with diverse bla NDM-5 and bla OXA-181 carriage status during cefiderocol treatment in an immunocompromised patient with multiple lung abscesses.
items.abstract: Multiple carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) have emerged in many countries and pose a global public health concern. Although cefiderocol has antibacterial activity against CPE producing carbapenemases of various types, few studies have tracked the genetic changes in causative strains that were continuously detected during cefiderocol therapy. Here, we describe a 54-year-old male patient transferred from Bangladesh with multiple lung abscesses caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae producing NDM-5 and OXA-181, who received cefiderocol for 89 days. Multiplex PCR was performed to detect carbapenemase genes in 12 carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae strains isolated before, during, and after cefiderocol treatment. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing and whole-genome sequencing analysis were performed on four representative carbapenemases-producing K. pneumoniae strains. While the pre-treatment strains carried blaNDM-5 and blaOXA-181, some of the strains during treatment carried only blaNDM-5 or blaOXA-181. Although the post-treatment strain retained both blaNDM-5 and blaOXA-181, it had a loss-of-function mutation in the cirA gene and was resistant to cefiderocol. All four strains submitted for whole-genome sequencing analysis were clonal strains of capsular genotype KL81 and sequence type 16. The strains during treatment exhibited plasmid fusion and partial deletions, leading to the loss of multidrug resistance-associated genes such as blaNDM-5, blaOXA-181, and rmtB. This case demonstrates that multiple strains with distinct resistance gene profiles, even within a single clonal lineage, may be involved during the treatment of an infection caused by multidrug-resistant bacteria.

items.title: Integration of Network Toxicology and Transcriptomic Data: Exploring Molecular Associations Between Polystyrene Microplastics Exposure and Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis.
items.abstract: Polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs), persistent and bioaccumulative environmental pollutants detected in human tissues, have been increasingly associated with hepatic oxidative stress and inflammatory disturbances; however, their potential molecular relevance in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) remains vague. In this study, we applied a systems-level integrative framework combining transcriptomic analysis, network toxicology, immune profiling, and molecular docking to explore the overlap between genes with curated chemical-gene interactions involving polystyrene in the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database (CTD) and differentially expressed genes in human MASH liver tissues. By intersecting MASH-associated differentially expressed genes from the Gene Expression Omnibus with polystyrene-related genes curated in the CTD, we identified 80 candidate genes representing an overlap between curated polystyrene-gene interaction records and disease-related transcriptional alterations. Functional enrichment and protein-protein interaction analyses further prioritized eight hub genes (MYC, ATF3, CXCL2, IL18, NOS2, SOD2, FASN, and ARG1) that were consistently associated with inflammatory signaling, oxidative stress regulation, and metabolic dysregulation. Immune infiltration analysis indicated close association of the hub genes expression with characteristic immune remodeling patterns in MASH. Upstream regulatory analysis identified several transcription factors (TFs) potentially involved in coordinating hub gene expression, among which JUN/AP-1 emerged as a central regulatory node linking inflammation, oxidative stress, and metabolism-related programs. Molecular docking analysis provided structural support for the potential physical feasibility of interactions between a polystyrene pentamer and the selected TFs. Collectively, these findings establish a systems-level framework integrating CTD-curated polystyrene-gene interaction information with key transcriptional and immunometabolic features of MASH, generating testable hypotheses about the potential molecular relevance of PS-MPs to MASH for future mechanistic studies and environmental health risk assessment.

items.title: Lysosome-associated oxidative signals and membrane permeabilization contribute to intracellular ROS accumulation and alveolar epithelial cell death induced by zinc oxide nanoparticles.
items.abstract: With the increasing production and application of zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnONPs), their potential pulmonary toxicity has attracted growing attention. Exposure to ZnONPs has been shown to induce lung epithelial cell death, contributing to pulmonary injury; however, the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Oropharyngeal aspiration of ZnONPs induced significant pulmonary oxidative stress in mice, as evidenced by elevated 4-hydroxynonenal levels and activation of the NRF2 antioxidant response. Notably, more pronounced tissue injury and lysosomal membrane alterations were observed in the alveolar compartment than in the bronchial compartment, as indicated by reduced co-localization of LAMP2 and CTSD. Further in vitro investigations revealed that clathrin- and cholesterol-dependent pathways may contribute to the cellular uptake of FITC-labeled ZnONPs, with subsequent lysosomal trafficking. ZnONPs increased lysosomal lipid peroxidation and altered the levels of lysosome-associated proteins, including CALPAIN1, mature CTSB, and mature CTSD. Time-dependent changes in Lysotracker, Lysosensor, and acridine orange (AO) fluorescence further supported lysosomal dysfunction and lysosomal membrane permeabilization (LMP). Notably, both the antioxidant N-acetylcysteine (NAC) and a CTSB inhibitor attenuated ZnONP-induced lysosomal injury, oxidative stress, and subsequent cell death. Silencing Nrf2 exacerbated ZnONP-induced oxidative stress, LMP, and cell death, which were partially attenuated by NAC. However, NAC did not completely abolish the difference in LMP between ZnONP-treated Scramble and Nrf2-silenced cells, suggesting that additional NRF2-dependent mechanisms may contribute to lysosomal protection beyond NAC-sensitive oxidative stress. Collectively, these results support a role for lysosomal oxidative alterations and dysfunction in ZnONP-induced alveolar epithelial cell death and highlight the protective role for NRF2 in this process.

items.title: Digoxigenin is a Broad-Spectrum Antiviral Agent against Influenza A Virus via Degradation of Nucleoprotein.
items.abstract: Seasonal influenza A viruses (IAVs; H1N1 and H3N2) and their zoonotic variants (e.g. H5N1 and H3N8) pose persistent threats to public health, highlighting an urgent need for innovative therapeutic strategies. Through high-throughput screening with the constructed reporter virus H3N8-GFP, we initially identified a panel of potential antiviral agents from FDA-approved compounds. Further validation revealed that digoxigenin (Dig), the aglycone of digoxin, significantly inhibited the proliferation of H3N8, H1N1, H3N2, and H5N1 in infected primary murine alveolar epithelial cells and ESC-derived human alveolar organoids. Dig treatment protected mice from lethal challenge with H1N1 and H3N8 by increasing survival rates and reducing viral loads.Mechanistically, Dig exerts its antiviral activity by directly binding to the host Na+/K+-ATPase α1 subunit (ATP1A1), which triggers the degradation of viral nucleoprotein via both the ubiquitin-proteasome and autophagy pathways, without affecting other components of the viral ribonucleoprotein (vRNP). Our study reveals the Dig-mediated antiviral mechanism that targets the host cell degradation machinery, and identifies Dig as a promising broad-spectrum antiviral agent against IAVs.

items.title: Pathways and recruitment opportunities for pharmacy exploration and learning: Building a multi-tiered pharmacy workforce pipeline for rural communities.
items.abstract: Rural and urban populations experience profound health disparities alongside persistent shortages in the pharmacy workforce. Creating intentional, multi-tiered pipelines from under-resourced rural and urban communities to and through pharmacy education is a critical strategy to address geographic health disparities and alleviate the prevalence of community pharmacy deserts. To design, implement, and evaluate the Pathways and Recruitment Opportunities for Pharmacy Exploration and Learning (PROPEL) program, a comprehensive initiative aimed at increasing rural and urban pharmacy career awareness, strengthening academic pathways into pharmacy education, and expanding rural and urban-focused training within a Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) curriculum. PROPEL deploys a two-aim approach. Aim 1 focuses on precollege students through pharmacy career awareness and recruitment activities in rural and urban middle and high schools, expansion of an Early Assurance Program (EAP), development of an open-access introductory course, and implementation of a bridge program to support college readiness. Aim 2 focuses on PharmD education through a specialized rural and urban curriculum, immersive service-learning opportunities, and expansion of rural-focused Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience (APPE) infrastructure. During its first year, PROPEL engaged 24 middle and high school teachers (11 rural and 13 urban) in focus groups to inform pharmacy career awareness activities. An Early Assurance Program partnership with Ohio University, a public institution serving Appalachian Ohio, was finalized. A new two-credit-hour rural service-learning elective provided 16 PharmD students with immersive clinical and community engagement experiences in rural southeastern Ohio. Additionally, a housing partnership with Ohio University was established to subsidize accommodations for students completing rural APPE rotations. PROPEL demonstrates the feasibility of an integrated, rural and urban-focused pathway model to strengthen the pharmacy workforce. By connecting early recruitment, academic partnerships, and immersive experiential training, the program provides a sustainable framework for developing a culturally responsive workforce committed to serving rural and underserved communities.

items.title: Education and exercise compared to education alone for hip osteoarthritis: Protocol for the EDUEX randomized controlled trial.
items.abstract: Patient education (EDU) and exercise are universally recommended as first-line treatment for hip and knee osteoarthritis (OA). Specifically in hip OA, the evidence that exercise is a necessary addition when comprehensive EDU is delivered is sparse. Additionally, no randomized trial has evaluated effects of exercise on articular cartilage in hip OA assessed by magnetic resonance imaging. This randomized trial will evaluate whether adding progressive resistance training (PRT) to EDU results in superior improvements in 1) patient-reported physical function and 2) collagen integrity of the hip articular cartilage. This multicenter, stratified, block randomized, controlled, parallel-group, efficacy, superiority trial will be conducted at hospitals and physiotherapy clinics in Denmark. A total of 150 people with hip OA will be enrolled and randomized in a 1:1 ratio to only participate in an EDU program or to the same EDU program and additionally 12 months of partly supervised group-based PRT. The primary outcome is between-group difference in change from baseline to 12 months in 1) the Hip Disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score activities of daily living function subscale for the primary clinical superiority study and 2) T2 relaxation time mapping of the hip articular cartilage for the primary mechanistic superiority study (P-MECH). The EDUEX trial will provide high-quality evidence for assessing the clinical efficacy of adding PRT to EDU in people with hip OA while also assessing the effects on hip articular cartilage. ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT06391554.

items.title: Universal barcoded connectomics for massively parallel single-neuron projection mapping in diverse vertebrate species
items.abstract: Neuroscience relies on diverse model species to understand animal behavior and brain function. Yet, tools for rapid, high-resolution brain connectivity mapping remain unavailable in most vertebrate species, slowing progress in many neuroscience models and rendering cross-species circuit comparisons challenging. Here, we overcome this barrier by establishing sequencing-based barcoded connectomics for rapid single-neuron tracing in seven vertebrate species ranging from frogs to birds to non-human primates. We develop a general solution to viral tropism and barcode trafficking, validate our reagents by mapping the projections of thousands of neurons in the songbird HVC, and discover a single set of reagents that functions across highly divergent species. Together, we provide ready-to-use barcoding reagents for diverse species and a simple framework for further adapting them if necessary, enabling high throughput single-neuron tracing across vertebrates.

items.title: The prevalence of multiple sclerosis (MS) in the American continent: a systematic review.
items.abstract: Background America is a continent covering more than 42,549,000 km 2 and making up most of the land in the western hemisphere of the Earth. Thirty-five countries are located in the American continent. The prevalence of multiple sclerosis (MS) in different countries of America varies, so we designed this systematic review and meta-analysis to estimate the pooled prevalence of MS in the American continent. Method We systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and also references of included studies, review articles, and conference abstracts on 1 December 2022. Results Fifty studies were included. Most studies were conducted in the United States of America (USA) (between 1915 and 2020) and Canada (between 1982 and 2014). Crude prevalence rates of MS per 100,000 population varied substantially across the Americas, ranging from as low as 0.5-5 in parts of Brazil, Colombia, Panama, and Argentina to more than 300 in several high-prevalence regions of Canada and recent national estimates from the United States. Across the continent, MS prevalence has shown a consistent upward trend over time. A marked female predominance was consistently observed, with female-to-male ratios generally ranging from 2.0 to 3.6 across studies. Conclusion The result of this systematic review showed that the prevalence of MS differs dramatically in the America continent with marked geographical heterogeneity consistent with the established latitudinal gradient.

items.title: Self-guided home-based rehabilitation for upper limb motor recovery in people with stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Purpose This review examined the efficacy of self-guided, home-based rehabilitation (SGHBR) for upper limb recovery in people with stroke (PwS). Material and methods PubMed, Scopus, CINAHL, Web of Science, and PEDro were searched using terms related to stroke, upper limb, home-based rehabilitation, and self-rehabilitation. Included articles were randomized controlled trials involving adults with stroke receiving home-based upper limb rehabilitation assessed with standardized clinical scales. Studies were excluded if the SGHBR intervention involved technological devices, telerehabilitation, or direct therapist supervision. Results Four reviewers screened 501 records, and 14 articles were included in the systematic review. Eight independent cohorts from 10 studies provided data for meta-analysis; remaining findings were narratively synthesized. SGHBR showed no significant advantage over other rehabilitation interventions, although the pooled estimate slightly favored SGHBR (SMD = 0.10, 95% CI -0.23 to 0.44), with low-to-moderate heterogeneity (I 2 = 31.8%). Methodological quality was overall moderate, with variable risk of bias. Interventions differed in structure, duration, and strategies, but most included task-oriented or task-specific practice. Conclusions SGHBR may provide upper limb functional benefits comparable to conventional therapy, but higher-quality studies are needed to confirm efficacy, generalizability, and cost-effectiveness across stroke survivor populations in routine practice.

items.title: rTMS Attenuates Microglial Phagocytosis and Promotes Neurorepair in a Photothrombotic Stroke Mouse Model.
items.abstract: Objective This study investigated the effects of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) on functional recovery in photothrombotic (PT) stroke mice and whether rTMS promotes neurorepair by modulating microglial phagocytosis. Methods Eight-week-old male C57BL/6J mice were used to establish a focal stroke model via photothrombosis (PT group). The Sham group and PT + rTMS group were included. rTMS was initiated 24 h after modeling. Neurological deficits were assessed. Microglial activation, synaptic phagocytosis, neuronal injury, and the levels of tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and interleukin-1β (IL-1β) were evaluated. Differentially expressed proteins and core regulatory pathways were analyzed. Results rTMS treatment significantly increased body weight, prolonged the latency to fall and shortened the balance beam crossing time, reduced foot faults, and improved the discrimination index in PT mice. rTMS reduced the number of Iba1-positive microglia and CD68-positive cells, attenuated microglial synaptic phagocytosis, and alleviated neuronal loss and apoptosis. rTMS significantly decreased the levels of TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β in the brain. A total of 416 differentially expressed proteins were identified between the PT and PT + rTMS groups. The differentially expressed proteins were significantly enriched in microglial phagocytosis pathways and related signaling pathways. Conclusion rTMS significantly ameliorates neurological deficits and cognitive impairment in PT stroke mice. The underlying mechanism may involve the inhibition of excessive microglial activation, attenuation of microglia-mediated synaptic phagocytosis, and alleviation of neuroinflammation. Proteomic analysis reveals that rTMS modulates the expression of proteins associated with microglial phagocytosis-related signaling pathways, which may contribute to the observed post-stroke neurorepair effects.

items.title: Engineered autophagy receptors for selective protein clearance in neurodegeneration.
items.abstract: Engineered autophagy receptors offer a way to direct intracellular degradation toward proteins implicated in neurodegeneration. Guo and colleagues fused cytoplasm-stable antibody fragments to microtubule-associated protein 1A/1B-light chain 3 alpha (LC3A) and delivered the resulting constructs using small extracellular vesicles. Their experiments show reduced pathological tau and cytoplasmic TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) in neuronal cultures and reduced tau pathology in mice. A separate adeno-associated virus experiment reduces TDP-43 pathology and improves motor performance in mice. These findings connect selective cargo recognition with intracellular delivery and raise questions about how engineered autophagy receptors might be adapted to different disease contexts. Here, we discuss which pathological protein assemblies are most accessible to these receptors, how selective clearance interacts with neuronal autophagic capacity, and how intracellular exposure relates to sustained functional benefit. We consider these questions with particular attention to preserving physiological protein function and linking cargo turnover to neuronal outcomes.

items.title: Aged Extracellular Vesicles and Whole Serum Disrupt a Multicellular Human Blood-Brain Barrier Model Through Distinct Mechanisms.
items.abstract: Age-associated changes in circulating factors contribute to blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction, yet the relative effects of serum and serum-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) remain unclear. Here, we used a human multicellular transwell BBB model, composed of primary brain microvascular endothelial cells (BMECs), astrocytes, pericytes, and neural progenitor cells (hNPCs) derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), to compare the effects of serum and serum-derived EVs from young-adult and aged mice on BBB integrity. Barrier function was assessed by transendothelial electrical resistance (TEER) and permeability to 3-5 and 40 kDa FITC-dextran, and cellular organization and junctional integrity were evaluated by immunofluorescence. Although TEER exhibited treatment-dependent differences, permeability assays revealed distinct age- and treatment-associated changes in macromolecular transport. Aged EVs increased permeability to both dextran tracers relative to young EVs and markedly reduced ZO-1 coverage, whereas aged serum produced the greatest permeability to the 40 kDa tracer and the most pronounced loss of BMEC alignment. These changes occurred without a significant reduction in overall vWF-positive endothelial area, indicating structural and functional remodeling rather than overt endothelial loss. Additionally, young serum increased TUJ1-positive area and claudin-5 coverage, pointing to broader cell-type-specific effects. Together, these findings show that aging shifted the BBB toward greater macromolecular permeability and poorer endothelial organization, with aged EVs acting primarily on junctional integrity and aged serum driving the larger increase in permeability and loss of endothelial alignment.

items.title: Immediate Postpartum Mental Health and Sleep in Mothers and Fathers with Healthy Newborns.
items.abstract: Background The postpartum period represents a critical window for parental psychological adjustment, but whether this is the case immediately after birth remains understudied. Furthermore, while many aspects of maternal mental health have been widely investigated in high-risk contexts, less is known about critical factors such as sleep-related vulnerability and attachment-related processes in low-risk situations, how these relate to early mental health in fathers, or how these factors may be associated with neonatal behavior. Methods Thirty-two mother-father-newborn triads, comprising 32 mothers, 32 fathers, and their 32 healthy, full-term newborns, were included in the study. Newborn behavioral functioning was evaluated with the NBAS on Day 2. Mothers completed the EPDS, ECR, and STAI on Day 3. Both parents completed the CES-D, PSS, SCI, and FIRST on Day 3. Correlation, paired-comparison, and exploratory regression analyses were conducted. Results Clinically relevant elevations on at least one psychological or sleep-related measure were observed in 59.4% of mothers and 28.1% of fathers. Mothers showed significantly higher depressive symptoms, poorer sleep quality, and greater sleep reactivity than fathers. Among mothers, depressive symptoms were associated with greater sleep reactivity, with trait anxiety showing the strongest association with depressive symptoms. Maternal and paternal depressive symptoms were also positively associated across partners. Newborn behavioral functioning was broadly within expected ranges, and no association between parental psychological or sleep-related measures and NBAS cluster scores survived FDR correction. Discussion Psychological and sleep-related vulnerability was detectable in parents during the immediate postpartum period in this low-risk clinical context, with higher levels observed in mothers. Cross-partner concordance was limited to depressive symptoms. These findings suggest that early screening of both parents may be clinically relevant. Sleep reactivity and anxiety were associated with maternal postpartum distress, but their potential predictive value requires confirmation in longitudinal studies.

items.title: An AAV packaging protocol suitable for production of small batch sizes for in vivo prototyping and pilot studies.
items.abstract: The use of adeno-associated viral vectors for delivery of genetic information into the mammalian CNS remains popular but producing highly purified vectors for in vivo applications requires a significant investment of resources and time that can impede the development and testing of AAV vectors for experimentation. To address this issue, we have developed a simplified AAV packaging protocol that does not require large capital equipment (ultracentrifugation or chromatography machines) yet still produces transduction competent particles in quantities that are sufficient for testing AAV prototypes in the rodent CNS. This protocol is serotype agnostic, and has been successful with AAV1, AAV9, AAV-DJ, and rAAV2-retro. Intracranial injection of AAV-EF1a-GFP-KASH into rats demonstrated that our "single plate" AAV preps produce patterns of transgene expression and inflammation that are comparable to those produced by the same AAV vector purified by affinity column chromatography. Our protocol allows for multiple vectors to be packaged and processed in parallel, making it ideal for production of multiple variants, constructs, and prototypes simultaneously.

items.title: Temporal deconvolution of mesoscale recordings.
items.abstract: Mesoscale calcium recordings, such as wide-field imaging, enable high-temporal-resolution recordings of neuronal activity across extensive brain regions. However, because these recordings capture light emitted by calcium indicator fluorescence, the underlying neural activity is obscured by the temporal dynamics of the indicators. Here, we develop and evaluate four deconvolution methods to recover neuronal spiking rates from fluorescence traces recorded in wide-field imaging. The methods-dynamically binning (using adaptive discrete-time bins), continuously varying (estimating smooth spiking rates), first differences (providing efficient estimation), and a modified Wiener filter (robust to large fluorescence magnitude variations)-consistently outperform the previously used adapted Lucy-Richardson algorithm on both synthetic data and simultaneous fluorescence-spike recordings. Critically, we demonstrate that using raw fluorescence signals in advanced analysis methods can yield distorted results, including spuriously inflated correlations between brain regions' activity. This highlights the necessity of accurate temporal deconvolution for reliable interpretation of brain activity.

items.title: Environmental Bacteriophages as Biocontrol Agents Against Waterborne Multidrug-Resistant Pathogens Across South Asia
items.abstract: Waterborne multidrug-resistant pathogens pose a significant public health concern in South Asia, yet the studies regarding environmental phages remain underrepresented in existing reviews. This narrative review examines phage ecology and evaluates phages targeting five waterborne pathogens: Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Salmonella Typhi, and Vibrio cholerae. It focuses on Nepal, India, and Bangladesh, while comparing available findings with research from Iran, Southeast Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa, and South America. Studies reveal that South Asian rivers have diverse phage communities and phage activity against all five pathogens. Metagenomic analysis performed in the Yamuna River of India documented 28,993 viral contigs, out of which 19% were linked to the pathogenic bacterial hosts, while crAssphage was detected in 72% of the samples from Bagmati River, Nepal. Phage administration reduced Klebsiella loads in mice by 3-7log10 CFU/mL in Nepal and vibriophage abundance was reported to predict cholera burden one week in advance. No field deployment for water treatment has been reported in South Asia. Compared with Iran, where phage cocktails reduced bacterial loads in hospital wastewater, South Asian research remains largely at the isolation and characterization stage. Priorities include systematic pathogen monitoring, standardized genomic methods, phage cocktail development, and regionally appropriate regulation.

items.title: GO- and calcium silicate NP-modified diamides for enhanced antimicrobial activity: structural, morphological, and in silico investigations.
items.abstract: We herein report the preparation and investigation of antimicrobial nanohybrid systems based on antimicrobial diamides and GO, as well as CaSiO 3 NPs. Diamides were synthesized by condensation of 4-nitrobenzoyl chloride with aromatic diamines under catalyst-free conditions, followed by non-covalent conjugation of the obtained compounds with GO and CaSiO 3 . Synthesized diamides, NPs, and nanoensembles were investigated by spectroscopic, microscopic, and diffraction techniques. The obtained two-component nanohybrid systems were examined against bacterial and yeast strains, which demonstrated their potent antimicrobial efficacy in comparison to parent compounds and NPs alone; in particular, F8@GO MIC in the case of B. cereus was 8 µg mL -1 . Furthermore, the ultrastructural investigations of bacterial cells treated with F8@GO using TEM demonstrated significant morphological changes such as extensive cytoplasmic rarefaction, disruption of intracellular organization and ghost cell formation in contrast to control bacterial cells. Taking into account the phenotypic damage observed in TEM analysis, key cell division and peptidoglycan-synthesizing as well as glycolytic enzymes were selected for molecular docking analysis that revealed a promising binding affinity between the targeted compound F8 and the identified pocket on TubZ. Furthermore, a 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation provides consistent, multi-parameter evidence for a stable and well-tolerated TubZ-F8 complex.

items.title: Mitochondrial Phylogeny Reveals Deep Intraspecific Divergence and Fine-Scale Regional Structure in Orangutans.
items.abstract: Orangutans ( Pongo spp.) are a valuable model for investigating how past climatic and geological events have shaped population structure and species diversification. We reconstructed 237 complete mitochondrial genomes from whole-genome sequencing data and combined them with 50 available mitochondrial sequences, resulting in a dataset of 287 orangutans spanning the current range of Sumatran and Bornean orangutans. Among Sumatran orangutans ( P. abelii ), we identified five geographically distinct mitochondrial clades corresponding to Langkat, North Aceh, Tripa, West Leuser and Batu Ardan. These clades showed strong differentiation, indicating long-term persistence of distinct maternal lineages across the Leuser landscape. For the recently described species, P. tapanuliensis , we added 10 newly reconstructed mitogenomes, increasing representation from 3 to 13 individuals. P. tapanuliensis formed a monophyletic, deeply divergent clade, confirming strong mitochondrial differentiation and long-term isolation. In Bornean orangutans ( P. pygmaeus ), we identified seven major regional mitochondrial clades corresponding to Sarawak, Central Kalimantan, South Kalimantan, Southeast Kalimantan, East Kalimantan and the North and South Kinabatangan populations in Sabah. Within the subspecies P. p. morio , the North and South Kinabatangan, East Kalimantan and Southeast Kalimantan clades formed distinct maternal lineages, revealing substantial mitochondrial structure within the currently recognised subspecies. Our findings suggest that current geographic and taxonomic divisions may under-represent the extent of regional maternal diversity across orangutans. Female philopatry has preserved ancient mitochondrial structure across Sundaland, with its geographic distribution shaped by refugial persistence, major riverine barriers and long-term population fragmentation.

items.title: Anthropogenic Disturbance Significantly Affects the Abundance and Distribution Patterns of Butterflies, Not Species Richness: A Case Study in Kunming, China.
items.abstract: With the advancement of urbanization, especially in developing countries, human activities are profoundly influencing the distribution of biodiversity. As a key indicator group in urban ecosystems, butterflies play an important role in maintaining ecological functions. Anthropogenic disturbance not only directly affects butterfly community activity, but also may indirectly influence butterfly community structure by altering other environmental conditions. Identifying the impact mechanism of anthropogenic disturbance on butterfly communities in urban areas is helpful to clarify the response of butterfly diversity to human disturbance and provide scientific reference for species diversity conservation. Our study systematically investigated the impact of anthropogenic disturbances on butterfly diversity and distribution patterns by establishing survey transects in various disturbed sites in Kunming and conducting 24 field surveys over a 2-year period. The results indicated that at the species level, there were no significant differences in butterfly species numbers across three different levels of anthropogenic disturbance, but differences in species composition were observed. An investigation of butterfly alpha diversity under different anthropogenic disturbance intensities revealed no significant changes in the alpha diversity index of butterflies across the disturbance gradients in Kunming. Beta diversity analysis showed that butterfly community composition exhibited a gradient change pattern under the three disturbance intensities, with the highest community similarity observed between the medium and low disturbance gradients, and the lowest similarity between the low and high disturbance gradients. Beta diversity partitioning indicated that species turnover was the primary driving factor affecting the difference of butterfly community structure across the disturbance gradients. Our findings suggest that anthropogenic disturbance has a significant impact on butterflies in Kunming, primarily affecting species abundance rather than richness, with variation in the effects observed across different groups. Our results provide a scientific foundation for building biodiversity conservation friendly cities.

items.title: Zinc oxide-containing material prepared in the presence of Agrimonia eupatoria extract: antimicrobial activity, effects on cell viability, and DNA damage responses.
items.abstract: A zinc oxide (ZnO)-containing material was prepared by alkaline precipitation of zinc acetate in the presence of an aqueous Agrimonia eupatoria extract, followed by thermal treatment at 200 °C. The material was characterized using UV-vis spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with selected-area electron diffraction (SAED), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). SAED revealed crystalline ZnO in the examined regions, while XPS indicated the presence of Zn(ii) and organic and oxygen-containing surface species. The material exhibited strain-dependent antimicrobial activity, with minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) ranging from ≤78 to 10.000 µg mL -1 . MTT assays revealed concentration- and time-dependent changes in cell viability in cancer and non-malignant cell lines; however, the absence of cell-free interference controls and an independent viability assay limit the interpretation of these findings. Changes in assay signals associated with superoxide production, nitrite accumulation and total NF-κB p65 levels were also observed. In the Drosophila melanogaster comet assay, the two lowest tested concentrations (0.25 and 0.5 mg mL -1 ) did not produce a detectable increase in comet scores, whereas higher concentrations were associated with increased scores. Co-exposure with ethyl methanesulphonate (EMS) resulted in lower comet scores than EMS treatment alone, particularly at lower concentrations, but these observations do not establish a specific DNA-protective mechanism. The absence of plant-free ZnO and extract-only controls, bulk X-ray diffraction (XRD), and measurements of Zn 2+ release under biological exposure conditions limits the attribution of the observed effects to individual components. Overall, the findings describe the antimicrobial and cell-based responses associated with the tested ZnO-containing preparation and highlight the need for further controlled studies to clarify its composition and biological effects.

items.title: Machine Learning-Enhanced Vibrational Spectroscopy for Mammalian Wildlife: A Critical Review of Conservation and Forensic Applications.
items.abstract: Mammalian species differ in the biochemical composition of their tissues and fluids-subtle but statistically discriminable variation that vibrational spectroscopy can detect and machine learning can decode for applications spanning forensic investigation, conservation monitoring, and physiological assessment. This review critically examines machine learning applications across near-infrared (NIR), mid-infrared (MIR/FTIR), and Raman spectroscopy specifically for mammalian wildlife samples. We examine unsupervised and supervised learning methods, from principal component analysis and hierarchical clustering to partial least squares discriminant analysis, support vector machines, random forests, and deep learning architectures, alongside the preprocessing, validation, and performance assessment strategies essential for reliable deployment in wildlife contexts. Each approach is evaluated with theoretical grounding and specific mammalian case studies spanning blood species identification, live animal monitoring, tissue analysis, and fecal dietary profiling. Despite reported classification accuracies frequently exceeding 95%, the field remains fragmented by inconsistent validation practices, limited external testing across species and geographic populations, and a critical shortage of standardized mammalian spectral reference databases, constraints that limit reproducibility and translation from controlled laboratory conditions to operational conservation and forensic practice. By bridging these methodological gaps, this review provides wildlife researchers, conservation biologists, and forensic scientists with a critical synthesis and practical framework for implementing machine learning-enhanced spectroscopy in mammalian wildlife conservation and crime investigation.

items.title: Integrative Taxonomic Revision of the Tachysurus argentivittatus Group (Siluriformes: Bagridae) Illuminates Cryptic Diversification Along the Northern Margin of the East Asian Tropics.
items.abstract: The Tachysurus argentivittatus group represents the smallest-bodied lineage within Tachysurus with adults not exceeding 50 mm in standard length (SL), and is widely distributed across East Asia. Owing to pronounced morphological conservatism, species delimitation within this group has long been challenging. Previous studies recognized two species within this species group, T. argentivittatus sensu stricto, restricted to the Pearl River and Tachysurus mica , distributed from the Yangtze to the Amur Rivers and also indicated that the Hainan Island population represents an undescribed lineage. In this study, geographic sampling encompasses the northern margin of the East Asian tropics, including populations from central and northern Vietnam and coastal mainland China. Using an integrative framework, we confirm the validity of Tachysurus longispinalis from the Red River basin. Furthermore, this species forms part of a species complex, comprising four reciprocally monophyletic lineages. Within this complex, two allopatric lineages from Hainan Island and the Moyang River (in Guangdong Province of China) exhibit consistent genetic divergence and diagnostic morphological differences, and are described herein as Tachysurus lativittatus sp. nov. and Tachysurus stenomaculatus sp. nov., respectively. The central Vietnam lineage shows shallow genetic divergence and limited morphological differentiation from T. longispinalis and is provisionally treated as T. aff. longispinalis . Divergence-time estimates suggest that diversification within the complex occurred from the late Pliocene to the middle Pleistocene, potentially overlapping with major climatic transitions associated with the onset and intensification of Northern Hemisphere glaciation. Repeated sea-level declines during this period may have facilitated ancestral dispersal and subsequent divergence. Moreover, our findings refine the morphological boundaries of the T. argentivittatus group.

items.title: The H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> Signalling Continuum: From Organelle Homeostasis to Crop Resilience.
items.abstract: Plant responses to environmental stress involve dynamic redox changes that vary across subcellular compartments, tissues and time. Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is a key component of this response, but its signalling effects cannot be inferred reliably from bulk abundance alone. Here we develop the H 2 O 2 signalling continuum as a testable framework linking compartmental redox events to cellular, tissue, whole-plant and rhizosphere scales under environmental stress. We define the continuum along spatial, temporal and functional dimensions, and distinguish it from related concepts including ROS waves, retrograde signalling and systemic acquired acclimation. Mechanistic evidence indicates that compartment-specific H 2 O 2 dynamics contribute to chloroplast protection and repair, to mitochondrial redox adjustment and AOX-associated respiratory flexibility, and to energy and carbon flux remodelling. Signal amplitude and duration are shaped by scavenging through catalases, peroxidases, ascorbate, glutathione and peroxiredoxins, while H 2 O 2 interfaces with abscisic acid, auxin, cytokinin and jasmonate and participates in extracellular perception via aquaporins and HPCA1-dependent pathways. Emerging evidence connects H 2 O 2 dynamics with rhizosphere communication and root-microbe interactions. We distinguish direct mechanistic evidence from orthology-supported and physiological or associative evidence, particularly in crops. Advances in genetically encoded biosensors, spatially resolved measurements and systems-level analyses now allow us to test how H 2 O 2 amplitude, duration, localisation and recovery relate to biological outcomes, including under combined and recurrent stresses. Crop translation should therefore focus on coordinated signal generation, buffering and recovery, integrating natural variation, priming, redox traits and field validation.

items.title: A three-tier screening pipeline for identifying plant immune inducers and growth promoters from marine microbial metabolite libraries.
items.abstract: Background Plant immune inducers and growth-promoting biostimulants provide promising tools for sustainable crop management, but their development is limited by the shortage of bioactive natural products with agricultural relevance. Marine microorganisms from diverse habitats, including deep-sea environments, represent an underexplored source of structurally diverse secondary metabolites. This study aimed to establish a screening pipeline to identify marine microbial metabolites with plant immune-inducing and growth-promoting activities. Results Two marine microbial metabolite libraries were constructed, comprising 2986 crude extracts and 2747 purified compounds. Two parallel three-tier screening platforms were developed. Plant immune inducers were first screened using a reactive oxygen species burst assay and then evaluated in whole-plant Arabidopsis thaliana resistance assays and rice field trials. Growth-promoting candidates were screened using the auxin-responsive DR5::GUS reporter system, followed by seedling growth assays and rice yield-related trait evaluation. The screening cascade progressively enriched active candidates. Representative metabolites, including L299, CR-222-8, HZA-5, 3J00027, and TWA-1, showed immune-inducing or growth-promoting activities in laboratory assays, and selected candidates exhibited field-relevant effects on rice pest infestation or agronomic traits. However, the field infestation level of the striped stem borer Chilo suppressalis was extremely low during the experimental season, limiting the evaluation of efficacy against this pest. Conclusion This study establishes a practical pipeline linking molecular plant-response assays, whole-plant bioassays, and field validation for prioritizing marine microbial metabolites. The results support marine microbial secondary metabolites as a promising source of candidate plant immune inducers and biostimulants for sustainable pest management and crop production. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

items.title: Metabolism-based non-target-site resistance to nicosulfuron in Digitaria sanguinalis: transcriptomic and functional evidence implicates DsCYP78A9 and DsGSTU10.
items.abstract: Background Digitaria sanguinalis is a major annual grass weed in maize fields, and the evolution of resistance to the acetolactate synthase (ALS)-inhibiting herbicide nicosulfuron (Nsf) threatens its sustainable control. However, the contribution of metabolism-based non-target-site resistance to Nsf resistance in this species remains insufficiently understood. Results Whole-plant bioassays showed that the resistant biotype (DsR) exhibited markedly greater resistance to Nsf than the susceptible biotype (DsS). DsR also showed higher glutathione S-transferase (GST) activity, lower malondialdehyde accumulation and a more pronounced decrease in the relative parent-Nsf peak response between 1 and 3 days after treatment. No amino acid substitutions were detected at the examined ALS resistance-associated positions, and ALS expression and enzymatic sensitivity to Nsf did not differ significantly between DsR and DsS. By contrast, pretreatment with the cytochrome P450 (CYP450) inhibitor malathion or the GST inhibitor 4-chloro-7-nitrobenzofurazan (NBD-Cl) significantly increased the sensitivity of DsR to Nsf. Transcriptomic analyses revealed coordinated differences in CYP450-, GST-, UDP-glycosyltransferase (UGT)- and ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporter-related genes and in pathways associated with flavonoid, phenylpropanoid and carbohydrate metabolism. Among the candidates identified, DsCYP78A9 and DsGSTU10 showed strong transcriptional responses. Molecular docking predicted favourable interactions with Nsf, while heterologous expression of either gene enhanced yeast growth under exposure to Nsf, rimsulfuron and tembotrione. Conclusion These findings indicate that Nsf resistance in DsR is primarily associated with detoxification-based non-target-site mechanisms rather than detectable alterations in ALS. The inhibitor, transcriptomic and heterologous-expression evidence collectively implicates DsCYP78A9 and DsGSTU10 as candidate contributors to herbicide resistance and provides potential molecular targets for further mechanistic investigation and resistance management. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

items.title: Integrating fish biology, population genomics, and fishery policies for informed management of interjurisdictional multispecies fisheries.
items.abstract: Coastal fisheries are typically managed within bounds set by political jurisdictions of nations and their provinces. This approach often results in multiple states/provinces managing a single genetically distinct fish population autonomously and typically without coordination. In multispecies, decentralized, and data-poor fisheries, this can lead to inadequate assessments and fisheries overharvests. We developed an integrative risk indicator for interjurisdictional stocks (IRIIS) to assess the overexploitation risk to interjurisdictional populations. IRIIS incorporates species-specific vulnerability, distribution of genetically distinct populations with respect to jurisdictional boundaries, and differences in management practices across jurisdictions. As a case study, we used genetic tools and policy analysis to evaluate nine common target species spanning multiple jurisdictions along India's western coast. We showed that distinct populations of a species differed greatly in how they are managed by respective fisheries, and management disparities across jurisdictions can strongly influence the overexploitation risk for a population. IRIIS clearly identified these differences and helped determine specific fisheries policies that need reconciling across jurisdictions to reduce the risk of overexploitation. As a comprehensive management instrument, IRIIS is dynamic and sensitive to periodic revisions in fishery policy and could guide managers across jurisdictions in lowering the overexploitation risks to multispecies coastal fisheries.

items.title: Amino-functionalized Fe<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub>@SiO<sub>2</sub>-NH<sub>2</sub>@MIL-101(Fe)-NH<sub>2</sub> for magnetic solid-phase extraction of PFOA and PFOS from water and milk.
items.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, known as PFASs, are persistent organic pollutants. Perfluorooctanoic acid and perfluorooctane sulfonate, referred to as PFOA and PFOS, respectively, require selective sample preparation before trace-level LC-MS/MS analysis. Herein, an amino-functionalized magnetic MIL-101(Fe) composite, Fe 3 O 4 @SiO 2 -NH 2 @MIL-101(Fe)-NH 2 , was synthesized and applied as an MSPE sorbent for PFOA and PFOS in water and dairy matrices. The composite integrates magnetic Fe 3 O 4 @SiO 2 -NH 2 nanoparticles with an amino-functionalized MIL-101(Fe) porous framework, enabling rapid magnetic separation and multiple adsorption interactions. Adsorption equilibrium was reached within 10 min, and the adsorption mechanism was dominated by electrostatic attraction, hydrogen-bonding, and hydrophobic interactions. Under optimized conditions, the method exhibited satisfactory linearity within the ranges of 0.05-50 ng mL -1 and 0.5-50 ng mL -1 for PFOA and PFOS, respectively. The limits of detection were 0.25 ng L -1 for PFOA and 2.5 ng L -1 for PFOS in water, and 0.005 ng g -1 for PFOA and 0.020 ng g -1 for PFOS in dairy samples. Recoveries ranged from 73.86% to 118.30% with RSDs no more than 15%. The sorbent remained stable over five consecutive cycles and was successfully applied to spiked water, milk, and milk powder samples. This work provides a practical strategy for designing amino-functionalized magnetic MOF composites for rapid and sensitive enrichment of PFOA and PFOS in complex environmental and food matrices.

items.title: Navigating Identity Discordance Through Values-Based MentorSHIP: An Educational Workshop Anchored in a Tool From Clinical Psychology.
items.abstract: Introduction Since medical trainees and physicians identifying as female or as underrepresented in medicine often struggle to find identity-concordant mentors, structured training to support identity-discordant mentorship pairs is important for fostering diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) in medicine. This workshop for mentors and mentees aims to teach participants about identity concordance/discordance in mentorship and provide strategies for developing mentorship relationships through intentional discussion of values and self-reflection. Methods We developed an interactive, 75-minute workshop for medical students, residents, fellows, faculty, and graduate medical education staff consisting of didactic content; small-group exercises, including a values card sort activity; and large-group reflections. We used a postworkshop survey to evaluate participants' satisfaction with and main takeaways from the workshop. We analyzed Likert-scale questions with descriptive statistics and open-ended questions with content analysis. Results We presented the workshop at 3 local conferences in varying formats (in-person, hybrid in-person/virtual, and virtual). Fifty-four of 65 total participants completed the postworkshop survey (83% response rate). Most participants reported the workshop met its learning objectives (50/52, 96%) and they will apply the information they learned through participation in the workshop (49/52, 94%). Participants reported intended future behavior changes of value reflection and self-reflection, openness to identity-discordant mentorship pairs, thoughtfulness of mentorship type and navigation of unsuccessful mentorship relationships. Discussion This well-received workshop promoted participant reflection surrounding concordant and discordant mentorship matches, how mentorship pairings can promote DEI in medicine, and how to discuss values with mentors/mentees to promote self-reflection and self-improvement in mentorship.

items.title: Intensive communicative and linguistic intervention in Noonan syndrome: A case study.
items.abstract: Noonan syndrome (NS) is a genetic developmental disorder within the RASopathies and is frequently associated with language and communication impairments affecting multiple linguistic domains. Evidence regarding the effectiveness of intensive speech-language intervention in this population remains limited. This case study evaluated the effectiveness of an intensive, individualised, and multimodal communicative and linguistic intervention in a school-aged girl with NS. An 8-year-old girl with NS received an intensive speech-language intervention (20 hours/week for four weeks). The program targeted speech intelligibility, phonological skills, morphosyntax, lexical-semantic development, and pragmatic communication, using play-based strategies in clinical and natural contexts. Pre- and post-intervention assessments included standardised and criterion-referenced measures of language and communication. Post-intervention outcomes showed clinically meaningful improvements in communicative intentionality, pragmatic skills, receptive vocabulary, and speech intelligibility. Standardised language scores showed limited quantitative change, but functional communication and social participation improved substantially. Intensive and individualised intervention may promote significant gains in functional communication in children with Noonan syndrome.

items.title: Network Analysis of the Relationship Between Adolescents' Active Health Behaviors, Academic Stress, and Academic Burnout Across Different Latent Profiles.
items.abstract: Academic burnout in adolescence is associated with academic stress and active health behaviors. Prior research has often emphasized bivariate associations without considering heterogeneity in active health behavior profiles or profile-specific conditional associations among these constructs. We conducted a cross-sectional study of 933 adolescents in China. Participants completed the Adolescent Active Health Behavior Scale, the Middle School Student Academic Stress Scale, and the Adolescent Academic Burnout Scale. Latent profile analysis (LPA) identified active health behavior profiles, and network analysis estimated conditional associations and compared network characteristics across profiles. Bootstrap procedures were used to assess stability and accuracy. Three profiles were identified: the Moderate Active Health Behavior Group (55.30%), Low Active Health Behavior Group (15.01%), and High Active Health Behavior Group (29.69%). Academic Detachment showed the highest strength centrality in the estimated overall and subgroup networks, and academic burnout nodes showed higher bridge strength across communities. Low Achievement had the lowest expected influence, indicating lower net signed connectivity with other nodes. The node with the highest expected influence varied across networks (overall network: Health Responsibility; Moderate group: Social Pressure; Low group: Physical and Mental Exhaustion; High group: Parental Pressure). The High group had the densest estimated network and the largest average edge weight, whereas the Low group had the sparsest network. Network structure also differed by gender. The three active health behavior profiles differed in their estimated network characteristics. Academic Detachment showed the highest strength centrality, whereas Low Achievement showed the lowest expected influence and lower net signed connectivity with other nodes. These exploratory cross-sectional findings describe conditional association patterns and may inform hypotheses for future longitudinal and intervention studies; they do not identify causal mechanisms or established intervention targets.

items.title: Understanding negative experiences and harm in eating disorder treatment: a systematic review and meta-synthesis.
items.abstract: Whilst research has documented experiences of harm and negative experiences in mental health treatment more broadly, to date no review has focused on eating disorders. The aim of this systematic review was to synthesise the qualitative literature documenting service user experiences. Databases were systematically searched according to PRISMA guidelines. Fifteen studies were identified and analysed using thematic synthesis. Four themes were identified: power and control, constructions of identity, the causality of negative experiences, and the nature of harm. Our findings highlight the complexities of conceptualising negative experience and harm in eating disorder treatment, particularly in the context of managing significant physical health risks. Recommendations for further research and considerations for clinical practice are outlined.

items.title: Early-Life Overfeeding Drives Lasting Species-Level Shifts of the Gut Microbiome and Exacerbates Allergic Asthma in Mice.
items.abstract: Early-life overweight is associated with increased asthma risk in children, but the mechanisms linking metabolic status, the gut microbiome and airway disease remain poorly explored. To address this, we used a litter-size reduction model in mice to examine how early-life overfeeding and overweight shape gut microbial development and later allergic asthma severity. Overfed offspring displayed increased body weight, adiposity and altered body proportions from early postnatal life onward, with more pronounced effects in females. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing identified a specific, lasting dysbiosis in the overweight female mice, characterized by reduced alpha diversity and species-level shifts in Lactobacillus, Muribaculum and Bacteroides. Crucially, upon allergic sensitization in adulthood, these animals displayed an exacerbated disease state consistent with an 'obese-asthma' phenotype, marked by heightened airway inflammation, intense eosinophilic and neutrophilic infiltration, higher Type 2 cytokine levels (i.e., IL-4, IL-5) and altered bronchoalveolar immune profiles. These findings suggest that early-life nutritional imbalance establishes an altered immunometabolic trajectory via the gut-lung axis, providing a mechanistic basis for the increased severity observed in obesity-associated asthma.

items.title: High Dispositional Mindfulness Is Associated With Lower Insomnia in College Students: A Retrospective Analysis.
items.abstract: Mindfulness-based interventions have been shown to be effective for lowering insomnia symptoms in college students; however, it is not yet clear whether higher dispositional mindfulness is associated with lower insomnia symptoms. This information could help guide individual risk assessment for developing insomnia and future insomnia interventions. Thus, this secondary analysis was conducted to examine whether high dispositional mindfulness (corresponding to scores ≥ 3.71 on the MAAS) and low dispositional mindfulness (corresponding to scores < 3.71) are associated with severity of insomnia symptoms. Subjects (n = 2152) were selected from a sample of college students (n = 3160; 71.7% women; X¯ age = 22 ± 3.72 years). Subjects completed questionnaires assessing dispositional mindfulness, depression, anxiety, chronotype and insomnia symptoms. Linear regression models examined the association between dispositional mindfulness and insomnia symptoms and were used for moderation analyses to determine whether depression, anxiety, or chronotype moderated this relationship. High dispositional mindfulness was significantly associated with lower insomnia symptoms (Est = -4.166, SE = 0.225, p < 0.001). Neither depression, anxiety, nor chronotype moderated this relationship such that higher levels of any such variable were not associated with greater insomnia symptoms regardless of dispositional mindfulness. There was significantly lower anxiety and depression scores for those with high dispositional mindfulness (p < 0.05). These results suggest that those with high dispositional mindfulness may be less susceptible to insomnia. Findings support the plausibility of mindfulness training to ameliorate insomnia risk in young adults.

items.title: Leveraging administrative health data to advance eating disorders research and care.
items.abstract: Eating disorders (ED) carry substantial morbidity, mortality, and economic burden, yet remain underprioritised relative to their prevalence. Administrative health data from National Health Service (NHS) secondary mental health services hold significant untapped potential for advancing ED research and care provision. However, a range of structural and methodological barriers create siloed systems which limit the quality and representativeness of these cohorts. These barriers include fragmented care pathways, inconsistent diagnostic coding, and clinically rich information held within unstructured free-text notes. This paper argues that these barriers are best addressed with a coordinated and comprehensive strategy aimed at improving the quality and utility of administrative health data in the context of ED. This strategy should include integrating data in secure data environments, natural language processing, and national harmonisation of data standards to enable detailed and scalable investigation. The resulting evidence would be more inclusive and clinically-representative, enabling evaluation of real-world treatments and improving outcomes for people living with eating disorders.

items.title: Freeze-thaw aging enhances microplastic phytotoxicity in rice via root metabolism and DNA methylation.
items.abstract: Freeze-thaw cycling (FTC) accelerates microplastic (MP) aging in cold-region soils, yet the mechanisms underlying their amplified phytotoxicity remain elusive. This study integrated physicochemical characterization, metabolomics, and DNA methylation sequencing to evaluate the root toxicity of pristine and FTC-aged polystyrene, polyvinyl chloride (PVC), and polyethylene in rice (Oryza sativa). FTC aging induced surface oxidation and structural fragmentation, increasing hydrodynamic diameters by 8.8-26.7% and elevating negative surface charge by 5.17-5.36 mV. The aged PVC elicited the most severe phytotoxicity, disrupting root membrane integrity and suppressing superoxide dismutase activity by up to 54%. Metabolomic profiling revealed pronounced malate depletion coupled with lactate accumulation, indicating alterations in central carbon metabolism consistent with a potential shift toward glycolysis-associated metabolism, alongside significant perturbations in branched-chain amino acid and glycerophospholipid metabolism. Whole-genome bisulfite sequencing demonstrated that DNA methylation reprogramming was dominated by the CHH context, accounting for > 96% of all differentially methylated regions. Correlation network analysis revealed that aged PVC induced targeted CHH promoter hypermethylation in key redox hubs (e.g., NTRC, Trx M3), effectively decoupling antioxidant defense signaling from core energy metabolism. The work pinpoints that FTC-aged MP induced CHH methylation could connect to root metabolic reprogramming, establishing a basis for assessing risks of MPs in cold-climate agriculture.

items.title: Integrating plasma biochemistry and stable isotope analysis as a monitoring framework for loggerhead sea turtles (Caretta caretta) in the eastern Mediterranean: seasonal physiological variation and ecological context.
items.abstract: Plasma biochemical analysis is a core tool for assessing the health of free-ranging sea turtles. Its interpretation, however, depends on population-specific reference intervals (RIs), which vary with physiological state, season, sex and habitat. Such intervals remain scarce for the eastern Mediterranean, despite the region supporting some of the basin's most important loggerhead ( Caretta caretta ) rookeries; the only prior dataset for the Turkish coastline ( n = 22) was too small for formal estimation. Using 147 loggerhead turtles from Türkiye, we (i) established the first population-level RIs for 24 plasma biochemical parameters following Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute guidelines; (ii) quantified variation between nesting females from two rookeries and overwintering (OW) individuals; (iii) examined sex- and maturity-related variation within the OW population; and (iv) integrated stable carbon (δ 13 C) and nitrogen (δ 15 N) isotope values, measured in the same blood samples, to provide ecological context. Plasma biochemistry differed strongly with physiological state: OW individuals had markedly higher urea (≈108 vs ≈28-32 mg/dl), consistent with continued protein intake during OW, whereas nesting females showed elevated lipids, calcium, phosphorus and total protein, consistent with vitellogenesis. Erythrocyte δ 13 C correlated with urea and lipid fractions after false-discovery-rate correction, whereas δ 15 N correlations did not survive correction. These isotope-biochemistry associations were driven primarily by differences between physiological-state groups rather than by individual-level relationships, indicating that habitat- and foraging-state structure is reflected in, and can help contextualize, plasma biochemical variation. Together, the RIs and paired isotope data provide a practical monitoring framework for an underrepresented loggerhead population.

items.title: Surface Cues Over Structure: Probing LLM Behavior on Brain Connectivity Graphs
items.abstract: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) provides a noninvasive view of functional interactions across the brain, which can be represented as connectivity graphs for neurological disease analysis. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being paired with such representations, yet it remains unclear whether they genuinely reason over the underlying connectivity or simply respond to surface-level cues that may trigger learned priors. We probe this question through a controlled study of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) diagnosis from resting-state functional connectivity, isolating one factor at a time to determine what drives an LLM's predictions on brain connectivity graphs. Across six models, from small open-weight LLMs to a proprietary one, the same pattern holds: the results provide little evidence that predictions are consistently grounded in subject-specific connectivity. Brain region names, numeric formatting, and prompt framing shift what a model predicts without improving how well it separates ADHD subjects from Controls; perturbing the graph changes predictions no more for clinically meaningful regions than for random ones; and the models' own justifications contradict the values they cite, inconsistently interpreting the connectivity evidence provided to them. Across every probe, predictions follow the model's built-in class bias and the surface form of the prompt rather than the subject's connectivity, calling into question a premise underlying current LLM brain integration work. Our code is available at https://github.com/Roy025/ADHD-code.

items.title: Self-Supervised Learning with Recursive Quadrature Filters for Neural Time Series
items.abstract: We develop self-supervised methods for training Recursive Quadrature Filter (RQF) encoders on unlabeled time series. RQFs are biologically motivated, complex-valued temporal filters that form a special class of diagonal state-space models (SSMs). Each RQF acts as a band-pass filter whose selectivity is determined by two learnable parameters: its tuning frequency and bandwidth. We separately introduce a self-supervised learning objective based on prediction error; the encoder is trained so that its current state predicts its own future activity. In the windowed mode, the summary of the current window predicts the summary of a later window; in the dense mode, the state at the current timestep predicts future log-power. Each RQF encoder is pretrained on a dataset and then a readout (e.g., a task-specific classifier) is trained on the output of the RQF encoder, with the encoder either frozen or fully fine-tuned. For multichannel EEG and intracranial recordings, a shared encoder processes each channel separately, and a spatial readout combines the channel representations using electrode locations. Across four neural benchmarks using scalp or intracranial EEG, the pretrained RQF system performs close to the state of the art while using a small fraction of the parameters of the competing models. For example, a 110k-parameter RQF system achieves 0.9247 +/- 0.0022 test AUROC on 100-s TUAB segments, above SAMBA (0.9054) at the same context with 9 times as many parameters, and 0.9040 +/- 0.0019 on 10-s segments, comparable to EEG foundation models with 3.2M-369M parameters.

items.title: The Effect of Dust Grain Growth and Stellar Metallicity on Gas Giant Planet Formation by Disk Instability
items.abstract: The formation of gas giant planets by the gas disk gravitational instability (GDGI) mechanism depends sensitively on the thermodynamics of the protoplanetary disk gas: disk gas must be able to cool on orbital timescales for dense clumps to become gravitationally unstable and contract to form protoplanets. Since disk cooling is regulated by the opacity of the dust grains embedded in the gas, the properties of these dust grains are critical for the GDGI mechanism. Grain growth to larger sizes than assumed in traditional opacity models for solar metallicity, as well as protostars with sub-solar metallicity, should have lower opacity disks that are more conducive to planet formation by GDGI. Here we use a three dimensional radiative hydrodynamics and gravitation code to compute the evolution of the GDGI in $0.091 M_\odot$ disks with varied initial minimum values (1.3 to 2.7) of the Toomre criterion orbiting solar-mass protostars. Three sets of eight models are computed: one with the standard opacity, and two more with the opacity reduced by arbitrary factors of 10 or 100. As expected, the reduced opacity models result in enhanced disk fragmentation by the GDGI and the production of more self-gravitating clumps than the standard opacity models. Nevertheless, all three opacities form similar self-gravitating clumps at this early phase of clump evolution, with masses of 0.2 to 0.7 $M_{Jup}$ and semimajor axes between 6 and 13 au. Significant dust grain growth should enhance the ability of the GDGI to form protoplanets around super-solar metallicity protostars.

items.title: Searching for substellar companion candidates with Gaia IV. New planetary-mass companions found in debris disks
items.abstract: When spatially resolved, debris disks often exhibit structures (gaps, rings, and spirals) that may indicate the presence of unseen planetary-mass companions. However, such planets have not been detected in most cases. Gaia opens a new mass-separation parameter space for detecting unseen planets. A tool named GaiaPMEX has been developed to detect and characterize companions to stars. It is based on two binarity indicators derived from DR3: the Gaia astrometric signature and, when the sources were also observed by Hipparcos, the Gaia-Hipparcos proper motion anomaly. We used GaiaPMEX on 94 stars hosting resolved debris disks to search for companions. When companions were identified, we combined GaiaPMEX results with high-contrast imaging and radial velocity data to further constrain their mass and orbital properties. We found stellar or substellar companions around five targets (HD 54341, HD 146897, HD 206893, HD 107146, and HD 106906) and indications (2 sigma) for companions around three additional targets (BD+45 598, TWA 7, and HD 120326). The companion to the 150 Myr star HD 107146, which harbors a ring-like dust disk, is found to be a 2-6 Jupiter-mass planet orbiting between 2-10 au. A massive 3-20 Jupiter-mass companion is found 3-10 au from the close binary HD 106906, which already hosts a remote planet orbiting at more than 700 au, and an edge-on disk. The tentative companions to TWA 7 and HD 120326 are planetary-mass companions at 1-3 au. Both stars host a multiple-ring system. We finally provide meaningful upper limits on the possible presence of companions in the range of 0-100 au around a few emblematic stars (49 Cet, AU Mic, beta Pic, and epsilon Eri) and stars hosting well-defined ring-like structures.

items.title: PLATON 7: An ultra-fast exoplanet atmospheric retrieval code
items.abstract: PLATON is an open source Python package for atmospheric retrieval, first released in 2018. We introduce PLATON 7, a complete rewrite of PLATON using Claude Fable 5. The biggest changes are that PLATON now uses JAX for all intensive calculations, and these calculations are now performed in single precision instead of double precision. These two changes speed up the code by a factor of ~60 with negligible decrease in accuracy, allowing it to compute a 0.8--5.3 um transmission spectrum at R=20k in 0.35 ms on a RTX 5090. We also introduce several new features, including support for two-limb retrievals, patchy clouds, and more opacities (particularly OCS and CS2). PLATON is available on GitHub at https://github.com/ideasrule/platon.

items.title: Stellar activity demotes GJ 9404 b to a planetary candidate
items.abstract: GJ 9404 is a nearby M dwarf ($d=23.8\,\text{pc}$), around which a $13.4586^{+0.0044}_{-0.0067}\,\text{d}$ planet has been claimed in a recent study using 54 publicly available HARPS-N radial velocities (RVs). We re-analyse the spectroscopy associated with this study, and carry out a joint modelling of: (i) stellar rotation in RV, FWHM, and Mount Wilson S-index through Gaussian processes; (ii) long-term trends in all physical quantities; (iii) planetary signals in RV. Current evidence supports the existence of planets in the period range $2-100\,\text{d}$ by at most $Δ\ln Z=-0.4$ for any considered stellar-activity model, which is insufficient for a widely accepted planet detection. Additional spectroscopy is necessary to accurately quantify the stellar activity of GJ 9404 and determine whether any RV signals warrant further attention.
