items.title: When Does Continual Pre-Training Help? A Controlled Study of Dialectal Adaptation for Québec French
items.abstract: Continual pre-training (CPT) is widely used to adapt pretrained language models to dialectal and non-standard language varieties, yet it remains unclear when this additional training is necessary, what drives its benefits, and whether aggregate evaluation scores adequately capture its effects. In this paper, we present a controlled study of CPT for Québec French language understanding across nine LLMs spanning different families and scales. Using a budget-matched protocol of 30M tokens per experiment, our results show that the benefit of CPT depends strongly on the starting model's existing competence in the target variety. When CPT is beneficial, the improvements are driven more by corpus composition than by data volume, with literary text accounting for most of the gain. Paired Québec and standard French evaluations further show that CPT primarily improves expression comprehension rather than grammatical competence, and that corpus register determines which regional expressions are acquired. These gains also involve capability-specific trade-offs, including declines in reading comprehension that aggregate scores can conceal. Overall, these findings show that CPT for dialectal adaptation should not be treated as a uniformly beneficial default. Instead, adaptation strategies should begin with a careful assessment of the base model's existing competence, accompanied by source-level data analysis and task-level evaluation.

items.title: Depth Before Breadth: Reverse-to-Forward Curriculum with Advantage Decomposition for LLM Agent
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a common approach for training large language model (LLM) agents on long-horizon tasks. However, learning from sparse terminal rewards makes credit assignment and exploration difficult. We approach these challenges through a policy-induced capability region, the set of states from which the current policy can reliably complete a task. Near its boundary, an agent may need only a few actions to reach a more solvable state, even when the goal remains distant. This reduces long-horizon learning to two coupled subproblems of reaching that state and completing the task from there. We address them with paired advantages and a progressive reverse-to-forward curriculum. The advantages provide separate signals for reaching more solvable states and completing the task from them, while the curriculum expands the capability region backward along successful reference trajectories and then into off-reference states through on-policy exploration. On ALFWorld and WebShop, our method outperforms competitive agentic RL methods at both model scales, achieving success rates of 90.1%/96.1% and 80.2%/82.6% with Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B-Instruct, respectively.

items.title: Movie2Game-Bench: Holistic Evaluation of Film-to-Game Adaptation Beyond Playability
items.abstract: Adapting a film into a game requires selecting source elements and translating them into player actions, rules, and feedback. We introduce Movie2Game-Bench (M2G-bench), a benchmark for evaluating film-to-game adaptation beyond playability. M2G-bench combines general evaluation, movie-specific evaluation, and playtesting by three GUI model players. The protocol connects source content to gameplay steps and implementation evidence, capturing both content preservation and interactive realization. The benchmark comprises 22 films and 658 source-specific reference items. Evaluating 14 models on the same films with their selected primary harnesses reveals complementary strengths in game quality, adaptation, and player experience. A shared weakness concerns playable sequences: this category has the lowest content-presence mean in all 14 models, averaging 37.9 out of 100 compared with 54.8 for iconic elements. Among judgments of retained emotionaldevelopment content, narrative choices account for 60.0% and scenario operation for 7.2%. These findings identify two linked priorities for film-to-game adaptation: preserving source situations that can support gameplay and connecting retained content to player actions and consequences.

items.title: Piccolo: Co-Evolving Decision Models and Data through Recursive Self-Improvement
items.abstract: We present Piccolo, a family of multimodal decision models (0.8B to 27B) that coevolves model capabilities and training data via Agentic Data Engineering and recursive self-improvement (RSI). The models predict probabilities over candidate answers for general-purpose text and visual judgments, agent harnesses, data workflows, and interactive games. Piccolo-27B tops the Decision Index Vision Full leaderboard with a score of 75.59, while Piccolo-9B and Piccolo-4B achieve 68.35 and 67.46, respectively. All three rank first on the Private benchmark in their respective model-size categories. Research agents analyze model behavior, construct training data, conduct experiments, and use the results to refine subsequent proposals. Semantic slices and a shared research memory connect these actions across the model family's development. With training recipes comprising hundreds of thousands of examples, data selection and feedback-driven refinement are central to the self-improvement process. Our large-scale RSI exploration yields three counter-intuitive insights for decision-model development: (1) Backbone-recipe co-adaptation outweighs raw model recency: earlier backbones can surpass newer generations on visual tasks under identical recipes; (2) Targeted data curation enables 4B-9B models to rival 27B baselines on specialized workflows; and (3) Continuous loss reduction can decouple from and even degrade discrete decision accuracy. Together with the released weights and tools from the Data-Juicer and AgentScope ecosystems, Piccolo provides an actionable blueprint for building frontier decision models and scaling data-driven RSI.

items.title: Self-Rewarded Reinforcement Learning for Better-Structured Medical Explanations in Small Language Models
items.abstract: Small language models (SLMs) can run on commodity hardware and support privacy-preserving, on-premises clinical deployment, but their medical explanations are often short and poorly structured compared with large language models. Recent supervised approaches such as Meerkat transfer chain-of-thought reasoning into 7B-8B backbones, yet their training objective does not directly target the style or organization of the generated rationales. Building on the instruction-tuned Mistral-7B backbone, we investigate whether a lightweight reinforcement learning (RL) step can improve explanation structure without human preference labels.We apply Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with LoRA adaptation to 2,000 Meerkat-derived medical prompts, guided by a simple self-supervised reward that favors longer, lexically diverse, and well-punctuated responses while penalizing very short ones. Training for about 170 PPO steps on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU yields a stable increase in the average reward. Quantitative and qualitative comparisons show that the RL-tuned model produces longer, more organized, multi-point explanations while preserving the underlying medical content.We discuss the promise and the limitations of self-rewarded RL for shaping the style of medical explanations.

items.title: Choosing the Right Representations: Task-Aware Fusion for Multimodal Materials Language Models
items.abstract: Multimodal language models for materials science rely on effective mechanisms for incorporating three-dimensional structural representations. MatterChat addresses this challenge using a large bridge module between a pretrained structural encoder and the LLM, together with a separate contrastive alignment stage. We instead ask whether this bridge can adaptively select and combine representations from multiple structural encoders according to the target property. We find that supervised and generative material encoders provide complementary information for property prediction. We found that, for Zatom-1, this information is not concentrated in the final layer. Instead, the most informative representations occur at different depths depending on the target property. This motivates Task-Conditioned Attention Fusion (TCAF), a lightweight attention-based bridge that uses task-conditioned latent queries to combine CHGNet features with intermediate Zatom-1 representations. The bridge is trained directly on downstream prediction tasks, allowing representation selection and material-language alignment to be learned jointly without separate contrastive pretraining. Across classification and regression tasks, TCAF outperforms MatterChat, with up to 47.8% lower RMSE, while using substantially fewer trainable parameters and halving the overall training time. Further experiments incorporating UMA-S demonstrate TCAF's flexibility across encoder combinations, with the three-encoder configuration achieving the highest macro-average classification accuracy of 89.61%.

items.title: Hypnos: A Dual-Phase End-to-End Platform for Scalable Continual Learning at the Edge
items.abstract: Continual learning (CL) enables neural networks to adapt to non-stationary data streams by mitigating catastrophic forgetting, offering a path to robust, private, and adaptable edge devices. Yet, porting CL to real-world edge devices remains challenging for two reasons: (i) online operation, where sensor data arrives one sample at a time and the device must adapt on-the-fly, and (ii) the low footprint of edge devices, which makes traditional error backpropagation training prohibitive. Inspired by the brain's wake and sleep cycles, the former for rapid adaptation with minimal resources and the latter for long-term consolidation, we introduce Hypnos, an open-source dual-phase platform for efficient CL at the edge. In the wake phase (e.g., daily operation), Hypnos relies on a low-footprint system-on-chip with a RISC-V microcontroller unit (MCU) targeting efficient inference and supporting lightweight gradient-free prototype updates. In the sleep phase (e.g., night-time charging), where wall-plug energy and larger memory budgets are available, a smart charger performs rehearsal-based gradient updates for consolidation. Deployed on a ZCU104 field-programmable gate array (FPGA) and synthesized in a 28-nm process, Hypnos is benchmarked on the CORe50 NICv2-391 protocol. It sets a new state-of-the-art accuracy of 78.6%-81.6% for edge CL systems, with an on-device latency of 7.79s-10.54s per sample depending on activation precision, and requires $3.8\times$ fewer learning steps and $22\times$ less learning compute than quantized latent replay at higher accuracy and comparable latency.

items.title: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview Technical Report
items.abstract: We introduce Clover-35B-A3B-Preview (Clover), a mixture-of-experts diffusion language model with 35 billion total parameters and 3 billion activated parameters, supporting thinking-mode generation. Clover adapts Gated Delta Networks to block diffusion by combining recurrent memory of previously generated context with bidirectional softmax attention inside the current block. Historical memory readout competes with current-block tokens in a shared softmax, with learnable block-size calibration and a separate, zero-initialized right-context convolution branch. Clover leads the seven evaluated agent metrics, including 73.6 on SWE-bench Verified and 51.7 on Terminal-Bench 2.1. On internal agent workloads, it reaches a reported generation speed of 680 tokens/s using one NVIDIA GB300 GPU at BF16 precision and batch size one. We organize the evaluation around model quality, drafting and verification costs, and deployment under constrained memory. We also describe a decision-model variant that generates answers to related questions in one denoising pass. On an internal set of 500 groups, joint prediction raises question accuracy from 90.37% to 93.88% and all-correct group accuracy from 65.4% to 77.0%.

items.title: H3Remover: Reinforcing Video Object Removal without Paired Data
items.abstract: Pretrained video editors possess rich removal and completion priors, yet may retain targets or alter unrelated content. We present H3Remover, which reinforces MiniMax-H3 Base Ref2VA for video object removal without paired object-free training targets. To discourage superficial edits such as recoloring, a target-removal reward favors calibrated depth changes consistent with revealing farther content. To limit unintended scene changes, a background-geometry reward encourages preservation of relative depth ordering. To preserve background appearance without retaining unwanted shadows or reflections, an appearance reward constrains RGB changes in source-derived protected regions while exempting targets and estimated effects. Frozen HPSv3 complements these constraints with perceptual-quality feedback for synthesized content. Evaluation regions remain fixed across candidates, and DiffusionART optimizes LoRA adapters with the backbone frozen. Experiments show substantial reconstruction gains over original H3, with qualitative comparisons demonstrating more effective object removal and better preservation of surrounding scene content.

items.title: GateWatch: Low-Overhead LLM Monitoring with Boolean Circuits
items.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) and LLM-based agents are increasingly deployed, monitoring their behavior becomes important for detecting unsafe or unintended actions. Activation probes offer an efficient approach, but existing methods face trade-offs between accuracy, interpretability, and computational overhead. Probes on raw activations lack interpretable inputs, whereas sparse autoencoder (SAE) probes use interpretable features but often rely on additive classifiers and large SAE encoders, limiting interpretability and increasing memory overhead. We introduce GateWatch, a compact, interpretable classifier that expresses its entire decision rule as an explicit Boolean logic over a small number of binarized SAE features. We explore three approaches to constructing these circuits under a specified gate budget. For efficient deployment, GateWatchServe computes only selected SAE features, enables streaming of their binary values across layers during inference, and evaluates multiple GateWatch classifiers in parallel using compact lookup tables. Across 24 tasks on Gemma-2-9B, GateWatch achieves 80.49% mean test accuracy using only 3.8 SAE features and 3.5 logic gates per probe on average, just 1.17 percentage points below full 16K-feature SAE probes, while matching or outperforming them on 10 tasks and reducing probe memory by 99.98%. Inside vLLM, 1,000 concurrent multi-layer, multi-token GateWatch classifiers retain 97-98% of baseline throughput and 99.8% of KV-cache capacity.

items.title: Negotiating Control and Accountability among Stakeholders in High-Risk AI Use Cases: Development and Evaluation of the Method ALIGN
items.abstract: Characteristics of Artificial Intelligence (AI) severely restrict human control. This creates new challenges for socio-technical systems design especially in safety-critical domains, where control over risks is essential along with the accountability for any harm caused. Drawing from human factors and AI governance literature, expert interviews and participant observation in a complex high-risk AI use case from the railways, we developed ALIGN, a scenario-based method that supports the governance of and stakeholder involvement in AI development and implementation in three ways: raising awareness for potential accountability-control misalignments in socio-technical systems and their negative consequences, offering a structured approach to assessing the alignment between accountability and control for stakeholders in a given use case, and supporting effective design decisions to mitigate AI risks. We describe the iterative development and evaluation of ALIGN and discuss how this method promotes AI governance by highlighting the relevance of control-accountability alignment throughout the AI life cycle.

items.title: Chain-of-Thought Hidden States Reveal Task-Solving Directions for Direct Answers
items.abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting improves the performance of Large Language Models by eliciting intermediate reasoning steps. However, CoT is far from perfect: on some tasks, models perform worse than with direct-answer prompting, and on others they generate a few hundred tokens to reach the correct answer. We start by labelling each CoT hidden state as recovering if patching it into the direct prompt yields the correct answer, and failed otherwise. A linear probe shows that the model encodes these two classes differently. We then show that the representation space of the direct prompt holds a direction for each question that leads the model, in a short generation, to the correct answer more often than CoT does. Specifically, we rotate the direct prompt's last hidden state once, before generation, towards a direction built for each question from its own recovering and failed states. Across 25 tasks, these directions raise the direct prompt's mean accuracy from $46\%$ to $85\%$ on LLaMA 3.1 8B (CoT: $69\%$) and from $52\%$ to $86\%$ on Qwen 2.5 7B (CoT: $77\%$), with a tenth of CoT's tokens. CoT is thus not the shortest route to this accuracy, and these directions can be used in future work to train models to align their states with them.

items.title: Think Offline, Act in Real Time: Self-Improving Visual Game Agents through Code
items.abstract: Pre-trained models can read screens and reason about games, yet on an unfamiliar game, an agent still has to learn to play. We ask how an agent can self-improve on such a game from a few of its own attempts, in real-time visual games where the agent sees only the screen and the game keeps running while the agent thinks. We study two kinds of policy that can carry this improvement. In model as policy, a model selects actions during play; we adapt real-time chunking so that committed actions keep executing while the model reasons, and train a 2B controller for this interface. In code as policy, a model writes, tests, and revises a program between attempts, and the program acts during play. Across 170 GameWorld tasks, with at most eight one-minute executions per run, code as policy reaches 47.80% mean progress, against 30.90% for our trained controller, and leads in all five game categories. Improving the controller's weights on a single game, by contrast, yields only modest gains. These results favor letting a model think offline and storing what it learns in a program that acts in real time. Project repository: https://github.com/TabibitoQZP/SIGame

items.title: BaseRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of a Base Vision-Language Model via Training-Free Harness Internalization
items.abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) is moving from the harness of prompts and tools around a base model toward the model itself. However, existing RSI still faces key challenges, including harness-bound gains that stay outside the base model, black-box supervision that reads only the model's outputs, and imprecise edits whose site and strength are fixed in advance. To address these challenges, we propose BaseRSI, a new paradigm of Recursive Harness Internalization: the base model improves its harness, then writes what the harness adds into its own weights through training-free edits, round after round on its own responses. To support this paradigm, we introduce ReGap, a mechanism that supervises every transformer block with the high-dimensional activation difference that the harness makes at that block alone, and updates the block's weights along this signal in a low-dimensional subspace. Building on this mechanism, we further propose ReKey, an algorithm that writes this signal by regression into a few key-value neurons of every block, and measures the site and strength of each edit on the model's own responses. Moreover, the base model fills every role of this recursion with forward passes alone, and its edits, written at different sites, compose in one checkpoint without refitting. Experimental results on ten visual reasoning benchmarks show that BaseRSI consistently improves a base vision-language model both in distribution and on held-out benchmarks. Our code is available at https://github.com/beita6969/BaseRSI.

items.title: AGAMOTTO: An AI-Enabled Framework for Time-Critical Tactical Course-of-Action Evaluation and Generation
items.abstract: Current command and control (C2) platforms lack integrated simulation capabilities that would allow commanders to dynamically explore courses of action (COAs) during live operations. This paper presents ongoing research and contributions to the development of AGAMOTTO (Advanced Guidance and Analytics for Military Operations, Tactical Threats, and Outcomes) as part of the overarching NGC2 program, which advances the Army's efforts to modernize C2 systems, such as the Tactical Assault Kit (TAK). The paper outlines the current design, preliminary findings, and the remaining research tasks, with an emphasis on how the completed work will support tactical decision-making in future time-constrained environments. While the full system is still under development, initial development and results demonstrate the feasibility of AGAMOTTO. Early experiments highlight both the potential benefits and practical constraints of deploying AI-enabled tools in operational settings, and introduce lessons learned and a viable training strategy to make AI-generated COAs feasible in tactical scenarios.

items.title: NaviGATE: Noise-Aware Dual-View Generation for Multimodal Knowledge Graph Reasoning
items.abstract: Multimodal knowledge graph reasoning (MKGR) aims to infer missing facts by jointly exploiting relational structures, textual descriptions, and visual evidence. Existing embedding-based methods effectively capture graph topology, but their fixed multimodal representations are less effective for query-specific fine-grained semantic reasoning, while generation-based methods are vulnerable to noisy retrieval and may produce invalid entities. To address these challenges, we propose NaviGATE, a noise-aware generative framework for MKGR. NaviGATE first aligns graph-derived structural representations with textual semantics, then performs structure-aware internal knowledge activation by fine-tuning the multimodal language model with multimodal entity summaries and injected structural tokens. In the noise-aware dual-view instruction tuning stage, NaviGATE jointly optimizes retrieval-free and retrieval-aware views: reliable retrieved candidates are reinforced through contrastive logit sharpening, while misleading candidates are suppressed through parametric consistency distillation. In inference, structure-constrained decoding restricts generation to valid entities in the target knowledge graph. Experiments on standard benchmarks show that NaviGATE consistently outperforms strong unimodal, multimodal, and generation-based baselines, and remains robust under noisy retrieval scenarios.

items.title: Old Matches, New Frames: Schedule-Gated Stereo Memory from Human Vision to Machine Matching
items.abstract: Human vision and video stereo networks both reuse disparity evidence across time, yet a refresh of the input can invalidate a match formed milliseconds earlier. What tells a system whether an old match still counts? We answer this from limited human data in three steps. First, nine temporal mechanisms share a frozen binocular-energy front end and an equal-capacity readout, so held-out behavior isolates the temporal selection rule: on 240 conditions from 10 observers, down-weighting aged evidence that has lost binocular support lowers subject RMSE from 12.6% to 10.3% and reproduces a period-dependent reversed-depth illusion, across all 59 readings of the unpublished protocol and 8 front-end perturbations. Second, four propositions establish what such data can identify: gating is identified at the level of the refresh schedule, and candidate binding is invisible to standard stimuli but exposed by a single-eye geometry flip that separates the readouts by up to 7.1%. Third, the identified rule becomes a two-field stereo memory that separates sample validity from hypothesis support. It removes a 50 ms recovery lag after geometry flips, and its regime analysis explains why plain integration stays preferable on MPI-Sintel, where 71.1% of pixels change appearance but not disparity.

items.title: Inferring Neural Activity Changes under Recording Uncertainty with Transformers and Variational Inference
items.abstract: A difference in recorded firing rate across days may reflect a change in neuronal activity, missed spikes or recording a different neuron. We present a statistical approach that combines neuron tracking with Bayesian estimates of stationary mean recorded firing rates. Bounds under assumed differences in spike detection connect recorded rates to biological rate changes. We assess recording loss and uncertainty in rate changes in simulations, and count-model fit in recordings. We also compare two transformer estimators with Gaussian and flow variational inference under a shared temporal negative-binomial model. Flow variational inference agrees most closely with reference posteriors, while predictive performance varies across mice. Rate-change intervals contain true simulated changes less often than intended. In UnitMatch recordings from five mice, some inferred changes remain supported when spike detection is allowed to differ between days; others depend on equal detection. These interpretations require a correct neuron match. The approach identifies which inferred rate changes remain supported under specified recording assumptions and where uncertainty limits interpretation.

items.title: A structure-based model of the bacterial chemosensory array reveals how the scaffolding protein CheW tunes sensory responses
items.abstract: We introduce a structure-based Ising model of the bacterial chemosensory array to investigate how the scaffolding protein CheW tunes signaling responses. The model couples the activity states of core signaling units and of CheW subunits within hexameric rings on a lattice with the structure observed in cryoEM experiments. Recent experiments show that increasing CheW participation in hexameric rings raises response cooperativity in non-adapting cells and sensitivity in adaptation-proficient cells. Our lattice model quantitatively reproduces both effects, while mean-field theory shows that CheW increases the effective coupling between core units, sharpening the response in both cell types. The statistics of CheW placement (complete hexameric rings versus random distribution) substantially alter how responses vary with CheW abundance. Moreover, different coupling strengths can yield the same static response yet markedly different activity fluctuations and dynamics. CheW abundance further controls a crossover from relaxational to oscillatory fluctuations, whose location depends on the spatial distribution of CheW. These dynamical signatures, including oscillations predicted near native CheW levels, are testable by single-cell dynamics measurements. Combined with CheW titration and our modeling results, these measurements can probe the array's assembly dynamics and allosteric couplings. Beyond the chemosensory array, our approach can generalize to other large protein complexes, providing a framework to study the functional role of scaffolding proteins and allosteric interfaces in signal processing.

items.title: A Dual-SOM Learner Model of Instructional Efficiency within Cognitive Load Theory
items.abstract: This paper presents a novel methodological framework, integrating a dual self-organising map (SOM) neural network architecture with Cognitive Load Theory (CLT), for assessing instructional efficiency within learning environments. By representing curriculum content as a directed acyclic graph of topic dependencies, the proposed model captures collective learning behaviour across two core dimensions: academic performance and subjective/introspective mental effort. During SOM training, representative data sets of successful learner trajectories are compressed into two topologically ordered, identically structured neural networks: PSOM (performance space) and ESOM (mental effort space). By pairing these behavioural maps, the model serves as a decision-support tool that enables instructors to simultaneously pinpoint structural instructional design defects, such as hidden topic prerequisites, and evaluate collective cognitive load profiles. The implementation and performance of the PSOM component (and, by extension, its symmetrical twin, ESOM) is linked to an earlier modelling study employing a SOM with identical structure and encoding semantics situated in the same domain (i.e., a learning environment). This paper combines the study of behavioural phenomena with theoretical work on human cognitive architecture via SOM neurocomputational cognitive behavioural modelling.

items.title: GramStatTexNet: Efficient, Interpretable, and Neuro-Inspired Texture Analysis-by-Synthesis
items.abstract: Deep networks achieve high realism in texture synthesis but often rely on opaque, over-parameterized representations that have limited direct connection to biological vision. Neuroscience-informed pyramid models are interpretable, compact, and biologically inspired, but rely on small, hand-curated statistics sets that are difficult to generalize or extend. We introduce GramStatTexNet, a hybrid analysis-by-synthesis framework that combines the multi-scale Gabor filter structure of classical models with the flexibility of Gramian-based correlations, organized into structured filter families. This structured representation enables analyses that are challenging for deep-feature methods: each statistic carries a named filter-family identity, allowing us to decompose synthesis fidelity into per-family contributions and to learn an interpretable, low-dimensional embedding that preserves perceptual texture content. We compare our framework to classical and deep texture-synthesis baselines across diverse texture categories, and on multiple perceptual metrics, highlighting the compactness and interpretability advantages of this hybrid representation, alongside competitive synthesis quality. This same framework extends naturally to peripheral textures via spatial pooling, and to dynamic textures using a spatiotemporal filter bank. GramStatTexNet provides a unified, interpretable framework for analyzing and modeling visual information with natural extensions across space, time, and eccentricity. Project page: https://vdutell.github.io/gstn

items.title: Discovery of a Massive Outer Companion to the TOI-178 Resonant Chain
items.abstract: We report the discovery of a massive outer companion around TOI-178, a known planetary system with six inner small planets within 0.15 AU, five of which are in a 2:4:6:9:12 resonant chain. We analyse the astrometric anomalies in the combined Gaia DR2/DR3 - Hipparcos catalogue (G23H) and literature radial velocities, revealing strong evidence for a massive outer companion at several AU. We combine the resulting orbital fit posterior with archival high-contrast imaging to constrain the properties of the corresponding massive outer companion, TOI-178 h. We also study the dynamical stability of the inner resonant chain in the presence of this previously unknown outer companion via both heuristic and N-body simulations. We find that the inner system appears to be robust to the perturbing influence of TOI-178\,h, in line with the systems several Gyr age. Our analysis results in a final posterior solution for TOI-178\,h with a semi-major axis of $6.9^{+12.3}_{-3.3}$ AU, a mass of $21^{+47}_{-11} M_J$, and eccentricity of $0.76^{+0.18}_{-0.35}$, likely corresponding to an eccentric brown dwarf. TOI-178 is currently the only known system that has maintained a high-multiplicity resonant chain whilst in the dynamical presence of a massive outer companion, showcasing a unique outcome of planet formation.

items.title: A Homogeneous Benchmark of Exoplanet Mass-Radius Relations
items.abstract: The mass-radius ($M$-$R$) relation is fundamental to inferring the bulk composition and internal structure of exoplanets. However, published relations remain difficult to compare directly because studies adopt different planetary samples, fitting procedures, and evaluation metrics. We construct a homogeneous, quality-controlled benchmark of 963 exoplanets with dynamically measured masses and transit radii from the NASA Exoplanet Archive. We compare empirical power laws, probabilistic models, and machine-learning (ML) regressors using point accuracy, interval coverage, and probabilistic calibration. On the full test set, a multi-feature random forest has the lowest root-mean-square error, 0.329~dex in $\log_{10} M$ versus 0.368~dex for a fitted two-parameter power law ($p = 0.007$ unadjusted; $p = 0.059$ after Holm correction across 13 comparisons). Radius-only ML models perform comparably to the single power law. In three ranges of the measured radius, several methods improve on the power law below 1.6 $R_\oplus$, but none does between 1.6 and 4 $R_\oplus$. Including stellar and orbital covariates significantly improves predictions only for low-mass planets ($M < 4.4\,M_\oplus$), although this result is sensitive to missing covariate data and weakens when the training and test sets are separated by host star. Within their calibrated radius domains, the published empirical and probabilistic relations remain highly competitive. Finally, a first-order variance decomposition shows that formal measurement uncertainties account for only $\sim$3\% of the residual variance (0.067 of 0.401~dex), and the remaining $\sim$0.396~dex arises from compositional diversity, selection effects, and model approximation error.

items.title: Potential spectral markers of intrinsic magnetic fields of hot exoplanets in the UV range
items.abstract: A method for detecting the intrinsic magnetic fields of exoplanets, based on the effect of atomic alignment (the redistribution of populations among magnetic sublevels under the action of anisotropic radiation from the host star), has been adapted for observations with the Spektr-UV space telescope. A procedure for selecting sensitive transitions is proposed, and triplet absorption lines in the UV range that are sensitive to alignment are identified. On the basis of three-dimensional aeronomic models of the hot Jupiters KELT-20 b and HAT-P-32 b, absorption spectra in these lines are calculated for cases with and without intrinsic magnetic fields of the exoplanets. Using the Spektr-UV exposure-time calculator, the observability of the effect is assessed, and an observing program is proposed, specifying the optimal duration of individual exposures and the number of transits required to detect the signal.

items.title: Polycentrality in Urban Socioecological Systems: A Multilayer Analysis of Social Infrastructure in Iztapalapa, Mexico City
items.abstract: The spatial distribution of infrastructure and activities, along with the networks and interactions that connect them, is key to understanding the relationship between urban form, function, and sustainability from a complex systems perspective. Within this dynamic relationship, the extent to which localized social infrastructure can reinforce existing functional centralities or create conditions for the emergence of new ones remains insufficiently understood. This study examines these relationships through the UTOPÍAS program in Iztapalapa, Mexico City, where 15 public social facilities have been established across a historically underserved urban territory. We develop a multilayer network framework integrating pedestrian infrastructure, GTFS-based public transport services, and UTOPÍAS as a target layer to assess multimodal connectivity, travel-time accessibility, and spatial coverage. These conditions are examined alongside indicators of local economic centrality (PCI and wPCI) to investigate how infrastructure interdependencies relate to the functional organization of urban space. The analysis reveals spatial heterogeneity in multimodal accessibility and differences in the integration of UTOPÍAS with existing transport networks. By relating these patterns to pre-existing economic centralities, we examine whether distributed social infrastructure may reinforce established functional centers or create conditions favorable to emerging centralities, without assuming that spatial decentralization necessarily produces polycentrality. The findings contribute a relational, data-driven approach to understanding how social infrastructure and mobility shape urban functions, emphasizing accessibility and territorial integration as critical conditions for more equitable and sustainable urban development.

items.title: The Structural Number of Parties: An Electoral-Outcome-Independent Baseline for Comparing Party-System Scale
items.abstract: How many parties can a country structurally sustain? Standard measures such as the effective number of parties (ENP) cannot answer this question. They are descriptive and post hoc: they summarize competition only after an election, and they depend on electoral returns that are often missing, interrupted, or unreliable in many developing democracies, particularly in Africa. They also offer no common scale for comparing the size of party registers with realized electoral fragmentation. We introduce the Structural Number of Parties (SNP), an outcome-independent baseline derived from two universally available quantities: population size and territorial area. Building on the logic of the seat product model and the cube-root law of assembly size, the SNP gives an ex ante benchmark that can be computed for any country and year, including where electoral data are absent. Applied to African states, the SNP enables a structural gap diagnosis that distinguishes under-fragmented systems, marked by hegemonic-party dominance, from over-fragmented ones, marked by excessive atomization. The framework thus provides a transparent and reproducible tool to inform institutional reform and the rationalization of party systems across the continent.

items.title: Modelling population distribution across cities on spatial networks using the kinetic theory of multi-agent systems
items.abstract: We investigate the urban population distribution of the Italian region of Sardinia through the kinetic theory of multi-agent systems on spatial networks, interpreting cities both as agents and vertices of a graph, and representing interurban links as edges. We consider various emigration rules to model the interactions between agents, obtaining two main results: the bimodal lognormal fit of the total population distribution among cities and the Pareto fit of the tail. Overall, our model provides results consistent with the actual distribution derived from ISTAT data of Sardinia; furthermore, the bimodal lognormal fit generally follows the distribution tail more accurately than the Pareto one, although the two coincide in the first half.

items.title: Thermodynamics of gas giants accreting via shocks: the role of molecular hydrogen dissociation
items.abstract: Within the core-accretion framework, gas giants acquire most of their mass through accretion shocks during runaway gas accretion. The shock thermodynamics---governed by radiative cooling, accretion history, and equation of state (EoS)---sets the post-shock gas entropy and initial thermal state, strongly influencing both observables and subsequent evolution. We aim to build a coupled evolutionary model predicting the initial thermodynamic conditions, intrinsic luminosities, and upper limits on magnetic field strengths of gas giants across diverse accretion histories. We couple radiation hydrodynamics and $\mathrm{H_2}$ dissociation to long-term planetary interior evolution by training a physics-informed neural network (PINN) predictor on 1000 first-principles simulations resolving the shock physics. This PINN provides post-shock outer boundary conditions for MESA to evolve the planetary envelope beyond runaway accretion. The PINN predicts higher post-shock temperatures than the canonical cold-start model, with the discrepancy widening with planetary mass, while post-shock entropy jumps sharply when $\mathrm{H_2}$ dissociates at $\sim 2000$ K. Gas giants evolved with PINN-derived boundary conditions achieve intrinsic luminosities 4--10 times higher than cold-start models. Under optimistic assumptions, the maximum magnetic field strength at $2 R_{\mathrm{J}}$ reaches a few gauss for a $0.3 M_{\mathrm{J}}$ planet, $\sim 100$ G for $1 M_{\mathrm{J}}$, and $\sim 500$ G for $3 M_{\mathrm{J}}$. Incorporating detailed radiation hydrodynamics and realistic thermodynamics into accretion shock models yields higher initial entropies, brighter intrinsic luminosities, and stronger magnetic fields, providing improved constraints on the masses and accretion rates of directly imaged exoplanets.

items.title: Analytical formulae for planet-planet or moon-moon tides
items.abstract: Almost negligible among the solar system planets, mutual tides raised by a secondary on another secondary orbiting the same primary may gain increased importance in tightly packed systems, e.g., between the components of close-in exoplanetary systems or between the moons of gas giants. In this work, we derive an analytical formula for the planet-planet tidal potential and for the effect of mutual tides on the rotational and orbital evolution of moons or planets in a coplanar configuration. The procedure follows closely the steps of W. M. Kaula (1961), and the resulting potential and derived quantities are presented in the form of an expansion into modes of different frequencies (in the temporal domain) and spherical harmonic components (in the spatial domain). The analytical formulae are implemented into a code and compared with an independent numerical solution.

items.title: Asgard/NOTT: L-band nulling interferometry at the VLTI IV. Prospects for characterising hot exozodiacal dust
items.abstract: Near-infrared interferometric surveys have revealed extended emission around the photosphere of $\approx 40$ main-sequence stars, attributed to the presence of hot exozodiacal dust (HEZD). A promising technique for investigating this phenomenon is nulling interferometry. The Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI) nulling interferometer NOTT (Nulling Observations of exoplaneTs and dusT) is designed to characterise exoplanets and HEZD in the $L'$ band ($3.5-4.0\,μ$m). We aim to assess NOTT's potential for the detection and characterisation of HEZD with various instrumental and model parameter configurations. We model the HEZD as an optically thin dust ring, using the nearby Sun-like star $τ$ Ceti with HEZD as a reference model. Applying the end-to-end nulling tool SCIFYsim to model the instrumental response of NOTT to simulated HEZD brightness distributions, we evaluate how variations in HEZD and instrumental parameters affect NOTT's key observables: the photon flux rate and the null depth. We demonstrate that NOTT is capable of disentangling stellar and dust contributions to the signal and detecting HEZD. The null depth and photon flux rate are sensitive to the HEZD geometry, with inclination, position angle, and ring location having the strongest impact on the signal. Although the detailed temporal signatures are target-specific, the results can be generalised to other systems. NOTT has the potential to deliver unprecedented sensitivity for HEZD observations, granting access to detailed information through spectral dispersion, beam-combination schemes, and exploitation of sky rotation. This enables more sensitive HEZD detections than is possible with current instruments, and improved spatial constraints on the dust, as well as variability studies.

items.title: Neither graphs nor hypergraphs: structural moments of higher-order interactions determine stochastic social-impact dynamics
items.abstract: Whether higher-order interactions can be reduced to simpler representations is a question about the dynamics they drive, not only about their structure: what can be discarded is whatever the dynamics does not see. We make this precise for binary-state stochastic dynamics in which each agent, when updated, interacts with a randomly selected group and changes state according to the fraction of disagreeing members, as in generalized voter and social-impact models on hypergraphs. We ask which statistics of the group-interaction process determine the resulting Markov dynamics. For response functions that are polynomials of degree $q$, the answer is a hierarchy of size-weighted inclusion moments, which we call structural moments, involving at most $q$ neighbors at a time, regardless of how large the groups are. These moments are not only sufficient but also necessary: two interaction structures produce identical dynamics for all such rules if and only if their moments coincide. More generally, each class of rules selects its own minimal structural description, ranging from weighted pairwise links for linear rules to the full distribution of co-membership by group size for arbitrary rules. For voter-type rules, the same moments also reconstruct exact pairwise copying representations of these dynamics.

items.title: Enabling joint chemical and meteorological data assimilation with an atmospheric foundation model
items.abstract: The hydroxyl radical (OH) is the main oxidant in the troposphere and accounts for 88% of the methane sink, yet its abundance and trends remain poorly constrained. Satellites observe many of the chemical and meteorological drivers of OH, but assimilating both requires a model that represents chemistry and meteorology together. Existing chemistry-climate models are too expensive for joint data assimilation. Here, we present AuroraChem, a fine-tuned version of the Aurora atmospheric foundation model that jointly simulates meteorology and the GEOS-Chem chemical fields needed to constrain OH. A one-year AuroraChem rollout takes 12 minutes on one GPU. Free rollouts remain stable for one year but do not fully capture seasonal cycles. Using idealized data assimilation, we find that chemical observations can constrain the meteorological state and meteorological observations can constrain the chemical state. Inserting only the chemical fields raises the annual mean spatial correlation of 500 hPa temperature from 0.89 to 0.92 and recovers the moisture and circulation pattern of the Indian summer monsoon. Inserting only the meteorological fields raises the 500 hPa OH correlation from 0.89 to 0.93, close to the 0.94 from inserting the chemical fields themselves, and recovers the OH seasonal cycle. Inserting only NO2 columns sampled at TROPOMI pixels gives an OH correlation of 0.93. These relationships likely reflect learned covariances rather than physical coupling, and covariances are what data assimilation uses to let an observation of one variable update the others. AuroraChem therefore provides a new pathway to joint chemical and meteorological data assimilation.

items.title: Localized active phase in the coevolving voter model with fixed links
items.abstract: The coevolving voter model (CVM) describes the evolution of node states and network topology through copying and rewiring dynamics. It traditionally assumes that all ties can be rewired, overlooking unbreakable real-world relationships like family or close friendships. To address this, we introduce fixed links that cannot be rewired and study how these structural constraints modify the collective dynamics of the CVM. In addition to the active and frozen phases of the CVM, we find a new localized active phase in which activity is sustained, beyond a percolation transition, by a giant component of fixed links. The existence of this new phase is predicted by a moment-closure approximation that goes beyond the standard pair approximation. The finite-size manifestation of this phase is an asymmetric fragmented phase. In addition, the active-frozen transition of the CVM, manifested as a fragmentation transition for finite systems, is delayed by the existence of fixed links to larger values of the rewiring rate.

items.title: NEXONN: Advancing the NEXOTRANS Exoplanet Atmospheric Retrieval Framework with Transformer-Based Neural Posterior Estimation for JWST Transmission Spectroscopy of WASP-39b
items.abstract: The James Webb Space Telescope is delivering unprecedented constraints on exoplanet atmospheres, but computationally intensive Bayesian retrievals challenge the transition from individual planets to population-level studies of planetary formation and evolution. We introduce NEXONN, a transformer-conditioned normalizing-flow framework within NEXOTRANS that enables rapid atmospheric posterior estimation with uncertainty quantification. Incorporating PandExo-based JWST noise, we benchmark NEXONN against PyMultiNest using simulated spectra and JWST observations of WASP-39 b (0.6-12 microns). For simulated MIRI/LRS data, eight posteriors achieve a mean overlap of 80.32%. Retrievals of combined NIRISS, NIRSpec, and MIRI observations yield consistent atmospheric properties. For the full dataset, NEXONN infers C/O = 0.82 (+0.01/-0.02) and [M/H] = 1.13 (+0.04/-0.04), compared with PyMultiNest values of 0.80 (+0.03/-0.01) and 1.19 (+0.05/-0.03). Divergence metrics, Wasserstein distances, posterior overlaps, and coverage tests assess posterior fidelity and uncertainty calibration, revealing parameter-dependent differences. Once trained, NEXONN performs posterior inference within seconds, enabling scalable population studies of exoplanet atmospheric composition, formation, and evolution.

items.title: MAIC-2 v2.3: A Fortran program for simulating the surface temperature, atmospheric water transport and surface glaciation of the planet Mars
items.abstract: The Mars Atmosphere-Ice Coupler MAIC-2 is a computationally efficient, zonally-averaged model designed to simulate Martian surface temperature, atmospheric water transport and surface glaciation over timescales of 10^5 to 10^7 years. While sophisticated General Circulation Models (GCMs) provide high-resolution simulations of the Martian atmosphere, their high computational cost makes them largely unsuitable for studies covering millions of years of orbital evolution. MAIC-2 addresses this gap by utilizing physically-based, zonally-averaged parameterizations, including a Local Insolation Temperature (LIT) scheme and a mass balance engine driven by free-convection and instantaneous mixing physics. Version 2.3 introduces a fully modularized Fortran architecture that improves maintainability and ensures that the software remains entirely self-contained, requiring no external numerical libraries or specialized data formats for execution. Demonstrated through a 20-million-year transient simulation, the model successfully reproduces the primary characteristics of the Martian polar layered deposits. MAIC-2 provides the planetary science community with a versatile, open-source tool for investigating the long-term climatic impacts of orbital variations on the Martian surface.

items.title: LUC3D: Multi-animal 3D pose tracking in the browser
items.abstract: Animal behavior unfolds in three dimensions over time, yet accessible scientific tools for analyzing it in its natural form remain limited. Uncertainty from popular 2D pose methods can be refined with multi-camera approaches to produce more accurate 3D estimates. This paper presents LUC3D (Label Unification and Correspondence in 3D Annotation GUI), a browser-based 3D GUI for reducing the amount of manual labor required for labeling, proofreading, and multi-camera multi-animal tracking while requiring no installation to maximize accessibility. As proof-of-concept we present two datasets of proofread multi-camera 3D triangulated pose data of mouse social behavior, a protocol for generating 3D consistent labels, and a cross-view re-identification tracking algorithm for multi-animal multi-camera pose data. This tool allows for the widespread adoption of 3D pose estimation techniques for studying social behavior while reducing the cost of entry for neuroscience labs across the world.

items.title: Spectral and complexity-based signatures of advanced concentration absorption meditation: A high-density EEG study of jhana
items.abstract: Advanced meditation provides structured and reproducible alterations of consciousness that are increasingly used as model states for the neuroscience of consciousness. Jhana-type advanced concentration absorption meditation (ACAM-J) consists of eight progressively deepening absorption states (ACAM-J1-8) in which sensory and self-referential content gradually attenuate. We applied high-density EEG and a comprehensive multidimensional battery of spectral and complexity measures to characterize each ACAM-J state individually in 20 advanced meditators, together with phenomenological ratings. ACAM-J produced widespread posterior-central reductions in oscillatory and aperiodic power, posterior aperiodic flattening across all eight states, and convergent increases in entropy-based complexity over the posterior cortex, with power effects strengthening with phenomenological depth. Crucially, neural complexity remained elevated even in the late, most minimal and unified states, in opposition to the prevailing account that links higher neural entropy to richer phenomenal content. Between practitioners, lower power and higher entropy accompanied more visual and auditory but less bodily content, a redistribution rather than an enrichment of experience; within practitioners, only reduced low-frequency power tracked wider attention and less narrative thought. ACAM-J thus emerges as a non-pharmacological model state at the high-complexity end of the spectrum of altered consciousness, and reveals a previously unquantified dissociation between neural complexity and experiential richness for specific ACAM-J states.

items.title: Development and Feasibility of the Bern Brain Training App for Older Adults With Subjective Cognitive Decline and Mild Cognitive Impairment: Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: Background Computerized cognitive training (CCT) aims to mitigate cognitive decline in subjective cognitive decline (SCD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI). However, adherence and long-term engagement remain challenging in remote CCT interventions. Objective Describe the development and design of the Bern Brain Training (BBT), a tablet-based app to remotely train cognitive functions and assess its feasibility, usability, and acceptability. This is a secondary analysis of a previously published randomized controlled trial (RCT). Methods Unity Game Engine and C# programming were used to design 16 games targeting episodic, semantic, and working memory, and spatial abilities. We assessed feasibility, usability, and acceptability of the BBT (50 sessions in 10 weeks, each 24 minutes) in 116 participants with subjective cognitive decline (SCD, n=89) or mild cognitive impairment (MCI, n=27). One session per week was played in-clinic in a group setting of 4-6 participants. Within the main RCT with parallel groups, participants were pseudo-randomized to one of three groups, with an allocation ratio of 1:1:1. The BBT was administered in all three treatment groups at different time points. Group 1 (n=36, 31%) started with the BBT (10 weeks); Group 2 (n=34, 29%) started with active control training (10 weeks), and then moved on to the BBT (10 weeks); Group 3 (n=46, 39%) started with the BBT (10 weeks) after a waiting period of 10 weeks. Results Feasibility was high (adherence rate: mean 5.10, SD 0.69 BBT sessions/week; weekly group sessions: mean 9.18 SD 1.05; concluded BBT sessions: 5891, 91%). On a 7-point Likert scale, participants showed high motivation across cognitive domains and training groups (mean 6.15, SD 1.05), and groups did not differ significantly in adherence ( P>. 05). Usability was good with 61 (0.94%) help button presses recorded across 6489 sessions played. Acceptability (7-point Likert scale) was satisfying in game experience ratings of entertainment (mean 5.43, SD 1.39), with low frustration rates (mean 3.01, SD 1.79), despite the BBT being perceived as challenging (mean 5.52, SD 1.22). The games were perceived as most efficient in training memory (mean 5.7, SD 1.20) and thinking abilities (mean 5.43, SD 1.18). SCD and MCI did not differ significantly in game experience and perceived game efficacy ( P >.05). Conclusions The BBT demonstrated high feasibility, usability, and acceptability. Its innovation lies in the participatory and professional game design, task diversity, adaptivity, and social elements, with a large sample size that sets it apart from other studies. These findings advance the field by demonstrating that tablet-based, remote cognitive training is feasible and well accepted in older adults with cognitive impairment, emphasizing the importance of these parameters for high training adherence and supporting its potential integration into clinical practice. Future research should extend evaluation to care-home settings and populations with more advanced cognitive impairment.

items.title: [Deciphering the fate of somitic multipotent progenitors through lineage tracing].
items.abstract: Somites are composed of multipotent progenitors expressing the transcription factor PAX3 (paired box 3). These progenitors (PAX3-MPs) give rise to skeletal muscle, dorsal dermis, brown adipose tissue, and a subset of vascular cells. Deciphering their fate is essential for understanding tissue organization during development. Lineage tracing approaches, conducted at either the population or clonal level, allow us to reconstruct the trajectories of these cells with high precision and thus understand how they specialize. In this article, we explore different lineage tracing strategies and show how they have revealed the mechanisms that govern progenitor fate in a wide range of systems. Understanding the mechanisms that determine the fate of multipotent progenitors such as PAX3-MPs opens up opportunities in regenerative medicine by facilitating the directed differentiation of induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) toward specific cell lineages.

items.title: Perceptual glimpses are locally accumulated and globally maintained at distinct processing levels.
items.abstract: Making decisions often requires the integration of multiple pieces of information. An extensive body of research has investigated the neural architecture underpinning evidence accumulation in perceptual tasks where information is continuously present, but less is known about how this neural architecture operates in situations affording only intermittent glimpses of an evidence source. In two electroencephalography experiments, human participants judged the direction of up to two pulses of motion evidence separated by gaps of varying duration. Our behavioural analysis found that participants used both pulses but underutilised the second and showed no systematic decrease in accuracy as a function of gap duration. At the neural level, motor beta lateralisation tracked cumulative evidence across pulses, maintaining a sustained representation of the decision variable through the gap and until response. In contrast, the centroparietal positivity (CPP), a previously characterised signature of evidence accumulation, built up transiently to a peak that scaled with each pulse's contribution to the decision variable (i.e. the absolute belief update it produced), falling back to baseline in between pulses. These patterns were recapitulated in a model where pulse-information transiently integrated at the CPP level is fed to and maintained at a bounded motor level. In this model, the evidence in the second pulse is only integrated to the extent that the evidence in the first pulse falls short of the bound, or not integrated at all if a bound has already been hit.

items.title: Silent Teachers in Anatomical Education: A Historical Review of Paradigm Shifts in Human Cadaver Procurement Since Ancient Persia.
items.abstract: Human cadaveric dissection has played an important role in the development of anatomical knowledge and remains an established component of medical education. The availability of human bodies for anatomical study has varied across historical periods, reflecting changes in educational institutions, procurement practices, and ethical and sociocultural considerations. This narrative review examines the historical development of human dissection and cadaver procurement, with particular emphasis on Iran. Relevant literature was identified through searches of MEDLINE via PubMed and supplemented by historical publications, scholarly sources, locally sourced literature and contextual information, reference-list screening, and citation tracking. The literature was synthesized chronologically and thematically to examine the development of anatomical knowledge, the emergence of modern anatomy education in Iran, and reported changes in cadaver procurement practices. The historical literature documents a long tradition of medical scholarship and anatomical knowledge in Iran, followed by the gradual development of formal anatomy education through modern medical institutions. Reported sources of cadavers for anatomical education in Iran have included unclaimed bodies, imported cadavers, and voluntary body donation. However, the available evidence is insufficient to establish a comprehensive chronology of these practices or to determine their relative contributions across institutions and historical periods. The increasing recognition of voluntary body donation represents an important development in contemporary anatomical education, alongside continuing ethical and sociocultural considerations concerning informed consent, respect for human remains, and public acceptance. Cadaveric dissection continues to be used alongside alternative teaching approaches, including anatomical models and digital technologies. The historical development of cadaver procurement in Iran reflects broader changes in anatomical education and institutional practice. Further research based on historical records and institutional documentation is needed to clarify the chronology of procurement practices and their implications for contemporary anatomical education and ethical governance.

items.title: The hippocampus as a latent diffusion engine for memory, perception and cognitive dysfunction.
items.abstract: The hippocampus is a central cognitive hub whose dysfunction contributes to most neurodegenerative dementias. Despite extensive knowledge of its anatomy, physiology and circuitry, a unifying account that links hippocampal dynamics to cognition and clinical syndromes remains lacking. Drawing on systems neuroscience and recent advances in generative artificial intelligence, we conceptualize the hippocampus as a latent diffusion engine that compresses sensory, interoceptive and cognitive inputs into low-dimensional representations and regenerates percepts, episodic memories and imagined scenes for cortical integration. Travelling waves of cortico-hippocampal oscillations, aligned with large-scale functional gradients, schedule and structure this generative process and organize distributed neural activity into coherent, semantically grounded constructs. We formalize this proposal as stochastic latent oscillatory diffusion (SLOD), a biologically grounded framework that maps hippocampal-cortical computations onto specific anatomical substrates and dynamical processes. While we do not suggest that the hippocampus implements diffusion algorithms per se, we show that its computations can be decomposed into homologous operations including compression, stochastic exploration, conditioning and reconstruction, whose formal structure closely parallels that of latent diffusion models. Finally, we demonstrate how major neurodegenerative dementias, including the Alzheimer's disease spectrum, dementia with Lewy bodies and frontotemporal dementia, can be understood as selective breakdowns of distinct components of this generative architecture.

items.title: Deferiprone modulates osteoclast-mediated bone resorption while preserving axial bone microstructure in β-thalassemic mice with iron overload.
items.abstract: Deferiprone (DFP), an iron chelator, is widely used to alleviate iron overload. However, its effects on bone metabolism remain incompletely understood. Herein, we demonstrated that DFP reduced osteoblast viability and in vitro mineralization. Interestingly, DFP delayed osteoclastogenesis, suppressed osteoclast marker expression, and appeared to influence iron efflux by upregulating Nrf2 and ferroportin-1. Although DFP effectively reduced iron accumulation in bone, it did not reverse persistent microstructural defects in the axial skeleton of β-thalassemic mice. Under high-iron conditions, DFP appeared to increase osteoclast turnover, leading to a transient accumulation of multinucleated osteoclasts followed by enhanced apoptosis. Collectively, our findings suggest a trade-off whereby reduced iron toxicity is accompanied by attenuated bone formation and resorption in β-thalassemic mice.

items.title: Aortic stiffness and brain perfusion: a population-based study.
items.abstract: ObjectivesThe objective was to examine the association of aortic stiffness and age with brain perfusion, brain structure, and cognitive function in a population-based sample.DesignThe sample included randomly selected descendants from a large community study. Aortic stiffness was assessed using carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (CFPWV) measured by applanation tonometry. Brain perfusion and structural brain measures were obtained using magnetic resonance imaging, and cognitive performance was evaluated using standardized neuropsychological tests. Participants were stratified by the median CFPWV ( ≤ or >8.6 m/s) for comparison and associations were examined in multivariable regression analyses adjusted for age, sex, heart rate, mean arterial pressure, use of antihypertensive medication and CFPWV.ResultsThe study included 269 subjects, average age 62 years. Participants with higher aortic stiffness (>8.6 m/s) were older, had higher heart rate, blood pressure, and more frequently used antihypertensive medication. Total brain, grey matter, and white matter perfusion were significantly lower in those with higher aortic stiffness. Relative brain volume was lower, and white matter hyperintensity (WMH) burden higher in unadjusted analyses, whereas cognitive performance did not differ. In multivariable models, increased aortic stiffness was independently associated with lower total brain perfusion, while chronological age was independently associated with lower brain volumes and greater WMH burden.ConclusionsThese findings indicate that aortic stiffness and aging represent related but distinct contributors to brain health. Aortic stiffness was independently associated with reduced brain perfusion, whereas age was the dominant determinant of structural brain changes.

items.title: BeeHive: a flexible open electronics platform for controlling research equipment and teaching electronics principles.
items.abstract: In this manuscript, we present BeeHive, a standardized, open-source hardware electronics ecosystem designed to address challenges faced by researchers when developing custom scientific equipment. BeeHive is flexible and interoperable, since it is organized around minimal design rules. It consists of a microcontroller-based main board and function-specific daughter boards (DBs) for controlling actuators or reading sensors, allowing researchers to rapidly combine and repurpose components to build complex, specialized systems. This modular approach significantly reduces the time and cost associated with instrumentation development, promoting effective collaboration through shared, standardized solutions. The platform's versatility is demonstrated across several neuroscience applications, including a reward delivery system for head-fixed mice, a modular mouse maze and an odour stimulator, alongside a dedicated training DB and curriculum designed to teach electronics and MicroPython programming in an integrated, project-based manner. By embracing open-source principles for hardware and software, BeeHive lowers the barrier to entry for researchers in developing their own set-ups, fostering greater accessibility, reproducibility and innovation. The system is also discipline-agnostic and could be used to create tools in different fields.

items.title: Shifting the Pressure-Natriuresis Curve: The Cellular Mechanisms of Female Renal Resilience.
items.abstract: Female and male kidneys exhibit markedly different patterns of transporter abundance and activity along the nephron, yet the physiological significance of the differences remains incompletely understood. Recent experimental and computational studies suggest that many of these differences can be interpreted through the lens of pressure natriuresis, the kidney's primary mechanism for long-term regulation of extracellular volume and arterial pressure. We review evidence that the female nephron exhibits a transport architecture that may facilitate enhanced pressure natriuresis and greater flexibility in effective circulating volume regulation. This framework provides new insights into sex differences in acute and chronic blood pressure control and connects pressure-natriuretic mechanisms with renal adaptations during pregnancy and lactation, hypertension, and aging.

items.title: Imaging fast neural circuit activity in brain and nerve with electrical impedance tomography (fnEIT): review, method and engineering aspects.
items.abstract: Fast neural electrical impedance tomography (fnEIT) is a technique for imaging neural activity in the brain or nerves, with a resolution of milliseconds and millimetres, using a probing applied current and boundary or depth voltage measurement. Proof of principle has been demonstrated in animal studies, but it is yet to be adopted into common use. Objective. The purpose of this review is to provide an introduction and overview of the method and technical aspects of fnEIT research and its place in the biomedical sciences. Topics covered include the bioimpedance of action potentials, fnEIT studies to date, similar EIT methods and technical innovations. Approach. A methodical critical review of the fnEIT literature has been performed. Promising areas of future work and their applications are highlighted, including challenges that must be overcome. Main results. It is shown that the fields of nerve imaging and neuromodulation, cognitive neuroscience in animals and humans, and epileptic seizure localisation could benefit from the ability of fnEIT to image millisecond scale neuronal depolarization throughout brain or nerve. This is achievable with existing methods but with current limitations of the need for implanted cranial or nerve electrodes and averaging to a repeated stimulus. Current approaches to overcome this include CMOS integrated active electrodes, frequency division multiplexing for parallel signal acquisition, and recording with atomic magnetometers. With these, it is a realistic possibility to achieve non-invasive imaging of fast neural activity in real-time with an electrode-atomic magnetometer helmet in human subjects with a resolution of mm and msec. Significance . This review serves as a general guide for those working in related fields or those considering the use of EIT. With the above advances, it is a realistic possibility to achieve non-invasive imaging of fast neural activity in real-time with an electrode-atomic magnetometer helmet in human subjects with a resolution of mm and msec.

items.title: Modeling exhaled aerosol deposition in an impaction filter across clinically measured breath flowrates.
items.abstract: Exhaled breath offers a non-invasive matrix for detecting recent drug use, but high intra- and inter-study variability in collected drug mass currently hinders its transition into reliable quantitative clinical and forensic tools. To enable standardized, reproducible sampling protocols, we evaluated flowrate-dependent aerosol capture in an impaction filter device (). We expanded a computational fluid and particle dynamics (CFPD) model across a flowrate spectrum informed by clinical data from 38 participants (exhalations; mean flowrate). We also enhanced the near-wall transport model to resolve turbulent aerosol dispersion at high resolution. CFPD simulations showed that turbulent forces account for up to 20% of mass deposition for submicrometer-size aerosols within this operational range. Crucially, capture efficiency varied more than two-fold-ranging from 42% at 0.05 Lto 90% at 0.3 L-at a constant exhaled volume. These findings demonstrate that breath flowrate directly impacts aerosol recovery, suggesting that participant flowrate guidance or mathematical recovery normalization could improve the reproducibility of drug quantification. Ultimately, this work demonstrates how combining real-world clinical data with CFPD modeling can inform standardized, quantitative breath diagnostics.

items.title: A unifying framework for structured population dynamics in modern coexistence theory
items.abstract: Variation within populations is ubiquitous in nature, yet many models and frameworks in community ecology assume that all individuals within a population interact with the community identically. Modern coexistence theory is no exception; however, several subfields of ecology have independently been integrating coexistence theory, each asking the same underlying question: how do structured population dynamics shape coexistence outcomes? Here, I propose a unifying framework for integrating population variation into modern coexistence theory that is applicable across all fields of ecology. The application of this framework is presented in three case studies: niche overlap and fitness differences between influenza substrains, mutual invasibility between competing perennial plants, and fluctuation-dependent invasion outcomes in apparently competing prey with a foraging-predation risk tradeoff. Together, these examples illustrate the framework's broad applicability, power to resolve the interaction between population and community level processes, and its potential to reveal novel ecological phenomena.

items.title: Ontogenetic and seasonal variation in the trophic niche of a threatened Amazonian freshwater stingray revealed by diet and stable isotope analyses
items.abstract: Abstract Ontogenetic changes and seasonal variation in river flow influence trophic interactions in freshwater ecosystems, but their relative effects on tropical freshwater elasmobranchs remain poorly understood. We investigated how these factors affect the trophic ecology of the threatened freshwater stingray Potamotrygon leopoldi , endemic to the Xingu River (Amazon Basin), in a regulated river section influenced by the Belo Monte Hydroelectric Complex. We combined stomach content and stable isotope (δ¹³C and δ¹⁵N) analyses to examine variation in diet composition, trophic niche breadth, prey size, trophic position, and resource assimilation according to body size, sex, and river discharge. Potamotrygon leopoldi had a broad trophic niche and an opportunistic diet, consisting mainly of mollusks, crustaceans, fish, and aquatic insects. Ontogeny was the main driver of trophic variation. Larger individuals consumed larger prey, had broader isotopic niches, and assimilated resources from a wider range of basal carbon pathways than juveniles. River discharge had a secondary effect, influencing prey diversity and resource assimilation, whereas differences between sexes were negligible. Stomach contents and stable isotopes revealed complementary aspects of recent prey consumption and longer-term resource assimilation. Overall, our results indicate that resource use changes throughout the life cycle, mainly in association with body size, while hydrological variation further influences trophic patterns in Potamotrygon leopoldi .

items.title: Genetic Variability and Yield Determinants of Upland Rice Genotypes in Akungba Akoko Agro-Ecology
items.abstract: Abstract Background Rice is one of the world's most important cereal crops and a major source of food and income for millions of people, especially Nigeria, which has almost reach her self-sufficient production capacity. However, genetic variability significantly influences yield component traits in rice for stability and adaptability. Therefore, this study assessed the genetic variability and trait associations influencing grain yield in upland rice genotypes evaluated under the Akungba Akoko agro-ecology. Methods Fourteen genotypes were tested under field conditions in a randomized complete block design at the experimental field of the department of Plant Science and Biotechnology, and data were collected on yield and related agronomic traits, analyzed using GLM models of SPSS version 27. Result The analysis of variance revealed highly significant differences among genotypes, confirming the presence of considerable genetic diversity. Plant height, number of tillers, effective tillers, flag leaf length, panicle length, panicle weight, number of grains per panicle, number of spikelets, thousand grain weight, grain length and width, days to panicle initiation, days to maturity, and grain yield per hill all vary significantly among the genotypes. These significant differences suggest considerable genetic variability within the tested genotypes, which is favorable for selection and breeding. Coefficient of variation (CV) provides a measure of experimental precision and variability relative to the mean. Most traits have CV values below 20%, with some lower than 10%, which suggests good experimental consistency. For example: Plant height CV 5.8% (high precision). Number of tillers CV 16.4%. Grain yield CV 25.8%, which is typical for yield traits due to their inherent variability. Estimates of genotypic and phenotypic coefficients of variation indicated that while some traits were strongly under genetic control, others were more sensitive to environmental influence. Grain yield showed positive and significant correlations with key yield components, particularly productive tillers, panicle weight, number of grains per panicle, and thousand-grain weight, highlighting their value as indirect selection criteria. Genetic parameter estimates further demonstrated high heritability (> 90%) for traits such as plant height, number of tillers, panicle weight, and maturity, coupled with high genetic advance values, suggesting strong additive gene action and effective selection potential. Conversely, traits like panicle length exhibited lower heritability, reflecting greater environmental influence. Conclusion The study shows good genetic variability and heritability for most important yield and agronomic traits in upland rice genotypes from this agro-ecology, indicating strong potential for selection and breeding improvements. Traits like panicle weight, grain yield, and tiller number are particularly promising targets for breeders.
