items.title: A minimal pangenome graph for Salminus brasiliensis, a freshwater migratory Neotropical flagship species: it takes two to tango
items.abstract: Abstract Two chromosome-level, reference-guided consensus genomes of Salminus brasiliensis are presented for an Upper Paraná Basin specimen (Brazil), representing a potentially distinct lineage from the Vertebrate Genomes Project reference specimen, from Argentina. These resources allow for a genomic variation framework, including the minimal reference pangenome graph. Short reads mapped against the VGP reference assemblies yielded two ~ 1.07–1.08 Gb pseudohaplotypes (N 50 =38.9–40.8 Mb), with union k-mer completeness of 94%, Q V ~33 each. BUSCO completeness scores are 97.8% for the principal genome and 97.4% for the lifted annotation proteome. The reference pangenome graph for S. brasiliensis was obtained from four chromosome-level haploid sets, using minigraph. It is 1.1 Gb, comprising 288,788 segments (average length 3,826 bp), 404,621 links (809,242 arcs), with average node degree 1.4 (maximum 3). Additional read-to-graph alignments (GAM/GAF) and other accompanying genomic datasets, such as gene annotation, are also provided. The bioinformatics datasets made available for this model Neotropical migratory freshwater species—relevant for conservation, fisheries and aquaculture—can be applied in fields such as ecology, evolution and biotechnology.

items.title: A comprehensive review of craniomandibular morphometric indices in carnivora: Anatomical basis, functional significance, and comparative applications.
items.abstract: The skull of carnivorans represents a highly integrated anatomical structure shaped by selective pressures associated with feeding ecology, sensory specialization, locomotion, and phylogenetic history. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of craniomandibular morphometric indices in the order Carnivora, integrating their anatomical definitions, morphometric foundations, and functional significance. Standardized cranial and mandibular measurements are reviewed together with 11 widely used proportional indices, including the Cranial Index (CI), Skull Index (SI), Facial Index (FI), Facial Length Index (FLI), Cranial Length Index (CLI), Cranial Height Index (CHI), Orbital Index (OI), Palatal Index (PI), Foramen Magnum Index (FMI), Mandibular Body Index (MBI), and Mandibular Ramus Index (MRI). The review highlights the biomechanical and evolutionary relevance of these indices by examining their relationships with bite performance, craniofacial organization, sensory adaptations, feeding ecology, and morphological diversification among carnivoran families. In addition to summarizing published morphometric indices, several proportional indices that have rarely been reported as independent variables are derived from previously published linear craniometric measurements, providing standardized quantitative descriptors for comparative analyses across species. By compiling anatomical landmarks, measurement protocols, functional interpretations, and comparative data within a unified framework, this review identifies current knowledge gaps and promotes greater methodological consistency in future studies. Although some proportional indices were calculated from published measurements rather than directly reported in the original literature, they provide valuable complementary metrics for evaluating cranial and mandibular morphology. Overall, the integration of these 11 morphometric indices offers a comprehensive approach for investigating craniofacial evolution, functional morphology, feeding adaptations, and taxonomic diversity in both extant and fossil carnivorans. This review provides a practical reference for researchers in comparative anatomy, evolutionary biology, paleontology, and veterinary morphology.

items.title: Brønsted Acid Enrichment Around Zeolite-Encapsulated Pd Promotes Efficient Tandem Catalysis.
items.abstract: Metal-acid bifunctional catalyst design is essential for selectivity control in tandem catalysis. However, reactive intermediates often experience a kinetic mismatch between metal- and acid-catalyzed elementary steps, thereby being consumed through competing pathways and diverted toward undesired products. Herein, we developed a metal cation-directed Al siting (MCD-Al) strategy to enrich framework Al sites around Pd nanoparticles encapsulated in Beta zeolite (Pd@Beta-MCD), enabling tunable Brønsted acid site density close to metal sites by controlling metal precursor loading. When Pd@Beta-MCD was employed in benzene hydroalkylation, the spatial proximity of metal-acid sites accelerated transfer of Pd-generated cyclohexene to adjacent acid sites, and the high Brønsted acid site density around Pd nanoparticles remarkably facilitated cyclohexene protonation for alkylation. Pd@Beta-MCD achieved its maximum cyclohexylbenzene yield of 48.1% with a corresponding selectivity of 77.5%, outperforming Pd/HBeta (21.1% and 30.1%) and Pd@HBeta (27.7% and 38.3%), representing the best performance reported to date for this reaction. Moreover, Pd@Beta-MCD showed superior cycling stability over eight runs. We demonstrated that the concentrated Brønsted acid sites adjacent to metal centers resolve the kinetic mismatch and steer the cyclohexene intermediate toward an alkylation-dominated pathway. This work provides an effective strategy to strengthen metal-acid synergistic matching and facilitates precise control of key intermediates in tandem catalysis.

items.title: Bidirectional Interplay Between the Skin Microbiota and the Host: An EAACI Task Force Report.
items.abstract: The skin microbiome is a diverse community of bacteria, fungi, archaea, and viruses colonizing the human skin and is thought to play an important role in skin health. Skin homeostasis and immunity are influenced by a dynamic interplay between the host immune system, the skin microbiome, and other host factors. Disruption of the skin microbiome well-functioning by environmental, lifestyle, and host-related factors can lead to dysbiosis, which has been associated to some pathological skin conditions, resulting in skin inflammation and an impaired barrier function. Building on the previous work from the EAACI Task Force that emphasized how environmental and lifestyle factors impact host resilience through the skin microbiome, the present review focuses on intrinsic host factors. We provide a comprehensive discussion on how the skin composition differs at different anatomical locations and is influenced by age, gender, hormones, immune system activity, and how the host "multi-omes" (genome, transcriptome, proteome, and metabolome) interact with the skin microbiome. Additionally, we review current strategies to modify skin microbiome functions, including the role of diseases and medication, as well as topical microbiome-targeting biotic and bacteriophage therapies. Overall, this review highlights current knowledge and key research gaps, offering insights to guide future investigations and therapeutic innovations in skin health.

items.title: [The law of muscular fatigue across history and species].
items.abstract: Since the earliest anatomical descriptions, comparative studies of muscle tissue have revealed a common architecture within the animal kingdom. This structural invariance implies that the fundamental laws governing muscle function are also universal. The law of fatigue represents a typical case: during exertion, a critical intensity exists below which the muscle can work indefinitely without fatigue onset, and above which fatigue sets in abruptly, inevitably leading to exhaustion. This fatigability threshold is critical, for it delineates sustainable effort from that which is not. Overcoming what has historically been a limited permeability between disciplines, research in human physiology and animal ecology now converge to test this law in free-ranging animals. This approach shows that there can be considerable value in moving beyond classical experimental models, so as to explore muscle tissue more broadly across the immense diversity of the animal kingdom. Moreover, by revealing a method applicable to species in the wild, hitherto inaccessible to study, this approach paves the way for its transfer to preclinical and clinical research. By relying on spontaneous activity so as not to disturb the animals concerned, it addresses important ethical considerations, facilitating both the non-invasive longitudinal monitoring of mice and the assessment of patients for whom the evaluation of physical capacity also remains a delicate matter.

items.title: A change in sex chromosomes caused by allopolyploidy in a willow lineage triggered new evolutionary changes in descendant species.
items.abstract: Polyploidization through hybridization between species with different sex chromosomes is evolutionarily surprising. To understand stable sex-determining systems in such hybrids, we studied a dioecious allotetraploid (4n) willow lineage that arose by hybridization between Salix species from the Salix and Vetrix clades. We generated chromosome-level assemblies for three allotetraploids and one related diploid, characterized their sex-linked regions (SLRs) to infer their evolutionary history, and analyzed mRNA and small RNA (sRNA) expression profiles of candidate sex-determining genes. Female genome assemblies confirmed that the same two subgenomes contributed to all allotetraploids studied. Both progenitor species have male heterogamety (XY systems), with SLRs on different chromosomes (7 and 15), whereas the allotetraploids have female heterogamety (ZW systems). Three 4n species, Salix babylonica, Salix matsudana, and Salix chienii, retained Z-SLRs in the former chromosome 15Y pericentromeric location, which carry male-determining partial duplications of the ARR17 gene, and an inversion between the SLRs arose adjacent to these duplications in their common ancestor. Another 4n species, Salix pentandra, split before these 4n species diversified, and the ARR17 partial duplications are in the chromosome's pseudo-autosomal (recombining) region. We identify a W-linked ARR22-like gene and propose it as a candidate sex-determining factor in this species, pending functional testing.

items.title: Dominance hierarchies are structured similarly in females and males across primate groups.
items.abstract: Classic socioecological theory predicts that males and females experience different sources and mechanisms of social competition. Whether these differences translate into sex‑specific structural properties of dominance hierarchies remains unclear. Here, we compiled 156 dominance interaction matrices from 80 studies and extracted three commonly used metrics-hierarchy steepness, linearity and the directional consistency-to investigate the structural characteristics of male and female dominance hierarchies across primates. All three metrics were strongly affected by methodological and demographic variables. Steepness increased with the number of recorded interactions and group size, linearity decreased as matrices became sparser, and directional consistency declined with increasing numbers of interactions. The metrics covaried: groups with steeper hierarchies also exhibit more linear and more directionally consistent relationships. We found no sex differences in steepness, linearity or directional consistency. These results suggest that current metrics primarily reflect variation in the sampling effort and the rate of interaction and that, at a basic level, agonistic interactions are similar among female and male primates. Our findings highlight the need for alternative measures of potential power asymmetries that are less confounded by sampling effort and demographic variation to better understand how competition and conflict are structured across societies.

items.title: Comparative genomics reveals contrasting candidate adaptive signatures in two ecologically similar plateau fishes.
items.abstract: Plateau aquatic environments expose fishes to chronic cold, hypoxia, ultraviolet radiation and low productivity, providing natural systems for studying genomic features associated with environmental adaptation. Whether related fishes inhabiting similar cold-water plateau environments exhibit comparable or divergent genomic responses remains unclear. We compared two plateau cypriniform fishes, Aspiorhynchus laticeps and Diptychus maculatus , within a 12-species phylogenomic framework, integrating orthogroup inference, gene-family turnover, coding-sequence divergence, chromosome-scale synteny and duplicated gene-pair divergence profiling. The strongest contrasts occurred in species-specific orthogroups and gene-family turnover. Aspiorhynchus laticeps had a larger set of apparent species-specific orthogroups, enriched mainly in oocyte and reproductive processes, and its expanded families and elevated- ω orthogroups were associated with immune, receptor-mediated and membrane-associated functions. By contrast, D. maculatus had fewer species-specific orthogroups enriched for neural and synaptic processes and a contraction-dominated gene-family profile involving host defence, mucosal immunity and chromatin-related processes. The focal contrast did not exceed empirical background variation, and expansion-related computational analysis of gene family evolution (CAFE) estimates were associated with assembly continuity and input-gene properties. These findings indicate that ecologically similar plateau fishes may exhibit different combinations of candidate genomic features, highlighting the joint influence of ecological adaptation and genome history.

items.title: Behavioural responses to a range of mineral salt concentrations in the buff-tailed bumblebee (Bombus terrestris audax).
items.abstract: Mineral micronutrients are essential for maintaining animal physiological function but can induce toxicity at high concentrations. Given this, micronutrients should be increasingly attractive to foraging animals up to an optimal concentration threshold and then be rejected. Little is known about micronutrient detection and regulation in bumblebees. Using a multi-choice foraging assay, we tested the responses of buff-tailed bumblebees ( Bombus terrestris audax ) to artificial nectar containing five concentrations of the mineral salts calcium (Ca), potassium (K), magnesium (Mg) and sodium (Na), alongside a sucrose-only control. Bumblebees avoided the highest concentrations of all minerals tested. For K and Mg, the sucrose control was consumed significantly more than the highest mineral concentration, whereas Na consumption followed a negative quadratic relationship with concentration, peaking at 2000 ppm w/v. This concentration exceeds Na concentrations typically reported in floral nectar, suggesting that the Na response observed here may reflect a mineral appetite not normally satisfied by floral nectar alone. Our findings demonstrate that bumblebees can detect and regulate their intake of essential mineral micronutrients in artificial nectar. This study provides a baseline for investigating mineral regulation, Na limitation and alternative sources of dietary minerals in bumblebee nutritional ecology.

items.title: Photographic assessment of tissue responses to consolidated implantable telemetry tags in southern right whales (Eubalaena australis).
items.abstract: Implantable satellite tags provide critical information on whale movements, but information on tag-related wound healing remains limited. We assessed wound progression using photography in southern right whales ( Eubalaena australis ) instrumented with fully integrated consolidated satellite tags anchored below the fascia (transdermal/subfascial; n = 19) or within the blubber (blubber-only/supra-fascial; n = 22) regularly for up to 70 days post-deployment and opportunistically using long-term resightings up to 71 months post-tagging. External tag wounds followed a predictable sequence of localized swelling, tissue extrusion, remodelling and stabilization. Several wound features varied with tag design and deployment characteristics, including tag surface, anatomical position on the whale and deployment angle. Despite these differences, tissue responses remained localized and progressed predictably, with no photographic evidence of abnormal wound evolution or substantial externally apparent shear-related tissue damage. Contrary to expectations, more superficially implanted blubber-only tags did not produce milder external tissue responses than transdermal tags during the observation period. These findings support standardized photograph-based assessment as a practical approach for evaluating tag effects and guiding refinements in tag design and deployment.

items.title: Evolutionary selection pressures give rise to risky preferences in value-based decision-making.
items.abstract: We are living in a dynamically changing world, where optimal decision-making under uncertainty is linked to the survival of species. However, evolutionary selection pressures that shape value-based decision-making (VBDM, i.e. choosing between available options based on their expected value) under uncertainty have received only limited attention. The current work demonstrates that fitness associated with different VBDM preferences is influenced by the value properties of the environment, as well as the characteristics and the density of competitors in the population. Computational model-based analysis shows that, when there are an increasingly large number of discrete strategies competing for fitness, risk-seeking tendencies can eventually dominate the population. We demonstrate that the strength of these strategies was minimizing suboptimal decisions by tracking the expected value difference between available options more precisely. We discuss the broad implications of our finding across behavioural ecology, behavioural economics and also in relation to the evolutionary basis of vulnerability to psychiatric conditions such as gambling addiction.

items.title: Maximum threshold of eco-geological suitability evaluated with geodiversity of a region: the natural ecological potential applied as a quantitative baseline for ecological status assessment.
items.abstract: Quantitatively assessing the correspondence between ecological status and natural ecological potential is important for ecological protection and sustainable development in ecologically fragile areas. However, most conventional ecological assessments lack a quantitative baseline of natural ecological potential. Thus, it is difficult to determine whether and to what extent ecological restoration is needed, increasing the risk of excessive or insufficient restoration. To address this gap, eco-geological suitability (EGS) was introduced to quantify natural ecological potential by integrating key geodiversity-related indicators. Zhangbei, China, was selected as a case study to evaluate EGS in an ecologically fragile area. Nine eco-geological indicators were integrated using the entropy-weighted Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (EW-TOPSIS) model to quantify EGS. Soil thickness, soil texture, and soil parent material contributed most to EGS. The quantitative identification of areas with relatively high or low EGS provides a baseline for evaluating ecological status. Ecological status was characterized using the Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI). Ecological status and potential correspondence assessment (ESPCA) was conducted using normalized RSEI and EGS values. RSEI was substantially lower than EGS in central and northern Zhangbei, mainly associated with intensive agriculture. RSEI was substantially higher than EGS in the low-potential southern and eastern hills under extensive afforestation. ESPCA enabled the first quantitative identification of potential ecological overload areas associated with excessive afforestation. This study establishes a transferable framework for assessing ecological status and potential correspondence in fragile regions, helping to avoid land degradation risks from inappropriate intervention.

items.title: Unraveling the role of surface structure and a generalized coordination number descriptor in H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> decomposition: insights for green Fenton systems.
items.abstract: The electrocatalytic green Fenton process has attracted increasing attention for wastewater treatment due to its mild operating conditions. However, the influence of surface structure and metal properties on this process remains poorly understood. In this work, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, combined with free energy calculations, were performed to systematically investigate the H 2 O 2 decomposition on various Pt surface structures and other metal surfaces. The catalytic behavior depends on the Pt facets, with Pt(112) being the most active. Step and vacancy sites also substantially lower the activation barriers for H 2 O 2 decomposition compared to flat surfaces. For example, the decomposition barrier becomes barrierless (0.004 eV) on a Pt(120) step surface. Among other transition metals studied (Pd, Ni, Au, Ag, Ir and Co), Co and Ir are promising cathode materials, whereas Au(111) shows the highest activation barrier (0.249 ± 0.005 eV). Although a Brønsted-Evans-Polanyi (BEP) relationship exists between the activation energy and the dissociative adsorption energy on flat surfaces across different metals, we identify a unified and simple descriptor-the local generalized coordination number (GCN)-that directly determines the activation energy for a given metal ( e.g. Pt), regardless of surface structure or site type. These findings provide a theoretical framework for understanding H 2 O 2 decomposition on metal catalysts and rationally designing cathode materials for electrocatalytic green Fenton systems.

items.title: Habitat preference in two European fireflies is reflected in their colour vision.
items.abstract: Colour vision has so far been demonstrated in only a single firefly species, the European Lampyris noctiluca. Lamprohiza splendidula is another widespread European species that often co-occurs with L. noctiluca. First, in field surveys, we quantitatively demonstrated that the former species prefers open habitats, while the latter shows a stronger preference for densely vegetated areas. Second, by measuring compound eye spectral sensitivity with electroretinography and assuming dichromatic colour vision, we used a basic psychophysical colour space model to quantify the physiological experience sensed by L. splendidula and L. noctiluca males viewing the females' bioluminescent signal with eyes adapted to spectral conditions of densely vegetated areas and open areas illuminated by the late twilight sky, when the activity of these fireflies is maximal. Dark-adapted eyes of both species were mostly sensitive to the yellowish green spectral region (559-568 nm), well matching the bioluminescence peak wavelength of the females (556 nm). Recordings on green-adapted eye preparations revealed the presence of a second, blue-sensitive photoreceptor (423-456 nm). We also found that the spectral separation between the blue- and green-sensitive receptors was greater in L. splendidula than in L. noctiluca. According to our colour vision modelling, differences in the spectral sensitivities of the two species' visual systems may help maintain colour vision performance and facilitate female detection in their respective preferred habitats.

items.title: Volatile dialogues between plants and microorganisms.
items.abstract: Covering: up to 2026Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are key mediators of long-distance communication in biological systems. While their roles in plant-insect interactions are well established, emerging evidence highlights their importance in plant-microbe interactions. In this highlight, we discuss the biosynthesis and ecological functions of plant VOCs (pVOCs) and their impact on microbiome assembly and function. We examine how constitutive and stress-induced pVOCs shape microbial community composition and how microbial VOCs (mVOCs) influence plant growth and defense by modulating hormonal and metabolic pathways. We further address the bidirectional nature of volatile-mediated interactions and the challenges associated with studying complex VOC blends in natural environments. Understanding these dynamic volatile dialogues provides new opportunities for microbiome engineering and sustainable crop production.

items.title: The Unified Model Graph: Drawing the Statistical Models of Psychology
items.abstract: Psychologists describe their statistical models with diagrams. The conventions in use, path diagrams, multilevel panels, plate notation, and causal graphs, each grew inside one modeling tradition, and they disagree on basic symbols. As a result, one figure can stand for two different models. An ellipse with three arrows can show a factor model or a latent profile model. A labeled arrow can show a fixed slope or a person-varying slope. A mediation triangle can show a regression decomposition or a causal claim. This article introduces the Unified Model Graph (UMG), a notation built so that the figure identifies the model that was fitted. Three visual cues type every quantity: fill for observed versus latent, shape for continuous versus categorical, and outline for inferential role. Four edge types separate regression, covariance, deterministic, and mixture relations. Plates mark replication, and a badge states whether the figure makes a causal claim. Every well-formed UMG corresponds to exactly one family of distributions, and path diagrams, plate notation, and causal graphs are special cases; the formal results and proofs are in the supplemental material. The accompanying R package \pkg{} builds diagrams from code or from fitted lavaan, lme4, mirt, and brms objects, validates them, translates them to and from lavaan syntax, checks necessary identification conditions, derives testable implications, and generates model-implied data displays. A benchmark of eight R diagramming packages on ten representational features and ten operations locates what the notation adds. All materials, scripts, and outputs are openly archived.

items.title: The Unappreciated Helper: When an AI Facilitation Agent Improves Group Efficiency Despite Poorer User Perceptions
items.abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence make it possible to embed AI facilitation agents in collaborative settings, where they can deliver real-time recommendations based on ongoing group discussions. This experimental study examined how group members perceive a collaborative platform with or without such an agent and evaluated the agent’s effects on group communication and performance. A total of 187 undergraduate psychology students collaborated in 50 groups of three or four members on a digital platform with a synchronous text chat. items.title: Trust miscalibration across cultures and social classes
items.abstract: Do people accurately judge how trustworthy others are? Trust in strangers underpins modern societies, yet people sometimes misjudge others’ trustworthiness, with potentially detrimental implications for social cohesion and public well-being. In pre-registered studies across 23 countries (N = 9,758), we quantify the trust gap: the discrepancy between people’s belief about how many people would return a wallet lost in the street and how many people actually do return it. In line with prior research, people in Western, high-income countries underestimated others’ trustworthiness. However, people in non-Western, low- and middle-income countries overestimated trustworthiness. As anticipated, the trust gap varied with socio-economic status within countries: People of lower socio-economic status were more likely to underestimate others’ trustworthiness than people of higher socio-economic status, consistent with exploitation being more costly for people with fewer resources. Finally, a randomized controlled trial showed that informing participants about actual wallet return rates reduces trust miscalibration. Information provision led those who had underestimated others’ trustworthiness to increase their generalized trust, and those who had overestimated others’ trustworthiness to decrease their generalized trust. These findings demonstrate the value of studying the psychology of trust beyond high-income individuals and societies; and of providing accurate information about everyday cooperation to reduce miscalibrations in how people trust one another.

items.title: Avoiding the worst leaders is more important than getting the best
items.abstract: Society and organizations invest heavily in selecting the best leaders 1, and existing research shows a positivity bias by focusing on the bright side of leadership 2–4. Yet, according to Popper 5, the central question of institutional design is not who should rule, but how to prevent bad leaders from doing too much damage. This raises the question of which approach is more consistent with human psychology: Aim for the best leaders, or avoid the worst? We provide robust evidence for an “avoid-the-worst” principle in human leadership preferences. Although text analyses indicated that the top 100 business schools emphasize good leadership far more than the prevention of bad leadership, actual employee experiences from 9.9 million Glassdoor reviews show that people mentioned their leader 70% more often in the negative than positive section, and negative leader mentions predicted company ratings 1.5 times more strongly. Providing causal evidence, five high-powered experiments across 40 countries (N = 51,433) revealed that people were more willing to sacrifice time and money to avoid a bad leader than obtaining a good leader—across morality and competence, hypothetical and incentivized choice, ideology and culture. People care more about avoiding the worst leaders than getting the best.

items.title: Cognition in older adults with epilepsy: A review of existing interventions and a proposed conceptual framework for integrated care.
items.abstract: Older adults with epilepsy (OAE) represent one of the fastest growing yet least studied subgroups within the epilepsy population, encompassing both individuals with chronic epilepsy persisting into later life and those diagnosed with late onset epilepsy after ages 50-60 years. This population faces a convergence of risk; epilepsy is associated with substantial cognitive comorbidity, with up to 80% of OAE demonstrating cognitive impairment and more than half meeting criteria for mild cognitive impairment (MCI), alongside 1.8-4-fold increased odds of developing dementia. Cognitive dysfunction in OAE is typically multidomain, affecting memory, executive function, and language, and has been associated with demographic, lifestyle, epilepsy, medication, comorbidity, genetic, and neuroimaging factors. Despite this convergence of risk, we identified no adequately tested intervention specifically developed for OAE. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from two historically parallel literatures, epilepsy self-management/rehabilitation programs and cognitive interventions developed for individuals with MCI, to identify strategies that could be merged or adapted for OAE. Epilepsy-focused programs, including foundational self-management models and cognitive interventions, have shown improvements in self-efficacy, quality of life, and select cognitive outcomes, but were evaluated largely in younger and middle-aged adults and have not been developed for or tested in OAE. Similarly, MCI-focused compensatory, restorative, and multimodal interventions offer adaptable strategies for preserving cognitive function but do not account for the complexity of epilepsy management, including antiseizure medication effects, polypharmacy, and seizure-related cognitive fluctuations. Building on this synthesis, we propose a conceptual, not yet tested, integrated intervention framework for OAE that combines epilepsy self-management, comorbidity care, cognition-focused strategies, and lifestyle modification within a unified, multidomain model, alongside recommendations for implementation, outcome assessment, and future trial design. Advancing this field will require deliberate cross-disciplinary integration and a broader conceptualization of successful epilepsy care in later life, one that treats cognitive health as a central therapeutic target alongside seizure control.

items.title: Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination-III (ACE-III): Preliminary psychometric properties, normative data, and normative thresholds for functionally independent French older adults.
items.abstract: The Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination-III (ACE-III) has demonstrated good psychometric properties across different languages and populations. However, psychometric evidence and normative data for the French version remain limited. Therefore, this study aimed to examine the psychometric properties of the ACE-III in functionally independent French older adults and to establish normative data. A total of 103 community-dwelling, functionally independent older adults living in France completed a semistructured interview, the ACE-III, Fried Frailty Phenotype, Geriatric Depression Scale, and University of California Los Angeles Loneliness Scale. Internal consistency, construct validity, and concurrent criterion validity were examined. Regression-based normative equations, normative trajectories, and individualized normative thresholds were developed using age and education. The ACE-III demonstrated good internal consistency (Cronbach's α = .81) and satisfactory construct and concurrent criterion validity evidenced by strong correlations between the global score and subdomains (r = .67 to .92). Age significantly predicted ACE-III performance. Education was retained in the normative models following a theory-driven approach. Regression-based normative equations, normative trajectories, and individualized normative thresholds were established for the total score and each neurocognitive domain. These findings support the use of ACE-III for neurocognitive screening in French older adults. Longitudinal and process-based studies are warranted to further establish its clinical utility.

items.title: Gender differences in perceptions, use, and treatment outcomes of self-guided internet-delivered cognitive behavioural therapy among public safety personnel.
items.abstract: Mental health concerns are prevalent among public safety personnel (PSP), particularly among PSP women, but the role of gender in PSP mental health is not yet well understood. Internet-delivered cognitive behavioural therapy (ICBT) is an effective treatment for various mental health concerns. The current study assessed for gender differences in PSP's perceptions of, use of, and response to ICBT. In this longitudinal single-group open trial, 267 Canadian PSP (53.9% women) participated in self-guided ICBT tailored for PSP. Clients completed questionnaire measures at pre-treatment and 8 weeks post-enrollment. We assessed gender differences using ANCOVAs, independent-samples t-tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, and chi-square tests. Women and men did not differ in posttreatment symptoms of depression, anxiety, or post‑traumatic stress after accounting for pre‑treatment symptoms (all p 's ≥ .26); number of lessons accessed within the ICBT course ( p = .75); or treatment satisfaction (all p 's ≥ .36). Women had more favourable pre-treatment attitudes toward ICBT (all p 's ≤ .002) and were more likely to report prior mental healthcare ( p < .001). These findings support prior literature demonstrating no significant differences in ICBT treatment outcomes between women and men PSP despite more favorable perceptions of it among women PSP.

items.title: Personality traits shape emotion regulation strategies in children with developmental language disorder.
items.abstract: Children with Developmental Language Disorder (DLD) often face socio-emotional challenges beyond language needs, yet the role of personality traits in shaping their emotion regulation (ER) remains underexplored. This study compared ER strategies between children with DLD and typically developing (TD) peers, examined personality predictors of ER and explored the associations between these ER strategies and psychosocial adjustment. Sixty-eight children (DLD = 27; TD = 41), aged 8-12 years, completed self-report measures of personality, ER strategies, including Cognitive Reappraisal (CR) and Expressive Suppression (ES), and psychosocial adjustment. Children with DLD reported higher ES use, whereas no group differences emerged for CR. In the DLD group, higher Extraversion predicted greater use of both CR and ES, Neuroticism predicted lower CR and Agreeableness predicted lower ES. Regarding adjustment, higher ES predicted poorer psychosocial adjustment across both groups. Findings highlight personality influences on ER in children with DLD, with implications for socio-emotional assessment.

items.title: Adverse Event Reporting in Trials of Digital Eating Disorder Interventions: A Systematic Review of Current Practice and Recommendations for the Field.
items.abstract: Objective Balancing the benefits and risks of digital eating disorder interventions is essential for informed decisions regarding their implementation, yet remarkably little is known about the adverse events associated with their use. This systematic review aimed to characterise the frequency, extent, and nature of adverse event reporting in randomized trials of digital eating disorder interventions. Method Databases were searched for randomized trials of digital eating disorder interventions that reported on adverse events. Data on adverse event definitions, assessment, monitoring, management, and reporting were extracted and synthesised qualitatively. Results Only 16 of 53 identified digital intervention trials reported on adverse events. Considerable heterogeneity was observed in adverse event definitions, assessment methods, monitoring procedures, and reporting practices. Reported events from 11 trials ranged from psychological harms to physical complaints, but it was often unclear whether these events were attributable to the intervention. Few trials reported safety procedures, and 10 of the 11 trials that identified adverse events did not describe how these events were managed. Conclusion Adverse event reporting in digital eating disorder trials remains uncommon and highly heterogeneous. We propose a series of recommendations to improve the monitoring, management, and reporting of adverse events in future digital intervention trials.

items.title: Parent-Adolescent and Peer Relationship Quality, Academic Pressure, and Depressive Symptoms in Chinese Late Adolescents: Latent Growth Curve Model Combined With Network Analysis.
items.abstract: Introduction The close relevance between adolescents' academic pressure, depressive symptoms, and interpersonal relationships with parents and peers has been well-documented in extant literature. However, few studies have examined the developmental trajectories of these variables and how they dynamically relate to one another over time. Methods Using data from three waves spaced 8 months apart and integrating Latent Growth Curve Modeling (LGCM) with network analysis, this study explored both the average levels and the rates of change over time in these variables. The participants were Chinese high school students (n = 643, M age = 16.87, SD = 0.55; 44.3% male). Results Results revealed that both depressive symptoms and peer relationship quality increased over time. Depressive symptoms and academic pressure were positively associated at both the average level and in their developmental trajectories, indicating a parallel pattern of co-development. Moreover, average levels of parent-adolescent and peer relationship quality were negatively correlated with the average levels but not the slopes of both depressive symptoms and academic pressure over time. Conclusions These results highlight the importance of monitoring academic and emotional indicators simultaneously, rather than in isolation, to better understand and support adolescents' adaptive functioning. Interpersonal relationship quality emerges as a potential candidate for identifying adolescents who may be at risk for elevated academic pressure and depressive symptoms.

items.title: Bullying Situational Cues and Adolescents' Bystander Behaviors: Associations With Empathy and Moral Disengagement.
items.abstract: Introduction Bystander defending behaviors are regarded as a key component in preventing bullying among adolescents. Although previous research has primarily focused on individual factors influencing bystander behaviors, less is known about whether the way a bullying episode is presented, and the socio-emotional information available through that presentation, is associated with adolescents' bystander responses. To address this issue, the present study examined how empathy, moral disengagement, and the presentation modality of a traditional bullying episode were associated with bystander behaviors. Methods In the pre-study, a factor analysis was conducted with 789 students, which revealed four stable bystander behavior dimensions in traditional bullying: aggressive defending, constructive defending, remaining an outsider, and reinforcing the bully. A subsequent behavioral experiment was conducted with an independent sample of 366 students, in which the same bullying episode was presented through three modalities: text, audio, and video. Participants' bystander behaviors, empathy (affective and cognitive), and moral disengagement were then measured. Results Two-part models, distinguishing the occurrence and intensity of each bystander response, showed that presentation modality was associated with several bystander responses. Compared with text, audio and video were associated with a higher likelihood of constructive defending; audio was associated with a higher likelihood of aggressive defending; and audio and video were associated with greater intensity of aggressive defending. Audio was also associated with lower intensity of remaining an outsider and a lower likelihood of reinforcing the bully. Affective empathy and moral disengagement showed differentiated associations across the four bystander response dimensions. Conclusion These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing bystander response dimensions and considering how socio-emotional information is presented when examining adolescents' responses to traditional bullying.

items.title: Incidental social category information influences scene evaluation and memory across cultures.
items.abstract: Visual cognition in naturalistic settings is inherently social, yet much of what is known about social categorisation derives from tasks in which group membership is made explicitly relevant. The present study examined whether social category information influences visual evaluation and memory when it is incidental to the task and embedded within visual scenes, and whether these effects differ across cultures. Two hundred and thirty-one participants from East Asian (China), South Asian (India) and European (United Kingdom and Poland) cultural groups evaluated images depicting either ingroup or outgroup individuals, followed by an unexpected memory test. Racial attitudes and the quality and quantity of intergroup contact were also measured. Images depicting ingroup members were evaluated more positively and remembered more accurately than those depicting outgroup individuals. Memory for images containing outgroup (but not ingroup) individuals was selectively associated with perceived interest. Negative racial attitudes predicted less favourable evaluation of outgroup images, but only among participants reporting lower intergroup contact. There was no evidence that these effects were moderated by participant nationality. Together, these findings suggest that social category information can influence evaluation and memory even when it is task irrelevant, with effects shaped by racial attitudes and intergroup contact.

items.title: The smiling side of politics: smile asymmetry predicts the left-cheek pose in political portraits.
items.abstract: The left-cheek posing bias has been attributed to greater emotional expressivity on the left side of the face. Politicians also tend to adopt left-cheek poses in their portraits, possibly to strategically convey emotional signals to others. We tested whether smile asymmetry predicts posing direction in political portraits. Using campaign photographs of 1,107 candidates in a Japanese national election, we quantified left- and right-sided zygomaticus major activity using image analysis. Candidates showed an overall leftward asymmetry in smiling. More importantly, stronger leftward smile asymmetry predicted a greater likelihood of adopting a left-cheek rather than a right-cheek pose, irrespective of political orientation. These findings provide evidence for an association between lateral posing asymmetries and facial emotional expression.

items.title: Development of the Sexual Experiences Survey-Victimization-Short Forms (SES-V-SF) and a Psychometric Evaluation of SES-V Standard and Short Forms.
items.abstract: The Sexual Experiences Survey-Victimization (SES-V) was substantially revised in 2024 to broaden the range of sexual exploitation victimization assessed. Although the revised SES-V offers important advantages, its length may limit its usefulness in some research and applied contexts. The purpose of this study was to develop a short form of the SES-V and to evaluate the psychometric performance of both the short-form and the standard-form SES-V. Using a predefined process, we selected two to four items from each SES-V module. These items captured 89% to 96% of the victimization reported within each module in a national dataset. We then recruited 1,103 adults through CloudResearch, oversampling groups previously underrepresented in SES-V research. Participants were randomized to complete the standard-form SES-V or one of two short-form versions along with measures to assess convergent validity. A subsample of participants ( n = 640) completed the same SES-V form again two weeks later to assess test-retest reliability. The short forms performed well and were comparable to the standard form in convergent validity and test-retest reliability. Endorsement rates on the short forms were similar to the standard form across three of four modules, and the short forms required less than half the administration time (i.e. a median of under five minutes). Findings were generally consistent across demographic subgroups. This study provides psychometric support for the short forms and additional psychometric evidence for the standard form. Future research should further examine whether the short forms capture the full range of victimization across diverse populations.

items.title: Identifying important behavioural change techniques to deliver in communication partner training for people with cognitive-communication disorder following acquired brain injury: A national e-Delphi of UK speech and language therapists.
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo establish consensus regarding the behaviour change techniques considered most important when delivering communication partner training to people with acquired brain injury and their communication partners.DesignThree-round e-Delphi. Participants rated 86 behaviour change techniques linked to 16 mechanisms-of-action using a 9-point Likert scale. Consensus for techniques was defined as >70% agreement. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, latent content and sentiment analysis.SettingUK clinical practice in acquired brain injury rehabilitation.ParticipantsSpeech and language therapists working with people with acquired brain injury.ResultsA total of 118 speech and language therapists participated in Round 1, 90 participated in each of Rounds 2 and 3, and 81 completed all three rounds. Consensus was reached on 80 behaviour change technique-to-mechanism of action links, representing 47 distinct techniques. Ratings did not differ by years' experience or clinical setting. Most agreement (>90%) was linked to setting goals, practising skills and goal feedback. Qualitative comments were largely positive (67%), especially for goal setting and skills practice. Therapist reservations focused on material and monetary rewards, while therapist comments on feedback techniques underlined a need for individualised and tailored training.ConclusionsThis is the first UK e-Delphi of speech and language therapists in acquired brain injury. Behaviour change theory provided a framework to identify key techniques, highlighting the complexity of training. Analysis revealed diverse attitudes and areas for further consideration. Consensus on the importance of communication partner training techniques offers an opportunity to develop a clinically relevant programme with potential for uptake in clinical practice.

items.title: Comparison of Personal and General Views on Aging Between UK Dementia Caregivers and Non-Caregivers.
items.abstract: IntroductionAlthough positive Views on Aging (VoA) are important for the well-being of dementia caregivers, maintaining them while being in frequent/constant contact with a person with significant cognitive and physical decline may be difficult. This cross-sectional study investigated the associations of caregiving status with VoA and the moderating roles of age and sex.MethodsParticipants were 259 family dementia caregivers matched with 548 non-caregivers (1:2 matching for 229 participants and 1:3 matching for 30 participants). Indicators of VoA were Felt Age, Awareness of Age-Related Change, Non-Essentialist Beliefs about Aging, and Expectations Regarding Aging.ResultsCompared to non-caregivers, caregivers had an older felt age, perceived fewer age-related gains, perceived more age-related losses, and reported more essentialist beliefs about aging.DiscussionFamily dementia caregivers may be at risk of negative VoA. Because this may have negative consequences on caregivers' well-being, the support offered to caregivers should address, among other things, their VoA.

items.title: Psychological Assets and Cardiovascular Health in Adulthood: A Mixed Methods Investigation.
items.abstract: Background Psychological risk factors like depression increase risk for poor cardiovascular outcomes but psychological assets like purpose in life are protective and linked to reduced risk of cardiovascular events. However, most assets are investigated individually, and not all have been explored in relation to cardiovascular health (CVH). This study used mixed methods to assess multiple psychological assets and evaluate associations with CVH 12 years later. Methods Data came from 2092 participants in the National Child Development Study. At age 50 years, participants wrote open-ended responses describing their futures. Two trained researchers qualitatively coded each response by rating them for 7 commonly assessed psychological assets (1=not at all; 7=very): optimism, purpose, satisfaction, personal growth, agency, enjoyment, and overall positivity. At age 62, CVH behavioral factors (exercise, smoking status, sleep) were self-reported; CVH clinical factors (blood pressure, lipids, glucose, body weight) were measured during nurse visits. Following Life's Essential 8 guidelines, CVH components were combined into total CVH scores. Linear regressions examined associations between each age 50 asset and age 62 CVH scores, adjusting for age 50 confounders. Results All age 50 assets were positively associated with better CVH scores 12 years later, accounting for sociodemographic characteristics and word counts ( p ≤0.05). Purpose (b=0.81 [95% CI, 0.33-1.29]) and personal growth (b=0.82 [95% CI, 0.34-1.20]) showed the strongest associations with CVH in fully adjusted models. Conclusions Higher levels of most midlife psychological assets were linked with better CVH over time, suggesting multiple paths to health protection. These findings highlight assets that could be prevention targets.

items.title: The Stockholm Declaration advocates a broad approach for reformation of science publishing in a complex stakeholder world.
items.abstract: Because integrity and trustworthiness of science rely on the attitude and behaviour of scientists and publishers, the recent flood of fake publishing and rising publishing costs motivated us to propose an extensive reformation of science publishing. Our Stockholm Declaration suggested 34 concrete actions to counter this unhealthy development, with a call to action for science and educational institutions, science academies and organizations, funders and publishers to unite in an effort to achieve fundamental changes. However, Csaba Szabo argued in a comment that the Stockholm Declaration 'fundamentally misdiagnosed' this science crisis and that a 'true reform' would require the publishing infrastructure to be rebuilt as a public utility with open access and post-publication review. Open access is certainly a desired goal for the future because science and science communication are a public good. However, post-publication reviews are problematic, leaving many poor studies unquestioned. By contrast, the Stockholm Declaration proposes to gradually transform publishing systems in a complex landscape of academic disciplines and publishers with different publishing models in a fast-moving AI world. Such a complex ecosystem requires a broad range of actions to be implemented as quickly as possible, especially independent integrity screening of scientific manuscripts and publications and adjustment of academia's assessment systems of scientific achievements.

items.title: A systematic review of the challenges experienced by parents of multiples.
items.abstract: Background In recent years, growing attention has been directed towards the postnatal challenges experienced by parents of multiples. However, no systematic review has synthesised these challenges comprehensively across multiple domains (psychological, physical, financial and healthcare-related challenges). Aim This review aimed to systematically identify, explore and synthesise the postnatal challenges experienced by parents of multiples within the UK. Methods The review was conducted in accordance with the 2024 Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) guidelines and followed the PRISMA framework for study identification, screening, inclusion and exclusion. A quality appraisal of included studies was also undertaken. Results Nine studies with varied methodological designs met the inclusion criteria. Thematic synthesis revealed a range of postnatal challenges, which were categorised into four domains: psychological (e.g. stress, guilt), physical (e.g. exhaustion, feeding difficulties), healthcare (e.g. lack of specialist support) and financial (e.g. increased childcare costs). Conclusion These findings highlight the complex and cumulative nature of parenting multiples. They demonstrate the need for tailored psychological interventions, enhanced professional training and revised postnatal guidance that better reflects the lived realities of families with multiples. Future research should support this by addressing gaps in evidence, particularly around daily accessibility challenges and the perspectives of healthcare professionals.

items.title: Video Game Preferences, Behaviors, Motivations, and Empathy Development in Adults With and Without Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Cross-Sectional and Experimental Pilot Study.
items.abstract: This study examined video game use, motivations, and effects among adults with and without autism spectrum disorder (ASD). We compared gaming practices and motivations (Study 1) and evaluated whether playing the social simulation game The Sims was linked to changes in psychosocial skills, particularly empathy (Study 2). Study 1 used a cross-sectional design with 126 typically developing (TD) adults and 77 adults with ASD, who completed measures of gaming habits, the Videogaming Motives Questionnaire, the Empathy Quotient (EQ), and the Systemizing Quotient (SQ). Study 2 was an intervention in which 43 participants (13 ASD, 30 TD) played The Sims for 20 min daily over 5 weeks. EQ and SQ were assessed pre- and post-intervention. In Study 1, adults with ASD preferred simulation games (p = 0.024), while TD adults favored action/adventure (p = 0.017) and sports (p = 0.010). Adults with ASD reported lower motivations for violent rewards (p = 0.028), competition (p = 0.004), and social interaction (p = 0.004), but higher coping motivation (p = 0.006). No differences emerged for gaming time or platform use. In Study 2, the ASD group showed a within-group increase in cognitive empathy (one-tailed p = 0.026), while no other significant effects were found. In this pilot study, limited exposure to a commercial game was associated with an exploratory increase in cognitive empathy in autistic adults; this finding should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample and absence of a control condition. These results highlight the potential of video games as tools for socio-emotional development in ASD.

items.title: Common early-life exposure of the colorectal epithelium to the microbiome-derived mutagen colibactin
items.abstract: Colibactin is a mutagen produced by bacterial strains in the colorectal microbiomes of some healthy people. It generates somatic mutations characterised by the mutational signatures SBS88 and ID18 in normal human colorectal epithelial cells in vivo. Increasing prevalence of colibactin mutagenesis during the 20th century is hypothesised to have caused recent international increases in early-onset colorectal cancer incidence. Here, we establish the early-life prevalence, timing, mutation burdens and distribution through the colon of colibactin mutagenesis by sequencing normal colorectal epithelial cell genomes to detect SBS88 and ID18 in 90 healthy and inflammatory bowel disease affected children and adolescents. Colibactin-induced mutagenesis was present in ~43%, with or without inflammatory bowel disease. It usually begins shortly after birth and ceases by age five years. Mutation burdens are higher in the left than right colon and show substantial variation, with some children displaying mutation burdens comparable to those of healthy non-exposed individuals greater than 60 years of age. The future public health implications of this common early life mutagen exposure will depend on clarification of its role in colorectal cancer causation.

items.title: “A slippery slope, then this pushed it off the edge": The Psychological Impact of the UK Supreme Court ruling on the Meaning of Sex in the Equality Act for Trans and Gender Diverse People
items.abstract: Background: Following the UK Supreme Court's For Women Scotland (FWS) ruling, concerns have emerged regarding its implications for the health and wellbeing of transgender and gender-diverse (TGD) people. Although structural stigma is increasingly recognised as a determinant of health inequalities among marginalised populations, little is known about how major legal and policy changes influence psychological wellbeing within TGD communities. This study examined perceptions of structural stigma following the FWS ruling and investigated its association with mental health, suicidality, loneliness, social gender-role recognition, and community resilience. Method: Two convergent studies were conducted. Study 1 involved a qualitative analysis of asynchronous audio interviews with UK-based TGD adults exploring experiences and perceptions of the FWS ruling. Reflexive thematic analysis was used to identify key themes. Study 2 utilised a cross-sectional survey of UK TGD adults to examine associations between perceived structural stigma, loneliness, mental health, suicidality, social gender-role recognition, and community resilience. Structural equation modelling was used to test loneliness as a mediating mechanism and community resilience as a moderating factor. Results: Across both studies, participants perceived the FWS ruling as contributing to structural stigma by undermining social recognition, belonging, and feelings of citizenship. Qualitative findings suggested that participants responded to these experiences through heightened vigilance, changes to public self-presentation, and withdrawal from social environments. Quantitative analyses indicated that greater perceived structural stigma was associated with poorer mental health, higher suicidality, lower social gender-role recognition, and greater loneliness. Loneliness emerged as a significant mediator of these relationships. Although community resilience did not moderate associations between loneliness and mental health, greater levels of community resilience were associated with lower loneliness and suicidality. Conclusions: Findings provide the first empirical evidence that the FWS ruling may function as a form of structural stigma with important implications for the wellbeing of TGD people in the UK. Loneliness appears to be a key mechanism through which structural stigma influences psychological outcomes, while connection to LGBTQ+ communities may serve as an important psychosocial resource. The findings highlight the need for continued monitoring of the mental health impacts of legal and policy changes affecting TGD populations and for interventions that strengthen belonging, social connection, and community support.

items.title: Trends in acute malnutrition during a decade of conflict in Yemen from 2015 to 2026
items.abstract: Abstract Objective Malnutrition remains a critical public health concern in Yemen. This analysis reviewed whether acute malnutrition among children under five in Yemen has systematically changed over a decade of conflict (2015–2026), described governorate-level trajectories, and examined the influence of survey method on trend estimation. Methods We compiled all available anthropometric nutrition surveys in Yemen, from 2015 to 2026, and analysed time trends in GAM and SAM. Ordinary least squares (OLS) regression and linear mixed-effects models were performed to estimate temporal trends in GAM and SAM. Descriptive, paired-method, and ecological sensitivity analyses pooled all survey methods were also conducted. Results Among comparable SMART-WHZ observations (n = 67), neither GAM nor SAM showed a national trend (GAM: OLS − 0.033 pp/year, p = 0.879; mixed-effects − 0.124 pp/year, p = 0.335; SAM + 0.002 pp/year, p = 0.975; mixed-effects − 0.015, p = 0.748). Pooling all methods (n = 107) suggested an apparent increase (GAM + 0.37 pp/year, p = 0.119; SAM + 0.232 pp/year, p = 0.025) that disappeared after adjustment for survey method. MICS estimates exceeded paired SMART-WHZ estimates (Wilcoxon p = 0.011; n = 22 pairs), and WHZ-based GAM exceeded MUAC-based estimates by 4.64 pp. In total, 32.3% of observations fell within the WHO Emergency GAM band and 27.7% within the Serious band. Prevalence was higher in lowland/coastal than highland or urban zones, with heterogeneous governorate trajectories. Conclusion Acute malnutrition in Yemen remained at severe levels throughout 2015–2026 with no clear evidence of a sustained national increase or decrease. The pattern was one of persistently high prevalence, short-term fluctuations, and recurrent hotspots, with substantial geographic heterogeneity. These findings underscore the need for targeted, context-specific programming, harmonised longitudinal surveillance, and stronger linkage between anthropometric data and contextual drivers to detect genuine change while accounting for geographical and seasonal variation.

items.title: Nested cell-level voltage-window selection for partial-charge state-of-health estimation of lithium-ion batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Estimating the state of health (SOH) of lithium-ion batteries from a short part of the charging curve is attractive for battery management systems, because vehicles and devices are rarely charged from empty to full. Published errors are often very low, but the voltage window and the data split are usually chosen by the authors, and the sensitivity to measurement conditions is seldom reported. We study a simple pipeline: five features from a voltage window of the constant-current charging phase feed a ridge regression, and the window is selected using only the training cells (nested leave-one-cell-out). On three public datasets of LCO/NMC-type cells (lithium cobalt oxide or nickel–manganese–cobalt oxide cathodes; NASA, 4 cells; CALCE, 6 cells; Oxford, 8 cells), the mean root-mean-square error (RMSE) of SOH is 3.01, 2.28 and 0.72 %, against 5.9, 2.8 and 2.3 % for a linear model that knows only the cycle index. Ridge regression is statistically indistinguishable from random forest, gradient boosting and support-vector regression (paired Wilcoxon \(\:p\approx\:0.42\), 18 cells) and is much cheaper. The best window differs between datasets; a window shift of 0.02 V increases the error by a factor of 1.6 to 3.3 on NASA and Oxford; 10 mV of voltage noise doubles the NASA error unless the voltage is filtered; and models do not transfer between datasets. On 119 lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells (Supplementary Material), ridge does not beat the cycle-index baseline, and tree ensembles are only moderately better.

items.title: Food Insecurity Patterns and Risk of Poor Glycemic Control, Acute Complications of Diabetes, and Ability to Obtain Diabetes Technologies in Youth and Young Adults With Youth-Onset Type 1 Diabetes.
items.abstract: Objective Household food insecurity (FI) is linked cross-sectionally to diabetes-related outcomes. However, prior studies have not fully considered temporal relationships or the evolving nature of FI. We explored the patterns of FI and associations with hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), severe hypoglycemia, diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), health care use, and the ability to obtain diabetes technologies among youth and young adults (YYAs) with youth-onset type 1 diabetes (T1D). Research design and methods Longitudinal data (2016-2022) from 956 YYAs with T1D were analyzed using multivariable logistic and linear regression. Food security was measured thrice (t1, t2, and t3) with the Household Food Security Survey Module and patterned into persistent food security (PFS), intermittent FI (IFI), and persistent FI (PFI). We evaluated FI patterns derived from repeated assessments with follow-up diabetes-related outcomes. Results The prevalence of IFI was 20.8% and PFI was 7.7%. Compared with YYAs experiencing PFS, the odds of inability to obtain continuous glucose monitors were higher for IFI (1.9, 95% CI 1.1, 3.3) and PFI groups (2.3, 1.0, 5.2), independent of individual characteristics. PFI was additionally associated with higher HbA1c (β = 0.6, P 9.0%, 3.0-fold higher odds of diabetes-related emergency department visits, and 2.5-fold higher odds of inability to obtain an insulin pump. Conclusions Among YYAs with T1D, IFI and PFI over time both seem to be associated with severely impaired ability to maintain glycemic targets, increasing the risk of adverse outcomes.

items.title: Iron deficiency activates the GABARAP-FLCN/FNIP1-TFEB axis to promote pexophagy.
items.abstract: Peroxisomes are dynamic metabolic organelles whose dysfunction results in severe diseases. The homeostasis of peroxisomes is also ensured through pexophagy, a type of selective autophagy targeting these organelles. Pexophagy can be activated by several stressors, such as starvation, mTOR inhibition, and iron deficiency. However, the regulatory mechanisms underlying pexophagy are poorly characterized. Here, we identify a novel regulatory axis of iron deficiency-induced pexophagy, which preferentially engages GABARAP among the mATG8 family members. Comparative analysis of the mATG8 interactomes reveals that upon iron depletion, GABARAP selectively interacts with the tumor suppressor complex FLCN/FNIP1 triggering the activation of the autophagy and lysosome transcription factors TFEB and TFE3, thus promoting efficient cargo degradation. Our findings thus identify the GABARAP-FLCN/FNIP1 axis as a molecular sensor that bridges iron deficiency and TFEB/TFE3 activation to prime pexophagy execution.

items.title: Decision making around end-of-life: Focused ethnography in two intensive care units in Vietnam.
items.abstract: Literature on the quality of death and dying has predominantly drawn on high-income contexts, while much less is known about end-of-life care in low-middle-income settings. In Vietnam, policy and practice around palliative and end-of-life care has not kept pace with the ageing of the population. This study explores factors influencing end-of-life decision making in intensive care units (ICUs) where formal protocols are lacking. This analysis is a part of a larger ethnographic study examining vital sign monitoring in two ICUs in Vietnam, including observations, informal conversations and formal interviews with healthcare workers. In addition to learning about the care practices around vital sign monitoring, we noted the various complexities that influenced physicians and family members' end-of-life decision making in these contexts. Factors included patients' prognosis, family wishes, cultural practices surrounding death and financial considerations. Financial concerns were a significant factor in discontinuing treatment, particularly for uninsured patients. The lack of accessible out-of-hospital care made it difficult for patients to spend their final moments at home with their families, which is important in Vietnamese cultures. This paper sheds light on the preferences and practices of families and staff at the end-of-life with the longer-term goal of improving end-of-life care across Vietnam.

items.title: IFT20 mediates trafficking of ciliary proteins to support mammalian motile ciliogenesis in testicular efferent ductules and respiratory tract.
items.abstract: Intraflagellar transport (IFT) is essential for ciliary assembly and maintenance. IFT20, a component of the IFT-B complex, participates in cargo trafficking during primary cilium and sperm flagellum formation. However, its role in multiciliated cells (MCCs) remains unclear. Here, we investigated IFT20 function using mice with conditional deletion of Ift20 in FOXJ1-expressing cells. Most conditional knockout (cKO) mice survived to adulthood and exhibited reduced body weight without apparent left-right asymmetry defects or hydrocephalus. Adult cKO males were subfertile, with significantly shortened motile cilia and reduced ciliary beat frequency (CBF) in the efferent ductules (EDs). Ultrastructural analysis revealed abnormalities in peripheral doublet microtubules, inner and outer dynein arms, and the central pair apparatus. These defects were accompanied by ED luminal dilation and sperm aggregation, along with seminiferous tubule dilation, testicular atrophy, and increased germ cell degeneration. In contrast, tracheal cilia were only slightly shortened and exhibited reduced CBF without obvious ultrastructural abnormalities. Interestingly, immunofluorescence analysis revealed abnormal accumulation of the central apparatus proteins SPAG16 and SPAG17, outer dynein arm protein DNAI2, and inner dynein arm protein DNAH2 in the apical cytoplasm of ciliated cells in both EDs and trachea. Together, these findings demonstrate that IFT20 is critical for maintaining somatic motile cilia structure and function, with more pronounced defects in the EDs. The apical accumulation of axonemal proteins further suggests that IFT20 facilitates their trafficking from the cytoplasm into motile axonemes.

items.title: Sleep as a partial mediator of the association between residential greenness and biological ageing: A population-based study in China.
items.abstract: Residential greenness has been associated with healthier ageing, but its relationship with sleep behaviours and the role of sleep in this association remain unclear. This study examined associations among residential greenness, sleep indicators, and biological age in middle-aged and older Chinese adults. This population-based study included 8,527 Chinese adults aged 45 years and older. Residential greenness was assessed using city-level normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI). Sleep indicators included night-time sleep duration, nap duration, total sleep duration, and categorical sleep measures. Biological age was estimated from chronological age and eight blood-based or physiological biomarkers. Multivariable regression and mediation analyses were used to examine the associations and potential mediating role of sleep behaviours. Higher NDVI was associated with lower biological age, with each 0.1-unit increase linked to a 0.529-year reduction. Longer night-time sleep was associated with younger biological age, whereas longer nap duration was associated with older biological age. Higher NDVI was modestly associated with longer night-time sleep and shorter naps. Mediation analyses indicated that night-time sleep duration, nap duration, and long naps partially mediated the association between NDVI and biological age, accounting for 2.7%, 5.7%, and 3.3% of the total effect, respectively. Residential greenness was associated with younger biological age. Sleep behaviours may partly explain the link between greener environments and healthier biological ageing.

items.title: Structural basis of avian-to-human receptor-binding adaptation in H9Ny influenza A virus hemagglutinin.
items.abstract: The receptor-binding specificity of influenza A virus (IAV) hemagglutinin (HA) is a major determinant for viral host tropism, enabling interspecies transmission. The molecular determinants for receptor-binding properties of HAs vary among different IAV subtypes. In this study, we performed a comprehensive analysis on the receptor-binding determinants of IAV subtype H9 HA and found that the receptor-binding characteristics of H9 subtype influenza viruses have exhibited temporal variations over decades. Q226L (hydrophobicity switch) substitution in the 220-loop is the key determinant for H9 subtype HA to acquire human receptor-binding preference. The amino acid residues of the 130-loop greatly affect the binding of HA protein to canonical receptors. Organoid infection models demonstrate that all three representative viral strains could infect human bronchial epithelial organoids. These findings increase our understanding of the molecular determinants of receptor-binding properties of different HA subtypes and call for the surveillance and response to potential influenza outbreaks, or even epidemics/pandemics.IMPORTANCEInfluenza A virus (IAV) subtype H9 poses persistent zoonotic spillover risks due to its adaptive receptor-binding capacity, yet the molecular determinants remain incompletely defined. This study systematically characterizes the receptor-binding determinants of H9 hemagglutinin over decades of viral evolution and identifies two critical functional domains: the 220-loop residue Q226L substitution, which serves as the key mutation conferring human receptor-binding preference, and the 130-loop residues that predominantly modulate canonical receptor-binding affinity. Functional assays using human bronchial epithelial organoids further confirm the robust human infection ability of prevalent H9 viral strains. These findings clarify the molecular mechanisms underlying H9 IAV host tropism and adaptive evolution, provide critical theoretical evidence for targeted influenza surveillance and pandemic preparedness against emerging H9 influenza outbreaks.

items.title: Sheep or cattle fecal contamination? Using long-read amplicon sequencing for fecal source attribution and apportionment.
items.abstract: Fecal contamination of freshwater poses a risk to environmental and human health. Accurately attributing contamination to specific sources is critical for remediation. However, discriminating between closely related ruminants, sheep and cattle, remains a challenge. This study evaluated the use of f ast e xpectation m a ximization microbial s ource t racking (FEAST) and mitochondrial and microbial source tracking (MST) qPCR markers for fecal source identification. The focus was differentiation between cattle and sheep sources using a spiked laboratory experiment with known fecal inputs and field testing of samples from an agricultural stream. Sheep and cattle fecal samples were diluted into urban stream water, with spiked samples containing either single or mixed feces at varying ratios. Field samples were collected from a rural stream where adjacent sheep and cattle grazed. Full-length 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing of spiked fecal and field samples was conducted, and the resulting taxonomies were used as input to FEAST; the results were also compared with those of MST analysis. Single cattle or sheep fecal sources could be identified by FEAST, but thresholds need to be established to avoid misattribution. FEAST results for field samples were consistent with ruminant and cattle MST markers, but the low sensitivity of cattle/sheep MST markers complicated comparisons. Using taxonomic groupings for FEAST analysis gave greater discrimination. However, apportionment of source contributions was not consistent within groupings. Inclusion of an aquatic source reduced misattribution of non-fecal microflora to animal sources. FEAST is a promising tool for source tracking but struggles to differentiate between mixed sources with similar fecal microflora and to produce accurate source apportionment.IMPORTANCEFecal contamination of freshwater is an issue for communities across the world because it has both environmental and health consequences. Therefore, differentiating between potential sources of contamination is important for both remediation and risk assessment. Microbes from fecal material are one of the main indicators used to track fecal contamination and identify its potential sources. In recent years, the use of the entire gut microflora to determine the origins of fecal contamination events has become a promising area of research and has the potential to overcome the low sensitivity of ruminant host-associated MST markers in field samples. The research demonstrated that an algorithm developed for this purpose could identify contamination from single sources. However, when applied to mixed-source scenarios, it struggled to differentiate between the similar microflora of livestock ruminants, cattle and sheep. Inclusion of an aquatic source was important for reducing misattribution of non-fecal microflora to animal sources.
