items.title: Experimental disturbance-induced functional shifts in protected soft-sediment benthic communities.
items.abstract: Benthic communities form the foundation of food webs in coastal and shelf seas worldwide. However, these communities face severe threats from anthropogenic bottom-disturbing activities. Marine protected areas (MPAs) effectively safeguard benthic communities against such disturbances. Nevertheless, the effectiveness of MPAs in recovering benthic communities in highly dynamic soft-bottom areas is widely debated, as these communities are thought to be adapted to natural dynamics and therefore resistant to human impacts. In this study, we examined whether MPAs in highly dynamic seas support sensitive communities that are affected by bottom-disturbing fishing gear. Utilizing a before-after, control-impact (BACI) experimental design, we investigated the effects of disturbance caused by shrimp trawl gear on macrozoobenthic communities within MPAs in a dynamic coastal soft-bottom sea over 2 years. We assessed changes in taxonomic and functional diversity and community composition across three levels of trawling intensity and frequency (low intensity and high frequency, high intensity and low frequency, and high intensity and high frequency) and compared the changes with those in undisturbed control areas. The study was carried out in the less dynamic areas of the study system, where we found that even lighter gear altered functional diversity and community composition, whereas taxonomic diversity was unaffected. Taxonomic and functional turnover increased most under frequent disturbance. Moreover, disturbance reduced the recovery of long-lived species, whereas scavengers and predators increased at the cost of suspension feeders. Our findings demonstrate that anthropogenic disturbance remains a relevant ecological pressure, even in areas that appear resilient through their dynamic nature, and thus, MPAs provide ecological benefits by protecting sensitive and functionally important species. As taxonomic metrics fail to detect these changes, impact assessments and MPA management should incorporate functional traits to better evaluate protection effectiveness and identify communities and ecological functions that require targeted conservation.

items.title: Growth-reproduction trade-offs in woody plants are common but changing: a meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Growth and reproduction draw on a common resource pool, yet empirical studies of woody plants report widely differing relationships between seed production and growth. We synthesized 685 estimates from 78 studies covering 79 woody species, with study locations concentrated at northern temperate latitudes, to test how growth-reproduction correlations vary across time, species, and environments. Growth and reproduction measured within the same year were negatively correlated, suggesting an immediate cost of reproduction. Given the limited and uneven taxonomic sampling, phylogenetic patterns in growth-reproduction correlations remain uncertain. The correlations were not systematically related to functional traits or climate. Trade-offs were strongest in species with high interannual variability in seed production and weakened markedly over recent decades in these species. Together, these results show that growth-reproduction trade-offs in woody plants are common but not fixed, and that shifts in reproductive variability under environmental change can alter how trees balance growth and reproduction, with consequences for long-term forest functioning.

items.title: Beyond B-DNA: the biology of Z-DNA and Z-RNA recognition.
items.abstract: Z-DNA and Z-RNA (Z-NAs) have long been regarded as rare alternative structures of uncertain in vivo relevance. However, accumulating evidence demonstrates their formation across diverse biological systems. Only a limited number of proteins have been validated as direct, conformation-selective Z-NA binders. Proteins may also stabilize Z-states or promote transitions into or out of them, respond to the surrounding topological conditions, or associate indirectly with Z-prone loci. In this article, we propose five potentially overlapping modes of engagement for Z-NA-associated proteins: conformation readers, stabilizers, conformational remodelers, topology-coupled factors, and context-dependent interactors. By linking canonical Zα readers with topoisomerases, chromatin factors, immune sensors, and viral antagonists, this framework provides a basis for mechanistic classification, experimental validation, and future discovery.

items.title: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum in vegetable food waste valorization: A Swiss army knife spanning plant polysaccharide transformation and comprehensive metabolic versatility.
items.abstract: Lactic acid bacteria (LAB), particularly Lactiplantibacillus plantarum (formerly Lactobacillus plantarum), are promising microbial platforms for the sustainable bioconversion and valorization of vegetable food wastes and agro-industrial residues. Their metabolic versatility and adaptability allow them to transform plant-derived biomass into diverse value-added bioproducts, supporting circular bioeconomy and biorefinery strategies. While previous studies have extensively addressed L. plantarum genetic diversity, health effects and role in food fermentation, increasing attention has turned on its application in biomass utilization and waste-to-value processes. This review critically examines current efforts to employ L. plantarum in plant waste valorization, identifying major technological and biological bottlenecks while highlighting opportunities for a more rational exploitation of this species in bioconversion processes. However, the limited integration of genomic and functional data remains a key obstacle to developing more efficient and predictable valorization strategies. To complement the literature analysis, a pan-genome exploration of 348 publicly available genomes was conducted, focusing on carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) as an example of how genomic information may support strain selection and process design. This analysis revealed a conserved genetic core alongside a highly variable accessory genome, together with pronounced differences among strains in their CAZyme repertoires. This genomic diversity suggests substantial variation in carbohydrate-processing potential and may contribute to differences in fermentation performance across different matrices. While these observations require experimental validation and cannot directly predict performance in complex substrates, they illustrate how genome-informed approaches may help guide future screening strategies beyond the largely empirical methods currently reported.

items.title: Genetic diversity, selective constraint and phylogenetic signal of the melanocortin 1 receptor (MC1R) gene across Lagomorpha.
items.abstract: Coat color contributes to camouflage and fitness in mammals, yet the adaptative and evolutionary variation of the melanocortin-1 receptor (MC1R) gene, a key gene in pigmentation, remains incompletely characterized across Lagomorpha. We sequenced the complete 954-bp MC1R coding region in 19 species representing 14 Leporidae (Bunolagus monticularis, Lepus californicus, L. castroviejoi, L. capensis, L. europaeus, L. granatensis, L. saxatilis, L. timidus, L. townsendii, Oryctolagus cuniculus, Pentalagus furnessi, Romerolagus diazi, Sylvilagus floridanus, and S. nuttallii) and five Ochotonidae (Ochotona alpina, O. dauurica, O. hyperborea, O. macrotis, and O. pusilla) and compared the resulting alleles with public sequences. The diversity dataset comprised 21 haplotypes (Hd = 0.987), with 249 variable sites and marked sequence divergence between families (F ST = 0.667). Codon-based analyses showed significantly lower nonsynonymous than synonymous substitution rates in Leporidae, Ochotonidae and the complete dataset, indicating purifying selection and strong functional constraint. Phylogenetic analyses consistently separated Leporidae from Ochotonidae, although relationships among recently diverged Lepus species were weakly resolved. Most intraspecific polymorphisms were synonymous, whereas only a limited number of missense variants were detected. Unique amino acid substitutions in the dark-coated Pentalagus furnessi and Romerolagus diazi are of particular interest as candidate pigmentation variants, although their functional effects require experimental validation. Overall, MC1R combines substantial phylogenetic signal at deeper taxonomic levels with limited resolution of recent divergences, while its coding sequence remains strongly constrained. These data provide a comparative framework for future functional, population genetic and phylogenomic studies of pigmentation and evolution in lagomorphs.

items.title: Size-Divergent Contributors and Interactions to PM Oxidative Potential: EC-Organics Additivity and Ion-Metal Synergy.
items.abstract: Atmospheric particulate matter (PM), with complex physicochemical properties such as composition and size, poses serious health risks. Oxidative potential (OP) is considered a key factor in PM's health effects, but its relationship with PM properties and sources remains unclear. This study investigated approximately 100 PM components (environmental and bioaccessible concentrations) across nine size fractions using ion chromatography, carbon analysis, inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectrometer, and gas chromatograph-mass spectrometer. OP was detected by dithiothreitol (DTT) assay, and bioaccessibility was evaluated using simulated epithelial lung fluid (SELF). The dominant components and their interactions were found to be different across sizes. Fine PM OP is mainly driven by elemental carbon (EC), organic compounds (e.g., 9,10-phenanthrenequinone), and ions, while coarse PM OP is dominated by bioaccessible metals (e.g., Ni, Cu, As, Mn). Integrating ambient data and experimental validation, we find interactions among components: additive effects of EC and 9,10-phenanthrenequinone with high intrinsic OP dominate in fine particles, while in coarse fractions, ions drive OP enhancement by facilitating metal bioaccessibility. Furthermore, it's found that bioaccessibility greatly affects the contribution of metals to OP but has limited impact on organics. By integrating positive matrix factorization (PMF) and an extreme gradient boosting model combined with SHapley Additive exPlanations (XGBoost-SHAP), this study evaluates how PM sources influence OP. Key sources contributing to OP vary by size: traffic, secondary aerosols, and combustion show greater relative importance in predicting OP V in PM V in PM 2.1-3.3 ; traffic and dust are among the more influential sources in PM 3.3-10 . This study provides the first comprehensive evidence that the key components and their interactions associated with OP differ across sizes.

items.title: Survival and swim speed performance of Alewife, a small, laterally compressed prey fish, following acoustic transmitter implantation.
items.abstract: Alewife (Alosa pseudoharengus) is a small, pelagic fish that is an important prey source for piscivores in the Laurentian Great Lakes, yet its spatial ecology is poorly known, which limits the ability to monitor populations. Acoustic telemetry is a tool to understand spatial ecology; however, there may be tagging effects on a smaller body-sized population of Alewife where tag burden is higher than in larger-bodied marine populations. We assessed survival, swimming abilities and healing of Alewife from Lake Ontario after acoustic transmitter implantation. In a laboratory setting, tagged Alewife were compared across tag sizes (Innovasea models V6 and V7-4x), controls and shams (surgery conducted with no tag implantation) in fall 2024 (n = 76). Tagging survival was also assessed in spring 2025 (variety of V7 tags) when Alewife had developed gonads and across sex (n = 126). Capture, transport and laboratory introduction resulted in moderate mortality in fall 2024 (40%), which was reduced in spring 2025 (4%), an improvement we attribute to the refined protocols reported here. Post-treatment (transmitter, sham, control) survival was high (100% in fall; 91% in spring) with tag burdens from 2 to 8%. We attribute lower spring survival to gonad development, but it was also influenced significantly by a holding tank effect. Two weeks post-tagging, Alewife achieved critical swimming speeds of 37.9 ± 7.6 cm s -1 , with no significant differences among treatments. Incisions were all scored as moderately to highly healed 2 weeks post-surgery. Our findings establish the feasibility of tagging smaller, freshwater Alewife with acoustic tags, following best practices reported here, for telemetry applications in the Great Lakes to better understand the spatial ecology of this lower trophic species of major management and ecosystem importance.

items.title: Disentangling intrinsic and extrinsic drivers of gill ectoparasitism in an endemic North African leuciscid.
items.abstract: Seasonal variation in fish parasite burden reflects the interplay between parasite transmission, environmental conditions and host characteristics, yet the relative contributions of these factors remain incompletely understood in many wild freshwater fishes. We investigated gill ectoparasitism in the Maghrebian Bleak (Tropidophoxinellus callensis), a freshwater fish endemic to Algeria and Tunisia, examining variation in parasite burden in relation to season, host age, physiological condition and dietary breadth. Three ectoparasite taxa were identified, Gyrodactylus barbi, Trichodina sp. and Dactylogyrus fraternus, providing the first characterisation of the gill ectoparasite assemblage of this species. Parasite burden peaked in summer, and season remained significantly associated with ectoparasitism after accounting for host characteristics, although much of the explained variation was shared among predictors. Parasite abundance increased with host age in unadjusted analyses, but the relationship reversed after accounting for hepatic condition and other predictors. Furthermore, parasite burden exhibited a nonlinear relationship with hepatic condition, reaching its highest values at intermediate hepatosomatic indices. These findings demonstrate that seasonal variation in ectoparasitism is closely intertwined with host ontogeny and physiological condition, highlighting the importance of considering intrinsic and extrinsic factors jointly when investigating host-parasite relationships.

items.title: Quantifying time-dependent meteorological controls on lake eutrophication through cumulative-hysteresis response mapping: Evidence from Erhai Lake.
items.abstract: Lake eutrophication can respond to meteorological drivers through both cumulative and hysteresis (C&H) effects, but these time-dependent effects are difficult to identify with conventional correlations or fixed-lag analyses. This study proposed a cumulative-hysteresis response mapping to identify the sensitive climate factors and determine the influencing time window on lake eutrophication. Specifically, a C&H matrix of a meteorological indicator and its C&H effect matrix was constructed. The C&H effect matrix, a three-dimensional dataset comprising cumulative days, hysteresis days, and correlation parameters, was used to screen meteorological indicators (SMIs). Regression models incorporating SMIs and the trophic level index (TLI) were further developed to evaluate predictive performance. The proposed approach was applied to Erhai Lake in the Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau. Seven categories of SMIs were identified: radiation, precipitation, evaporation, wind field, temperature, humidity, and air pressure. Their cumulative effect windows ranged from 71.25 to 149 days, while hysteresis windows ranged from 29.25 to 194.08 days. Temperature, air pressure, humidity, and evaporation had a positive effect on TLI. In contrast, radiation, precipitation, and the wind-field variables showed negative effects. Regression models based on the 7 SMIs were developed to simulate variations in TLI. The model achieves satisfactory performance in reproducing whole-lake TLI and adequately captures the temporal trends of TLI across the 11 investigated sites. These results demonstrate that the cumulative-hysteresis response mapping can effectively identify key meteorological drivers and their response windows.The identified sensitive meteorological indicators further facilitate meteorology-informed evaluation of lake eutrophication risk.

items.title: Foraging Habits and Habitats of the Indian Swiftlet (Aerodramus unicolor), in Maharashtra, India.
items.abstract: Specialized aerial insectivores, such as swifts and swiftlets, are essential for sustaining ecosystem equilibrium by regulating insect populations. Despite their ecological significance, the foraging ecology of many swiftlets remains understudied. Therefore, we aimed to understand the foraging extent, habits, and habitat of the Indian Swiftlet. We conducted this study between January and December 2022 across seven representative habitats in Sindhudurg, Maharashtra. We collected the primary data through a presence survey, while the secondary data were sourced from GBIF.org. Distance matrix analysis was used to estimate the foraging extent at the regional and global levels. We used a scan sampling method to document foraging habits and a handheld environmental meter to record microclimatic variables. We documented the tree composition at every foraging site using quadrat sampling. The proximity of their breeding colonies primarily influences the Indian Swiftlet's foraging range, extending up to 20 km in Sindhudurg and over 80 km from the known breeding sites in India and Sri Lanka. Over 715 h of observations (2860 sets each of 10 min) revealed 15 different foraging habits of the Indian Swiftlet. The species prominently uses wetlands surrounded by agricultural lands and plantation areas as primary habitats, whereas the rocky shores and lateritic plateaus were avoided. Out of all the microclimatic drivers, relative humidity influences flutter activity in the swiftlets, which corresponds to the feeding maneuver. This study contributed to understanding the foraging dynamics of the Indian Swiftlet in Sindhudurg. It also highlighted the importance of wetlands in sustaining swiftlet populations and the need to prioritize habitats for conservation in the face of habitat degradation and a changing climate.

items.title: Toward standard testing methods in biophotovoltaics based on cyanobacteria.
items.abstract: Microbial biophotovoltaics (BPVs) are an emerging renewable energy technology that harnesses photosynthetic microorganisms to generate electric current. Despite the rapid growth of the field, the lack of standardized testing and reporting methods currently prevents the benchmarking of devices, slowing technological progress. This article provides a critical analysis of the experimental practices used in BPV research, highlighting the significant variability in device configurations, light sources, electrode materials, biomass quantification methods, and electrochemical measurement protocols reported in the literature. It further considers the historical standardization of protocols for conventional photovoltaics (PVs) and the resulting acceleration of the maturation and market adoption of PV technologies. Drawing inspiration from conventional PVs, the article outlines key steps toward BPV standardization, including defining common testing conditions, methods for data normalization, shared reference systems, and round-robin testing protocols. Establishing consensus in the testing protocols would significantly improve reproducibility and enable meaningful comparisons across laboratories, accelerating the development and deployment of BPVs.

items.title: Collective Movement in the Wintering Oriental Storks (Ciconia boyciana): Longer Food Handling Time Is Associated With Successful Initiation.
items.abstract: Collective movement is a widespread phenomenon among social animals and plays a key role in shaping both individual fitness and population dynamics. By enabling individuals to exploit social information from conspecifics, collective movement can improve foraging efficiency, reduce predation risk, and facilitate coordinated decision-making. Despite growing interest in collective movements, studies on waterbirds remain limited, largely because tracking individual level traits and social relationships in large, mobile populations is difficult. In this study, we examined the effects of individual behavioral characteristics, flock characteristics, and position within a flock on the collective movement of Oriental Storks ( Ciconia boyciana ) in winter from 2024 to 2025, controlling for the effects of other variables (winter period and habitat type). Our results show that individuals who spent more time tracking and handling food resources were more likely to become leaders during collective movements. We found that initiation success was positively associated with the initiator's food handling time and flock size, whereas successful foraging rate, failed foraging rate, locomotion rate, and flock position were not independently associated with initiation success after adjustment for the flock-level, temporal, and habitat variables. Among successful initiation events, movement duration increased with food handling time but decreased with flock size. Successful foraging rate, failed foraging rate, locomotion rate, and flock position were not independently associated with movement duration. Therefore, our study demonstrates that storks exhibiting these foraging patterns were more likely to act as unintentional leaders when initiating collective movement, and these individuals typically exhibited longer food handling times. Further studies using marking and GPS tracking are needed to identify which individual traits most strongly influence follower responses and to clarify how social interactions shape decision-making and the maintenance of collective movements.

items.title: Persistence of Multifractal Dynamics at the Mammalian Neuromuscular Junction Across Extracellular Calcium Conditions
items.abstract: The neuromuscular junction represents a relevant experimental model for revealing important biophysical mechanisms underlying synaptic transmission. In this work, we revisited the time-series analysis of electrophysiological recordings obtained from mammalian diaphragm neuromuscular junctions. We applied multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis (MFDFA) to assess whether intervals between spontaneous potentials exhibit multifractal behavior at physiological extracellular calcium concentrations and at hypocalcemic and hypercalcemic levels. Surprisingly, we observed a robust, stable multifractal profile across all electrophysiological recordings, regardless of calcium concentration. Therefore, our results provide support for a rich and complex scenario governing neurotransmitter release. Based on these findings, we discuss their biophysical significance and physiological implications.

items.title: Analytical Modeling of Thermal Shield-Induced Tilt Noise in Lunar Regolith: Constraints on Future Lunar Seismometers and Gravitational waves Detectors
items.abstract: Surface features such as thermal shields, insulating blankets, and exposed rocks modify the absorption of solar radiation in the lunar regolith, producing lateral temperature gradients missed by one-dimensional thermal models. These gradients cause thermoelastic deformation that tilts surface-deployed seismic instruments, adding long-period noise. We develop an analytical framework, based on Hankel transforms in a semi-infinite regolith, that treats these features as perturbations to a laterally uniform diurnal thermal state; linearity allows multiple features to be superposed. The framework is applied to the Apollo 14 Passive Seismic Experiment, including the seismometer thermal shield and surrounding instruments. The Apollo shield is a multilayer insulation (MLI) blanket that passes a fraction of the solar-flux fluctuation to the ground. Near local noon the shadow of the instrument body shifts by 2-5 cm across this dimly lit ground. This asymmetry dominates the tilt; its median amplitude spectral density reaches 7-8 x 10^(-11) rad/sqrt(Hz) in the 1-5 mHz band, about three orders of magnitude above that of an opaque shield. Enlarging an opaque shield lowers the tilt, but the body-shadow tilt of an MLI shield does not decrease with shield radius. Thermal heterogeneity can thus generate a tilt bias, present even during seismically quiet intervals, that should be included in the noise budget of future lunar horizontal seismometers and inertial GW accelerometers, and the optical transmission of the shield and the instrument's own shadow can matter more than shield size. The analytical framework provides a computationally efficient way to evaluate thermal-shield geometry, albedo contrast, and instrument placement for future lunar seismic and inertial gravitational-wave sensor deployments.

items.title: By Land or By Sea: Ecology in a Foreign (Scot)Land
items.abstract: Biology has taken me from studying coastal mangrove ecosystems in South Florida to surveying ancient temperate rainforests in the Scottish Highlands. In this talk, I'll share the windy path that connected those two very different worlds and the unconventional experiences that shaped my path toward a career in ecology. I'll discuss how undergraduate research opened the door to scientific discovery, why I chose to spend two years traveling across the United States after graduation before pursuing graduate school, and what ultimately led me across the Atlantic to the University of Edinburgh. Along the way, I'll introduce my current dissertation research on Scotland's Atlantic temperate rainforests, where I study how herbivore impacts influence communities of rare rainforest lichens, remarkable organisms that serve as important indicators of forest health. This presentation will focus on the many paths a career in biology can take. I'll share what it's like to conduct ecological fieldwork in Scotland, the realities of graduate school abroad, and the lessons I've learned about embracing uncertainty, seeking opportunities, and following your curiosity. Whether your interests lie on land, beneath the sea, or somewhere above or in between, I hope this talk demonstrates that the path to your goals doesn't have to be a straight line. About the presenter Joe Dubner is an MSc student in Ecology, Evolution and Biodiversity at the University of Edinburgh and an aquarist at Scotland's National Aquarium. He earned dual Bachelor of Science degrees in Biology and Marine Biology from Nova Southeastern University in 2023, where he was also a Razor's Edge Research Scholar. Through RER, he conducted undergraduate research in marine biogeochemistry under Dr. Tyler Cyronak. During his undergraduate studies, Joe served as President of the Nature Club, chaired the Sustainability Club's Climate Change Committee, and was actively involved in science outreach and environmental initiatives. After graduating, Joe spent two years traveling throughout the United States as a professional petsitter and tutor, an unconventional experience that reinforced his passion for wildlife, conservation, and exploring new environments. In 2025, he moved to Scotland to continue his education at the University of Edinburgh. His current research focuses on Atlantic temperate rainforests, investigating how herbivore impacts influence epiphytic lichen communities in Scotland's internationally important rainforest ecosystems. Joe hopes to continue to ultimately build a career as a university professor, combining ecological research, teaching, and mentorship. The path there is not a straight line, and it doesn't have to be.

items.title: Compassionate technology in teacher education: Advancing connection, care, and digital wellbeing in a digital society
items.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies into teacher education has transformed teaching, learning, and professional preparation worldwide. While these innovations have enhanced accessibility, personalisation, collaboration, and instructional efficiency, they have also intensified concerns regarding techno-stress, digital fatigue, emotional disengagement, ethical dilemmas, and diminished human connection. These challenges highlight the need for educational approaches that balance technological advancement with compassion, inclusion, and digital wellbeing. This conceptual paper proposes a Human-Centred Framework for Digital Wellbeing in Teacher Education, developed through a critical synthesis of contemporary literature on compassionate pedagogy, ethical AI, digital wellbeing, inclusive education, and human-centred learning. The framework comprises five interconnected dimensions: Human-Centred AI Integration, Emotional and Psychological Wellbeing, Compassionate Pedagogical Practices, Inclusive and Equitable Digital Learning, and Ethical and Mindful Technology Engagement. Collectively, these dimensions position technology as a means of strengthening empathy, meaningful relationships, equity, and sustainable learning rather than merely improving efficiency. The paper discusses implications for teacher education curricula, digital pedagogy, institutional policy, and professional learning. It argues that preparing future teachers for AI-enabled classrooms requires not only digital competence but also the capacity to create ethical, inclusive, and compassionate learning environments that promote human flourishing in an increasingly digital society.

items.title: A Latent Variable Perspective on EEG Measures of Attentional Control
items.abstract: Attentional control is a core cognitive function, yet there is still a significant debate revolving around its definition, factorial structure and underlying neural mechanisms. Research in this domain has largely developed along two largely disconnected traditions. Psychometric approaches assess individual differences using latent-variable models (e.g., structural equation modeling, confirmatory factor analysis), while cognitive neuroscience focuses on group-level behavioral and neural effects. This raises a critical question: can neural measures robust at the group level validly capture stable individual differences? Or more specifically, can some of the principles and analytical methods adopted in individual-differences research be directly applied to neural correlates of attentional control? The current study aims to address this question. Electroencephalogram data were recorded from participants as they completed four attentional control paradigms: a change detection task, the go/no-go task, the Simon task, and the Stroop task. From each task, we extracted the P3 component and a data-driven decoding accuracy measure as indices of conflict processing and tested whether these neural measures load onto a common latent factor of attentional control. Results revealed weak and largely non-significant correlations. Structural-equation modeling provided no evidence for a common latent factor, despite robust within-task effects at the group level reflected both in the behavioral and the EEG parameters. These findings suggest that EEG components may lack the construct validity needed to reliably capture individual differences in attentional control.

items.title: Subtractive and Divisive Methods for Isolating Neural Oscillations From Broadband Activity Yield Different, Even Conflicting, Power Estimates
items.abstract: Understanding the role of oscillatory brain activity in cognition is a key objective in cognitive neuroscience. However, quantifying the power of narrowband neural oscillations is made challenging by the presence of non-oscillatory broadband activity in the signal. Recently, there has been a proliferation of methods designed to separate oscillatory from non-oscillatory (aperiodic) signals. To perform this separation, these methods must model the relationship between oscillatory and aperiodic components. Crucially, however, such methods rarely explicitly clarify whether they assume that this relationship is additive or multiplicative, an issue compounded by the common use of log-transformed data (i.e., subtraction in log space is equivalent to division in linear space). Here, we show the importance of justifying which assumption about component relations is applied. Using simulated power spectra with additive oscillatory and aperiodic components, we illustrate that methods that assume a multiplicative model, such as the popular specparam (formerly fooof) toolbox, systematically mis-estimate oscillatory activity in ways that can obscure real oscillatory differences between conditions, or even reverse their sign, creating an illusory effect. We then demonstrate these effects in two complementary empirical datasets: (a) a cross-sectional, between-subjects analysis of age-related differences in alpha power, showing how separation approaches impact effect size and detectability; and (b) a within-subjects analysis of pre-stimulus changes in alpha power in a detection task, showing how switching between approaches can greatly reduce the evidence for an effect, leading to different conclusions. These results highlight that researchers must explicitly report and justify assumptions about aperiodic and oscillatory signal combination, as these assumptions have implications not only for analyses of oscillatory activity and resultant conclusions, but also for integration of results across reports (which may implicitly employ different assumptions), and ultimately for the development of theories regarding electrophysiological features and their putative relations to cognition.

items.title: From Pipeline Automation to Scientific Discovery: A Multi-Layer Agent-Driven Bioinformatics Framework
items.abstract: Abstract AI-driven bioinformatics is undergoing a multi-layer evolution from script automation to autonomous scientific discovery. We present a three-layer agent-driven framework spanning this complete spectrum. Layer 1 (Foundation Validation) benchmarks three OpenClaw agents—DESeq2 differential expression, GO/KEGG enrichment, and variant calling—against standard pipelines on TCGA liver cancer and E. coli genomic data, achieving near-perfect padj correlation (r ~ 1.0), >90% pathway overlap, and 95.8% variant concordance. Layer 2 (Domain Tool) presents CRISPR Agent, a multi-layer pipeline integrating Cas-OFFinder candidate discovery, multi-backend off-target scoring (mm_only/CFD/MIT), genomic context annotation, and end-to-end report synthesis, validated on GUIDE-seq/CIRCLE-seq/CHANGE-seq benchmarks. Layer 3 (Scientific Discovery) introduces SciOS, a ten-agent autonomous discovery system governed by a five-gate FORUM review chain (Plan-Execute-Audit-Synthesize-Ratify). Deployed across three single-cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets (457,000 cells, 154,000 spatial spots), SciOS produced three findings: (i) effector genes encoding ion channels, synaptic adhesion, and axon guidance proteins are significantly more conserved across cortical regions than transcription factor identity genes (P = 1.2 x 10^-16, d = 1.27)—a genuinely novel discovery inverting the standard neuroscience hierarchy; (ii) APOE expression is spatially coupled to oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (r = 0.673) but not mature oligodendrocytes (r = 0.136) in the human entorhinal cortex; and (iii) independent pseudobulk validation of CALB1/SOX6 dopamine neuron depletion in Parkinson's disease. The framework's Critic agent mandated average confidence reductions of -0.06 across all claims, while a Literature agent corrected a directional error introduced by autonomous analysis without domain context. These three layers collectively define an evolution from "doing" to "designing" to "discovering," establishing a methodological foundation for fully autonomous scientific discovery systems.

items.title: Adolescent social isolation and re-socialization increases alcohol intake and aversion-resistant drinking in male and female rats.
items.abstract: Rationale Adverse experiences during adolescence, especially social isolation, increases risk for alcohol use disorders (AUDs). Previous rodent studies of adolescent social isolation (ASI) encompassed all stages of adolescence and/or maintained isolation into adulthood, limiting identification of vulnerable stages of adolescence. Utilizing males only, or combining the sexes, also may have contributed to contradictory findings. Objectives Investigate social isolation restricted to discrete adolescent stages in combination with re-socialization and then persistent alcohol drinking. Determine whether adolescent isolation during specific developmental time periods, with or without subsequent re-socialization, leads to increased alcohol drinking in males or females. Methods Male and female Wistar rats underwent one of six housing conditions: (1) isolation from postnatal day (P)21-42 followed by re-socialization (ASIR-Early), (2) isolation from P42-63 followed by re-socialization (ASIR-Late), or (3) continuous isolation from P21 onward (ASI), or (4​-6) one of three appropriate control treatments. Alcohol-related behaviors were assessed in adulthood using intermittent-access two-bottle choice drinking (IAP), limited daily access (LDA-20) procedures, quinine-adulterated aversion-resistant drinking (ARD), and alcohol re-exposure following prolonged abstinence. Results In general, ASIR-Early and ASI elevated alcohol drinking in males and females, when compared to contemporary controls, during IAP, LDA-20, ARD, and after prolonged withdrawal, while ASIR-Late had largely similar effects as control conditions. However, for females, only ASI led to greater ARD at the highest quinine dose and also increased alcohol drinking after prolonged withdrawal. In contrast, for males, ASIR-Early and ASI had largely similar enhancement of alcohol drinking. Conclusions Under these conditions, isolation housing that encompassed the early adolescent period produced enduring increases in alcohol-related behaviors, with re-socialization perhaps more protective in females against ARD and elevated intake after abstinence. These results inform future studies that will investigate neural mechanisms underlying ASI-induced enhancement of alcohol drinking.

items.title: Competition Indices and Environmental Variables Weakly Improve Predictions of Natural Population Fluctuations on Independent Data
items.abstract: The debate about the relative importance of interspecific competition and environmental factors in annual population fluctuations has persisted in ecology for many decades. Ecologists face the challenge of determining the extent to which interspecific competition and environmental factors impact population growth rates. We assess the predictive ability of models with and without interspecific competition and environmental covariates to predict population size one year beyond the model-building data. For 11 of 14 datasets a model with interspecific competition and/or environmental factors make better mean ‘absolute’ prediction error. However, none of the models with interspecific competition and/or environmental variables make predictions that are statistically significantly superior to the random walk model. Overall, in about 60% of the sites, models with interspecific competition and environmental variables show performance worse than the random walk baseline model on independent data. We conclude that there is weak evidence that incorporating interspecific competition and/or environmental covariates leads to improved model predictive ability. A thorough assessment of the relative importance of interspecific competition and environmental factors in annual population fluctuations will require evaluating the predictive power of a broader range of models that incorporate ecology of species traits at each generational time.

items.title: Spatial distribution and uncertainty assessment of heavy metals in coastal groundwater of northern Hainan Island using sequential Gaussian simulation.
items.abstract: Heavy metal contamination in coastal aquifers has attracted increasing attention, yet probabilistic characterization of spatial uncertainty remains limited. This study investigated the coastal aquifer of northern Hainan Island using 315 sampling locations. Sequential Gaussian simulation (SGS) was applied to characterize the spatial heterogeneity, prediction uncertainty, and threshold exceedance probabilities of Fe, Mn, As, and Pb, and was compared with ordinary kriging (OK). Mean concentrations followed the order Fe > Mn > As > Pb. Mn had the highest exceedance percentage among the measured samples (26.35%), followed by Fe (2.54%), As (1.59%), and Pb (1.59%). Spatially, Mn and Pb concentrations generally increased from coastal to inland areas. Mn formed an extensive high-concentration zone in the central-southern region, whereas As formed a relatively continuous high-concentration belt along the northern coast. OK and SGS produced highly consistent regional trends, but SGS better preserved local spatial variability and reduced the smoothing effect of OK. The SGS simulation standard deviations showed that uncertainty for Mn was concentrated in the southern region, whereas high uncertainty for As occurred in the northeastern coastal area. Threshold exceedance probability analysis identified a continuous high-risk belt for Mn in the southern region, where probabilities exceeded 0.6 and locally approached 1.0. Mn was therefore the contaminant requiring the highest management priority. Overall, SGS extends conventional concentration interpolation into a probabilistic risk-zoning approach and supports refined identification and management of heavy metal contamination risks in coastal groundwater.

items.title: No effect of post-meiotic sperm aging on male fertility in a species with finite sperm production.
items.abstract: Post-meiotic sperm aging occurs when mature sperm cells are stored in the male reproductive tract before mating. In most species, males produce sperm throughout their life, thereby partially mitigating sperm aging by replenishing their sperm supply. By contrast, sperm production is finite in some species, preventing aging sperm to be replaced by new gametes. Finite sperm production is therefore predicted to impose strong selective pressure to minimize post-meiotic sperm aging. In this study, we tested this prediction by investigating post-meiotic sperm aging in a species with finite sperm production and pre-mating sperm storage in males, the buff-tailed bumblebee (Bombus terrestris). We adopted an integrative multi-level approach combining high-throughput flow cytometry, dual-type DNA methylation profiling, and untargeted proteomics. We identified molecular and cellular hallmarks of aging in sperm cells during male storage, including reduced sperm viability, elevated oxidative stress, increased DNA damage, and altered DNA methylation and proteomic profiles. However, these changes were modest in magnitude. Accordingly, neither male fertility nor reproductive fitness declined with age: males (hence, sperm) of different ages achieved similar mating success and sired colonies that did not differ in foundation success, productivity, composition, or lifespan, indicating that post-meiotic sperm aging has no significant impact on male reproductive performance. Together, our results support the prediction that finite sperm production is associated with limited post-meiotic sperm aging. More broadly, they challenge the assumption that advancing paternal age inevitably compromises reproductive function and highlight the importance of life history in shaping reproductive aging.

items.title: The Curse of Dimensionality: How Does it Affect Dynamical Systems Research in Clinical Psychology?
items.abstract: The dynamical systems approach is gaining attention across many subfields of clinical psychology. Although the systems are assumed to involve many variables, theoretical and methodological work in this field often relies on low-dimensional stability landscapes, creating potential mismatches. In this article, I discuss how high-dimensional stability landscapes may challenge intuitions derived from low-dimensional landscapes, put forward a potential solution based on sufficient low-dimensional descriptions, and propose a future research agenda centered on dimensionality reduction approaches that emphasize preserving information about stability and transitions.

items.title: Estimating the replicability of psychology experiments after an initial failure to replicate
items.abstract: When a replication fails, scientists have to decide whether to make a second attempt or move on.Psychology researchers who attempt to replicate studies often face this decision, given the empiricalrate of replication success in psychology, which is lower than desired. Here, we report 17 re-replicationsof experiments for which an original replication had failed. In 5/17 of these “rescue” projects (29%),the “rescue” study mostly or fully replicated the original results, albeit with a smaller effect size;in the other 12, the second replication was also judged to have failed. We speculate that successfulrescue projects were due to larger sample sizes or methodological changes such as attention checks. Inthe absence of obvious weaknesses in a failed replication study’s sample or procedure, however, it maybe most efficient to stop pursuing an effect after a single failed replication.

items.title: Behavior–emotion decoupling as micro-level spatial injustice: Why urban villages morphology fails to heal marginalised groups in China
items.abstract: Abstract Urban villages host tens of millions of rural-to-urban migrants in Chinese cities, yet their dense, fragmented morphology is widely assumed to erode residents' mental health (Wu, 2016). Drawing on spatial justice theory and environmental psychology, this study asks whether urban villages morphology shapes healing environments differently for marginalised groups versus indigenous residents.Using Kuidong Village (Xuzhou, China) as a case study, we integrate Baidu POI and heatmap data, SegNet-based street view segmentation, behavioral observation, and a seven-dimension emotion survey (N = 162) into a multi-group mediation framework linking spatial configuration, daily behavior, and emotional perception. We identify systematic behavior–emotion decoupling among migrants: their activity patterns respond to spatial form, yet no behavior produces emotional returns. All three mediation pathways (enclosure via necessity to depression, greenery via spontaneity to safety, and permeability via sociality to relaxation) fail for migrants while remaining significant for indigenous residents. Healing resources thereby remain visible yet unusable. We interpret this decoupling as a form of micro-level spatial injustice, extending spatial justice theory from the macro distribution of resources to micro psychological pathways. We accordingly propose differentiated spatial interventions to restore migrants' behavior–emotion linkage, transforming urban villages from mere dwelling spaces into healing places.

items.title: Sensitivity to Physical Activity Predicts Daily Physical Activity Levels in People with Chronic Musculoskeletal Pain.
items.abstract: Objective This study investigated whether Sensitivity to Physical Activity (SPA, a measure of changes in pain responses to standardized physical tasks) predicts self-report and objective physical activity levels in individuals with chronic musculoskeletal (MSK) pain. We also examined whether SPA offers predictive value in activity levels beyond psychological factors and quantitative sensory testing (QST). Methods Sixty-one participants with chronic MSK pain completed a standardized SPA lifting task, psychological questionnaires (Tampa Scale of Kinesiophobia, Pain Catastrophizing Scale), and QST (pressure pain thresholds, temporal summation of pain). Participants wore an accelerometer for up to nine days to objectively measure physical activity. Self-reported activity was assessed using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire. Hierarchical regression analyses were conducted to evaluate the predictive value of SPA, psychological, and QST measures on physical activity outcomes. Results SPA significantly predicted objectively measured daily physical activity levels, explaining unique variance in both average daily steps (ΔR²=11.6%, P=0.005) and time spent performing moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (ΔR²=6.1%, P=0.030), after controlling for age and pain levels. SPA was not associated with self-reported physical activity. Neither psychological factors nor QST measures significantly predicted objective or subjective activity levels. Discussion Lifting-based SPA emerged as a unique predictor of real-world physical activity in individuals with chronic MSK pain, outperforming traditional psychological and sensory predictors. These findings support the potential of SPA as a biopsychosocial marker for physical inactivity and the importance of objective activity monitoring in rehabilitation planning.

items.title: Burden and Trends of Antimicrobial Resistance Among Major Clinical Bacterial Pathogens in Bangladesh (2019–2024): A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a severe global public health threat, particularly in low- and middle-income countries like Bangladesh, where factors such as unregulated antibiotic use, weak surveillance, and inadequate healthcare infrastructure exacerbate the problem. A unified, up-to-date assessment of recent resistance trends is crucial to guide effective public health interventions and optimize clinical decision-making. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the prevalence and antimicrobial resistance patterns of major clinical bacterial pathogens in Bangladesh between 2019 and 2024. The analysis followed PRISMA guidelines, with data sourced from PubMed, Google Scholar, ResearchGate, and DOAJ. A random-effects model was employed to synthesize data from 30 eligible studies encompassing over 270,000 clinical specimens, providing estimates for the pooled prevalence and resistance patterns of eight major bacterial pathogens. Median resistance (MR) and interquartile ranges (IQR) were also calculated to determine resistance levels for each pathogen–antibiotic pair. The findings revealed that Gram-negative bacteria were most prevalent, with Escherichia coli (12%), Klebsiella spp. (8%), and Pseudomonas spp. (7%) as the most common pathogens. Alarmingly high antibiotic resistance rates were observed across all species, particularly in Enterococcus spp. (70%), Pseudomonas spp. (56%), Acinetobacter spp. (53%), E. coli (46%), Proteus spp. (44%), Staphylococcus aureus (43%), Klebsiella spp. (41%), and Enterobacter spp. (40%). Resistance was notably high for conventional antibiotics such as β-lactams, cephalosporins, and fluoroquinolones, while concerning levels of resistance were also detected against last-resort antibiotics including carbapenems, colistin, and certain aminoglycosides. These findings highlight the urgent need for national antimicrobial stewardship programs, enhanced surveillance, and coordinated public health strategies to mitigate the escalating threat of AMR.

items.title: Network Pharmacology, Molecular Docking, and Molecular Dynamics Simulation Analysis Reveal Insights into the Molecular Mechanism of Schizandrin A in Treating Age-related Hearing Loss
items.abstract: Abstract Age-related hearing loss (ARHL) is a bilateral, symmetrical, and progressive sensorineural disorder associated with aging and represents a major public health challenge in aging societies. Schisandrin A (SchA), a biphenylocyclooctene-type lignan monomer isolated from the dried fruits of Schisandra chinensis, exhibits antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects, regulates mitochondrial autophagy, and inhibits apoptosis. This study aimed to investigate the potential molecular mechanisms underlying the therapeutic effects of Sch A against ARHL using network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Network pharmacology identified 137 potential targets. Gene ontology (GO) enrichment analysis revealed that these genes mediate cellular signaling responses, ion balance, and physiological homeostasis through kinase cascade signaling, ion channel regulation, and synaptic signal transmission. Kyoto encyclopedia of genes and genomes pathway enrichment analysis identified calcium and cAMP signaling pathways, neuroactive ligand signaling, and neuroactive ligand-receptor interactions as major enriched pathways. Molecular docking and MD simulations were used to screen binding affinities. The binding energies for SRC, STAT3, EGFR, HSP90AA1, HIF1A, and PTGS2 were all lower than − 5.0 kcal/mol, indicating high binding affinity and stable binding modes. Among these, PTGS2 exhibited the lowest binding energy. MD simulation revealed that the PTGS-deoxyschizandrin complex had an overall average root mean square deviation (RMSD) of 0.18 nm, a protein backbone and ligand RMSD of 0.22 and 0.09 nm, respectively. The mean radius of gyration and solvent-accessible surface area were 3.16 and 443.21 nm, respectively, suggesting that the complex did not undergo significant expansion or contraction. The average root mean square fluctuation values for A and B chains of PTGS were 0.12 and 0.13 nm, respectively, indicating low overall flexibility and a relatively stable conformation. The complex formed strong hydrogen bonds, potentially exerting a neuroprotective effect. This study demonstrated the potential molecular mechanisms underlying the effects of Sch A against ARHL and provides a theoretical basis for its application and further drug development.

items.title: Postnatal Family Planning Service and Documentation Gaps in Ondo and Kebbi States, Nigeria: A Four-Year Retrospective Analysis of Counselling, Recorded Acceptance, and Method Mix, 2022–2025 Running head: Postnatal family planning counselling and acceptance gaps in Nigeria
items.abstract: Abstract Background The postpartum period creates repeated opportunities to prevent unintended and closely spaced pregnancies, yet routine information systems often record counselling and contraceptive provision incompletely. We assessed postnatal family planning counselling, recorded contraceptive acceptance and method mix in public facilities in two contrasting Nigerian states. Methods We conducted a retrospective analysis of facility-month aggregate National Health Management Information System records from 23 public facilities in Ondo and Kebbi States, January 2022-December 2025. The primary counselling-to-acceptance ratio used months with both indicators recorded, more than zero women counselled, and acceptors not exceeding women counselled. Method mix was restricted to months in which all four recorded methods (IUD, Implant NXT, Jadelle and Depo-Provera) were present and their sum equalled the acceptor count. We reported counts, percentages, Wilson 95% confidence intervals and data-completeness indicators; no causal comparisons were undertaken. Results The analytic dataset contained 988 facility-months. Counselling was recorded in 902/988 (91.3%) and acceptors in 595/988 (60.2%). After excluding 10 internally inconsistent months and 117 paired zero/zero months from rate estimation, 456 months contributed 20,284 counselled women and 3,810 acceptors, a pooled ratio of 18.8% (95% CI 18.3–19.3). The ratio was 23.2% in Kebbi and 15.2% in Ondo, but acceptor reporting was substantially lower in Kebbi (219/556; 39.4%) than Ondo (376/432; 87.0%). Recorded annual ratios varied from 3.9% to 41.9% in Kebbi and from 7.4% to 19.4% in Ondo. Among reconciled complete method records, Ondo recorded 1,586 methods: IUD 35.8%, Implant NXT 32.0%, Jadelle 31.2% and Depo-Provera 1.0%. Kebbi contributed only 49 reconciled methods, precluding stable inference about its method mix. Conclusions Routine records indicate a substantial gap between documented counselling and recorded contraceptive acceptance, marked facility heterogeneity, and severe state- and level-specific incompleteness. The findings support integrating method provision with counselling, protecting contraceptive choice and commodity availability, and making completeness and internal consistency visible in routine dashboards.

items.title: From Reservoirs to Potential Vectors of Superbugs: Wild Birds Co-Harboring Extended- Spectrum Beta-Lactamases and Plasmid-Mediated Quinolone Resistance determinants in Enterobacteriaceae isolates in Pakistan
items.abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a significant health issue of the 21st century. Wild birds are increasingly recognized as reservoirs of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria. They are ecologically important because they have travelling ability across globe, and with no direct antimicrobial interaction making them an important part of One Health interface to predict environmental contamination of MDRs and its dissemination. This study aimed to assess the prevalence and co-occurrence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) and plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance (PMQR) determinants in Enterobacteriaceae isolates from the gut of wild birds in Islamabad region. Using standard bacterial characterization techniques in total, 342 Gram-negative Enterobacteriaceae isolates were obtained from fresh fecal droppings collected seasonally at eight locations with various types of facilities in Islamabad Pakistan including hospitals. zoo, parks and other public areas. Disk Diffusion test was performed to confer quinolones resistance and double-disk synergy test (DDST) was used to confirm ESBL production. Multiplex PCR was used to detect PMQR genes ( QnrA, QnrB, and QnrS ), whereas aac (6′)-Ib-cr was detected using conventional PCR. Statistical analysis was used to assess inter-variable associations. A total of 342 isolates were obtained, of which 118 (34.5%) were ESBL producers. Among ESBL-positive isolates that were phenotypically co-resistant to ciprofloxacin and/or nalidixic acid (Quinolones), 73 (61.8%) carried at least one gene of the PMQR family. The most common PMQR determinants were QnrS (76.7%) and aac (6′)-Ib-cr (47.9) %. The co-harboring isolates were dominated by Escherichia coli (82.2%). K. pneumoniae showed a high carriage of aac (6′)-Ib-cr (90%) and QnrB (60%) genes. The highest levels were observed in autumn and winter. Multi-gene co-carriage patterns, where ESBL and PMQR genes occur on a single plasmid, were inferred and were similar to those found in other major plasmid families, IncF, IncI, and IncHI. Wild birds are important reservoirs and active spreaders of MDR Enterobacteriaceae carrying ESBL and PMQR determinants on transferable plasmids in the urban environment of Islamabad. Based on these results, the need to involve wildlife surveillance in One Health-based AMR surveillance programs and increase antibiotic stewardship in Pakistan is highlighted.

items.title: A Sandwich-Structured Dual-Mode Fabric with Temperature-Adaptive Spectral Tunability for All-Season Outdoor Personal Thermal Management.
items.abstract: Owing to global warming, sudden temperature fluctuations are occurring with greater frequency, which exacerbates risks to public health. Passive radiative cooling and solar heating technologies have unique advantages of requiring no energy input, rendering them highly suitable for thermal management textiles. The operation of the dual-mode fabric with cooling and heating functions primarily relies on the contrast between the solar reflectance on the cooling side and solar absorption on the heating side. However, the regulation of infrared emissivity in both modes tends to be ignored. Here, we report a dual-mode woven fabric based on a sandwich structure that features temperature-adaptive spectral tunability for all-season outdoor personal thermal management. The combination of a polydimethylsiloxane/nano-zinc oxide (PDMS/nano-ZnO) radiative cooling layer with a polydopamine (PDA) solar heating layer constituted the basis of the dual-mode switchable fabric. More importantly, the introduction of eicosane into the porous fibers realized the spectral tunability in response to ambient temperature. The solar reflectance in the cooling mode showed an increase of nearly 6% at high temperature (>40 °C), while the infrared emissivity in the heating mode was reduced by 13.4% at low temperature (<10 °C). In addition, the introduction of eicosane also endowed the fabric with considerable latent heat to further improve thermal management performance. Its temperature range of response corresponds closely to the human thermal comfort zone. Under solar intensity (Isolar) of ∼500 W/m2, the resulting fabric achieved a temperature increase of ∼7.1 °C compared with bare skin in the heating mode and maintained the average temperature of the covered skin close to that of bare skin in the cooling mode. Thanks to the woven structure, the fabric exhibited desirable mechanical strength, waterproofness, washability, breathability, and moisture permeability. This dual-mode woven fabric was expected to provide further insight into developing responsive dual-mode personal thermal management textiles.

items.title: Association of dietary essential amino acid intake profiles with all-cause, cardiovascular, and cancer mortality.
items.abstract: Dietary essential amino acids (EAAs) are crucial for metabolic health, but their association with long-term mortality remains unclear. Existing studies often focus on individual amino acids, failing to capture patterns of overall combined EAA intake.We analyzed data from two prospective cohort studies: the UK Biobank (UKB; n = 126,336) and the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES; n = 35,084). Latent profile analysis (LPA) was used to identify distinct dietary EAA intake patterns. We examined the associations of these patterns with all-cause, cardiovascular, and cancer mortality using Cox proportional hazards models and pooled the estimates via inverse-variance-weighted fixed-effects meta-analysis. Over a median follow-up of 14.2 years, 14,518 deaths were documented. Four distinct EAA intake profiles were identified: low, moderate, high, and very-high. Compared with the low-profile group, higher EAA intake profiles were associated with a significantly lower risk of all-cause mortality in the pooled analysis (Moderate-profile: HR = 0.87, 95% CI: 0.83-0.92; High-profile: HR = 0.84, 95% CI: 0.78-0.90; Very-high-profile: HR = 0.87, 95% CI: 0.77-0.97). Similar protective associations were observed for cardiovascular and cancer mortality. In exploratory stratified analysis within the UKB cohort, the protective association appeared more pronounced among older adults (≥65 years).Over a median follow-up of 14.2 years, 14,518 deaths were documented. Four distinct EAA intake profiles were identified: low, moderate, high, and very-high. items.title: Sex chromosome turnover as an evolutionary escape from mitonuclear conflict
items.abstract: Mitochondrial and nuclear genomes must remain coadapted to sustain oxidative phosphorylation, yet their distinct inheritance often fosters conflict. Sex chromosomes are a key arena for these dynamics: by biasing co-transmission between nuclear-encoded mitochondrial (N-mt) genes and maternally inherited mtDNA, they can amplify or suppress mitonuclear incompatibilities. Existing syntheses emphasize stable XY (mammals) and ZW (birds) systems, where genomic context is conserved. In contrast, many fishes and amphibians undergo frequent shifts among XY, ZW, and polygenic or environmental sex determination, repeatedly resetting the linkage backdrop for mitonuclear interaction. I propose a comparative framework in which sex-chromosome turnover acts as an evolutionary “escape hatch” from Y- or W-linked deleterious N-mt alleles by entrapping N-mt loci into, or releasing them from, non-recombining sex-linked strata, thereby altering the sex bias and intensity of conflict through time. This hypothesis predicts cyclical pulses of hybrid dysfunction and genomic “scars’’ that record historical entrapment, offering testable predictions for when turnover entrenches versus relieves mitonuclear conflict. By integrating evidence from stable and labile vertebrate systems, this article outlines how sex-chromosome dynamics shape mitonuclear coadaptation, postzygotic isolation, and ultimately lineage diversification.

items.title: Ecological and economic impacts of increasing landscape connectivity in highly threatened ecological corridors of Tanzania
items.abstract: Abstract Ecological corridors facilitate the flow of ecosystem goods (e.g., wildlife movements) and services (e.g., water regulation) between protected areas, benefiting farmers and governments. To enhance landscape connectivity, farmers within ecological corridors are often encouraged to make pro-conservation decisions, ideally in a coordinated manner. These decisions, however, come along with costs to farmers (e.g., opportunity and transaction costs) as well as governments (e.g., mobilization and enforcement costs). Yet, outcomes of conservation decisions may not be certain due to risks such as droughts and global market crises. This study estimates the ecological and economic impacts of conservation decisions under different levels of landscape connectivity in the Igando-Igawa Wildlife Corridor (IIWC) and the Baga-Kisima Gonja Forest Corridor (BKG) in Tanzania. Using a Decision Analysis approach, we evaluate ecological (forest stock and African savanna elephant populations) and economic (conservation costs, benefits and risks) outcomes under low, medium, and high landscape connectivity scenarios. Then we estimate the expected impact of increasing connectivity as the expected change in outcomes, using low connectivity as a counterfactual. Results from Monte Carlo simulations show that increasing landscape connectivity to medium or higher levels enhances forest stock in both corridors and African savanna elephant movement in IIWC. The expected annual conservation costs for households and the government are two to three times higher in IIWC than in BKG. While the government can benefit from increased landscape connectivity, this was limited for household-level estimates. The results indicate that payment-based policies are necessary to mitigate household losses. Nonetheless, government environmental benefits alone cannot fully bridge this gap.

items.title: Dietary ecology of introduced predators in a fragmented biodiversity hotspot
items.abstract: Introduced predators, such as red foxes (Vulpes vulpes) and feral cats (Felis catus), threaten biodiversity, particularly in fragmented landscapes where loss of structurally complex vegetation reduces refuge for native wildlife. Quantifying predator diets is essential for understanding the pressures they impose. This study morphologically analysed 76 fox and 75 cat stomachs collected from the Fitz-Stirling macro-corridor in southwest Western Australia to compare dietary overlap, identify predation on native and threatened fauna, and assess use of anthropogenic resources. Twenty-seven native species were detected. Cat diet was richer than fox diet (23 vs. 18 species), but fox diet was more diverse. Over half the species consumed were unique to each predator, resulting in limited niche overlap (Schoener’s index: 0.142; Pianka’s index: 0.135). Native mammals were important food for both predators (Frequency of Occurrence (FOO), where FOOfox = 60.5% and FOOcat = 48.5%), with foxes generally consuming larger species than cats. Four threatened species were identified: tammar wallaby (Notamacropus eugenii; FOOfox = 5.5%), western brush wallaby (Notamacropus irma; FOOfox = 22.5%, FOOcat = 2.5%), chuditch (Dasyurus geoffroii; FOOfox = 1.5%) and malleefowl (Leipoa ocellata; FOOcat = 2.5%). Foxes exploited canola crops and carcasses originating from kangaroo culling and from deceased livestock, while cats frequently consumed introduced rodents. These findings highlight shared and distinct predation pressures and reinforce the need for ongoing predator management.

items.title: Age-independent physiological shifts, but no faster life history, in an urban Neotropical frog
items.abstract: This repository contains the raw data, R and Python code, model summaries and figures needed to reproduce all analyses of the article below (main text and Online Resource 1). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24294393 License Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) for data, figures and text, and MIT for code. Summary of the study We tested whether urban males of the Neotropical frog Leptodactylus podicipinus differ from rural males in escape behaviour, energy metabolism, immunity, reproduction, growth and skin traits, and whether these differences depend on age. Frogs were collected in 2024 in Campo Grande, Mato Grosso do Sul, central Brazil, at one urban pond (Lagoa Itatiaia) and two rural ponds (Chácara Buritis and Morro do Ernesto). We dissected 35 males (18 from Chácara Buritis, 17 from the urban pond) and measured 16 morphophysiological traits: somatic indices (liver, heart, spleen, kidney, testes), blood glucose, red and white blood cell counts, leukocyte composition, hepatic melanin, testis locule area and percentage of spermatozoa, skin layer thickness (epidermis, Eberth-Kastschenko layer, total) and dorsal darkness. Six additional males from Morro do Ernesto provided blood cell counts and dorsal darkness. In a separate escape-behaviour experiment, we measured flight initiation distance (FID) and the distance of the first jump of 28 males (15 urban, 13 from Morro do Ernesto). The age of every frog (number of lines of arrested growth, LAGs) was estimated by skeletochronology of phalanges. Each trait was analysed with Bayesian multilevel models in brms (site — age, with frog-level random effects for repeated histological measurements), and a joint model with partial pooling across traits addressed multiplicity. The analysis report follows the Bayesian Analysis Reporting Guidelines (BARG; Kruschke 2021, Nature Human Behaviour 5:1282-1291) and documents priors, convergence diagnostics, posterior predictive checks, cross-validation (PSIS-LOO and 10-fold) and prior sensitivity. items.title: Microscopic Neuromodulation with Locally Enhanced Electric Field
items.abstract: Implantable neural stimulation devices play an important role in fundamental neuroscience research, clinical applications, and emerging technologies such as neuroprosthetics and brain machine interfaces, with increasing demand for spatially precise neuromodulation at cellular and circuit levels. Microelectrode based electrical stimulation relies on charge injection into neural tissue, where irreversible electrochemical reactions at the electrode electrolyte interface may lead to electrode degradation and tissue damage. Although microscale magnetic stimulation provides an alternative, it typically requires sophisticated microcoil architectures and complex fabrication processes. In this work, we introduce a novel neural stimulation mechanism based on localized electric field enhancement. The proposed device employs an electrically insulated sharp metallic tip to concentrate the electric field and generate localized displacement currents capable of activating nearby neurons. Finite element simulations were performed to investigate the underlying stimulation mechanism and establish design guidelines for device fabrication. MEMS based neural probes were subsequently fabricated and experimentally evaluated through in vivo animal studies, with neuronal activation observed at distances of less than 200 micrometers from the probe tip using two-photon imaging. By avoiding Faradaic charge transfer at the tissue interface while offering high spatial localization, orientation selectivity, and a compact device architecture, the proposed approach provides a promising alternative to existing stimulation technologies for chronic and high-density neural interfaces.

items.title: Advances in Neuroscience in an Age of Rapid Technological and AI Innovation – Towards Integration Across Scales
items.abstract: Rapid technological innovation and artificial intelligence (AI) have transformed not only the resolution at which the brain can be observed, but also the questions that can be asked, shifting the field from description toward prediction, regulation and generation. Yet progress has largely advanced along parallel trajectories, and findings at one level rarely inform or constrain the next. Here, we review recent advances in three exemplary domains and propose a future-oriented framework for their integration. First, molecular and cellular neurotechnology, including synaptic proteomics, cryo-electron tomography, super-resolution microscopy, optoacoustic and ultrasound imaging, sonogenetics and molecular MRI, resolves neural processes with unprecedented specificity. Second, AI-based decoding of human brain activity yields precise signatures of complex, subjective conscious experiences in naturalistic contexts and is beginning to inform diagnosis, drug evaluation and individualized neuromodulation in mental disorders. Third, large-scale neural recordings, mechanistic whole-brain simulations, neural foundation models and AI surrogate brains are converging toward individualized digital twin brains. We argue that the next level of progress requires integrating these domains into a closed loop of reciprocal constraints, in which molecular measurements inform model parameters, human signatures define and evaluate what models must reproduce, and model predictions prioritize perturbations that can be tested across domains.

items.title: From Social Brain Modules to Dynamic Network Dysfunction: An Integrative Neuropsychological Framework for Social Cognition
items.abstract: Abstract Social cognition is commonly partitioned into emotion recognition, empathy, theory of mind, and social decision-making, yet these labels do not map clearly onto discrete neural modules. Recent taxonomic, meta-analytic, network-neuroscience, and clinical evidence instead indicates that adaptive social behavior depends on context-sensitive coordination of partially specialized and domain-general systems. We conducted a structured, search-informed integrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE-indexed literature updated on 6 September 2026, supplemented by citation chaining and targeted 2024–2026 searches. We synthesize evidence across social perception and action observation, interoception and affective salience, mentalizing and social-semantic knowledge, valuation and executive control, and large-scale network dynamics. The incremental contribution of this review is not to introduce node dysfunction, disconnection, or network dynamics as isolated concepts, but to integrate them into a cross-diagnostic neuropsychological framework that links task demands and component computations to distinct mechanisms of clinical dysfunction. The framework distinguishes two comparatively evidence-grounded mechanisms namely, (1) node dysfunction, affecting a computationally important region or subsystem, and (2) disconnection, impairing integration among otherwise viable components from (3) hypothesis-generating network-reconfiguration dysfunction, concerning context-appropriate transitions among network states. Frontotemporal dementia provides convergent evidence for node and disconnection mechanisms; Alzheimer disease and Parkinson disease illustrate the importance of general cognitive support and network state; acquired brain injury demonstrates the consequences of focal injury and long-range disconnection; and schizophrenia and autism emphasize mechanistic heterogeneity. Recent psychometric and ecological-validity syntheses further show that conventional task performance maps only incompletely onto everyday social behavior. The framework generates falsifiable predictions for dynamic imaging, electrophysiology, perturbation, lesion-network methods, and naturalistic assessment, with the aim of linking neuropsychological profiles more directly to mechanisms and real-world function.

items.title: Level of Personality Functioning as a Marker of Clinical Stage in Older Adults with Personality Disorders: A Proof-Of-Concept Study.
items.abstract: Objectives Clinical staging has been proposed to improve assessment and treatment planning for personality disorders (PDs) in older adults. This proof-of-concept study examined whether level of personality functioning, assessed with the clinician-rated Level of Personality Functioning Scale - Brief Form 2.0 (LPFS-BF 2.0), might serve as a marker for determining clinical stage in older adults with PDs. Methods Eighty-four patients aged > 60 years receiving specialized mental health care for PDs were included. Clinical stage was established by multidisciplinary consensus based on severity of personality dysfunction and life-course progression of personality pathology. Differences in LPFS-BF 2.0 scores were examined using non-parametric tests and pairwise comparisons. Results LPFS-BF 2.0 scores differed significantly between stages 2 and 4 ( r = .42), but not between adjacent stages. Similar patterns were observed for Self-Functioning and Interpersonal Functioning. Jonckheere-Terpstra tests for ordered trends indicated increasing scores across stages, including for the Total score ( p r = .37). Conclusions These findings provide preliminary evidence of an association between level of personality dysfunction and clinical stage in older adults with PDs. The pattern suggests a gradual increase in severity across stages, but further research is needed to establish the validity of the staging model.
